author: cameronbrooks11
body:
Closes #285. Second item of epic #289, after #283.

## The problem

The set of provider kinds was declared **three times** — a glob over the vendored envelopes, `_SCHEMA_CONFIGS` in the sync script, and `_SCHEMA_CONFIGS` in the verify script — and none of the three was the sha-locked one. It was also circular: `--schema` was `choices=list(_SCHEMA_CONFIGS.keys())`, so a kind had to already be in the dict before it could be synced.

## What changed

Provider locks become `schema_version: 3`, gaining `kind`, `provider_version` and `distribution.templates` (the asset-name patterns, lifted out of the sync script). Both scripts and CI discover kinds by globbing `contracts/upstream/providers/`.

Adding a provider is now a **data change**: one lock + one envelope, no code edit and no workflow edit.

```bash
# Onboard — no code change
sync-upstream-schema-from-release.py --new-provider acme --repo vendor/anolis-provider-acme --tag v1.0.0

# Re-sync — repo and asset names come back out of the lock
sync-upstream-schema-from-release.py --schema provider-config-acme --tag v1.1.0
```

`--asset-template` covers a vendor whose naming differs; it is stored in the lock, so it is passed once and every later sync reads it back.

The three `anolis/` locks stay at v2 — a fixed set of three, not a registry.

## Three new checks the change makes possible

Being the single declaration is what makes these checkable at all:

- **locks ↔ vendored envelopes correspond 1:1** — a lock with no envelope is a kind nothing offers; an envelope with no lock is a kind whose provenance is unrecorded
- **a lock's `provider_version` equals its envelope's** — closes the #283 loop, so the skew warning can't name a version the envelope didn't come from
- **the templates re-render the asset names the lock pinned** — self-verifying, rather than a second copy that can drift

`verify --all-providers` enforces all three in CI (one line replacing three). The suite enforces them on every run too: `just test` never invoked the verify script, so a lock/envelope disagreement was invisible locally until CI rejected the push.

## Sync no longer writes a lock it would itself reject

Asset names are built from the **tag**, and `install.sh` derives provider asset names the same way — so the tag version is what a machine pins. An envelope declaring a different `provider_version` would make #283 report skew on every machine using that provider, permanently, with no way to clear it. Sync now refuses, **before anything is written**, so a rejected sync can't leave an envelope with no lock (itself a CI failure).

## Also

Deletes `releases.provider_repo` / `PROVIDER_ORG` — dead code that assumed every provider lives under `anolishq`. Collapses `ProviderKind` to `string`: the literals typed nothing next to `| string` and only read like an enum someone had to extend.

## Review

Two reviews ran before push and found nine defects, all fixed:

- **the change added a fourth hardcoded kind list** — `EXPECTED_KINDS` in my own new test, which would have failed the suite on the very PR shape this issue exists to enable. Now derived. Same for the pre-existing `available_kinds() == ["bread","ezo","sim"]`.
- sync wrote a self-inconsistent lock with **exit 0** when the tag disagreed with the envelope (reproduced end to end)
- `check_registry` **crashed** instead of reporting on a malformed lock filename (`EZO-...` case typo)
- `.format()` raised uncaught `KeyError`/`IndexError` on any placeholder other than `{version}` — newly reachable via `--asset-template`
- a lock missing `release.repo` silently re-synced from the **anolis** org
- `--repo` + `--upstream-repo` together silently ignored `--repo`
- `--repo-root` didn't compose with `--schema` (choices were built before the root was parsed)
- the new test module's justifying docstring was **factually wrong** about the CI paths-filter
- `scripts/` sat outside mypy, so the new 219-line shared module was unchecked

Mutation testing confirmed the tests discriminate: stubbing `check_lock_shape → []` fails 5, `check_registry → []` fails 7, `_KIND_RE → ^.*$` fails 7.

## Verification

`421 passed, 1 skipped` (up from 399), `101` + `49` frontend, ruff + mypy + svelte-check clean. Migration verified byte-exact — the only line removed from each lock is `"schema_version": 2,`; no sha, repo, tag or asset touched. `--all-providers` passes against the **live** release artifacts, and all three anolis locks still verify.

author: auser
body:
Follow-up to #360, on a fresh branch off `main`. Tests whether chain selection is
the graph path's defect. **It is not**, and the measurement corrects a framing I
recorded in #358.

## Chain selection is exonerated

Chain selection ranks by chain **length** first, with membership margin only
breaking ties among equal-length chains — so a deep chain the context barely
belongs to beats a shallow one it fits well. The hypothesis was that this
discards better-fitting regions which could have supplied the teacher token.

| graph slice | |
| --- | ---: |
| teacher emitted by an active region OUTSIDE the selected chain | **2.95%** |
| …and that region also fits the context better than the chain | **0.59%** |
| mean selected-chain depth | 2.73 |
| mean depth of best teacher emitter | 2.32 |

Usable evidence is discarded in 0.59% of positions. Chain selection is doing
about as well as the cover allows; the depth-first rule is not the defect.

## The correction

Teacher on chain is 1.35%, off-chain active 2.95% — so **active regions emit the
teacher only ~4.3% of the time**, against the 63% candidate recall measured in
#358. The candidate set is `active ∪ predicted ∪ root_top` (global prior top-B,
B = 256), so the teacher arrives via the prior or predicted cloud F, **not via
region emissions**.

I recorded in #358 that "retrieval works, ranking does not," attributing the 63%
to the graph. That attribution was wrong: retrieval works because of the
*context-free* global prior. The graph's regions rarely emit the answer, and the
scorer then boosts those emissions over a candidate list whose useful content
came from elsewhere.

## Open sub-question

This measured off-chain **active** regions only. The remaining ~59% is not yet
split between predicted cloud F and `root_top`, and that split locates the
defect: mostly `root_top` → region emissions carry almost none of the answer, and
the question is compiler-side emission construction; substantially predicted F →
the transition machinery is finding what the regions do not emit.

Relevant to #362 (trigram context rows), which adds context-conditioned evidence
against exactly this gap.

## Verification

`cargo fmt`, `cargo clippy -p uor-r4-graph-certify --all-targets -D warnings`,
and the certify suite (11 files) green. Figures from the Gate C fixture-corpus
run.

Adds one measurement-only accessor, `GraphScorer::node_emits`.

author: axisrow
body:
## Summary

Investigated upstream [openai/codex-plugin-cc#580](https://github.com/openai/codex-plugin-cc/pull/580) ("give the app-server broker an idle timeout, and kill the one it replaces") for portability here. Verified each claimed defect empirically on macOS against this fork's own code before porting anything — did not trust the upstream diff on its own.

**Defect 1 (no idle timeout) — not ported, already covered.** This fork's in-process `BrokerController` (`lib/broker-controller.mjs`) already ships a causal, test-driven idle-timeout mechanism (`CODEX_COMPANION_BROKER_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS`, default 15 min), architected around an injected clock rather than polling socket count on a wall-clock interval. Predates this investigation. No gap to close.

**Defect 2 (stale-replacement path never kills the process it replaces) — partially already fixed, one gap closed here.** `478be42` already tree-kills a just-spawned broker that never becomes ready. The remaining gap: `loadReusableBrokerSessionUnlocked` only tree-kills the recorded pid when the readiness probe confirms the endpoint is live, out of deliberate caution about killing a recycled pid (see the comment it replaces). When the endpoint is unreachable but the process is still alive — e.g. the broker's unix socket file gets swept by external tmp cleanup while the process itself keeps running — that pid was never trusted, so the process is orphaned for its full idle-timeout window and invisible to `session-lifecycle-hook.mjs` once the state file is overwritten by the replacement broker.

Reproduced locally: spawn a real broker via `ensureBrokerSession`, delete its socket file out from under it, call `ensureBrokerSession` again — the original process stays alive (confirmed via `isProcessAlive`) until it eventually self-exits on its own idle timer, not because anything killed it.

**Fix**: trust the pid for tree-kill when either the readiness probe succeeded OR the pid is alive right now (`isProcessAlive`). A live pid recorded in the state file has been the same process continuously since it was written — there's no recycling window to guard against — so killing it is exactly as safe as the existing endpoint-confirmed path. A dead/absent pid still skips the kill, preserving the original PID-reuse guard for the case it actually protects (confirmed the existing "stale reachable brokers preserved" test, which uses a fabricated dead pid `999999`, still passes unchanged).

**Not ported**: upstream's widened stale-probe retry (150ms → 150ms + 1s). This fork already serializes `ensureBrokerSession` via a file lock (`broker-lock.mjs`), so the concurrent-load probe race that retry targets doesn't reproduce here — confirmed empirically with concurrent `ensureBrokerSession` calls under contention; the lock keeps them from stepping on each other regardless of probe timing.

**Not touched**: upstream's stacked-on [#577](https://github.com/openai/codex-plugin-cc/pull/577) (Windows Git Bash/taskkill fix) — irrelevant on macOS, out of scope here.

## Test plan
- [x] Added `replacing a live broker whose endpoint became unreachable still kills its process` in `tests/broker-lifecycle.test.mjs` — spawns a real broker, deletes its socket file, asserts the replacement path still terminates the orphaned process. Uses a 10-minute idle timeout so the assertion can't pass "by accident" via the broker's own self-shutdown (the default test env's 2s idle timeout would otherwise mask a still-broken kill path).
- [x] Verified the test fails without the fix (times out waiting for the orphan to die) and passes with it.
- [x] `npm test` — 190/190 passing, both in this worktree (branched fresh off `main`) and the working branch it was authored on.
- [x] `npm run build` passes for the changed files. Note: `tsc -p tsconfig.app-server.json` currently fails on unrelated pre-existing type errors in `plugins/codex/scripts/lib/codex.mjs` (lines 1209) that exist on `main` independent of this PR — reproduced by stashing this change entirely and re-running build on a clean `main` checkout. Flagging separately, not fixed here (out of scope).

No version bump (targeted fix, no upstream-influenced behavior on the always-covered path).

author: nc1107
body:
Your instinct was right, and thread permissions were only part of it. This works through what each recently shipped feature now implies that nothing has met, separated into what bites now and what is latent.

## The three worth acting on

**1. A thread reply wakes the whole parent channel.** `push::message_recipients` resolves a thread's viewer set to its parent's, so a reply in a two-person side thread sends a push to every backgrounded member who can see the parent. That is the opposite of the Slack model you named as the reason to build threads, and it is the cheapest of these to trigger - a few replies and it is live.

**2. A DM call has no ring, no push, no passive signal at all.** #306 said ringing was out of scope, but this is worse than that admission: there is no voice event in the hub at all, and DM rail rows never consult the voice roster. The person being called has **no way to learn a call started** unless they already have that DM's call pane open. The feature only works if you already know to look.

**3. The report queue leaks thread content past a moderator exclusion.** `channel_scopes_moderation` treats a thread like a DM - opaque and unscoped - instead of resolving it to its parent the way permission checks do everywhere else. So a moderator explicitly denied `MANAGE_MESSAGES` on a channel by overwrite still sees reports for messages inside that channel's threads, **including the content snapshot**.

That third one is a real leak rather than a gap, and it is the same bug shape this project already found and fixed once in that exact file.

## What it looked for and did not find

I asked for each feature to be worked through independently rather than my list expanded, and for negatives to be reported. Markdown, image paste and drag-to-reorder were all expected to yield something and did not: the report card already renders markdown correctly, reorder does publish per-channel live updates, and paste is an alternate route into the existing bounded attachment path.

Each was verified rather than assumed, which is also why a couple of entries are flagged as lower-confidence or as deliberate trade-offs rather than stated as bugs.

## Latent, recorded, not worth building yet

Per-channel ceilings now apply per thread, nothing lists a channel's threads, and a thread cannot be made private, read-only or locked. Real, but none bites until scale or until somebody wants them.

author: robertoaraneda
body:
## Engine gaps: three of four now closed

| # | Gap | Constraints | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Type-name shadowing | `ref-1` | fixed in v1.4.0 |
| 2 | `%ucum` undefined | `age-1` `cnt-3` `dis-1` `drt-1` `ras-1` | **fixed in v1.5.1** |
| 3 | Published FHIR regex rejected as dangerous | `eld-19` `eld-20` | **open** |
| 4 | `Quantity` comparison | `rng-2` | **fixed in v1.5.1** |

v1.5.1 picked up `github.com/gofhir/ucum/v4` as a dependency — presumably how gaps 2 and 4 were closed, since both needed unit handling. That was the approach suggested at the end of gap 4 in the report.

Verified end to end that both now produce verdicts instead of could-not-evaluate warnings:

```
age-1   Condition.onsetAge with a non-UCUM system
        ERROR  Constraint failed: age-1: 'There SHALL be a code if there is a value ...'

rng-2   MedicationRequest ... doseAndRate[0].doseRange, low 10 mg, high 2 mg
        ERROR  Constraint failed: rng-2: 'If present, low SHALL have a lower value than high'
```

## `ucum` v1.0.1 → v4.2.0

We were **three majors behind**, and since fhirpath v1.5.1 depends on `ucum/v4` the build briefly carried **both**: `go.mod` listed v1.0.1 while the engine used v4.2.0. Now one version.

The API we consume is unchanged (`Service`, `New`, `Validate`), and v4's own docs confirm `New` remains correct:

> "Within this variant case carries no meaning... **FHIR uses the case-sensitive form, so New is the right choice there.**"

All 30 codes from the earlier audit return the same verdict — 20 valid, 10 invalid, no drift.

**Worth knowing for future updates:** tags v2 and above are only visible to Go under the `github.com/gofhir/ucum/v4` module path, so `go list -m -versions github.com/gofhir/ucum` stops at v1.0.1 and *looks* stale when it isn't. The repo has tags through v4.2.0.

## A correction to the audit itself

Its first v1.5.1 run reported **ten** failure classes, including `TypeError: expected a String, got HumanName` across 30 constraints. Those were **artefacts of the audit, not engine defects**.

It was cross-evaluating every expression against every synthetic instance — harmless while a mismatched navigation returned empty, but the engine is now strict about types and raises a TypeError instead. So a Timing constraint evaluated against a Patient reported a type mismatch that says nothing about the engine.

The audit now evaluates each expression only against an instance of its own type, which brings it to one real class. The full validator suite passing unchanged on v1.5.1 is what showed those classes were not real — worth noting, because reporting them upstream would have wasted the maintainers' time.

## `models`

Not a dependency of this project, so nothing to update. Its newer tags also resolve as `unknown revision` through the module proxy.

Full suite and `golangci-lint` clean.

author: bimapangestu28
body:
## Root cause

PR #75 fixed the nightly coverage job by passing `GITHUB_TOKEN` to `cargo binstall`, so it stops hitting the anonymous `api.github.com` rate limit. That was correct but it does not close the hole.

`cargo binstall` treats a 403 from `api.github.com` — anonymous rate limit *or* a transient GitHub API failure that a token does not prevent — as a **soft** failure. It does not error. It silently falls through to the `compile` strategy and installs from source instead.

In this workflow `--locked` is already present, so a `cargo install cargo-nextest` source build would technically succeed and the job would stay green. The cost is:

- **~11 minutes of pointless compilation** per affected tool, on every nightly.
- **The real cause is hidden.** The log looks like a slow-but-fine run, not "GitHub API returned 403".

The same degradation was root-caused in greenticai/greentic-cap#39, where the source fallback produced a hard failure rather than a slow green — same mechanism, louder symptom.

## The fix

Add `--disable-strategies compile` to the binstall invocation. The `compile` fallback becomes impossible, so a 403 surfaces as an immediate, legible failure at the install step instead of a silent 11-minute detour.

This is safe: `greentic-dev`, `cargo-nextest` and `cargo-llvm-cov` **all publish prebuilt binaries** (verified in the greentic-cap green run logs). Nothing in this job legitimately needed the compile strategy.

`--no-confirm` and `--locked` are preserved. `GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}` was already set as `env` on this exact step (added by #75) and is unchanged.

Also added `command -v` assertions for the three binaries after install, so a partial install fails at the install step rather than surfacing later as a confusing error inside `greentic-dev coverage`.

## Scope

CI-only. One file, one step. No source, schema, or locale files touched — `greentic-i18n` is a shared crate, so the diff is deliberately confined to `.github/workflows/nightly-coverage.yml`.

## Verification

`workflow_dispatch` run on this branch, checking the install log for:
- `has been downloaded from github.com` — expect 3 (one per tool)
- `installed from source` — expect 0
- `Forbidden` — expect 0

Recent nightly runs are green, so green here means no regression.

author: 404-page-found
body:
### What this PR does

Before this PR, `builtin_web_search` could send multiple complete pages into an Agent request because web-search compression defaulted to `none`. This could produce requests far beyond a model context window.

After this PR:

- Web-search cutoff compression is enabled by default.
- The default aggregate cutoff is 10,000 estimated tokens.
- Fresh installs receive the generated default from the data-classification source.
- V1 migrations and existing V2 databases upgrade only the previous default-shaped configuration; customized compression pairs are preserved.
- Short result sets skip token slicing when their total character count already proves they are within the token limit.
- Tests cover runtime defaults, V1 migration, existing-V2 upgrade, custom-value preservation, and the short-content fast path.

Refs #17735. This PR fixes the reported context-overflow path. The related redirect/403 degradation and large-page conversion concerns remain separate follow-up work, so this PR intentionally does not close the whole issue.

### Why we need it and why it was done in this way

Cutoff compression prevents unbounded fetched content without another model call or summarization cost. The 10,000-token default retains useful page content while remaining far below the reported multi-million-token payload.

The upgrade seeder runs before general preference seeding so partial legacy pairs can be recognized safely. Any non-default value on either compression key makes the pair user-owned and leaves it unchanged.

### Breaking changes

Web search now truncates fetched content by default. Existing V1/V2 data matching the previous default is upgraded once. The behavior change is recorded in `v2-refactor-temp/docs/breaking-changes/2026-08-02-default-web-search-compression.md`.

### Special notes for your reviewer

- `preferenceSchemas.ts` is generated from `target-key-definitions.json`; both are included.
- The character-count fast path is safe for `tokenx`: character count is a conservative upper bound on its estimated token count.
- The old default-shaped state cannot be distinguished from a user who explicitly selected **None** without first changing the cutoff limit; the release note calls out that one-time upgrade.

### Validation

- 19 related Vitest files, 182 tests passed.
- Full TypeScript typecheck passed.
- Full Biome format/lint check passed.
- Full Oxlint and ESLint checks completed with no errors (only pre-existing warnings outside this PR).

### Checklist

- [x] Branch targets `main` for active development.
- [x] Upgrade flows are covered for fresh, V1, and existing V2 databases.
- [x] Generated preference source is updated.
- [x] User-visible behavior is documented.
- [x] Focused regression tests are included.

### Release note

```release-note
fix: limit built-in web-search content by default

Built-in web search now limits fetched content to 10,000 estimated tokens by default, reducing request-too-large failures after fetching several pages. Previous default V1/V2 configurations are upgraded automatically while customized compression settings are preserved.
```

body:
Closes #248

23 `plan_<operation>` MCP tools that BUILD a reviewable plan and execute nothing. Sits on the merged #247 build/submit seam (ADR 0042): `build_plan_only` never takes the per-worktree guard, which is what makes an agent review roundtrip safe.

## Skeptic verdict: READY

The only chain in today's batch to clear its skeptic outright — gate green, live MCP handshake clean, ADR 0046 + PDF verified, and every load-bearing guard bit back under attack.

## Guards proven by mutation (11 run, all caught)

- Repointing `PLAN_ENDPOINT` away from `/api/plan` → caught (the test compares the literal, not the constant, so changing the constant cannot hide it).
- Making the plan handler also call `plan_and_execute_in` → **first attempt PASSED, which found a real defect in the guard itself**: the forbidden needle was `plan_and_execute(` and the doc-comment slice swallowed a legitimate prose mention. Guard rewritten to scan through `argv_boundary::code_only`; re-run → caught by two independent mechanisms.
- Moving `/api/plan` onto the always-registered router → caught by `the_lan_router_has_no_write_routes`, with the paired positive staying green.
- Adding a dispatch arm with no catalog entry → caught (the reachable-but-unadvertised path a catalog-only test cannot see).
- Silently ignoring `expected_remote_tip` beside `mode: "none"` → caught; a caller would have believed a compare-and-swap protected them when nothing did.
- Adding a 26th `GitOperation` variant → **fails to compile** at `exposure_of`. The compile-time guard verified rather than assumed.

## Follow-ups the skeptic asked for (none are correctness defects)

- Extend the cookie/CSRF leak test to `tools.rs:670` and `:608` — the branch that fires in real use is uncovered.
- Add `println!`/`print!`/`dbg!` to the forbidden-needle list; stdout purity is this crate's load-bearing protocol property and has no structural guard yet.
- `OperationHash` is an unkeyed SHA-256 of public JSON, so `validate` catches an inconsistent plan, not an attacker-recomputed one. Correct for today's model (the submitter *is* the authenticated client), but "approval" framing becomes false once a human-approves/agent-submits workflow is layered on — flagged for #249's ADR 0047.

author: bimapangestu28
body:
## Root cause

\`cargo binstall\` treats a failed prebuilt-binary lookup as a **soft** failure. When
\`api.github.com\` answers **403** (anonymous rate limit, or a transient block) binstall does
not error out — it silently falls back to the \`compile\` strategy and builds
\`greentic-dev\`, \`cargo-nextest\` and \`cargo-llvm-cov\` from source.

\`--locked\` is already present here, so that source build technically *succeeds*. That is
exactly the problem: the job still goes green, it just costs **~11 minutes of pointless
compilation**, and the real cause (token not reaching binstall / rate limited) never
surfaces. Root-caused in greenticai/greentic-cap#39.

## Fix

- Add \`--disable-strategies compile\` so a failed fetch is a **hard error** instead of a
  slow-but-green rebuild. All three tools publish prebuilt release artifacts (verified in
  the greentic-cap green run logs), so the compile strategy has no legitimate use here.
- Add \`command -v\` assertions for all three binaries so a partial install cannot slip
  through to the \`greentic-dev coverage\` step as a confusing "command not found".
- Rewrite the comment to explain the failure mode.

## Not changed

- \`--no-confirm --force --locked\` are preserved verbatim.
- \`GITHUB_TOKEN: \${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}\` was **already** set as \`env\` on this exact
  step (it is not at job or workflow level) — verified, and deliberately **not** duplicated.
- Nothing else in the repo is touched.

## Base branch

\`develop\`. It is the active integration lane (13 of the last 15 merged PRs target it), it
is 25 commits ahead of \`main\` and 0 behind, and \`_reusable_coverage.yml\` is byte-identical
on both branches, so there is no drift risk in landing here first.

## Verification

\`_reusable_coverage.yml\` is \`workflow_call\`-only. Both callers — \`coverage.yml\` and
\`nightly-coverage.yml\` — carry \`workflow_dispatch\`, so the change is exercised by
dispatching a caller on this branch. \`secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN\` is automatically available to
a called workflow, so neither caller needs \`secrets: inherit\` for this to work.

author: brendenhuntzinger1
body:
The two remaining defects from the false-activation report that could still show a customer wrong state. Follow-up to #70 and #71.

## 1. Subscriptions page showed benefits the account wasn't receiving

The page gated its entire plan card on `billingCycle === "free"`. A failed renewal leaves `billingCycle: "monthly"` with `status: "past_due"` — so a non-paying account got the full "Current plan" card, live perk figures (member discount %, monthly store credit, points multiplier), and the pause/skip/resume controls, while the pill beside them read "Payment needed". That's the contradictory state in the report.

Now three explicit states:

| State | Condition | Shows |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Free | `billingCycle === "free"` | Upgrade prompt (unchanged) |
| Active | `perks.isActiveMember` | Full plan card + live perks (unchanged) |
| **Lapsed** | paid cycle, not active | **New** — plan on record, reason it's off, what's actually applied |

The lapsed panel names the reason (payment failed / paused / ended) and lists what is applied to orders *right now* — "Member pricing — not applied" — instead of rendering perk figures that aren't in effect. The gate is `getMembershipPerks().isActiveMember`, the same one checkout and points use, so the page and the buyer's real treatment can't disagree.

Billing history no longer labels a $0 cancellation "Succeeded" in green next to real charges. Paid / lifecycle / failed are now distinct badges via `isPaidBillingEvent` from #71. The footnote claiming no processor is connected was stale — replaced with what the badges mean.

## 2. Membership checkout created one order per click

`createMembershipCheckoutSession` minted a fresh `order-<uuid>` and inserted unconditionally. A double click, a back-and-retry, or a refresh each left another "awaiting payment" order — the source of the two $249.90 rows seven minutes apart.

It now reuses the buyer's existing open attempt for the same tier and cycle.

Two deliberate choices:
- **Not time-boxed.** A stale open attempt is reused rather than expired.
- **Not a unique index.** A partial unique index on `(customer_user_id, order_type, membership_cycle) where payment_status = 'pending_payment'` would hard-fail a legitimate retry the moment an abandoned row lingered. App-level reuse is self-healing; an index is a footgun here.

The one reason to abandon an attempt is a **price change** — that retires the stale row and opens a fresh one, so nobody is sent to a checkout for an outdated amount.

The decision is a pure function, `decideMembershipAttempt`, so it's testable without a database.

## Changes

| File | Change |
| --- | --- |
| `src/app/account/(dashboard)/subscriptions/page.tsx` | Three-state gate on `isActiveMember`; new lapsed panel; honest billing-history badges; corrected footnote. |
| `src/lib/membership-billing-math.ts` | New `decideMembershipAttempt` — reuse / replace / create. |
| `src/lib/membership-billing.ts` | `createMembershipCheckoutSession` looks up the open attempt and follows the decision. |
| `src/lib/membership-billing-math.test.ts` | 7 tests: repeated calls all reuse, float tolerance on the money round-trip, reprice retires. |

## Verification

425 tests passing across 42 files, `tsc` and production build clean. No visual restyling — existing `vl-panel` / `vl2-btn-*` classes and tokens throughout.

## Summary
Fixes #146. The `phone_us` regex in `safety/pii_scrubber.py` used inconsistent
separator groups between the three digit groups of a US phone number — some
gaps allowed a space, dash, or dot, while others only allowed a dash or dot.
This meant common formats like `(555) 123-4567` and `+1 555 123 4567` were
never matched by `scrub()` or `detect()` and passed through completely
unredacted.

`tests/unit/test_pii_scrubber.py` already covered the four scenarios named

`test_detect_phone_pii`, `test_phone_at_start_of_text`). All four now pass.

### Motivation

- Ensure all relative input and output paths in a run YAML are resolved deterministically with respect to the directory that contains the run configuration file, not the shell working directory.
- Preserve already-absolute paths and store all resolved absolute paths in the in-memory configuration and persisted manifest for robust provenance.
- Make the shell orchestrator runnable from arbitrary working directories by anchoring script lookups and Python imports to the repository layout.

author: os-zhuang
body:
Fixes objectstack-ai/objectstack#4722

## 问题

`filterAppForUser`(`packages/rest/src/rest-server.ts`)是 app 元数据的**服务端权威可见性闸门**,但它只走顶层 `navigation` 树 —— `if (!nav) return item` 提前返回,`item.areas` 从头到尾没被读过。于是写在 **area 内部**导航项上的 `requiredPermissions` / `requiresService` 只有客户端 `NavigationRenderer` 会执行:该条目连同它的 `objectName` / `pageName` / `componentRef` 指向,照常出现在 `/meta` 响应体里。改一次前端状态、或者直接 `curl` 一下 `/meta` 的 JSON,就能看到本该被 gate 掉的条目。对 areas 型 app 而言,导航项级闸门此前**不是**服务端强制。

## 改法

同一个 `filterNav` 复用到每一棵 `areas[].navigation` 上 —— 不是第二份实现,所以两棵树对同一个键的语义不可能漂移(这是裁定第 2 问的要求)。列表 `GET /meta/:type` 与单项 `GET /meta/:type/:name` 两条路径都覆盖:两者都经过这个函数,且单项读对 app 类型本就绕过共享缓存,正是为了让这个 per-user 过滤能跑。

**同一提交修正了 `resolveRegisteredServices` 的探测面。** 它此前每个节点只取第一个命中的子数组(`navigation` / `children` / `widgets` 三选一),不下钻 `areas`。若不改,只在 area 内被引用的服务名根本不会被探测,而**未探测的名字在闸门看来等同于「服务不存在」** —— 会把一个服务确实注册着的条目误剥离。探测面必须与过滤面完全一致,这不是顺手改,是本改动的正确性前提(有专门的 pin)。

## 三问的落实

**1. 空 area 返不返回 —— 实测到的顶层既有行为,照抄。**

顶层 `filterNav` 的分组处理(`rest-server.ts` 第 1836-1854 行,本 PR 未改动这段逻辑,只是复用):只有当 `e.children` 是**非空数组**时才进入过滤分支;过滤后,若该条目 `type` 为 group 且孩子被滤光,`continue` 掉它 —— 即**剥离**;否则带着过滤后的 children 保留。而 `children` 缺失或本来就是空数组的条目走 else 分支,**原样保留**。

所以既有形状是:**被闸门滤空的分组剥离,作者本来就写成空的分组保留**。area 照此同形 —— 被 gate 滤空的 area 整个剥离(空壳标签没有消费价值),作者写成 `navigation: []` 的 area 原样返回。过滤只负责报告调用方看不到什么,不负责整理元数据。这条区分有独立 pin(`an area emptied BY the gate is dropped; an area authored empty is passed through`)。

**2. 两棵树一致** —— `filterNav` 复用,零复制。area 内的嵌套 group 折叠行为也自动与顶层一致(有 pin 对照)。

**3. `visible` CEL 明确不做** —— 服务端求值需要绑定 `user` 上下文,不是这个读路径现有的能力。这个不对称写进了三处:`filterAppForUser` 的文档注释、`packages/spec/liveness/app.json` 的账本 note、以及 `rest.test.ts` 里一条**新的 characterisation pin**(钉住「服务端在任何层级都不求值 `visible`」,并写明谁把 CEL 搬到服务端就该看到它红)。`requiresObject` 同理仍是客户端。

**退役键未复活**:#4651 移除的 **area 级** `visible` / `requiredPermissions` 一个都没回来。本次强制的是 area **里面**的项级闸门 —— 这正是 #4651 留下的真缺口。

## 已预期的钉,已按预案改写

`rest.test.ts` 里 `characterises the boundary the #4651 prescription warns about: areas is not walked` 那条 —— 它的注释写着「谁让服务端开始走 areas 就该看到它红,然后连同账本 note 一起有意识地改写」。这就是那次改写:重写成 `AREA level: the item gate applies inside areas[] too`,并同步改写 `packages/spec/liveness/app.json` 的 `areas.navigation` note(以及顶部 `_note` 里同一句已经变假的陈述、`navigation.requiredPermissions` 与 `navigation.visible` 两条 note)。

⚠️ **spec 零改动约束**:只动了 `packages/spec/liveness/app.json` 这一个文件的账本 note —— 派发时开的单文件例外。`packages/spec/**` 其余一行未改。

## 留了一个尾巴,已单独立单

`packages/spec/src/ui/app.zod.ts:662` 的 `AREA_REQUIRED_PERMISSIONS_RETIRED` 处方正文仍写着「the server does not walk `areas`」,`packages/spec/src/ui/app.test.ts:1374` 还有一条断言把这个措辞钉死。改它是处方正文 + pin + spec 生成物的耦合改动,撞上本单的 spec 零改动约束,故按 Prime Directive #10 记为 **#4749**(未认领)。方向上它是「过度保守」而非不安全 —— 劝作者把敏感项挪到顶层树,这仍然可行 —— 但它是错的,而且是说给作者听的那一份。

## 验证

```
pnpm --filter @objectstack/rest test
  Test Files  38 passed (38)
  Tests  571 passed (571)
```

新增/改写的测试**先证明它们能红**:把 `rest-server.ts` 的改动 stash 掉后重跑,

- `rest.test.ts`:`Tests 6 failed | 191 passed` —— 4 条 AREA level + 2 条 `[#4722]` requiresService/探测面
- `meta-app-area-nav-gate.test.ts`(新增,路由级):`Tests 3 failed | 2 passed`

路由级那一份是验收标准的直接证据 —— 断言的是**响应体字节**:无权限调用方拿到的 `/meta` 列表与单项 JSON 里,`secret_forecast` / `secret_ops_page` / `secret_sys_user` 这些 gate 掉条目的指向一个都搜不到,同时有权限的调用方拿到完整树(不过度过滤)。

其他:`pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec check:liveness` ✓(账本改动通过,evidence 行号已同步);`eslint --no-inline-config` 三个文件干净;`tsc --noEmit -p packages/rest` 错误数 67,与 `origin/main` 基线逐一相同(该包在 #4311 的 DEBT 账本里,无 `typecheck` 脚本);`node scripts/check-type-check-coverage.mjs` OK。已合入最新 `origin/main`(#4742)后重装、重建、重跑,增量提交不与 `packages/rest` / `packages/spec` 重叠。

## 消费方注意(changeset 已写清)

服务端响应形状**收紧**:无权限用户拿到的 app 元数据里,被 gate 的 area 内导航项不再出现,被滤空的 area 整个不见。任何依赖「服务端全量下发、客户端自己藏」的消费方需要改为信任服务端已过滤的树 —— 这正是本次收紧的目的。

author: ttraenkler
body:
## Read this first: acceptance here is NOT pass-count

Per #4010's slice plan, agreed with the tech lead:

> Accept on the **delete-column cells going STILL-PRESENT → genuinely-absent**,
> verified **both** by value read **and** by the store's own record.

Tombstones alone flip few test262 files, because currently-invisible properties
fail *earlier* in `propertyHelper`. Deletability and visibility only pay out
**together**, and visibility is S3. **A low corpus flip count is the expected
outcome of this slice, not a failure** — see the numbers at the bottom.

## The defect

`__delete_property`'s non-`$Object` arm returned **1 (success) without deleting
anything** — a loud claim of success covering a silent wrong answer. Measured on
current main, standalone:

```js
const a = [1,2,3]; a.q = 12; delete a.q;   // returns TRUE
a.q                                        // => 12   (STILL PRESENT)

function f(){}  f.p = 12;  delete f.p;     // returns TRUE
f.p                                        // => 12   (STILL PRESENT)
```

Both values live in a per-receiver `$Object` **bag** — `vec-props.ts` (#3537)
for arrays, `closure-props.ts` (#3468) for functions — that the delete native
had never heard of.

## The fix

A bag **is** an ordinary `$Object`, so all of OrdinaryDelete already exists for
it (§10.1.10 configurability preflight, `FLAG_TOMBSTONE`, count/tombstone
bookkeeping). The new `__carrier_bag_delete` finds the right bag and delegates.
**No delete semantics are re-implemented** — which is why a non-configurable
entry still refuses correctly, byte-identically to the `$Object` control.

**The half the design sketch did not predict.** The sketch flagged as a *risk*
that a companion-only tombstone *might* leave `__extern_get` answering from the
bag. It does, always — `__obj_find` **skips** tombstoned entries, so tombstoning
the companion simply restores the fall-through:

```js
a.q = 12;
Object.defineProperty(a, "q", { writable: true });   // now in BOTH tables
delete a.q;                                          // companion tombstoned
a.q                                                  // => 12   (measured)
```

So the vec arm now also **shadows the bag** after a successful companion delete.

**Tri-state on purpose**: `-1` not handled / `0` refused / `1` deleted.
Collapsing `-1` into `1` reproduces the original defect exactly — "I could not
see anything" becoming indistinguishable from "there was nothing". It is also
what makes the change **strictly additive**: the arm fires only for a key the
bag *demonstrably holds*, so every receiver/key the old code answered for keeps
its answer bit-for-bit.

## Scope, and why the −684 stratum cannot fire

Per #4010's ordering law (*visibility cannot ship before deletability*), **no
own-property visibility surface moves**: `hasOwnProperty` / `__object_hasOwn` /
`__vec_gopd` / `Object.keys` reach is unchanged, pinned by SCOPE PIN tests
(S1′'s two are untouched; three more added).

The **#2896 builtin-fn arm still runs FIRST and returns**, so `delete fn.name` /
`delete fn.length` never reach the new code — `built-ins/**/{name,length}.js`,
the ~700-file population that cost #4055 v1 **−684** host-free passes, is
untouched. Pinned by a committed regression guard **and** measured (below).

## Acceptance evidence — two independent derivations per cell

Every case is precondition-gated (a failed precondition returns a distinct code,
so it fails loudly instead of measuring nothing) and every compiled module is
asserted to have **zero imports**.

| cell | derivation | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| array named expando | value read | **STILL PRESENT** | genuinely absent |
| array named expando | **bag's own record** — attribute-only redefine re-seeds from the bag via S1′, never touching the read lane | bag still held `12` | bag empty |
| array, key in BOTH tables | value read | **STILL PRESENT** | genuinely absent |
| array, companion-only key | value read + gOPD | already correct | unchanged |
| function expando | value read | **STILL PRESENT** | genuinely absent |
| function expando | **closure bag's own record** — `__desc_has_own` via #4055's function-as-descriptor path, a different consumer entirely | bag still held `42` | bag empty |
| `$Object` **CONTROL** | value read · hasOwn · non-configurable refusal | 3/3 correct | 3/3 correct |

One derivation was never enough here: the delete's own **return value already
answered `true` on both arms while the value survived**.

## Corpus numbers (low, as predicted — with denominators)

- **74 / 74 files identical**, base vs. this branch, over the population most
  likely to be affected: test262 files performing a member `delete` whose
  receiver is statically an array or function (74 of the 797 member-delete files
  in the 43,488-file corpus). Zero regressions, zero gains.
- **`built-ins/**/{name,length}.js` stratum (1,240 files)**: see the comment
  below for the base-vs-branch diff.
- **Equivalence gate: no new regressions** (32 failing / 1,619 passing / 36
  known-failures in baseline; 4 pre-existing baseline failures now pass, all
  unrelated — i32 peephole, `Math.pow`, Symbol — so the shared baseline is
  deliberately **not** ratcheted here).
- **gc/host mode is byte-identical** (same sha256 on a mixed probe module
  exercising array/function/object deletes and for-in). Only standalone (+166 B)
  and wasi (+133 B) change.
- 5 pre-existing failures in adjacent delete tests (#1821, #2130 ×3, #2992)
  reproduce **identically on base** — not caused here.

## Found while measuring, deliberately NOT fixed

**`Reflect.deleteProperty` throws for every non-`$Object` receiver**, including
plain success cases. Verified **identical on base and after** — pre-existing and
independent of S2. The `delete` operator is unaffected. Fixing it would move a
surface this slice promised not to move; it wants its own issue.

## Structure

`src/codegen/vec-overlay.ts` **shrank** — its `__delete_property` arm moved into
`vec-bag-seed.ts`, which now owns both directions of the overlay↔bag seam
(seeding a value in, taking a property out). `object-runtime.ts` shrank by 19
lines. No `loc-budget-allow` grant was needed or taken.

Closes the S2 slice of #4010; unblocks #4098. `status:` stays `in-progress`
because S3 remains.

author: bimapangestu28
body:
## Root cause

`cargo binstall` resolves prebuilt binaries by querying `api.github.com`. With no `GITHUB_TOKEN` in the environment those calls are anonymous, and the anonymous quota is **per runner IP** — shared with every other job on that machine. Once it is exhausted the API answers `403 Forbidden`.

binstall does not treat that 403 as fatal. It falls back to `cargo install` from source. Because this step already passes `--locked`, the source build succeeds, so the workflow stays green and nothing surfaces in the summary. The only symptom is roughly **11 minutes of pointless compilation** (cargo-nextest is the expensive one) inside a job with a 60-minute budget.

Root-caused in greenticai/greentic-cap#39.

## Changes

1. `GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}` on the install step, so the release lookups are authenticated and the anonymous per-IP quota no longer applies.
2. `--disable-strategies compile` on **cargo-llvm-cov** and **cargo-nextest** only. This converts the silent source-build fallback into a hard failure, so a future regression in prebuilt resolution shows up as a red step instead of a slow green one.
3. `command -v` assertions after install. Under the default `bash -e` shell this fails at the install step rather than several minutes later with `error: no such command`, which is the same class of failure the pre-existing `--force` comment already documents.

The existing `--force` / rust-cache comment is preserved verbatim; the new rationale is appended below it.

## Why tomlq is excluded from `--disable-strategies compile`

`cryptaliagy/tomlq` does **not** publish target-triple-named release assets. Its latest release (0.2.2) carries:

```
tomlq.amd64.tgz
tomlq.arm64.tgz
tomlq.armv7.tgz
tomlq.armv7hf.tgz
```

Prebuilt resolution for it therefore depends entirely on the `pkg-url` overrides the crate declares in its own `[package.metadata.binstall]` table, rather than on binstall's default naming convention. That path is unverified in this workflow. Adding `--disable-strategies compile` there risks converting a currently-working install into a hard failure, and the upside is nil — tomlq builds from source in seconds, not minutes. The line is left byte-for-byte unchanged.

Checking that tomlq installed is safe, and is included; only the flag was risky.

## Incidental correctness fix in the new check

The `tomlq` crate installs its binary as **`tq`**, not `tomlq`:

- `Cargo.toml` (tomlq 0.2.2) declares `[[bin]] name = "tq"`
- `tar tzf tomlq.amd64.tgz` lists exactly one entry: `tq`

So the assertion is `command -v tq`. Writing `command -v tomlq` would have failed the step on a perfectly good install — precisely the failure mode this PR is meant to avoid.

## Scope

CI-only. No Rust source, no flow/component semantics — greentic-dev remains a pass-through CLI.

author: nicolasburtey
body:
## Summary

Reworks the `Wallet` aggregate from creation-only (descriptor passed fully formed at startup) into a real lifecycle that mirrors how multisig wallets actually get set up: participants contribute xpubs asynchronously, and the wallet activates when the quorum is complete.

```
Initialized { threshold, participants }     ← policy only, no keys
    │  KeystoreAdded × M   (one per participant; KeystoreRemoved allowed pre-activation)
    ▼
Activated { descriptor, descriptor_fingerprint }

Initialized ──Cancelled──▶ Cancelled        (pre-activation only, terminal)
```

### Wallet lifecycle
- **`Initialized` carries the policy**: N-of-M `threshold` over a named `participants` set, on a network. No descriptor is required (or accepted) at creation.
- **`KeystoreAdded`** — one keystore per participant, enforced by the aggregate: non-participants can't submit, resubmitting the identical key is an idempotent no-op, a *different* key requires explicit removal first, and master fingerprints must be distinct across participants (two participants presenting keys from the same device is rejected).
- **`Activated`** — recorded atomically with the final keystore; derives the canonical `wsh(sortedmulti(NofM))` descriptor (keystores sorted, so submission order never affects the result) and its content-addressed fingerprint. The derivation happens *before* any event is appended, so an invalid key set fails without polluting the stream.
- **`KeystoreRemoved`** — pre-activation replacement flow for a wrongly uploaded xpub; the event keeps the removed keystore for the audit trail.
- **`Cancelled`** — abandons a wallet stuck in `CollectingKeystores` (quorum fell apart, registered by mistake). Terminal; active wallets can't be cancelled (retirement is future work).

### Persistence
- `core_wallets.status` column (strum↔VARCHAR shim, same pattern as sessions).
- `descriptor_fingerprint` is now **NULL until activation**, UNIQUE thereafter (Postgres allows multiple NULLs) — two wallets converging on the same descriptor collide at activation (on update), which the use-case layer turns into an idempotent find. Migration edited in place (scaffolding phase); dev DBs need `sqlx database reset`.

### Session gating
- `NewPsbtSession::try_new` now takes the `Wallet` aggregate instead of a free-floating `wallet_id` + `Policy`, and rejects non-`Active` wallets (`WalletNotActive`) — a wallet still collecting keystores (or cancelled) has no descriptor and cannot spend.
- The policy snapshot (`threshold` over keystore fingerprints) is *derived* from the wallet, so quorum validity is guaranteed by construction; the session-level `InvalidPolicy`/`DuplicateKeystore` validations and the `Policy` struct are gone.

### Tests
- 60 passing: 46 entity unit tests (wallet lifecycle: activation atomicity, order independence, participant binding, replacement, cancellation, hydration; session: gating, policy snapshot, plus existing state machine), 12 e2e crypto tests (now proposing against a real activated wallet), 2 DB round-trips (incl. fingerprint collision at activation across two wallets).
- `.sqlx` offline cache regenerated.

## Follow-ups (not in this PR)
- Wallet **retirement/archival** for active wallets (drained & retired; `ReplacedBy` links for policy changes).
- Authorization of `remove_keystore`/`cancel` (participant vs admin) — currently platform-attributed, enforcement belongs to the future user crate / use-case layer.
- Derivation index tracking for receive/change addresses.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Touches wallet identity, descriptor derivation, and spend proposal gating in custody coordination; migration/schema changes require DB reset in dev, but behavior is heavily covered by new entity and integration tests.
> 
> **Overview**
> Reworks the **`Wallet`** aggregate from “descriptor at creation” to a **policy-first lifecycle**: `Initialized` registers network, threshold, and participants only; participants submit keystores (`KeystoreAdded`), may withdraw pre-activation (`KeystoreRemoved`), abandon via **`Cancelled`**, and **`Activated`** is emitted atomically with the last keystore when the canonical sorted-multisig descriptor and fingerprint are derived.
> 
> **Persistence** adds `core_wallets.status`, makes **`descriptor_fingerprint` nullable until activation** (UNIQUE when set), and extends wallet repo queries/filters by status; `.sqlx` cache and the setup migration are updated accordingly.
> 
> **PSBT sessions** now take a **`Wallet`** reference in `NewPsbtSession::try_new`, reject non-**Active** wallets (`WalletNotActive`), snapshot policy from the wallet, and drop the separate **`Policy`** type and its duplicate-policy validation. E2E and repo tests build activated wallets through the new flow, including fingerprint collision at activation on duplicate convergence.
> 
> <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit dfc11cf9f6504017dd1c040352ed8a77f416a111. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup>

body:
## Summary

- reject absolute and canonical root-escaping `_tvl_overlay.extends` references before composition
- keep one immutable root from the initial overlay so nested overlays cannot re-anchor containment
- detect self/mutual cycles and cap distinct overlay chains at 64 before Python recursion exhaustion
- retain valid nested relative composition inside the initial root

Closes #43.

## Security properties

The resolver canonicalizes each target, including symlinks, and checks path components with `Path.relative_to()` before loading it. The cycle chain uses canonical paths, and the depth guard fails the 65th distinct overlay with a deterministic `ValueError`; cycle errors take priority at that boundary.

## Verification

- `uv run --frozen --extra dev pytest -q tests` — 468 passed
- `python -m compileall -q tvl_tools/tvl_compose`
- Black check and isort Black-profile check on both changed Python files
- `git diff --check`
- safe-push secret scan: `SAFE_PUSH_SCAN: PASS`
- fresh no-tools Claude Opus review of final exact diff SHA-256 `9c32ad3a266c22e7feb3a2439e526fe1b3cc5df032c9d1dbd66b9a3ed634a6ab`: **CONFIRM**, no blockers (session `4a28b67c-aa45-439d-a6e1-246582f85b6a`)

## Residual risk

A same-user concurrent symlink swap between canonicalization and file open would require fd-relative or `O_NOFOLLOW` I/O to eliminate. This local TOCTOU is not worsened by the patch; canonical traversal/symlink escapes from an untrusted spec are blocked. Absolute and initial-root-escaping references intentionally stop working.

body:
## Ownership claim

- Machine ID: `mbp-martin`
- Agent/session ID: `claude-opus5-loop`
- Task: the empire is unhappy and we never asked
- Claimed paths: `tools/civ6_control/mod/CivvisControlAgent.lua, src/mirror.rs`
- Coordinated with: none
- Related issue/request: operator request

## What changed

**Neither mod exported an amenity, happiness or luxury field, and `mirror.rs` imported
none.** CIVVIS's entire happiness picture was derived from its own rules on the
reconstructed board and never once checked against the host.

That derived number is not decoration. `Game::amenity_yield_mult_for` bands it straight
onto science, production, gold, **culture** and faith:

| surplus | multiplier |
|---|---|
| `>= +5` | 1.20 |
| `>= 0` | 1.00 |
| `>= -4` | **0.80** |
| `>= -6` | **0.70** |

CIVVIS's model puts the live empires at **-4/-5** — a 25-30% standing tax on every
yield, which would be the largest single multiplier on the board.

The city record now carries `GetAmenities`, `GetAmenitiesNeeded`, `GetHappiness` and
`GetHappinessNonFoodYieldModifier`, plus the breakdown by source. The economy drift line
reports all of it.

**This changes no decision.** It is the measurement that says whether the largest
multiplier on the board is real.

## Validation

- [x] Branch started from current `origin/main`
- [x] Ownership/overlap is coordinated above
- [x] Latest `origin/main` merged before ready
- [x] `git diff --check origin/main...`
- [x] `cargo test --profile ci --locked`
- [x] Relevant focused tests
- [x] Soak run for engine changes, or reason it is not applicable
- [x] No unrelated formatting, generated output, or runtime artifacts

## Notes for integration

Squash merge only. Delete the branch after merge.



### Why the existing instrument could not answer this

The economy drift line compares *model totals* against *host totals*. A spurious 0.75
here cancels against any offsetting overestimate elsewhere, leaving a clean-looking
number either way — and it currently reads CIVVIS *high* (science +25%, culture +5-11%),
which is consistent with both "the tax is real" and "the tax is invented". Only the
host's own figure decides it, and `GetHappinessNonFoodYieldModifier` is the host's own
version of the very quantity CIVVIS bands for itself.

### On not guessing the API

Every call is one the shipped `CityPanel` makes on `city:GetGrowth()`, read out of the
game Assets rather than inferred. This file has already paid for
`GetDistricts():GetDefenseStrength()` — a method on the collection, which read `-1` on
every city for the project's whole history — and for a hash lookup that segfaulted Civ 6
four times.

### On the sentinel

⚠ Unknown has **two shapes** and both are refused:

- a field the host never sent → `unknown_metric`, which is `f64::NAN`
- a read the host attempted and failed → the mod's `-1`

A mirror built before this export must not reconstruct as a perfectly happy empire —
that would be the instrument inventing good news. The `>= 0.0` test rejects both, since
every comparison against `NAN` is false; `!= -1.0` alone would let `NAN` through. Tested
both ways.

### Validation evidence

- `luac -p tools/civ6_control/mod/CivvisControlAgent.lua` — OK
- `python3 tools/civ6_preflight.py` — **preflight clear** (2 warnings, both pre-existing)
- `git diff --check origin/main...` — clean
- `origin/main` merged before ready
- `cargo test --profile ci --locked` — **1,677 passed, 0 failed**
- `the_schema_allowlists_cover_every_declared_field` failed on the first run and is fixed in a second commit — `CITY_KEYS` is a second list beside `StateCity` and that guard is exactly what caught it
- `civvis soak --games 6 --turns 120 --players 6` — **6/6 completed**
- New tests: `the_host_amenity_ledger_crosses_the_bridge_and_names_the_shortfall` (wire format — the real risk is a Lua key not matching a serde name) and `a_host_that_never_reported_amenities_says_nothing_rather_than_zero`

## Summary
- extend `coverage_handoff_server_validation_result.v1` to carry a safe high-quality FASTA quality-blocked preview from bounded download-smoke inspection
- surface that preview in package README/handoff and coverage status parent fields
- reject malformed preview rows such as payloads with ZIP paths or other extra fields

## Boundaries
- no live provider/API/download execution
- no external bioinformatics tools
- no manifest, selection, registration, or strict deliverable changes
- preview rows are limited to record IDs, accessions, assembly metadata, row status, and controlled blocker codes

author: vesta-upstream[bot]
body:
fix(daemons): a detached daemon's log stayed empty because its child was block-buffered

Every skill that re-execs its own CLI does it the same way:

    subprocess.Popen([sys.argv[0], "serve"], start_new_session=True, stdout=log, stderr=log)

stdout is a file rather than a tty, so CPython block-buffers it. A poller can print its startup
line, run for hours and never write a byte, because 4KB of output never accumulates.

Observed on a live box, and this is the part that makes it worth fixing rather than tidy:

    $ ps -o lstart -p $(cat ~/agent/data/daemons/finance.pid)
      Mon Aug  3 03:36:52 2026            <- started, prints immediately on entry to serve()
    $ stat -c %y ~/agent/logs/finance.log
      2026-08-02 04:31:35                 <- untouched for over 24 hours
    $ stat -c %y ~/.finance/seen_transactions.json
      2026-08-03 04:37:53                 <- polling normally the entire time

The log is the only liveness evidence anyone actually reads, so a stale mtime gets diagnosed as a
daemon that died. It cost me exactly that: I filed an issue about a watcher whose "stop cause is
genuinely unknown", and the log-mtime evidence in it was never evidence.

Fix is `env={**os.environ, "PYTHONUNBUFFERED": "1"}` on the Popen, in all eleven copies of
`daemon.py` that launch their own Python CLI. Popen calls that launch a compiled binary (voice) are
left alone, since the interpreter's buffering is not in play there.

Verified in the same call shape rather than by reasoning about it: a child printing one line then
sleeping, Popen'd with a file-backed stdout, read back while it is still alive.

    plain:      child_alive=True log=''
    unbuffered: child_alive=True log='daemon started, polling every 300s\n'

The regression test is a source check over every `daemon.py`, not a runtime one. A runtime test
would have to know which daemons print on startup, and one that prints nothing would pass by
saying nothing, which is the shape of test that let this through in the first place. It fails on
master naming all eleven files, and passes with the change.

---

body:
1.5 拆分的後半段（前半 = 1.5a 的 `TranslateTrack`）。8 個 AC / 5 個 task 全數完成，story `sub-1-5b` → `done`。

兩個 commit：實作，以及對抗式 code review 後的修正。

---

## 實作（`424b3cf8`）

- **AC #1 `ProcessItem`**（`process_item.go`，`[@contract-v1]`，消費者 sub-1-6）—— 完整單項流程：pre-flight → route → 依 verdict 分流 → serialize → 交付。
- **AC #2 Pre-flight（P5）** —— 述詞是「檔案存在 **且** `ParseSRT` 成功 **且** cue 數 > 0」三個 clause，不是只看存在。截斷／零位元組的檔案會被判定為不可接受並重新產生 —— 只看存在正是架構點名的反模式。`force` 一併繞過 P5 與快取讀取（仍然寫入）。
- **AC #3 片段快取**（`segment_cache.go`）—— key = `subseg:v1:` + sha256(cue 內容 + 完整 RunVersion tuple)，**內容雜湊而非 cue index**（SDH 過濾會讓同一句在不同輪帶上不同 index）。canonical `MetadataHash` 用固定 7 欄 `\x1f` 串接，集合型欄位排序在**副本**上做。TTL 30 天。
- **AC #4 Prompt-cache 策略** —— 最後一個穩定 system block 翻成 `CacheTTL1h`（prefix 語意，一個 breakpoint 就涵蓋前面）；`cache_enabled` 由**偵測**而非估算決定：讀第一塊的 `CompletionUsage`，兩個 cache 欄位都是 0 就記 `false`。不做 tokenizer 猜測，也不為了湊門檻去填充 prefix（D4 明文禁止）。
- **AC #5 D10 per-show gate**（`show_gate.go`）—— 每部劇的第一次請求獨自跑，回來後才放行等待者；50 分鐘暖窗（< 1h TTL）、Rule 14 有界 map、可取消、release 冪等。
- **AC #6 交付與 provenance** —— 嚴格 P9 順序：place → 確認成功 → `subtitle_runs` 更新 → media row 終態。順序是 load-bearing，反過來會讓 provenance 宣稱一個 crash 從未寫出的檔案。用共享 order log 證明，不是靠目視。
- **失敗政策** —— run `failed` + media 退回 `not_searched`（enum 沒有 `failed`；停在 `translating` 會留下幽靈 in-flight 狀態）。清理寫入走 `context.WithoutCancel`，所以關機也留得下紀錄。

Rule 24 lane ① 回頭修正 sub-1-6 的三處介面事實（`ProcessOptions` → `ProcessItemOptions`，因為 `subtitle.ProcessOptions` 已被搜尋引擎佔用；progress hook 改帶 `MediaRef`；`MediaStore` 不得寫入 search 欄位），並開一筆 `backlog-subtitle-status-writer-search-columns`。

## Code review 修正（`87ab272a`）

10 個發現（2H/4M/4L），HIGH + MEDIUM 全數處理。**兩個 HIGH 同源** —— 都出在這個 story 新增的接縫：把縮小後的 miss 子集餵進 sub-1-5a 已 stamp 的 `TranslateTrack`。

| | 問題 | 實證 |
|---|---|---|
| **H1** | FR16 的 5% 頑固門檻在對**子集**算，於是門檻隨快取變暖而收緊 | 20 條 cue、18 條命中、1 條頑固 → `1 of 2 cues … over the 5% ceiling` → 整集失敗、media 退回 `not_searched`；同一條軌冷快取下 1/20 恰好 5% 是會過的 |
| **H2** | 頑固 cue 的**英文原文**被當譯文寫進 30 天快取 | 快取值取回來就是英文原句。key 是 cue 內容 + show 級 MetadataHash，所以同一句會被當 hit 餵給該劇每一集，且是 hit 就不再送 LLM |

兩個修法都刻意走既有的 context-scope 機制（`cache_enabled`／showKey 已經是這樣走的），為的是不動 sub-1-5a 的 `[@contract-v1]` —— **不欠 Rule 20 bump，也不欠 stale-mark**。在 `TranslateResult` 加 `StubbornIndexes` 會欠，所以沒選。fail-soft 交付行為完全沒變，錯的只是「被當成譯文存下來」。

- **M1** D10 gate 在首次請求**失敗**後仍標記 warm，等於開了 50 分鐘暖窗卻沒寫進任何 prefix，同劇後續每一集各付一次 2x 寫入溢價 —— 正是 D10 要避免的成本。改成 `release(warmed bool)`；失敗的 leader 仍然關 latch（provider 抖動不能卡死 pool），但不留暖記號。
- **M2** `mergeCues` 補完整性守衛 —— 兩邊都沒覆蓋到的 cue 原本會靜靜保留英文出貨，而 `checkTimestampInvariant` 只比 Index/Start/End，結構上抓不到。新測試同時證明時間戳守衛**會放行**那個壞軌。
- **M4** `cache_enabled` 無法表達「根本沒送請求」（全命中的項目和 prefix 真的沒快取住的項目都落在 `false`，會污染 M1 pilot 的 A/B）。真解法要欄位改 nullable = migration = 被 AC #8 擋掉，因此先加 `requests_sent` 到完成 log 分離兩群，migration 計畫入 backlog。
- **M3** per-cue SELECT 的 N+1 **降級為 LOW 並歸檔** —— 實測 1000 次 7.0ms（7.0µs/次），約佔整個項目 0.02%，不值得擴充共用的 `CacheRepositoryInterface` + 兩個 mock + registry。數字寫進 backlog 條目，讓下一個人重推的是決策而非量測。

## 測試

+54 個測試函式（實作 46、CR 8），套件總數 250、0 FAIL。

- 每個 task 實作前先驗 RED（build 失敗且指名新符號）
- **七次反證檢查**（故意改壞 → 指定測試 FAIL → 還原）：D10 wiring、失敗政策、以及 CR 新增的四道守衛全部如預期失敗
- 誠實記錄了一個**沒有**被反證抓到的守衛（合併軌的 FR17 檢查），因為它是建構性守衛
- 整合測試跑真實 `:memory:` SQLite + 真實 `SubtitleRunRepository` / `CacheRepository` / `Placer`（Rule 15、bugfix-20-1 的教訓）

## Gates

`go test ./...` exit 0 · subtitle `-race` clean · `nx run api:lint`（vet + staticcheck）clean · `pnpm lint:all` 0 errors · 觸碰檔案 `gofmt` clean · `prettier --check` clean

Rule 7 **PASS**（0 個 error-code 常數在範圍內）· Rule 20 **N/A**（無 bump；AC #1 是新的 v1）· Rule 25 **N/A**（`project-context.md` 未改動）

## 範圍界線（AC #8）

無 SSE 廣播、無 feature flag／endpoint／scanner enqueue／worker pool（全在 **sub-1-6**）、無 migration、無前端、無 `.pen`。

author: eswan18
body:
Previews cut their Neon branch from a registry-configured parent instead of the project's default branch.

## The bug

`CreateBranch` was called with an empty `parentID`, which makes Neon branch from the project's **default** branch. In all three projects that's the production branch:

| project | default (what previews got) | staging actually runs on |
|---|---|---|
| footstrike-api | `production` | `development` |
| identity | `production` | `development` |
| forecasting | `main` | `dev` |

Verified by matching the endpoint ID inside each `*_database_url` secret against the project's endpoints — not by trusting branch names.

So every preview came up as a copy-on-write clone of production data, on production's schema. The data was never publicly reachable (preview Ingresses are `ingressClassName: nginx`, and ingress-nginx's Service is a Tailscale LoadBalancer), but the schema half matters: promotion to prod is manual, so prod lags staging, and a preview started life behind whatever the branch was developed against.

`docs/preview-environments.md` already asserted previews branched from staging. This makes that true rather than aspirational.

## The change

`preview.neon.parent` in the registry holds a branch **name**, not an ID — `registry.yaml` is hand-edited and commented, and `br-solitary-sun-ad74wwhf` would be unreviewable. It resolves against the branch list `ensureNeonBranch` already fetches, so no extra API call.

**Omitting `parent:` preserves today's behavior exactly**, so anything without the key is unaffected.

An unknown parent is caught twice. Creation time is the real gate; `verifyNeonParents` is a deliberately redundant pre-flight that runs before `EnsureNamespace`, so a registry typo costs nothing instead of leaving a zombie namespace and burning build minutes:

```
preview: Up: pre-flight: neon parent branch for footstrike-api: neon project
aged-river-81935268 has no branch named "staging-typo" (registry preview.neon.parent)
```

Neither path ever falls back to the default.

## Testing

10 new assertions, each revert-checked. The fake seeds every project with a decoy `production` branch listed first, so "resolved the configured name" is distinguishable from "grabbed whatever came back first".

`go vet`, `go test ./...`, `golangci-lint run ./...` all pass.

## Known limitation

`verifyNeonParents` lists branches once per member without de-duplicating by project. Harmless today — the two services use different projects — and it would only mean a redundant API call if they ever shared one.

author: walkswithaswagger
body:
## The gap

`scripts/check_live_theme_parity.py` (issue #546) opens with:

> The repo's #1 risk is the live `kk-aurora` theme silently diverging from the version tracked in `main`.

It detects that correctly. **Nothing ran it automatically.** Not CI, not `make validate`, not `make morning-truth`. It only fired when someone typed `make check-live-parity` by hand.

Meanwhile the **Aurora Risk (Read-Only)** section of every morning-truth report covered only local `aurora/v2` worktree state and said nothing at all about the live theme version. So the repo's stated #1 risk had a working detector and no trigger.

There is real drift right now, and it was not showing up:

```
$ make check-live-parity
FAIL theme version drift detected:
  live (https://kriskrug.co/wp-content/themes/kk-aurora/style.css): 1.5.7
  repo (theme/kk-aurora/style.css): 1.5.8
```

## The change

Wires the existing detector into morning-truth. **No new drift logic** — this is one `run_command` call plus a render function.

### A skip is not a pass

The detector exits `0` both when versions match *and* when live is unreachable (a deliberate soft-skip so the check degrades gracefully offline). Collapsing those into one green line would launder a non-measurement into a pass, which is exactly what AGENTS.md warns about with *"readback, don't assume, in either direction."*

So the four states render distinctly:

| Detector state | Report line |
|---|---|
| exit 1, drift | **Aurora live vs repo: DRIFT.** + both versions |
| exit 0, `PASS` | Aurora live vs repo: in sync |
| exit 0, `SKIP` (unreachable) | **not measured** (live unreachable) |
| exit 2 | **could not measure** |

## Verification

Actual output from `make morning-truth` on this branch, in `morning-truth-20260803-024628Z.md`:

```
## Aurora Risk (Read-Only)

- **Aurora live vs repo: DRIFT.** FAIL theme version drift detected: live (...): 1.5.7 repo (theme/kk-aurora/style.css): 1.5.8
- Local `aurora/v2` worktree not detected from porcelain list.
```

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `make morning-truth` | emits the real current gap |
| unit tests | 15 pass, 4 new (drift / in-sync / unreachable / unreadable-repo) |
| `make python-test` | 0 failures across all suites |
| em dashes added | 0 |

## Note on the current drift

The 1.5.7 vs 1.5.8 gap is **expected and gated**, not a bug: it is the undeployed `aurora-tstm` CSS waiting on the #601 pixel gate. This PR surfaces it rather than gating on it, deliberately. Wiring the check into CI as a hard failure would block every PR until #601 ships.

## Related

Came out of the #566 front-door work. That lane added a hardcoded regex to `docs_truth_check.py` matching the exact string `Aurora 1.5.0 (live == repo`, which catches today's stale line but not tomorrow's. `docs_truth_check.py` is a regex blacklist by design and cannot catch novel staleness. This is the dynamic complement, and it lives where live checks already run.

## Safety

Read-only. One GET to the public `style.css`. No live WordPress writes, no theme changes, no deploys.

author: ajith-sirra-amd
body:
Adds the single-node AgentX (agentic-coding) recipe for **GLM-5.2 (MXFP4)** on **MI355X** with **SGLang**, **MTP only**.

Updated per @functionstackx's review: instead of adding MTP as a second arm, the recipe is now spec-decode only. Per [MODELS.md](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/blob/main/MODELS.md), agentic-coding recipes are run and published with speculative decoding enabled rather than as an STP/MTP A/B, and GLM-5.2 agentic non-MTP is deprecated after **2026-08-03** — so the non-MTP arm is neither wired into the master config nor kept as a separate script. Rebased on `main`.

## What's here

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `benchmarks/single_node/agentic/glm5.2_fp4_mi355x_sglang_mtp.sh` | New (renamed from `..._sglang.sh`). `_mtp` is the suffix `runners/launch_mi355x-amds.sh` resolves for `SPEC_DECODING=mtp`. |
| `configs/amd-master.yaml` | Config key `glm5.2-fp4-mi355x-sglang-agentic-mtp`, `spec-decoding: mtp`. |
| `perf-changelog.yaml` | Entry filled in, PR link added. |

## MTP

GLM-5.2 ships its own nextn head, so SGLang EAGLE runs off the checkpoint with no external draft model:

```
--speculative-algorithm EAGLE --speculative-num-steps 3 \
--speculative-eagle-topk 1 --speculative-num-draft-tokens 4
```

3 speculative tokens per verification step — the same shape as the B300 sibling #2447 and the GLM-5.2 GB300 dynamo-sglang agentic recipes.

The draft MoE backend is deliberately left unset. GLM-5.2's nextn layer is unquantized bf16, so it cannot inherit the target model's MXFP4 MoE runner once EP8 puts an all-to-all in the path — but upstream's `_deepseek_spec_moe_resolution` gates its fix-up hook on `is_hip()`, so ROCm resolves it automatically. This is the one place this recipe diverges from the CUDA sibling, which has to pass `--speculative-moe-a2a-backend none` / `--speculative-moe-runner-backend triton` explicitly.

## Synthetic acceptance length

Throughput runs pin acceptance to the golden AL, per the AgentX policy in [`golden_al_distribution/README.md`](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/blob/main/golden_al_distribution/README.md):

```
SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_LEN=2.99
SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_METHOD=match-expected
SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_TOKEN_MODE=real-draft-token
```

`EVAL_ONLY` runs leave it off — simulated acceptance commits drafted tokens regardless of the target logits, so the eval would score ~0.

2.99 is the GLM-5.2 curve at `num_speculative_tokens=3`, thinking_on, from SPEED-Bench `coding` ([speedbench-al.yml run 28058352479](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/actions/runs/28058352479)). **The curve file itself is committed by #2447** (`golden_al_distribution/glm5.2_mtp.yaml`) rather than duplicated here; it is not on `main` yet, so this PR should land after #2447. The curve was collected on the FP8 checkpoint — one curve per model, and the MXFP4 checkpoint ships the same nextn head.

## Image

`lmsysorg/sglang-rocm:v0.5.16-rocm720-mi35x-20260728`, unchanged from the first revision and verified on Docker Hub (pushed 2026-07-28). v0.5.16 is the first release that reads `SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_TOKEN_MODE` — `ACC_LEN` / `ACC_METHOD` exist further back, so an older ROCm image would silently honor only two thirds of the contract.

## Serve shape

ROCm low-latency arm, unchanged from the first revision outside the speculative and simulated-acceptance blocks: TP8 + EP8, `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3`, tilelang DSA prefill/decode, glm47 tool-call parser, glm45 reasoning parser, `--chunked-prefill-size 131072` at conc ≤ 16, HiCache host-DRAM offload (ratio 1.5 / write_through / direct / page_first_direct).

One deliberate change: `--mem-fraction-static` is held at **0.80** across the whole grid instead of taking the +0.05 the non-speculative shape could afford at conc ≤ 16. The nextn layer's weights and its own KV pool come out of the same static budget, and graph capture is over 4-token verification batches rather than 1-token decodes; an OOM mid-warmup costs the whole sweep point, and HiCache's host tier (ratio is relative to the device pool) absorbs the slightly smaller HBM KV pool.

Mooncake stays out of the master config as an offload backend on this SKU — the HIP/TCP transfer engine is not stable on gfx950 under sustained agentic load — but the branch stays in the script for on-node experiments.

## Search space

```yaml
- { tp: 8, ep: 8, spec-decoding: mtp, kv-offloading: dram, kv-offload-backend: { name: hicache }, conc-list: [1, 4, 8, 12, 16] }
```

The AgentX MTP concurrency grid: steps of at least 2 (single-step sampling can't separate configurations by more than run-to-run noise on the agentic corpus) and a hard stop at conc 16.

## Validation

- `bash -n` clean; `configs/amd-master.yaml` / `perf-changelog.yaml` parse.
- `generate_sweep_configs.py test-config` and `process_changelog.py` against `origin/main` both select exactly the 5 expected jobs (`glm5.2_tp8_conc{1,4,8,12,16}_kvdram-hicache_spec-mtp`).
- `validate_perf_changelog.py` passes.
- Launcher resolution simulated: `benchmarks/single_node/agentic/glm5.2_fp4_mi355x_sglang_mtp.sh`.
- No references to the old script / config-key names remain.

Sweep results to follow.

author: cameron-lyons
body:
## What
- validate response matrices and missing-value configuration through the shared response contract
- normalize NaN and every negative missing code before identifying patterns
- preserve first-appearance order while retaining packed-row deduplication
- support non-contiguous response views and add clear shape errors for expansion and aggregation helpers
- validate grouped collapsing and preserve first-appearance group order
- expose grouped collapsing, pattern likelihood, and weighted aggregation through the public namespaces
- document the expanded transformation API and add 28 focused regressions

## Why
The prior packed-string implementation required a contiguous last axis, ignored `missing_code`, treated different negative missing codes as distinct patterns, silently cast NaN values, and sorted patterns by packed bytes even though the documented result used first-appearance order. Group and expansion helpers also lacked contract validation and were not available through the public namespaces.

## Impact
- median collapse time on 250,000 respondents and 12 items improved from 0.1231s to 0.0750s (about 39%)
- sliced arrays, NaN input, alternate negative missing codes, polytomous responses, and grouped data now behave consistently
- collapsed indices reliably reconstruct the normalized original matrix

## Checks
- 1,594 passed, 17 skipped, 11 deselected; 62.06% coverage
- collapsing module coverage: 96%
- 34 focused and lazy-import tests passed
- module doctest passed
- Ruff formatting and linting passed
- mypy passed across 163 source files
- staged diff check passed

author: bforejt
body:
## What this is

A new sibling job, **RESTCONF Dev Tester**, that captures raw RESTCONF evidence from ONE device as Job Result file artifacts — exact response bodies, HTTP statuses, per-read timings, and a UTC-stamped `00-manifest.json` ledger of every request. Built so the Catalyst 9800-CL AP-predownload bench can be run as Nautobot jobs instead of ~17 hand-driven Postman requests (the tester's Postman burden drops to zero), and kept deliberately generic for future platform bring-up and field diagnostics ("run the Dev Tester, send me the Job Result").

## Design contract (locked, in the module docstring)

**The job RECORDS and never DECIDES.**

- **GET suites** — strictly read-only:
  - *Snapshot*: the bench sheet's P0–P7 reads (install-oper, stack-oper, system/inventory, predownload-data, capwap-data, ap-global-oper, q-filesystem) with log-only advisory analyses (the P3 "three worlds" count, ap-prime-info location and backup-controller coverage, boot-mode strings, partition free space) plus positively-validated custom `data/`-only paths — dot segments, absolute URLs, and `operations/` smuggling are refused **and ledgered in the manifest**.
  - *Watch recorder*: save-on-change polling of predownload-data + capwap-data with a steady-state early stop.
- **POST suites** (fire / abort / clear / dry-run AP predownload; RPC shapes verified against the published 17.15 YANG): exactly **one** operator-selected RPC behind an acknowledgement checkbox, recording before/request/response/after. No chaining, no retries (the only resend is the documented bodiless→`{}` shape fallback, both attempts attached under their own names), no interpretation.
- `jobs/restconf.py` grows `probe_get`/`probe_post`: never-raising evidence primitives — in this job an HTTP error is a *result to record*, not a failure. Bodies are decoded as UTF-8 per RFC 8040/7951 (never requests' chardet guess), with the device's true byte count carried alongside.

## Review findings a reviewer should know about (14 fixed across two adversarial passes)

- **Unreachable ≠ steady.** Transport errors return empty text; empty == empty, so five failed polls originally read as "nothing changing" and stopped the recorder exactly when the device stopped answering. Only genuine 2xx reads now participate in steady-state accounting; unreadable polls are logged distinctly and neither grow nor reset the streak.
- **The acknowledgement gate is an identity check** (`confirm_writes is not True`), not truthiness — stored ScheduledJob/API kwargs bypass form coercion and the string `"false"` is truthy. Same lesson as the transfer_method dropdown, applied to the one gate before a fleet-wide command.
- **Meta time limits** sized for the 240-min max watch (stock `CELERY_TASK_SOFT_TIME_LIMIT=300` would soft-kill even the default 30-min watch); a `SoftTimeLimitExceeded` handler attaches the manifest before failing.
- Evidence-integrity hardening: every manifest row carries a UTC timestamp (unchanged polls included — the bench's fire-time/done-time questions live on them); transport failures attach loud error stubs instead of zero-byte files; truncation counts encoded bytes; a 150 MB aggregate budget degrades a runaway watch to a manifest-only ledger; advisory analyses can never crash the recording (iterative walker, broad catch); the `{}`-fallback artifact reports the observed HTTP outcome instead of asserting "accepted form".

## What it deliberately does NOT do

Image staging and activation (bench P10/P15) stay with the IOS-XE upgrade job — stated in the job description. No automatic remediation, no verdicts about device state, no multi-device POST blast radius (single ObjectVar).

## Verification

- CI-exact: ruff lint + `ruff format --check` + byte-compile — green.
- Registers cleanly on a real Nautobot 2.4.36 loader (all six suites), with helper sanity checks: path-smuggling refusals, the readable-poll rule, deep-payload recursion, UTC stamps.
- **Not yet run against a real 9800-CL** — its first snapshot run *is* bench probe P1 by design; the Postman sheet remains the documented fallback.
