## Summary
Implements Phase 1 of the preregistration ([2026-08-03-aggregation-aware-recall-design.md](../blob/master/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-03-aggregation-aware-recall-design.md)). Three retrieval-side knobs, **all default OFF** — this PR changes no live behavior; the preregistered GPU gates decide which knobs flip on.

1. **`memory.search.contiguity_neighbors`** — each hit also surfaces its stream-adjacent neighbors (same episode, else same source), placed around the hit in `(timestamp, seq)` order, marked `via: "contiguity"`. Per-query scan, no derived index.
2. **`memory.search.timeline_channel`** — temporally-cued queries get lexical injections (BM25-style weight×norm, explicit floor honored, `via: "timeline"`) and the memory portion ordered by stream position instead of score.
3. **`--fact-render enum`** (bench) — numbered, dated, one-per-line supersession chains and set members; current value always leads (the autopsy showed the answerer miscounting inline "a -> b -> c" chains).

**Control-arm integrity:** `build_contexts` previously built rag and hybrid from ONE search call — a knob under test would have leaked into the control. The rag arm is now pinned to vanilla retrieval per-call (`contiguity_neighbors=0, timeline=False`); hybrid follows `--contiguity`/`--timeline`. With knobs at defaults, both calls return identical entries and pre-Phase-1 artifacts stay byte-identical.

## Notes for review
- `RetrievalResult` gains optional `via` (default `None` — every existing caller unaffected).
- Timeline cue lexicon deliberately omits "may" (modal) and bare weekday names; a false positive costs only chronological presentation.
- Timeline channel layers under BM25: when BM25 already injected a lexical hit, timeline correctly declines to duplicate it (covered by a controlled-embedding CMS test).
- Production stale demotion already holds structurally (`SUPERSEDED_SCORE_MULT=0.55` ranks stale below current; the cortex block serves only current facts with contested/stale flags) — no production rendering change was needed; the enumerable fix is bench-side where the measured failure was.

## Test plan
- [x] Watched RED per knob before implementation
- [x] 20 new tests across `test_search_contiguity.py` / `test_search_timeline.py` / `test_fact_render_enum.py`
- [x] Full suite: **2099 passed, 1 skipped** (bench Postgres up)
- [ ] Preregistered GPU gates (next step, banks reused from `alltypes-0803`): per-knob LME re-runs + combined, `compare_arms` paired permutation, rag tripwire, BEAM directional check → `agg-recall-phase1-verdict.json`

author: dean815
body:
`qm --help` and `CLAUDE.md` both promise *"Read-only. Nothing here writes to any Claude Code
config."* On a machine that already has `~/.claude.json` that holds. On one that does not,
running `qm audit` creates it — carrying a `machineID` and a `userID` the user did not have.

The write is the subprocess's, not ours. The user-visible effect is not.

```
HOME=$(mktemp -d) claude --version                  -> no file
HOME=$(mktemp -d) qm audit --json --no-plugin-cost  -> ~/.claude.json CREATED
```

It is the subcommands, not the binary: `claude plugin list --json`, `claude plugin details`
and `claude doctor` each initialise it.

## Disclosure, not refusal

Of the three options on DEA-140, this implements **detect and disclose**. Refusing on a fresh
machine would remove the resolver's only oracle for plugin cost and installation health
*precisely where a first-time user runs the tool*. Narrowing the promise to "*we* don't write
it" was rejected — that is not a distinction the user experiences.

New `src/disclose.ts`: **one door every `claude` spawn goes through**. It records
`existsSync(~/.claude.json)` at import — strictly before any spawn — remembers the run's
*first* invocation, and discloses only when all three hold: absent at start, something was
spawned, and the file is there now. A funnel rather than a check per call site, because the
disclosure has to *name* the command that ran and nothing held an inventory of where this
tool shells out.

**Human** (stderr, on every exit path, so `baseline` and `serve` disclose too):

> `claude plugin list --json` initialised `/Users/x/.claude.json`; it did not exist before
> this run. quartermaster did not write it — the first-party CLI creates that file on first use.

**`--json`**: exactly one new top-level key, `initialised`, beside the other non-finding
fields. Verified live — keys are now `projects, sessions, unreadable, unchecked, unpriced,
initialised, findings`, `null` on this machine, 23 findings unchanged.

**Never a finding.** It has no severity and is a property of *this run*, not of the
configuration. `unreadable` / `unchecked` / `unpriced` are the precedent.

## A correction the work surfaced

DEA-140 and my brief both said `claude doctor` sits behind `--full`. **It does not.**
`doctorAdapter()` is in *both* branches of the adapter list (`src/cli.ts:511-512`), so it runs
on every audit — which is why the `--no-plugin-cost` repro created the file. Recorded in
`doctor.ts` and in the CLAUDE.md entry.

## Mutations — six, each caught by a different scenario

```
never disclose                              the file was absent and the spawn made it: silent, expected "claude plugin list --json"
disclose without asking if it predated       the config file was already there: disclosed "claude doctor", expected silence
check at report time, not before the run     the file was absent and the spawn made it: silent, expected "claude plugin list --json"
disclose without asking if anything spawned  the file appeared but nothing was spawned: disclosed "(nothing ran)", expected silence
assume the spawn wrote it, don't check       the spawn was attempted and failed: disclosed "…", expected silence
name the last command, not the first         two commands ran: named "claude plugin details engineering", expected "claude doctor"
```

The second is the load-bearing one: **a disclosure that always fires is a banner, not a
disclosure.** Verified silent on a machine that already has the file.

Three further mutations were applied to the real source and confirmed red before restoring.
The mutants are hand-written rather than derived from `ClaudeCli` — a mutant borrowing the
real predicate would agree with it whatever it does.

**No test spawns `claude`** (0 exec calls in `test/disclose.test.ts`): doing so is what creates
the file, and on macOS a temp `HOME` also detaches the login keychain and raises a modal at
the user.

## Verification

`npm run typecheck` clean. `npm test` **381 → 395, zero failures, zero skips.** Config
untouched: 83 top-level keys intact. `CLAUDE.md` gains a Decisions entry framing this as the
`/doctor` rule applied to a case it missed, including the day the choice fails — it watches
one path, so a first-party command that starts initialising some *other* file goes unreported.

## Left out

No suppression flag. The opening line of `CLAUDE.md` is untouched — still literally true of
`qm` itself, with the nuance in Decisions. `pluginCost()` in `src/cost/plugins.ts` is dead
code (exported, called nowhere); routed through the funnel anyway rather than leaving a
bypass, but not deleted.

body:
## Summary
- Default the reComputer RK3588 to the open-source Panthor GPU stack, **switchable at boot via the `rockchip-rk3588-panthor-gpu` DT overlay** instead of compile-time kernel changes.
- Kernel: keep the vendor Mali KMD untouched (`CONFIG_MALI_BIFROST=m`, everything else restored to previous values) and add `CONFIG_DRM_PANTHOR=m`. The base DTB carries two mutually exclusive GPU nodes for the same hardware (`gpu@fb000000` for the Mali KMD, `gpu-panthor@fb000000` for Panthor); the overlay disables one and enables the other, so exactly one KMD binds per boot — flipping stacks needs no rebuild.
- Board: ship `overlays=rockchip-rk3588-panthor-gpu` by default (`RECOMPUTER_GPU_STACK=panthor`), skip the libmali userspace and install Mesa instead (bookworm: from backports). Removing the overlay from armbianEnv.txt switches back to the Mali KMD; libmali userspace for that path (OpenCL/Vulkan compute) is installed separately.
- Why Panthor as the default: on trixie and later the vendor libmali blob is ABI-incompatible with the newer desktop stack (grey screen / compositor fails); Panthor+Mesa works out of the box.
- Both drivers are modules and autoload via OF modalias from the enabled node only; the initramfs firmware hook from earlier revisions was dropped (the module requests `mali_csffw.bin` after the rootfs is mounted; the firmware is still installed to `/lib/firmware`).

## Testing (reComputer RK3588 DevKit, dual-driver 6.1.115 kernel)
- [x] Overlay on (default): `panthor.ko` autoloads, `bifrost_kbase` stays unloaded, `gpu-panthor@fb000000 => okay`, `panthor fb000000.gpu-panthor: [drm] mali-g610 id 0xa867`, Mesa render nodes present
- [x] Overlay removed: `bifrost_kbase.ko` autoloads, `panthor` stays unloaded, `gpu@fb000000 => okay`, rk kbase platform init in dmesg
- [x] Overlay restored → back on Panthor

author: kwsantiago
body:
## Summary

Documents the stack requirement the mbedTLS CTR-DRBG introduced on ESP targets, and ignores the build byproducts the QEMU smoke test generates.

## The hazard

#63 moved the ESP RNG from `esp_fill_random()`, which has no state, onto a cached CTR-DRBG so a failed draw can be reported instead of silently returning zeros. Seeding costs stack in whichever task calls first: `ctr_drbg_reseed_internal()` puts a 384-byte `MBEDTLS_CTR_DRBG_MAX_SEED_INPUT` buffer on the **caller's** stack, plus the entropy gather.

Verified against the ESP-IDF sources rather than quoted from memory: `mbedtls/library/ctr_drbg.c:452` declares the buffer, and `ctr_drbg.h` confirms `MAX_SEED_INPUT 384`, `MAX_REQUEST 1024`, `RESEED_INTERVAL 10000`.

## Measured, not estimated

Fixed cost, read from a built ESP32-S3 image with `nm`:

| symbol | bytes |
| ------ | ----- |
| `rng_entropy` | 420 |
| `rng_ctr_drbg` | 76 |
| `rng_initialized` | 4 |
| **total .bss** | **500** |

My original estimate on the issue was ~450 B, so this corrects it upward.

Stack behaviour, run under QEMU:

| first caller | result |
| ------------ | ------ |
| 2 KB task drawing from an already-seeded DRBG | passes |
| 2 KB task that seeds the DRBG itself | `Guru Meditation Error: Core 1 panic’ed (LoadProhibited)` |
| 8 KB `app_main` seeding, then 2 KB tasks drawing | passes |

That middle row is the point, and it corrected my first experiment. I initially just shrank the smoke test's task stack to 2 KB and it passed, which looked like the hazard was not real. It passed because `app_main` had already seeded with 8 KB of stack, so the task never paid the seed cost. Re-running with a 2 KB task as the genuine first caller crashes. The hazard is specifically the first caller, which is why the README recommends seeding deliberately from a task whose depth you control.

## .gitignore

Executing action: all (aliases: build)
Running cmake in directory /home/kyle/Documents/GitHub/libnostr-c/build
Executing "cmake -G Ninja -DPYTHON_DEPS_CHECKED=1 -DPYTHON=/home/kyle/.espressif/python_env/idf5.4_py3.12_env/bin/python -DESP_PLATFORM=1 -DCCACHE_ENABLE=0 /home/kyle/Documents/GitHub/libnostr-c"... and the QEMU step generate `sdkconfig`, `dependencies.lock` and `managed_components/` in `test/esp-idf`. None were ignored, so they were one `git add -A` away from being committed. `sdkconfig` in particular is per-developer. `sdkconfig.defaults` stays tracked, since that is what CI and a fresh checkout use.

## Test plan

- [x] Figures verified against ESP-IDF's own mbedTLS sources
- [x] `.bss` measured from a built ELF, not estimated
- [x] Stack claims reproduced under QEMU, including the crash
- [x] Smoke test restored and passing after the experiments: **SMOKE-PASS**
- [x] Generated files now ignored; `sdkconfig.defaults` still tracked
- [ ] CI

Closes libnostr-c-j31.

  - Documented cached cryptographic random generator behavior, initialization, memory usage, measured QEMU results, and CI task configuration.

- **Chores**

author: ihb2032
body:
A desktop build stopped shipping one segmentation engine while a stored
setting still named it. Every block then failed to compile, and what a reader
saw was a document gone blank — the structure tree childless, the braille pane
empty, the export empty — explained by one identical error per block.

The registry had no way to answer "is this installed?" short of loading the
adapter, and loading is not a neutral question: an engine's loader reads a
hundred megabytes of model. So a picker offered every registered engine,
including the ones that cannot work.

Three commits: a `probe` declaration and `available()` on the registry that
answers from `importlib.util.find_spec` without running the loader; the
shipped adapters declaring their modules, with `available_analyzers()` /
`available_resolvers()` for callers building a picker; and the pinyin `auto`
chain saying so when it runs out of candidates instead of landing silently on
the resolver that produces nothing.

author: xcomart
body:
The section claimed the log system can be configured before `CMDBM_Init`. It cannot: the log system lives in libcmutils and needs the memory system that `CMUTIL_Init` sets up, and `CMDBM_Init` is what calls `CMUTIL_Init`. Configuring earlier segfaults.

What the section documents now was verified by running it:

| Order | Result |
|---|---|
| configure before any init | SIGSEGV |
| `CMDBM_Init()` then configure | works; only the start-up messages go to the default logger |
| `CMUTIL_Init()`, configure, `CMDBM_Init()`, and `CMUTIL_Clear()` at the end | works, covers start-up too — `CMUTIL_Init` is reference counted |
| `cmutil_log.jsonc` in the working directory | works with no code, covers start-up |
| `CMUTIL_LOG_CONFIG=<file>` | works with no code, covers start-up |

Two more findings went in as well:

- `CMUTIL_LogSystemConfigureFomJson` installs itself as the global log system. Passing its result to `CMUTIL_LogSystemSet` destroys that object and then stores the dangling pointer — a use-after-free, confirmed under gdb. The section warns against it.
- A logger refers to its appenders with `appenderRef`; getting the key wrong silently produces no output at all.

Documentation only, no code change.

author: grnt426
body:
…o the visible panel

Two long-standing defects in the orbital-list scrollbar (and every other v-scrollbar in the game UI):

1. Dragging the thumb died the moment the cursor left the rail. The vue-custom-scrollbar wrapper deep-watches its `settings` prop and destroys + recreates its PerfectScrollbar instance on any identity change; our templates passed `:settings="{ ... }"` inline, so every parent re-render (row hover, store tick) minted a new object and the watcher tore down the instance mid-drag, unbinding the document-level mousemove/mouseup listeners that make an off-rail drag work. Settings now live as frozen singletons in utils/scrollbar.js; the seven mini-panels get theirs from MiniPanelMixin.

2. The rail itself scrolled out of the viewport. perfect-scrollbar keeps the rail inside the visible box by setting rail top = scrollTop, which assumes the .ps element is the rail's containing block — but .system-content-scrollbar was statically positioned, so the rail resolved against the outer container and slid below the screen as you scrolled. `.ps` is now position: relative (the library's own requirement). On short windows the panel also hung off-screen because min-height: 525px beats max-height in CSS; the floor is now capped by the same viewport budget so the panel and rail always fit between the navbars and the thumb is sized against what is actually visible.

author: slzwei
body:
## Task

**M1 (MED)** — Two independent QR lifecycle fields make deactivation ineffective.

## Defect (confirmed live)

`qr_tags` carried two independent lifecycle fields:
- Bulk activate/deactivate/archive wrote **`status` only** — but the public slug resolver (`resolveQrTag`) and the attribution resolver gate on **`active`**. A printed QR stayed publicly resolvable and kept recording scans after the admin received a successful deactivation response.
- `PUT {active:false}` wrote **the boolean only** — the status-gated authenticated `/:id/scan` path still accepted the supposedly disabled QR.

## Fix (canonical column + dual-write + data migration + constraint, as prescribed)

- **`status` is canonical** (only it can say `archived`); `active` remains as a dual-written mirror for API/frontend compatibility.
- Bulk ops write both fields **in one statement**. `PUT {active}` moves `status` with it: `false` preserves an archived state; `true` relaunches (matching the boolean's public effect it always had — pre-fix, `active:true` made an archived tag publicly resolvable).
- Both `trackerService` resolvers now gate on the canonical status; `recordScan` already did.
- **Migration 106**: reconciles drifted rows with **deactivation intent winning in both directions** (a row either side ever marked not-live goes not-live; `NULL` counts as not-live — fail safe, never fail live), then `SET NOT NULL` on `active` and `CHECK ck_qr_tags_lifecycle_coherent ((status='active') = active)` via NOT VALID → VALIDATE (migration 014 pattern). Model mirrors `allowNull: false` for the sync-built test schema.

## Test proof

**Pre-fix** (`qrLifecycleCoherence.test.js`, captured on this branch):
```
bulk deactivate → row {status:'inactive', active:TRUE} — still publicly resolvable
bulk archive    → row {status:'archived', active:TRUE} — same leak
PUT active:false → status stayed 'active' — scan path still open
Tests: 3 failed, 3 passed
```
**Post-fix: 6/6** — deactivate/archive kill resolver + scan + mirror; PUT couples both fields; relaunch restores.

author: kirihararingo
body:
Closes #147
Closes #148

触る場所が近いため 1 本にまとめた。

## 置き場所は逆になった

| | 置き場所 | 理由 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| パターンの色・線種（#147） | **設定** | どのパターンが直行かは路線の事実。その線が見分けやすいかはその人の目の話（#133 と同じ） |
| 運用の色（#148） | **プロジェクト（`view`）** | 運用番号はその文書のもの。`A` はダイヤが違えば違う車を指す。**渡した相手の画面でも同じ色で見えてほしい** |

設定に運用の色を持つと、別のファイルを開いたときに無関係な `A` の色を引き継ぐ。

## 色と線種は独立

片方だけ選んでも、もう片方は `route.json` のまま。**両方とも空になったら行ごと落とす**——空の上書きを覚えていると、「選んでいない」と「選んで既定と同じ」の区別がつかなくなる。

線種は**実線 / 破線 / 1 点鎖線**の 3 つ。刻みの打ち込みは許さない（#114 の判断を黙って戻さないため）。**回送の線種は選べない。**

## 決める場所は 1 つ

姿を決めるのは `patternStyles` 1 か所で、スジ（`selectDiagramScene`）も凡例（`PatternList`）もそこを通る。**別々に決めると、一覧とスジが違う姿になる。** 運用の色も `assignBlockColors` に渡す形にし、時刻表・サイドパネル・ダイヤグラムが同じ道具を使う状態を保った。

## 選ばせる色を配色に限らなかった

#148 では既定の 10 色から選ばせる案を書いたが、**任意の色**（`<input type="color">`）にした。淡すぎる色は地色に対して読めるよう調えられる（`readableOn`、§9.4）ため、当初の懸念（見えない運用を作れてしまう）は起きない。

試験でも確かめてある——`#abcdef` を選ぶと暗くして描かれ、**選んだ値そのものは残る**（次にテーマを変えたときに、選び直した色から出発できる）。

## 運用を足しても選んだ色は動かない

自動割り当ての代償（番号の増減で色がずれる）を、必要なところだけ打ち消せる。試験では、色を選んだ運用 `2` の手前に運用 `0` を足しても色が動かないことを確かめた。

## 実機で確かめた（headless Chromium、40 便）

- 設定の「表示」タブに 8 パターン（**回送は並ばない**）。線種の選択肢は「路線図のまま（破線）／実線／破線／1 点鎖線」
- S1 を緑・1 点鎖線にすると、**ダイヤグラムのスジと凡例の両方**が変わる
- 運用 A に色を選ぶと、サイドパネルの見本と時刻表の帯が変わり、戻す押しボタンが現れる

## 直した記述

#147 の本文に「色は 3 か所で使われている（ダイヤグラム・凡例・時刻表のパターン欄）」と書いたが、**時刻表のパターン欄は色を使っていない**（記号の選択欄である）。パターンの色が出るのはダイヤグラムと凡例の 2 か所、運用の色が出るのはダイヤグラム・サイドパネル・時刻表の帯の 3 か所である。

## 試験

1760 件通過、網羅率は文・分岐・関数・行すべて 100%。

## 文書

仕様書 v4.40（§6.5.3、§5.8）、実装計画書 1.35。

author: ryansinn
body:
## Summary

Second half of the visibility-chokepoint refactor (first half: `channel_visibility.py` + `ChannelRepository._apply_channel_filters`, already on `main`). The three remaining parallel "which channels are visible" implementations now route through `metatv.core.channel_visibility.apply()`:

- **`discovery_engine.py`** — the six module-level `_apply_*_filter`/`_apply_*_exclusion` helpers (prefix, provider, content-type, keyword, user-category, adult) now build a `VisibilityScope` and call `channel_visibility.apply()`. `get_all_collections()`/`get_by_collection()` inherit the fix automatically (they already compose these helpers).
- **`preference_engine.score_candidates`** — replaced its inline `is_hidden`/provider filters *and* its direct call into `discovery_engine._apply_prefix_filter` with one `channel_visibility.apply()` call. This also removes an unusual engine-to-engine import (preference_engine was reaching into discovery_engine).
- **`repositories/tag.py`** — `_scope_to_visible_channels` now builds its join scope via `channel_visibility.apply()` (keeping only the tag-specific `"##"` category-header filter alongside it). `get_facet_value_counts` gained the `excluded_prefixes`/`excluded_categories`/`excluded_tag_content_types` parameters it was missing (a **self-documented gap** in its own docstring), and the one caller (`MainWindow.initialize_filter_stats`) now resolves and passes all four Global-Exclusion axes instead of just the keyword one — closing the gap where the filter panel's counts disagreed with its own list.

## Divergence reconciled — behavioral change, not a pure refactor

`channel_visibility.py`'s docstring flagged a known inconsistency: `discovery_engine._apply_prefix_filter` used a **flat** `detected_prefix NOT IN (...)` check that never consulted `detected_region` for prefix-less channels, while the canonical predicate (`filter_utils.channel_exclusion_criterion`, already used by the channel list / tag-facet counts / EPG On-Now) is region-aware ("language wins over region").

**Decision: adopt the canonical, region-aware predicate everywhere.** It was already the standard on 3 of 4 surfaces (channel list, tag-facet counts, EPG) — `discovery_engine` (and by extension `preference_engine`, which called into it directly) was the outlier.

**User-visible consequence:** a title with **no** `detected_prefix` but an **excluded** `detected_region` is now ALSO hidden on Discover shelves and in Recommendations — previously it was shown there (though already hidden on the channel list). This is the structural fix for the reported **"Recommendations ignores global exclusions"** bug. A title WITH an un-excluded prefix still stays visible even when its (irrelevant) region tag happens to be excluded — "language wins over region" is preserved, not just "hide more indiscriminately."

Pinned by two dedicated tests (`test_discovery_engine_reconciles_prefix_region_divergence`, `test_score_candidates_reconciles_prefix_region_divergence`) proven to **fail on the pre-fix tree** (see Test plan).

## Known, unaddressed gaps (documented, not fixed by this slice — named files only)

- `score_candidates` has **no** `content_type`/`user_category` exclusion parameter at all today (a separate, pre-existing gap in Recommendations, not introduced or closed here — asserted explicitly in `test_score_candidates_excludes_prefix_and_keyword`).
- `discovery_engine`'s shelf queries never call `_apply_user_category_exclusion` — it was dead code before this migration and remains dead code after (migrated onto the chokepoint for when a future caller wires it up, but no shelf query invokes it). Asserted explicitly in `test_discovery_engine_excludes_prefix_content_type_keyword_adult`.

Both are natural follow-ups but touch GUI call sites the coordinating brief didn't name for this slice.

## Absolute gate preserved

Hidden/expired-provider content is never shown, counted, or revealed on any of the three migrated paths — proven directly (`test_*_hidden_provider_never_shown`, and the tag.py facet-count baseline).

## Incidental fix found while testing

While writing tests against a bare fake `Config` double, found that `main_window_channels.initialize_filter_stats` read `self.config.global_filter_paused` directly instead of `getattr(..., False)` like every other paused-check in the file — harmless with the real `Config` (always has the field) but would `AttributeError` against a minimal test double. Fixed to match the established defensive pattern; confirmed the existing `tests/test_filter_stats_async.py` (10 tests, unmodified) still passes.

## Test plan

New file: `tests/test_filter_paths_unified.py` — real `Database` on a `tmp_path` file (never `:memory:`), 10 tests + 3 parametrized cases, covering all three migrated paths:

- [x] `get_recently_added` (discovery_engine): hidden-provider absolute gate, combined prefix/content-type/keyword/adult exclusion, and the region-fallback reconciliation
- [x] `score_candidates` (preference_engine / Recommendations): hidden-provider absolute gate, prefix+keyword exclusion (documents the content-type/category gaps as unchanged), and the region-fallback reconciliation
- [x] `get_facet_value_counts` / `get_channel_ids_by_tag_facets` (tag.py): counts now agree with the list for prefix/category/content-type, individually and combined

**Proof the tests are real** (not shape coverage): stashed the 5 source-file changes (kept the new test file, which is untracked), reran — **6 of 10 tests failed** on the pre-fix tree:
- `test_discovery_engine_reconciles_prefix_region_divergence` — real `AssertionError` (region-fallback channel was shown, should be hidden)
- `test_score_candidates_reconciles_prefix_region_divergence` — same real `AssertionError`
- `test_facet_value_counts_gap_closed_matches_list` + all 3 parametrized `test_facet_value_counts_each_axis_drops_only_its_own_channel` cases — `TypeError: get_facet_value_counts() got an unexpected keyword argument 'excluded_prefixes'` (the params didn't exist pre-fix)

Restored the stash, reran clean: **10 passed**.

Ran `tests/test_filter_paths_unified.py` (new) once green, plus `tests/test_filter_stats_async.py` (pre-existing, at risk from the `initialize_filter_stats` signature change) once green as a targeted regression check. Did not run the full suite — that's the coordinator's single merge-gate pass.

## What's New

`metatv/whats_new/entries/0260_filter_paths_unified.py`, id 260, version 0.24.0, non-empty `test_steps`.

## Environment variables (action needed before PostHog works)

This app deploys to Vercel (per the README: "The `main` branch deploys to the connected Vercel project"), which keeps its settings in the Vercel dashboard rather than in a file committed to this repository, so I could not set these up automatically. This sandbox also isn't linked to the Vercel project, so I can't run the CLI equivalent for you either — someone with dashboard/CLI access will need to add them.

Environment variables are named settings your hosting provider passes to the app when it runs — they let the app know things (like the PostHog project token below) without hardcoding them in the code. PostHog will not receive any data until these two are set:

| Name                                 | Value                                            |
| ------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------ |
| `NEXT_PUBLIC_POSTHOG_PROJECT_TOKEN`   | `phc_vQTQMLJkPQTiLF9KKADgPoBW5NM8M4ByZpNfC5ETnF6T` |
| `NEXT_PUBLIC_POSTHOG_HOST`            | `https://us.i.posthog.com`                        |

To set them via the dashboard:

1. Open https://vercel.com/dashboard and click on this project.
2. Go to **Settings**, then **Environment Variables** in the left sidebar.
3. For each row in the table above: paste the Name and Value, leave all environments checked, and click **Save**.
4. Redeploy the app (Deployments tab, "..." menu on the latest deployment, **Redeploy**) — the new settings only take effect on the next deployment.

### Setting environment variables via a local CLI

If you have the Vercel CLI linked to this project, you can set them from a terminal instead:

```bash
echo "phc_vQTQMLJkPQTiLF9KKADgPoBW5NM8M4ByZpNfC5ETnF6T" | npx vercel env add NEXT_PUBLIC_POSTHOG_PROJECT_TOKEN production
echo "https://us.i.posthog.com" | npx vercel env add NEXT_PUBLIC_POSTHOG_HOST production
```

Then redeploy for the change to take effect.

author: soochol
body:
## 무엇

[#1021](https://github.com/Soochol/hoga-ops/pull/1021) 이 넣은 `ask_depth_renewal` 의 매수 대응 `bid_depth_renewal` 을 더한다. 판정식·파라미터(기준시각·문턱)·당일 전용 제약은 **동일**하고 보는 side 만 다르다.

```
기준시각 이후 그 side 총잔량 최댓값  ≥  (threshold_pct / 100) × 개장~기준시각 최댓값
```

## SQL 은 그대로다

테이블 프리미티브 `DepthSplitPeak` 이 이미 매도·매수 4개 값을 다 담고 있다 — #1021 에서 "매수 대응 조건이 생길 때 쿼리를 다시 짜지 않는다"고 적어둔 그 지점이 실제로 값을 했다. 쿼리 변경 0줄.

덤으로, **같은 기준시각이면 스냅샷 스캔도 한 번**이다(양측 값이 한 쿼리에서 나온다). 매도·매수 조건을 함께 걸어도 I/O 가 두 배가 되지 않는다 — 스캔 호출 횟수를 세는 테스트로 못 박았다.

## 기준시각을 side 별로 나눴다

사이드카에 `ask_renewal_start_hhmm` / `bid_renewal_start_hhmm` 을 둔다(기존 단일 `renewal_start_hhmm` 대체).

매도 12:00 · 매수 13:00 처럼 **섞어 쓸 수 있는데** 한 벌만 실으면 한쪽 배지가 남의 시각을 달고 나온다. peak 조건이 `ask_need_days`/`bid_need_days` 로 같은 문제를 이미 푼 적이 있어, 같은 방식으로 맞췄다. 배지도 side 별 행으로 일반화했다(양쪽 켜면 `매도`/`매수` 라벨 + 각자의 시각).

`renewal_start_hhmm` 은 몇 시간 전에 나갔고 소비자가 배지 하나뿐이라 이름 변경 비용이 없다. 저장 상태는 매 스캔 갱신되고, 검증기는 알려진 필수 필드만 보므로 구버전 레코드도 그대로 통과한다.

## 폼 문구를 side 중립으로

`이후 매도 총잔량이` → `이후 총잔량이`. `ParamForm` 은 `params`/`onChange` 만 받아 side 를 알 방법이 없고, `DepthPeakForm` 도 매도·매수 공용이면서 중립 문구(`과거 peak 대비`)를 쓴다. 어느 쪽인지는 조건 행 라벨이 말한다.

## 검증 — 실데이터

**side 분기가 실제로 갈리는지**가 이 PR 의 핵심 리스크라 거기에 집중했다(2026-07-31, 243종목).

| | 매도 | 매수 | 교집합 | 매수에만 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 12:00 · 100% | 133 | 99 | 57 | **42** |

- 두 집합이 다르고, 매수에만 잡히는 종목이 42개 — 같은 데이터를 그냥 복사한 게 아니다.
- AND 결합이 정확히 교집합(57).
- 혼합 기준시각 스크린에서 사이드카가 각자 값을 단다: `ask(1200) 120,824→134,562` / `bid(1300) 19,922→21,274`.
- 매수 문턱별: 100%→99 / 120%→67 / 150%→43 / 200%→19.

단위 테스트도 side 를 실제로 가리는지 본다 — 매도·매수가 **반대로 움직이는** 데이터를 넣어, 매수 조건은 통과하고 같은 데이터에 매도 조건은 미통과하는 것을 단언한다. 남의 side 사이드카가 새지 않는 것도 함께 본다.

## 게이트

`ruff` 통과 · `pytest` **3210 passed** · `typecheck` 3프로젝트 · `vitest` **4590 passed** · `vite build`.

메뉴 등록도 테스트로 덮었다 — [#1024](https://github.com/Soochol/hoga-ops/pull/1024) 에서 `CONDITION_GROUPS` 누락으로 조건이 안 보였던 회귀가 있어, 카탈로그와 그룹이 같은 집합인지 보는 단언이 이미 서 있고 이번 조건도 거기에 걸린다.

body:
Fixes https://github.com/tqbf/selfdrivingwiki/issues/1047

## Summary
- Add a `source add --url` CLI command and wire it through the async source-add path.
- Detect duplicate URL sources before fetching by comparing canonical URL provenance.
- Surface duplicates in the Add from URL sheet with options to open the existing source or add another copy explicitly.
- Preserve content-hash deduplication as a separate check after bytes are fetched.

## What changed
- Added URL identity normalization that lowercases scheme/host and ignores fragments while preserving path, query, port, and trailing slash semantics.
- Added store support to look up an existing source by URL provenance.
- Introduced `WikiStoreError.duplicateURL` so callers can distinguish URL provenance conflicts from content duplicates.
- Updated `WikiStoreModel.addURL` to reject duplicates before any network work unless `allowDuplicateURL` is set.
- Added `--allow-duplicate` to `wikictl source add --url` so non-interactive callers can intentionally create another source.
- Updated the Add from URL sheet to show a duplicate warning state with an `Open Existing` action and an explicit `Add Anyway` path.

## Tests
- Added coverage for URL identity normalization.
- Added coverage that duplicate URL intake does not call the fetcher unless duplication is explicitly allowed.

## Notes
- A progress note was added for issue 1047 documenting the behavior and verification.

author: jgangemi
body:
cmake/bb_generated.cmake gains bb_regenerate_wire_or_fail(), which runs bbtool codegen unconditionally at every real-pass CMake configure and rewrites examples/smoke and examples/floor's generated/bb_app_init.c from the current // bbtool:init marker set, instead of only checking the existing file for staleness. Both example main/CMakeLists.txt call it before the existing bb_verify_generated_or_fail symbol-existence check (kept as cheap belt-and-braces defense-in-depth against a codegen bug or an out-of-band write) and register component/platform headers AND component/platform CMakeLists.txt files (boards.derive_component reads each composed component's own CMakeLists.txt for REQUIRES/PRIV_REQUIRES independently of its headers -- an edit there with no header touched previously reconfigured nothing), the consumer manifest, the bbtool sources, and bbtool.toml via CMAKE_CONFIGURE_DEPENDS so a changed input reliably triggers a reconfigure (and therefore regeneration).

bbtool codegen's writer now shares version.py's write-if-changed helper (extracted to core.write_if_changed, a second hand-rolled instance triggering the Consolidation convention) so a content-stable regeneration never bumps the generated file's mtime and never forces a needless downstream recompile. The shared helper writes atomically via a per-call-unique tmp file (tempfile.mkstemp, never a fixed .tmp name, so two racing writers to the same generated file can't tear each other's output) and removes that tmp file on any write failure instead of leaving it behind. bb_regenerate_wire_or_fail's FATAL_ERROR also separates codegen's stdout/stderr with a newline instead of concatenating them unseparated.

make floor gains a floor-gen prerequisite, matching every smoke-<board> target's existing smoke-gen-<board> prerequisite.

Closes the gap #1208 (B1-1371's verify-generated) deliberately left open: a stale bb_app_init.c whose called functions still all exist (a pure ordering regression) passed that symbol-existence check silently; it cannot survive a build now.

Review finding 1: core.write_if_changed's atomic replace also now preserves file permissions. os.replace promotes the temp file's mode, and tempfile.mkstemp always creates at 0600 regardless of umask, so every regeneration was silently ratcheting bb_app_init.c and friends down to owner-only permissions. The temp file's mode is now chmod'd before the replace -- to the existing file's mode when overwriting, or to a umask-respecting default (0666 masked by the current umask) when creating a new file, never a hardcoded 0644. New permission-dimension tests in scripts/bbtool/tests/test_core_write_if_changed.py cover overwrite-preserves-0644, overwrite-preserves-an-unusual-mode, and new-file-respects-umask.

Review finding 2 / B1-1407 fix: the original landing of this change registered every component/platform CMakeLists.txt as an explicit CONFIGURE_DEPENDS entry, colliding with CMake's own automatic tracking of every CMakeLists.txt ESP-IDF actually add_subdirectory's -- the SAME absolute path registered from two directory scopes makes CMake's Ninja generator emit it as an output of the merged RERUN_CMAKE build edge twice, a hard ninja error (defined as an output multiple times) that PlatformIO could mask behind an overall SUCCESS while silently skipping the reconfigure, so bb_app_init.c was never regenerated even though the build reported success. This reproduced on a genuinely fresh build dir's second configure, not just a pre-existing .pio/build.

Fixed by de-duplicating: each example's main/CMakeLists.txt now filters its CMakeLists.txt candidate list against idf_build_get_property(... BUILD_COMPONENTS), ESP-IDF's own ground-truth list of components it is actually building, and only registers a candidate explicitly when its owning component is NOT in that list. BB_AUTOWIRE_REQUIRES (bbtool's own REQUIRES arg list) is NOT the right set to filter against -- examples/smoke never sets a project-level COMPONENTS allowlist, so ESP-IDF discovers and builds every component under components/ unconditionally regardless of REQUIRES (confirmed empirically: bb_attrs collided despite never appearing in BB_AUTOWIRE_REQUIRES); BUILD_COMPONENTS reflects ESP-IDF's actual resolved build regardless of which discovery/trim path a given example takes. Three consecutive configures of a fresh build dir are clean for both examples, and editing a component's REQUIRES/PRIV_REQUIRES line with no header touched still regenerates bb_app_init.c via a bare pio run, with no local .pio/build workaround needed any more.

Review finding 3 (pass 2): cmake/bb_generated.cmake's docstring falsely claimed the CONFIGURE_DEPENDS de-duplication filter currently registers nothing extra for either example, on the theory that no component in the current manifest is excluded from ESP-IDF's own BUILD_COMPONENTS tracking. Disproved empirically by instrumenting a real pio run configure of both examples on a fresh build dir: examples/smoke -e esp32 registers exactly components/display/bb_display_ek79007/CMakeLists.txt and components/display/bb_display_st77xx/CMakeLists.txt (excluded from that board's BUILD_COMPONENTS via EXCLUDE_COMPONENTS), and examples/floor -e esp32 registers 43 distinct components excluded from BUILD_COMPONENTS by floor's narrow COMPONENTS allowlist. Both docstrings (cmake/bb_generated.cmake and examples/smoke/main/CMakeLists.txt) are rewritten to state this observed, currently-live behavior with the concrete component lists, instead of the false 'registers nothing' claim, and examples/smoke/main/CMakeLists.txt's self-reference to its own -Werror loop is corrected to point at the sibling examples/smoke/CMakeLists.txt where that loop actually lives. codegen.py's run()/pio_main() now report 'wrote' vs 'unchanged' per output file based on core.write_if_changed's actual return value, instead of unconditionally printing 'wrote' on every real-pass CMake configure even when nothing touched disk.

body:
## Description

Wave 1 (Revision-2 order) opening PR of the ARIA full-autonomy program (`docs/plans/2026-08-02-aria-full-autonomy-program/PLAN.md`, PR 2.1) — deliberately independent of the state branch so it closes `ORPHAN-HIGH-433` standalone. Also carries the `ORPHAN-HIGH-523` close ceremony and the Wave-0 completion entry in PROGRESS.md.

**`ORPHAN-HIGH-433` (closed):** `covered_tool_ledgers` was a hand list — 4 required + 28 optional names — while `state_manifest` declared ~129 tools-root ledger surfaces. memory/*, enterprise/*, change-ledger/*, validation/*, queues/* were hash-chained on every write and never verified. Coverage now DERIVES from the manifest (`root_kind=="tools" ∧ state_class=="ledger"`; glob surfaces keyed per existing match; the core four — `runs`, `health`, `cycles`, `tools_governance` — unconditional so an empty root fails closed). Declaring a surface IS enrolling it; the projection test recomputes the set independently so a hand list cannot quietly return (I-W2-01).

**`ORPHAN-HIGH-525` (registered + fixed here — found by the fix):** widening coverage exposed a pre-existing defect the hand list had masked: the grouped index refresh REPLACES `ledger_hashes` with its own small membership on every indexed append, while `update_tools_index` and the verifier both worked from the wider covered set — full-rewrite entries were silently discarded, and verify stayed green only because it always ran right after full rewrites. `ledger.py`'s group table is promoted to the sole public authority (`tools_index_group_ledgers`) and all three parties consume it; chain verification stays on the wide derived set; index keys are unchanged on disk (no migration). The rewrite→append→verify sequence that used to corrupt is pinned green by test.

**`ORPHAN-MEDIUM-526` (registered; structural half fixed here):** an order/load-dependent flake in the shadow-run mutation detector reproduced twice during validation. Root cause of the intra-moment half: the scoped and raw views of one observation moment came from SEPARATE `git status` invocations, so one moment had two witnesses that could disagree under git's racy-stat heuristic — `_workspace_snapshots` now takes one `git status` per moment and projects both views from the same stdout. The finding stays OPEN for the cross-moment half pending soak evidence (its close needs green sequential runs over time, not one pass).

**Scheduled residue (recorded in 525's notes, owner + deadline):** `state_manifest`'s `index_group` column has zero runtime consumers and disagrees with live membership; reconciliation belongs to Wave-2 PR 2.2, which replaces `integrity_index.json` wholesale with signed snapshot manifests.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bugfix

## How Has This Been Tested?

- 4 new tests (`aria-kernel/tests/test_manifest_derived_integrity_coverage.py`): coverage equals an independently recomputed manifest projection; a previously-blind surface auto-enrolls on first write; tampering a previously-blind ledger fails public verification (the 433 property itself); and the rewrite→append→verify sequence agrees across all three index parties (the 525 kill-sequence).
- 1 test updated (`test_phase4_agent_network_invocations`) from hand-list alias keys to manifest surface names.
- Full kernel suite green sequentially on the final tree (3022 tests OK, including the snapshot-fix run); `aria:compile` green; `invariants:fast` green except the two `backup-production-secrets` cases that fail identically at `main`'s tip in this dev container (environmental; green in CI on today's merged PRs).
- `findings:verify` green (1332 entries); debt-plan mirror repinned; authority hash repinned (`43f1fde1` → `326a13e3`).

## Checklist

- [x] Code follows project's style guidelines
- [x] Self-review completed
- [x] Code is self-documenting (comments added where necessary)
- [x] Tests added/updated
- [x] Documentation updated
- [x] Security implications considered
- [x] No sensitive information committed
- [x] CI/CD pipelines will pass

## Deployment Plan

No deployment impact — ARIA kernel + registry/docs only. On live tools roots the first grouped index refresh after this lands rewrites `integrity_index.json` with the same key set as before (keys unchanged); verification simply starts covering all declared ledger surfaces.

## Issue Number

Registry findings: `ORPHAN-HIGH-433` (closed), `ORPHAN-HIGH-525` (registered + fixed), `ORPHAN-MEDIUM-526` (registered; structural half fixed), `ORPHAN-HIGH-523` (close ceremony). Program: Wave 1 §2.1.

author: fmbluesystem
body:
# Pull request

## Summary

- The bounded spectral gate now applies to **every anchor colour**, not only `MIXED`. RED, GREEN and BLUE anchors were never tightened by the predecessor change and were admitting tracks roughly **five times** further from the anchor than the bound they enforced.
- `same_color` gains the same gate, so its registered "Hard filter" description becomes true, and it **fails closed** instead of silently returning the whole library.
- `same_energy`, `same_genre`, `harmonic_journey`, `warmup`, `build`, `peak_time`, `chill` and `same_vibe` are unchanged.

Version `1.7.1` → `1.7.3`. Delivered as two reviewed slices: **#336** and **#337**.

## The defect this corrects

The predecessor change tightened `same_color_energy` for `MIXED` anchors on the stated reasoning that RED/GREEN/BLUE label equality was "already a real constraint, because a threshold was crossed".

**That reasoning was wrong, and measuring it is what exposed it.**

`_dominant_color()` classifies by per-band threshold excess. Over the simplex `r+g+b=1`, `MIXED` is a **bounded** triangle — L1 diameter `0.30`, `2.21%` of the simplex. RED, GREEN and BLUE are **not bounded above**: `r >= 0.45` reaches the simplex vertex. Crossing a threshold tells you that you passed it, not where you landed.

Measured on a real 10,367-track library, 400 samples per colour, all pairs, against the `0.08` bound already accepted as "sounds like the anchor":

| label | tracks | mean pairwise L1 | max pairwise L1 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| MIXED | 3342 | 0.1014 | 0.2834 |
| RED | 979 | 0.1427 | 0.5749 |
| GREEN | 4784 | 0.1629 | 0.7076 |
| BLUE | 1262 | 0.1585 | 0.6955 |

RED, GREEN and BLUE are **more** dispersed than `MIXED`, not less. And `MIXED` is only 32% of that library, so roughly two of every three anchors were taking the path that was never tightened.

## What changed

`same_color_energy` loses its `MIXED`-only short-circuit; the gate spans every label. The three constants lose their now-misleading `MIXED_` prefix and become colour-neutral.

`same_color` gets its own `_same_color_eligible` / `_apply_same_color_filter` / `_same_color_warnings` rather than widening the shared helper, so it gains the colour gate **without** gaining any energy limit — energy stays weighted, which is exactly what separates it from `same_color_energy`. The shared `_apply_color_filter` became orphaned and was removed after verifying the call graph; `_apply_genre_filter` is the genre path and is untouched.

## Measured effect, end to end

Driven offscreen through the real window against a scratch copy of the library. Maximum RGB L1 admitted, per anchor colour, before and after:

| anchor | before | after | bound |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| MIXED | 0.0799 | 0.0799 | 0.08 |
| RED | **0.4127** | **0.0796** | 0.08 |
| GREEN | **0.4523** | **0.0798** | 0.08 |
| BLUE | **0.3688** | **0.0799** | 0.08 |

`same_color` still ignores energy: 295 eligible candidates at a different energy level from the anchor, as intended.

## Two user-visible consequences a reviewer must not discover from the diff

**1. `same_color` no longer widens on an empty pool.** A DJ whose anchor matches nothing previously got the entire library back with a warning. They now get an honest empty result plus a warning explaining why. A strategy whose description claims a hard filter cannot silently return everything — that is the same promise-versus-behaviour defect this change exists to remove, and it left `same_color` inconsistent with its own sibling, which already failed closed.

**2. Candidate pools for RGB anchors shrink sharply.** At the busiest energy level per colour: RED `438 → 46`, GREEN `2295 → 93`, BLUE `796 → 172`. `MIXED` is unchanged at `466`. In the end-to-end run a GREEN anchor produced a 1-track set with an explicit shortage warning.

That is the honest consequence of the gate, not a regression in the filter — but it means the provisional bound may be too strict for RGB anchors in practice. The constants remain calibration-provisional and the delta spec binds the rule shape, not the numbers. Listening calibration across colours is the open acceptance gate, and a per-colour bound is a plausible outcome of it.

## Scope and review notes

- **What changed:** `src/xfinaudio/recommendation/playlist_service.py` and its tests.
- **What is intentionally out of scope:** `_dominant_color()` and its thresholds, `same_genre`'s unfiltered fallback, and every other strategy. No DSP, no new audio analysis, no schema migration, no RMS hard filter, no exact-key filtering, no audio mutation, no live Serato database V2 writes.
- **Reviewer should check first:** that `same_energy` and `same_genre` characterization tests are byte-untouched. Eight `same_color` tests were deliberately re-authored — they pinned exactly the fallback contract this change replaces, which is the one legitimate exception to never editing a characterization test, and each carries a docstring recording the reason.

## Tests run

- [x] `uv run pytest -q` — 1489 passed
- [x] `uv run ruff check .` — all checks passed
- [x] `uv run ruff format --check .` — 277 files already formatted
- [x] Focused tests: `tests/test_playlist_service.py`, `tests/test_playlist_strategies.py`
- [x] Also run: `uv run pyright src tests` (0 errors), `uv run pytest --cov --cov-fail-under=70 -q` (91%), `uv run python scripts/release_gate_check.py --run` (exit 0)
- [x] End-to-end offscreen run across MIXED, RED, GREEN and BLUE anchors against a scratch copy of the real library

## Safety checklist

- [x] No audio mutation.
- [x] No live Serato database V2 mutation.
- [x] Writes are limited to app-owned database, settings, or export files.
- [x] No private audio files, private library databases, or sensitive local paths are included.

## GPLv3 and open-source review

- [x] GPL-3.0-only and open-source documentation are unchanged or updated where relevant.
- [x] Third-party dependency/license documentation is unchanged or updated where relevant.
- [x] No binary, release, or legal clearance claims are made.

## Release gates

- [x] Not relevant.

author: nezreka
body:
# library manage layer → react — the enhanced view finishes its migration

part 3 of the library arc (after the list page and the artist-detail port). everything you can *do* from the enhanced view — every modal, poller, and admin action that still lived in library.js behind a `window.*` bridge — is react now. ten commits, one verified wave each.

## the headline: the artist meta panel was missing

when artist-detail went react, the enhanced view came over without its artist metadata card — no id badges, no match chips, no edit form, no Sync, no Reorganize All, and the reorganize status panel had nowhere to mount. nobody noticed because the vanilla renderer silently stopped being reachable. it's rebuilt from the vanilla source (`renderArtistMetaPanel`) with all of it back, including the live reorganize queue panel with its 1.5s/8s polling, cross-artist hints, and the debounced one-reload-per-batch refresh.

## what moved, wave by wave

- **deletes, source info, art pickers** — smart delete dialogs (track + album), the source-info popover with blacklisting, the parameterized art picker (album covers + artist photo)
- **enrichment + manual matching** — the enrich menus, the match modal with auto-search and provider override
- **tags + replaygain** — single and batch tag preview, the write pollers (they outlive the modal on purpose — progress arrives as toasts), track/album/batch RG
- **reorganize** — the per-album modal (mode/source/action + preview with the collision gate), reorganize-all, the status panel, cancel/clear queue
- **redownload** — the 3-step modal with streamed source columns, and the #911 canonical-source album redownload
- **missing tracks** — the manage chooser, wishlist-add with context, and the I Have This copy-import
- **satellites** — re-identify (#889, isrc-first), the discography download modal (gap-fill #1067, honest statuses #830), the hero watchlist button, mobile track actions, and the library page's Export Artists + Watch All Unwatched

**manual library match** didn't port — it's opened from still-vanilla pages (sync + tools), so it moved verbatim into its own file, `static/manual-library-match.js`, and joined the split ledger.

## vanilla bugs fixed on the way

- clear match called `renderEnhancedArtistView()` — a function that doesn't exist. the refresh path ReferenceError'd every time
- clear match used a bare `confirm()` instead of the app dialog
- the redownload flow kept its chosen metadata in `selectedMeta` — an undeclared global leaking onto window
- a streamed redownload result could silently steal your manually-picked source; the pick sticks now
- the track table's column sort actually sorts (the vanilla applied it and immediately re-sorted by disc/track, so the arrow moved and nothing else)

## verification

~120 new tests pinning the vanilla's toast wording, poller cadences, and request payloads. full webui suite green (209 files / 4,508 tests), zero type/lint/format errors, python guard suites green (split integrity, vanilla globals, cross-file contract). smoke-tested live: discography modal (caught a backdrop-filter clipping bug — fixed by portaling the hero-mounted overlays to body), write-all-tags, re-identify, watchlist button, export, library match.

library.js still loads — the state spine (`playLibraryTrack`, `navigateToArtistDetail`, `artistDetailPageState`, the breadcrumb + search handoff) rehomes in the follow-up PR that deletes the file and its dead markup.

author: nguyendung278
body:
## Vì sao

`ProductVariant` đã có SKU, giá và tồn kho riêng từ lâu, nhưng `cart-service` và `order-service` **không hề biết tới nó** — `grep -i variant` trong hai service này trả về 0 kết quả. Ledger giữ chỗ khoá theo `(order_id, product_id)`.

Hệ quả: khách chọn "áo size M" nhưng hệ thống trừ **tồn kho tổng** của sản phẩm. Vẫn oversell theo size dù pattern reservation đã đúng ở mức sản phẩm, và `variant.Price` khác `product.Price` thì không được áp vào đơn. Kiểm tra trên catalog đang chạy: **39/40 sản phẩm có variant**, nên đây không phải edge case mà là gần như toàn bộ hàng.

PR gồm ba phần: bịt lỗ hổng này, sửa hai bug có sẵn phát hiện khi verify, và thêm nghiệp vụ nhập kho.

---

## 1. Variant xuyên suốt cart → order → reservation

`sku` trở thành **một phần khoá định danh** của dòng giỏ hàng, dòng đơn và dòng ledger — không phải một field đính kèm.

| Thay đổi | Chi tiết |
|---|---|
| `stock_reservations` | PK đổi từ `(order_id, product_id)` sang `(order_id, product_id, sku)` |
| `order_items` | Thêm `sku` + `variant_label` (snapshot tại thời điểm mua, giống `name`/`price`) |
| Cart | Dòng giỏ khoá theo `(product_id, sku)`; sửa/xoá truyền `?sku=` |
| proto | Thêm `ProductVariant` và `Product.variants`, `StockReservationItem.sku` (additive) |
| Quy tắc | Sản phẩm có khai báo `variants` thì `sku` **bắt buộc** — bỏ trống bị từ chối thay vì lặng lẽ tính vào kho tổng |

`products.stock` giữ vai trò **số tổng hợp** cho listing/badge, đi theo cùng delta với variant nhưng không còn là nguồn sự thật khi mua.

### Điểm cần review kỹ

Guard chống oversell chuyển từ **CAS một câu lệnh** sang **row lock `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE`**.

Lý do: tồn kho variant nằm trong JSONB. Một câu `UPDATE` vừa đọc mảng đó làm predicate vừa ghi đè nó **không an toàn dưới READ COMMITTED** — subquery cấp dữ liệu cho predicate có thể được đánh giá trên snapshot chụp trước khi lock được cấp. Row lock cho cùng đảm bảo all-or-nothing, và `lockAndConsumeCoupon` vốn đã dùng đúng pattern này. Đây không phải làm yếu pattern, lý do đã ghi trong comment của hàm.

### Frontend

Backend mới từ chối mua sản phẩm có variant mà không kèm `sku`, mà storefront trước đó **không có chỗ chọn variant**. Nếu chỉ sửa backend thì 39/40 sản phẩm mất nút mua, nên PR làm cả bộ chọn phân loại: giá và tồn kho hiển thị theo variant đang chọn, variant hết hàng bị disable, card ngoài danh sách đổi thành "Chọn phân loại" và điều hướng sang trang chi tiết.

---

## 2. Hai bug **có sẵn**, phát hiện khi verify

Cả hai đều không do PR này gây ra. Với bug thứ nhất tôi đã dựng lại `order-service` từ code **trước** lô variant để xác nhận — vẫn hỏng y hệt.

**a. Huỷ đơn / đổi trạng thái luôn trả 500** — `UpdateStatus` dùng `$1` ở cả vế gán `status = $1` lẫn vế so sánh trong `CASE`. Postgres suy ra `varchar` từ vế gán và `text` từ vế so sánh cho **cùng một tham số**, rồi từ chối cả câu lệnh:

```
pq: inconsistent types deduced for parameter $1
```

Hỏng cả ba đường: user huỷ đơn, admin huỷ đơn, admin đổi trạng thái — đều 500 và kho bị giam. Trong DB dev, 10 đơn `cancelled` đều do `reservation-expiry-worker` tạo; đường huỷ qua API chưa từng chạy được lần nào.

Lưu ý khi review: ép `::text` ở vế so sánh thôi là **chưa đủ**, vế gán vẫn thắng suy kiểu. Phải ép ở mọi chỗ.

**b. Worker hoàn tiền không bao giờ nhận job** — `refund_next_retryAt` thiếu gạch dưới trong `ClaimPendingReturnRefunds`. Postgres hạ chữ thường mọi identifier không đặt trong nháy kép nên nó thành `refund_next_retryat`, câu lệnh luôn lỗi. Queue `refund_pending` kẹt vĩnh viễn, log spam WARN mỗi 2 giây. Có sẵn từ `13820d5` (22/04). Đã rà toàn bộ SQL trong repo bằng script quét identifier camelCase — không còn chỗ nào khác.

**Cả hai chỉ nổ ở tầng Postgres** nên unit test dùng repository giả không bắt được. Đã thêm regression test chạy testcontainers cho từng cái, và kiểm chứng test **đỏ với code cũ** trước khi sửa.

Kèm theo: `cancelOrderWithActor` trước đây nuốt lỗi từ `markOrderCancelled` — client chỉ thấy "failed to cancel order", không có dấu vết nào để lần ra. Đã thêm log, và chính nó cho ra thông báo lỗi gốc ở trên.

---

## 3. Nhập kho / điều chỉnh tồn

Trước đây tồn kho **chỉ có đường giảm** qua reservation, không có đường tăng nào qua API. Sửa thẳng `products.stock` bằng endpoint update sản phẩm thì mất dấu vết: không biết ai sửa, vì lý do gì.

`POST` / `GET /api/v1/products/:id/stock-adjustments` (admin + staff), ghi sổ cái `stock_adjustments`.

Các quyết định thiết kế:

- **`AdjustStock` lấy cùng row lock với `ReserveStockForOrder`.** Nhập kho và giữ chỗ checkout cùng chạm một bộ đếm, nên `stock = stock + $1` kiểu cộng mù sẽ đua với reservation đang đọc số tồn cũ. Có test chứng minh: 10 lần nhập 3 cái song song với 10 lần giữ chỗ 1 cái, từ 20 → đúng 40.
- **Lý do là tập đóng** (`received`/`recount`/`damaged`/`returned`/`correction`), không phải ô text tự do — kiểm kê lệch thì phải lọc được "lệch vì hỏng hàng" khỏi "lệch vì nhập thiếu".
- **Idempotent theo `Idempotency-Key`** vì double-click lúc nhập kho thổi phồng tồn kho âm thầm, chỉ lộ ra khi kiểm kê.
- **Chặn tồn kho âm**, và request bị từ chối **không để lại dòng sổ cái nào** — một dòng sổ cái phải luôn ứng với một biến động có thật.

---

## Kiểm chứng

`make ci` xanh toàn bộ module. Client `tsc -b` + eslint sạch.

Verify end-to-end trên stack docker thật (không chỉ test):

```
trước:  {AC-011-M: 5, AC-011-L: 3} agg 8
đặt 2 size M → {AC-011-M: 3, AC-011-L: 3} agg 6     ← chỉ M bị trừ
huỷ đơn      → {AC-011-M: 5, AC-011-L: 3} agg 8     ← trả đúng về M
```

Sổ cái nhập kho:

```
giờ       sku           delta  còn lại  lý do       ai      ghi chú
02:19:14  AC-011-M         -4  32       damaged     admin   vỡ khi vận chuyển
02:18:46  AC-011-M        +30  36       received    admin   nhập lô tháng 8
```

Add-to-cart không kèm `sku` đổi từ `HTTP 200` (âm thầm sai) sang `HTTP 400`. Sáu đường từ chối của nhập kho đều đúng status: trừ quá tồn `409`, thiếu sku `400`, sku lạ `404`, delta 0 `400`, reason bịa `400`, không token `401`.

Test concurrency then chốt: 40 đơn đồng thời mua size M (tồn 5) → đúng 5 đơn thành công, **size L không bị đụng tới**. Chạy trên code cũ thì size L sẽ bị rút xuống 0.

---

## Reviewer cần biết

- **Migration đụng dữ liệu có sẵn**: `stock_reservations` đổi primary key. Migration down có bước gộp dòng trùng trước khi dựng lại PK cũ. Đã chạy thử trên DB dev đang có dữ liệu, 10/10 dòng cũ nguyên vẹn.
- **Giỏ hàng cũ trong Redis** thiếu `sku` sẽ bị từ chối ở checkout với hàng có variant. `artifacts/scripts/prune-legacy-carts.sh` dọn đúng những dòng đã hỏng (giữ nguyên dòng của sản phẩm không variant), mặc định dry-run, chỉ ghi khi có `--apply`.
- **`.claude/launch.json`** đổi port preview 3000 → 3100 vì container `ecommerce-client` đang giữ 3000. Chỉ ảnh hưởng preview tool, không ảnh hưởng `make client-dev`.
- **Chưa làm**: worker cảnh báo tồn kho thấp (`ListLowStock` đã có sẵn, thiếu worker định kỳ đẩy qua `notification-service`). Đã ghi vào PROJECTS.md mục "Ưu tiên cao" thay vì bỏ lửng.
- **Không có UI cho nhập kho** vì `client/` không có bề mặt admin nào để nối vào.

author: davidmgdev
body:
Six reported problems.

**1. The die grew twice.** The hold animated one shared value and the roll animated a *different* one starting from zero, so the die snapped back to its resting size at the exact moment the roll sound played, then grew again. And when the roll finished the style fell back to the hold's value, still at 1, so a die held past the end of its roll jumped to full size and stayed there until release. One value now, animated continuously through both phases, ending at rest whether or not the finger is still down.

**2. The throw was sixteen token-widths in 620ms**, about four frames. It is seven over 1150ms. Throwing now works on **ordinary tokens** too: the whole leave animation moved out of the separate falling layer into the token itself, which is what makes mid-flight steering possible at all — the gesture and the thing it steers are finally the same view. A swipe adds an impulse from wherever the token has already got to rather than restarting it, so hold and hold-then-swipe are one motion with two endings. The token comes off the card when the animation *ends*, not when it starts. `FallingToken` is deleted.

**3. The action row leaked touches.** A plain `View` is not a touch responder, so the 8px gaps between the buttons, and the padding around the labels on the fixed-width ones, fell straight through to the focus veil and closed the card. The row swallows its own touches, each Pressable fills its button, and the buttons are 44 tall rather than 40. The gear-pad exclusion box was also still the lone Modifiers button's rect, so a tap on Toggle or # reached the gear underneath; it is the whole row now.

**4.** Opening the Card Type picker dismisses the keyboard.

**5. Armor sizes itself.** Five or fewer: exactly those shields, one row, 26px instead of 17. Six or more: the original twelve in two rows. Zero keeps one locked shield, because an empty band under the word ARMOR reads as a bug. Pure and tested.

**6. Unfilled Hope is opaque.** The diamonds were hollow, which never showed at rest (what is behind them is parchment) and was obvious the moment one grew: it scaled up over the gold rule behind the track and the rule showed straight through its middle. A parchment core inset 17%, which lands just inside the outline's inner edge.

## Verified

In a browser: tapping the gap between Modifiers and Toggle leaves the card focused, and a character at 0 armor shows one large shield instead of twelve small ones. 663 tests, 54 suites; `tsc` clean; `eslint` 0 errors. The forged-card signature is unchanged, so **no device re-forges its deck for this one**.

author: ohadavraham85
body:
## Summary
Root cause of a real duplicate slipping through the Gallery's upload-dedup check: the check only ever compares an incoming file's hash against photos that already have a stored `contentHash` — and only photos uploaded through the Gallery button *after* that feature shipped got one computed. Any photo already in the Gallery before then (i.e. most of a real library) has no hash to compare against, so re-uploading it isn't recognized as a duplicate, even though the hash-comparison logic itself is correct.

Adds a one-time (per device, guarded by a persisted setting) backfill that hashes every existing photo missing a `contentHash` when the Gallery tab is opened, so the duplicate check has something to compare against regardless of when or how a photo first entered the Gallery. Runs in the background on `activate()` (doesn't block opening the tab); the upload handler itself awaits it before checking, so an upload immediately after opening the Gallery is still covered correctly.

## Test plan
- [x] `npm run typecheck` / `npm run build`
- [x] Playwright: seeded a photo with no `contentHash` (simulating one that predates this feature) — confirmed it gets backfilled on Gallery open, and re-uploading its exact bytes afterward is correctly caught as a duplicate; confirmed revisiting the Gallery again doesn't redo the backfill or cause issues
- [x] Playwright regression (clean origin, distinct fixture bytes per photo): uploading two genuinely different photos both succeed, re-uploading one is blocked as a duplicate, and the species-specific association flow from a previous round still works correctly end-to-end

author: theangryraven
body:
Master half of the same fix as #126 (BETA). Docs-only, two lines.

## The bug

`CLAUDE.md` documented the DOVEX metadata line as:

```
datetime,driver_name,course_name,short_name,best_lap_ms,optimal_lap_ms,device_name
```

but `BirdsEye/dovex_header.cpp:55` emits:

```
datetime,driver,course,short_name,best_lap_ms,optimal_ms,device_name
```

Three of the seven names were wrong: `driver_name` → `driver`, `course_name` → `course`, `optimal_lap_ms` → `optimal_ms`.

## Why it matters

DovesDataViewer's `dovexParser.ts` is **key-mapped, not positional** — it builds a `header[i] → value[i]` map and looks the fields up by name. It matches the *code*, so anyone trusting this doc would have "corrected" the parser to look for names that never appear on the wire, silently blanking driver, course and optimal-lap for every log. Quiet failure that would have read as a firmware regression.

Found while surveying the viewer for sprint-mode work.

## Changes

Two lines in `CLAUDE.md` — the header line and the prose reference to `optimal_lap_ms` in the `device_name` note. CRLF preserved (this file is CRLF on master).

**Not changed:** `README.md`'s copy already had the right names, and `dovex_header.h:11` was right too — `CLAUDE.md` was the only place that drifted. Note also that the settings-JSON key `driver_name` is a *different* thing and is correct as-is; only the DOVEX column names were wrong.

## Difference from #126

The BETA version of this fix also adds `race_mode` to README's structure diagram, since sprint mode added that trailing column there. Master has no `race_mode`, so its README is already accurate and untouched here.

## Verification

Extracted the format string straight out of `dovex_header.cpp` and compared programmatically:

```
emitted: datetime,driver,course,short_name,best_lap_ms,optimal_ms,device_name
CLAUDE : datetime,driver,course,short_name,best_lap_ms,optimal_ms,device_name   MATCH
README : datetime,driver,course,short_name,best_lap_ms,optimal_ms,device_name   MATCH
```

author: arena-ai-coding-agent[bot]
body:
## Summary

The demo library and pipeline produced outputs that contradicted the advertised features, so no feature could be verified end-to-end ("nothing works"). This PR fixes the root causes, regenerates the fixture library, and pins every fixed behavior with regression tests.

## Bugs fixed

1. **Russian/Japanese fixtures contained no real text** — `create_test_fixtures.py` used PyMuPDF's default Helvetica font, which silently renders non-Latin glyphs as `·` bullets. Language detection reported `zh-cn` for *Война и мир* and *ワンピース*. Fixtures now embed a real Cyrillic TTF and PyMuPDF's built-in `japan` font → detection correctly reports `ru` / `ja`.
2. **Duplicate detection never worked on the demo library** — the "Duplicate Test" pair was saved twice from the same doc, but PyMuPDF embeds a fresh random document ID per save, so the bytes differed. Both files are now written from the same buffer → the pipeline finds 1 duplicate group.
3. **Every novel with ≥10 chapters was flagged as an omnibus** — `startswith('chapter 1')` also matches "Chapter 10"–"Chapter 19". Fixed with digit-boundary regexes in `_detect_omnibus`.
4. **Scientific American was classified as a *book* and its filename shredded** into author="Scientific American", title="01" → rename `Scientific American/01 (2023).pdf` lost the publication name. Classifier now uses periodical signals (ISSN, cover date, Vol/No/Issue, Article N, YYYY-MM filename date); parser keeps publication + issue → **`Scientific American/Scientific American (2023-01).pdf`**.
5. **Publisher extraction captured the next line** — `Publisher\nChapter 1` yielded publisher="Chapter 1". Patterns no longer cross line boundaries.
6. **Web/desktop app crashed after CLI-first setup** — launchers installed web deps only on fresh venv creation, so a venv created by `launch.sh`/`setup_and_test.sh` started with `ModuleNotFoundError: fastapi`. Launchers now install missing web deps; `setup_and_test.sh` installs them so `make test` runs the webapp tests instead of silently skipping; pip invocations use `python -m pip` (robust to venv relocation).
7. **Evidence docs recorded the broken outputs** — `PASS3_EVIDENCE.txt` regenerated from the corrected run; stale `zh-cn` claims in `PASS1_COMPLETE.md` / `PASS1_SUMMARY.md` corrected; full audit trail added as Finding 10 in `FIX_LOG.md`.

## Verification

- **134 tests pass** (120 existing + 14 new regression tests in `tests/test_fixture_features.py`), zero skips.
- Full pipeline on the demo library: `en:12 / ru:1 / ja:1`, `book:6 / comic:1 / magazine:1 / unknown:7`, 1 duplicate group, only the real omnibus flagged, publisher "Old Publisher".
- CLI scan/report, calibre import/export, webapp (setup → scan → review → apply), and desktop launcher exercised live.

## Notes

Wave 2B (vision) and Wave 3 (OpenLibrary/Crossref) still cannot be live-verified from a sandbox without a configured vision endpoint / network egress — they skip honestly and are covered by controlled local-server tests (see `BETA_EVIDENCE_BLOCKERS.md`).

author: famousdavis
body:
The `ADDITIONAL TERMS` block goes from four clauses to six, and every clause now tracks the wording of the GPL subsection that authorizes it. `LICENSE` grows **726 → 756 lines**.

This is the first of nine releases — the canonical copy lands here, and the eight app repos follow with the same text and the new digest.

## Why clause `b)` had to change

It required any modified version with a user interface to **display** a notice. §7(b) authorizes only **preservation** — *"in that material or in the Appropriate Legal Notices displayed by works containing it"* — and §5(d) says outright that a work *"need not make"* interfaces display Appropriate Legal Notices where the Program's do not.

A term outside the §7(a)–(f) list is a "further restriction" a recipient may simply delete. The old wording protected nothing against the one reader it was written for. The trigger is now the §0 defined term, and the repository link is conditional on the original displaying one — an unconditional requirement would smuggle the same defect back in, since GanttApp and spert-ssv display no repository link today.

## Two clauses added

| Clause | Authority | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `e)` Endorsement and Promotion | §7(d) | The author's name may not be used to endorse or promote a derived product. Nothing else covered this — the marks have trademark law behind them with or without this licence, a personal name does not, and `a)`/`b)` require that name to be present. |
| `f)` Indemnification | §7(f) | A reseller who conveys with contractual warranties covers liability those promises impose on the author. Licensing is personal here, with no entity in between. |

## Smaller corrections

- `d)` claims §7(c)'s unused misrepresentation-of-origin half, and matches its "in reasonable ways" wording.
- `c)` gains a narrow nominative carve-out with a no-sponsorship limit — resolving the tension where `c)` grants no rights to the marks while `d)` requires a fork to distinguish itself from them.
- The registration recital is date-stamped: asserting live USPTO registration as bare present fact acquires a shelf life.
- The preamble says "terms", not "restrictions" — the noun §7 reserves for the deletable category.

## Deliberately unchanged

`d)` keeps *"marked in reasonable ways as different from the original version"* and *"cannot reasonably be confused with"*. A review proposed stricter, off-text replacements; stricter-and-off-text is precisely how a term falls out of the safe harbour.

## Guards

All nine repos pin a SHA-256 of the LICENSE body with line 4 normalised. Updated here in `src/guards/suite-artifacts.test.ts`:

```
e9983ebf…4f64f  →  06d6dbc5fee76aa6b82198254e4a7489ef20718f7bd4445b87432878d2160630
```

The eight app repos assert the same constant and will each be updated in their own patch release.

## Verification

Ship gate passed: lint, typecheck, tests, build, plus all four `functions/` gates. No app behaviour change.

author: erkhesbold2005-blip
body:
## Description

#116 makes a preprocessed-flagged interaction term raise when no preprocessed
trace is supplied. Nothing in this repo could supply one — the values live in
the proving key's binary `<Air>.const` blob, and we only ever read the JSON
beside it. This is the producer half.

Values come from the key rather than a local recomputation. The key is already
our reference input (`scripts/extract_cexp.py` projects the same
`constPolsMap`) and it is the authority rw's own fixed-column oracle checks
against, so recomputing e.g. `CLK_0 = (r % op_cycle == 0)` here would invent a
second authority — one that drifts the moment riscv-witness#2189 answers the
period question differently than we guessed.

**The layout is reverse-engineered; pil2 ships no schema for it.** A bare
little-endian u64 matrix, row-major `(N, nConstants)`, canonical not
Montgomery, base domain (the extended LDE is `<Air>.consttree`). Three things
validate that reading, and they matter because the failure mode otherwise is a
*sheared* trace rather than an error:

- **The LDE round-trip is the strong one.** Extending the decoded matrix with
  pil2's own `extendPol` reproduces the const trace the native pil2 CUDA prover
  dumped for this AIR's instance, **byte for byte**. The LDE is over a coset, so
  the extended trace is not a subsample of the base one — reproducing it
  requires actually extending, which is why a wrong domain, a transposed read,
  or Montgomery-form values cannot pass by coincidence. This single assertion
  pins layout, canonical form, base domain and column order together.
- `__L1__` independently pins row-major: pil2 synthesizes it as the Lagrange
  basis at row 0, so it decodes as exactly one nonzero at row 0 under the
  row-major reading and as a column nonzero almost everywhere under the
  column-major one. Confirmed on all three air keys. Note that eyeballing
  values does *not* discriminate — `OPID` / `VALS` look plausible either way.
- The byte count is exact on all five keys available locally —
  fibonacci-square's FibonacciSquare / Module / SpecifiedRanges plus the
  vadcop_final pair, spanning `nConstants` 2..49 and `nBits` 8..16 — and it is
  re-checked on every load, so a format change surfaces as an error.

**What this deliberately does not answer:** `constPolsMap` order is pil2's, and
pil2 synthesizes selectors rw never authored, so it is not rw's preprocessed
index space. `columns=` (select and order by name, off a memmap) is the seam
for that rather than an encoded mapping. Pinning the two together needs rw's
`{"preprocessed": idx}` descriptors from riscv-witness#2189, which is still
open — no ZisK chip commits a fixed column yet, so there is nothing to pin
against, and guessing would reproduce the silent-wrong-column failure #116
exists to prevent. Note also that the join is not string equality: pil2 names
authored const pols `<Air>.<NAME>` and synthesized ones bare. The names side of
that contract is riscv-witness#2336.

The fixtures are a fibonacci-square air rather than a ZisK one because no ZisK
proving key is checked in; `.const` is pil2-stark's format, not a per-key one.

`zisk_zorch/constraints/testdata` is registered in the commit-lint exempt paths
alongside the sibling fixture trees, so the commits scope to `constraints`.

## Related Issues/PRs

Refs #115 (plan item 4 — the `<Air>.const` preprocessed-column reader)
Pairs with #116, which raises where this supplies. **Merge #116 first** — the
files are disjoint so neither blocks the other, but the guard should land
before the producer that satisfies it.
Names side of the cross-repo contract: riscv-witness#2336.

## Checklist

- [x] Branch name follows Branch Guideline
- [x] Commit messages follow Commit Message Guideline
- [x] Checked Pull Request Guideline

author: keilor9703
body:
Auditoría completa (frontend + backend) del módulo de parqueaderos con dos agentes; se implementan los hallazgos priorizados.

## Backend (⚠️ requiere deploy)
- **Cobro al dar de baja un vehículo** cobraba siempre por minuto plano, ignorando tarifa plena/mínimos → ahora usa el mismo cálculo que la salida normal (`_calcular_monto_estimado`).
- **"Tarifa mínima"** existía en BD pero no se aplicaba → ahora es un piso de cobro real; la salida por horas usa el helper unificado (se elimina lógica duplicada que ya había divergido).
- **Minuto iniciado = minuto cobrado** (`ceil` en vez de `round`, que regalaba hasta 30 s por salida).
- **Auditoría de descuentos**: monto manual ≠ calculado queda registrado en observaciones.
- **Zona horaria**: cierre FE e historial FE usaban día UTC (desde las 7 p.m. operaban el día siguiente) → ahora America/Bogota.
- **Suscripciones solapadas** para el mismo vehículo se rechazan (antes doble cobro).

## Frontend
- `fecha_entrada` se interpreta **siempre como UTC** en salida/impresión/editor de teléfono (el cobro estimado y la hora impresa salían con 5h de desfase).
- **"Guardar y reenviar" creaba una ENTRADA DUPLICADA** → ahora reenvía el comprobante del acceso existente.
- Diálogo de salida: recalcula cada 30 s, muestra el monto manual en la caja de cobro y aplica tarifa mínima.
- Fechas locales en Cierre FE / historiales (bugs de "día siguiente" tras las 7 p.m. y "día anterior" en fechas cortas).

body:
El proyecto ya está en producción en **https://urbanflowfullstack.duckdns.org** y no había nada escrito sobre cómo está montado.

## Qué entra

**`docs/despliegue.md`** — qué hay en la instancia, cómo actualizarla (`sudo urbanflow-deploy`) y por qué cada decisión:

- swap de 2 GB (el build de Vite no cabe en los 912 MB del `t2.micro`)
- Postgres solo en `127.0.0.1`
- la API corre como usuario `urbanflow`, con el servicio de systemd acotado a la carpeta de documentos
- nftables en la máquina además del Security Group, como segunda capa
- secretos generados en el servidor, no los del `.env.example`
- HTTPS con Let's Encrypt vía DuckDNS, porque Let's Encrypt no emite para `*.amazonaws.com` — sin él no funcionan ni la cámara del escáner QR ni el webhook de pagos

Y los **cuatro fallos que solo se manifiestan en un entorno limpio**, ya corregidos en `main` (PRs #24, #26, #27 y la configuración de nginx): `vexor`/`stripe` sin declarar en `package.json`, el cliente llamando al `localhost` del visitante, la cookie `Secure` atada a `NODE_ENV` en vez de a la conexión real, y el bloque `default_server` de Amazon Linux tapando el nuestro.

**Bruno** — el entorno `Produccion` traía `CAMBIAR-POR-EL-DOMINIO`; ahora apunta al dominio real, así que basta con cambiar de entorno en el selector.

**README** — enlace a producción, entrada de `docs/despliegue.md`, y el recuento del smoke corregido (183, no 167) junto con la suite `errores`, que no estaba listada.

Solo documentación y configuración de Bruno: no toca código de la aplicación.
