author: hychou0515
body:
Two things a chat someone shared with me couldn't tell me, both in the chat-first App rail (`ChatListRail`).

## 1. Who shared it

A shared row rendered its title and nothing else, so *"From a teammate"* read like a chat I'd forgotten writing. The code claimed otherwise —

```
/* Rename / Share / Delete only for chats I own; a shared-with-me chat just
   shows the "shared" tag (the backend would 403 those actions anyway). */
```

— and a `.chat-rail__shared` chip rule shipped in `chat-rail.css`, but **no element ever carried the class**: dead CSS behind a comment that described a feature that was never wired.

Replaced with the fact that actually identifies the row — a quiet second line naming the owner, who *is* the sharer (Share is an owner-only action, so nobody else can put a chat in your rail). Reuses `UserChip` (`nameOnly`) so a raw user id never reaches the UI.

## 2. The tab jumped back to "My chats"

The tab was `useState<"mine" | "shared">("mine")` — plain state in a component that is **destroyed on every navigation**. `AppWorkspaceInner` renders `<Msg>Loading…</Msg>` in place of the entire workspace, rail included, whenever `useAppItem` hasn't answered yet (a plain `useQuery`, no seeding from the already-fetched list — `useResources.ts:57`), which is every first visit to a chat.

So picking a chat out of "Shared with me" dropped you back on "My chats", with the chat you were now reading absent from the list in front of you. A reload did the same.

The tab is now **derived from the chat you're in**, with a click overriding it only while you stay in that chat:

```ts
const [picked, setPicked] = useState<{ chat: string; tab: Tab } | null>(null);
const tab = picked?.chat === currentId ? picked.tab : defaultTab(shared, currentId);
```

Derived state survives the remount *and* a reload with nothing persisted — the same "let the URL/route be the source of truth" fix as the KB-chat remount key. With no chat open (the App home passes `currentId=""`) it stays "My chats".

## Tests

Four added to `ChatListRail.test.tsx`; the two that pin the behaviour above fail on `master`:

- names who shared each chat in the Shared with me tab ← **red before**
- says nothing about sharing on my own chats
- opens on Shared with me when the chat you're in is one shared with you ← **red before**
- still lets you cross to the other tab from a shared chat

## Verification

- `tsc --noEmit` clean
- full FE suite: **338 files / 2708 tests passed**
- `pnpm run build` clean
- **Real Chromium layout check** — `.chat-rail__item` went from a horizontal flex row to a column, which touches *every* rail row, and happy-dom does no layout. Measured at 240px: my own chats stay a single 36.1px line, shared rows grow to 54.2px, the "Shared by" line sits below the title and stays unbolded on the active row, and both a long title and a long sharer name ellipsize with `overflowingRight: []` and no sideways scroll.

> Note: `@marp-team/marp-core` is declared in `web/package.json` but missing from the main checkout's `node_modules` — 37 test files fail to import there until `pnpm install` is re-run. Pre-existing, unrelated to this change.

author: jasadams
body:
Closes KYO-239

## Summary

Doc comments across the `server_fns` layer said `Mirrors <thing> in apps/server/src/routes/<file>.rs`. Fifteen of those route files were deleted wholesale during the React→Leptos migration and the comments were never swept.

The claim isn't merely stale, it's actively misleading. The standing rule is that server fns and REST routes *share* logic rather than duplicate it — so a reader honouring that rule goes looking for the route, doesn't find it, and has to guess whether it moved or died. That guess is where duplication comes back.

All 15 targets were deleted in three commits on 2026-04-22 — `60e6f56c` (#181), `0f9390b5` (#182), `13e957e1` (#183), all KYO-73. Every case was "route deleted, server fn is now the only implementation": no moves, no renames, and no deleted route turned out to still have a live caller.

## Three commits, by area

Per the ticket's instruction not to batch, each was separately reviewed and signed:

| Commit | Area | Refs |
|---|---|---|
| `59a5a847` | watches | 25 |
| `c0b857bc` | auth family (`auth`, `auth_password`, `auth_totp`, `auth_recovery`) | 25 |
| `125bdd23` | everything else (10 route files) | 38 |

## The counts moved since the ticket was written

The ticket says 96 stale references across 16 files. On current `main` it was **88 across 15** — `watches.rs` 25 (was 27), `workspaces.rs` 11 (was 13), `chat.rs` 9 (was 12), most likely KYO-193's server-fn deletions. There are also **40** valid references across **8** live route files, not 31/7: `push.rs` is newer than the ticket. All 40 are untouched.

## Comments were rewritten, not deleted

Where a comment was pure redundancy under a summary that already said the same thing, it's gone. Where it carried behavioural detail phrased as a comparison, the detail survives as a statement about *this* code:

- `disable_totp` deliberately doesn't require re-entering a TOTP code. That was recorded as a note about what the REST handler did; it now says what this function does and why. It was the only written record of the decision.
- `get_thinking_events` notes the deleted route wrapped this data in an envelope object.
- `AlertItem` now states the fact it was reaching for — `execution_trace` is always populated here, unlike on `WatchExecutionItem`.
- `get_websocket_config` pinned its 15 minutes to a deleted file; it now points at `jwt.access_token_expire_minutes`, where the number actually comes from.

Two module docs named live and dead routes in one breath. Only the dead halves were rewritten — `auth.rs` still calls the same service layer as `auth_google_oauth.rs`, `security.rs` still shares with `auth_passkeys.rs`, and both claims were verified true.

## Three follow-ups filed

Two comments were the only record of something worth keeping, so they became tickets rather than vanishing with the reference that carried them:

- **KYO-300** — `SampleDataIndexer::index_sample_data` and helpers (~150 lines) have zero callers. Its only caller was the route deleted in #183; `create_sample_datasource` uses a different generic indexer.
- **KYO-301** — `merge_custom_settings`/`custom_settings_get` are written twice, once per crate. The comment justified that by a route→auth-crate dependency that no longer exists.
- **KYO-302** — 14 comments make the same parity claim in *prose* without the path (`// matches REST handler validation`), so they escape this ticket's audit regex entirely. Zero MISSING does **not** mean the codebase is free of stale parity claims.

## Verification

- Audit command returns **zero MISSING**, with all 40 live references intact
- Comment-only, proven per commit: `git diff --cached -U0 | grep '^[+-]' | grep -v '^[+-][+-]' | grep -vE '^[+-]\s*(///|//!|//|\*|/\*)'` → empty
- `cargo check --workspace --locked` — clean
- `cargo clippy --locked --workspace --exclude kyomi-desktop --all-targets -- -D warnings -A clippy::unwrap_used` — clean

Those two passing is the point rather than a formality: this diff cannot affect behaviour, so a failure would mean something other than a comment got touched.

author: alexander-marquardt
body:
Closes #10.

## The rule that wins, and why

**The taxonomy's `name` field**, via a single function `display_label` in `src/off_demo_extract/taxonomy.py`, now names a category everywhere — both `category_path` segments and the flat `categories` values. The mechanical de-slug that `categories` used is gone; nothing in the package derives a category label any other way.

`name` wins because it is the upstream-authored human label:

* it carries correct hyphenation (`Plant-based foods`) that a de-slug flattens;
* it carries disambiguating parentheticals (`Crackers (Appetizers)`) that a slug cannot express;
* it is **localised**, which the slug can never be — the slug is built from the `en:`-prefixed id.

Verified before committing to it: **all 8,939 `en:`-prefixed nodes in the current taxonomy have an `en` name** (0 gaps), so on the English backbone the slug fallback never fires. It stays as the last resort for localised-only nodes and for `--no-taxonomy` runs, which now pass an empty mapping into the same function rather than calling a separate one.

## Before/after on real data

One pass over the **first 200,000 lines of the public Open Food Facts JSONL export**, computing the old-rule and the new-rule labels on the *same* records, so the two figures are measured identically. 132,340 of those products resolve a chain.

Metric: the share of products where **every self-tagged chain node's label appears verbatim (exact string) in `categories`**.

| labelling rule | products fully agreeing |
|---|---|
| de-slug (current `main`) | 99,387/132,340 = **75.10%** |
| single-sourced `display_label` | 132,337/132,340 = **100.00%** |

Top offenders under the old rule: `Plant-based foods and beverages` (24,174), `Plant-based foods` (20,011), `Plant-based spreads` (1,718), `Canned plant-based foods` (1,487), `Plant-based beverages` (1,486), `Tea-based beverages` (948).

The 3 residual products are **not** a labelling difference — they are `MAX_NUM_CATEGORIES = 20` truncating the tag list so the chain's leaf falls off the end of `categories` (`0036800388352` with 23 tags, `0051933012707` and `0078742086774` with 21). Filed separately as #14.

Full extractor runs over the same prefix, measured on the emitted NDJSON with the issue's own containment check:

| catalog | exact before | normalised before | exact after | normalised after | mismatch that was formatting-only |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `en` (15,340 docs) | 59.1% | 81.3% | **81.5%** | 81.5% | 22.2% → **0.0%** |
| `es` (399 docs) | 0.0% | 0.0% | **75.7%** | 75.7% | 0.0% → **0.0%** |
| `fr` (6,340 docs) | 1.8% | 1.8% | **80.9%** | 80.9% | 0.0% → **0.0%** |

The signature of the fix is that **exact now equals normalised** in every catalog and formatting-only mismatch drops to zero. The residual ~19% gap is structural and expected: since #13 a chain is anchored to a global taxonomy root, so it materialises ancestors the product never tagged (`Beverages and beverages preparations`, `Cereals and their products`), and `categories` legitimately never lists those. That is why the id-scoped table above is the honest measure — plain containment of every chain node has been unachievable since #13 regardless of labelling.

Spanish and French show 0.0%/1.8% before because the two fields disagreed on **language**, not just spelling; no normalisation could ever have closed that.

## Localisation, and what remains for elastic/prism#6280

The taxonomy does carry per-language names, and sourcing from it fixes formatting and language in one change. Coverage over the 8,939 `en:`-prefixed nodes:

| language | nodes with a name | share |
|---|---|---|
| `en` | 8,939 | 100.00% |
| `fr` | 7,690 | 86.03% |
| `es` | 3,096 | 34.63% |

So a French catalog is now largely French and a Spanish one partly Spanish, and — this is the part that matters for #6280 — where a translation is missing, **both fields fall back to English identically**. The tag list and the breadcrumb can no longer contradict each other in any locale.

**What remains for elastic/prism#6280:** roughly 65% of Spanish and 14% of French category labels still render in English, because the upstream taxonomy has no translation for those nodes. That is a data gap in Open Food Facts, not something this repo can resolve; it is not fixable by any labelling rule here. If #6280 needs a fully-localised tag list it needs a translation source beyond the taxonomy, or a decision to accept English fallback. What #6280 no longer has to work around is the *self-contradiction* — the same node appearing under two spellings, or two languages, on one result card.

## The inverse audit

Extended the `AddressAudit` added by #13 rather than adding a parallel mechanism. It already recorded one address per node; it now also records the node's label (taken as the last segment of its cumulative path — `display_label` neutralises the separator inside a label, so that split is exact) and the flat field's `(id, label)` entries, and reports:

* `categories_under_multiple_labels` — a node rendered under two strings. This is issue #10 itself; must be zero.
* `labels_shared_by_multiple_categories` — the inverse: one string claimed by two nodes, which makes the join ambiguous in the other direction.

Both land in the run report next to the existing address counters and warn on the extraction log.

The inverse count **found something real immediately**: the flat field carries the product's tags whatever their language prefix, and upstream holds duplicate nodes under two prefixes that render to one string — `en:capsicum-frutescens` / `fr:capsicum-frutescens`, `en:jugos` / `es:jugos`, `en:chicken-free-range-meat-and-skin-raw` / `fr:poulets-fermiers`. A real English run reports 2, Spanish 1, French 6. Surfaced rather than suppressed, because it bounds how far a label-to-segment join can be trusted. Filed as #15.

## Fail-before evidence

New test `tests/test_category_label_agreement.py`, checked out at the parent commit `70dd55c` in a **separate clone** (`/tmp/wt-ext10-failbefore`) with its **own** virtualenv, with only the new test file and its fixture copied in:

```
$ git -C /tmp/wt-ext10-failbefore log --oneline -1
70dd55c Anchor every category chain to a global taxonomy root (#13)
$ /tmp/venv-ext10-before/bin/python -m pytest tests/test_category_label_agreement.py -v
...
tests/test_category_label_agreement.py::test_labels_agree_in_english FAILED [ 16%]
tests/test_category_label_agreement.py::test_labels_agree_in_spanish FAILED [ 33%]
tests/test_category_label_agreement.py::test_labels_agree_in_french FAILED [ 50%]
tests/test_category_label_agreement.py::test_categories_are_localised_not_english_derived FAILED [ 66%]
tests/test_category_label_agreement.py::test_fixture_still_exercises_the_divergence PASSED [ 83%]
tests/test_category_label_agreement.py::test_run_report_audits_the_label_invariants FAILED [100%]
========================= 5 failed, 1 passed in 0.07s ==========================
```

The English failure, verbatim:

```

   0000260440264: 'Plant-based foods and beverages' not in ['Chutneys', 'Condiments',
   'Culinary plants', 'Fruits and vegetables based foods', 'Onion chutneys', 'Onions and
```

🚨 **Severity**: MEDIUM
💡 **Vulnerability**: The connector framework caught exceptions during argument parsing, parameter decoding, and policy hooks (`classify`, `extendDecision`) and surfaced the raw `err.message` directly in `ErrorEnvelope`s or stdout/stderr. If those exception messages originated from inputs containing sensitive tokens or credentials (e.g., failing Zod schema validations on credential-bearing objects), those credentials would be leaked verbatim.

author: patrickcleeve2
body:
Two threads: a layout rework that makes the widget usable at a sensible width, and a stage-safety bug found while testing it.

Verified in the running application, which matters here — both bugs need the connect-then-move ordering that only the tab has, and neither the standalone app nor any test fixture would have produced it.

## The layout, measured

The widget could not be made narrower than 1030 px, and a long message made it worse. All of that floor was the status row; the canvas asked for **10 px**.

| status text | before | after |
| -- | -- | -- |
| idle | 1030 px | **524** |
| a result | 1279 px | **524** |
| the out-of-bounds rejection | 1728 px | **524** |

Flat now, because nothing in the column reports its text as a minimum.

**FIB-471** — status text, progress bars and the actions stack at the foot of the settings column, the shape `FibsemMinimapWidget` already uses. The bars show only while a run is going.

`progress_slot` is gone, along with `PROGRESS_WIDTH`/`PROGRESS_HEIGHT`. It existed *only* to stop the bars dragging the buttons sideways when `reset()` hid them — with nothing beside them, show/hide came free as a consequence of the move rather than as extra work. The overall bar is shown again on a terminal state, since `FibsemProgressWidget` paints finished and failed differently and that colour is the at-a-glance answer.

The cursor readout moves onto the canvas, in the one free corner — toolbar top right, scalebar bottom right, info bar bottom left. It stays a **Qt label** rather than canvas text chrome because it updates on every motion event, and `set_info_text` costs 4.93 ms against a label's 0.08 ms.

**FIB-470** — `ElidedLabel`. A `QLabel` reports its text width as its size hint and a layout treats that as a minimum. `text()` still returns what was set (the widget compares against it to decide whether the line is its to overwrite) and the tooltip carries the whole message.

The same trap applied one level down: a long failure ran the progress bar out of the window. The bars take the width they are given now, and the bar carries the *fact* while the status line carries the *reason*.

**FIB-469** — the canvas states the pose in its bottom-left info bar: stage position and objective position, each dropped on its own if unavailable. No milling angle — a beam-side quantity that means nothing through the camera; it belongs on the FIB/SEM overview. The stage crosshair stays uncaptioned, since it sits on the data and the info bar can say what it is for free.

## FIB-491 — a click re-posed the stage

Reported from the app: double-clicking at t = -180 sent the stage back to t = 0.

`project_image_point` copies the base position and adjusts only x/y/z, so rotation and tilt come from the frame's origin. The origin is fixed the first time anything is drawn — and the tab is built when a microscope *connects*, so it records whatever pose the stage was in then, normally t = 0. Move to the FM position afterwards and every click resolves through the pose the instrument left behind:

```
origin fixed at    t=   0.0
stage now at       t=-180.0
clicked target     t=   0.0   y=+20.0um
```

**The tilt was the visible half.** The projection's y/z split is computed from the pose too, so `y` came out with the sign inverted — the stage went to the wrong place *and* flipped 180° getting there.

The origin was conflating two things. Canvas zero is a **place** (x, y, z) and stays fixed, which is what lets images accumulate against one frame; rotation and tilt are **how stage space maps onto the canvas at all**, and must follow the instrument.

The second commit fixes a defect in the first. `_frame` was corrected but `_offset_of` — which places acquired images — still measured from the raw origin, so the grid moved to the correct pose and the images did not. Worse than both being wrong together:

```
grid offset  : x= 200.0 um  y= -150.0 um
image offset : x= 200.0 um  y= +150.0 um    <- 300 um apart, mirrored
```

Kept as a separate commit rather than folded in, since the intermediate state is worth being findable if anyone bisects through it.

## Testing

2257 passed, 16 skipped.

The regression test that matters asserts the invariant rather than either half: **an image acquired at a position lands where a grid centred on that position is drawn**. Plus the equivalence that actually proves the pose fix — a widget with a stale origin resolves a click, and places an image, identically to one freshly built at the same pose.

Mutation-checked: the pose fix, the placement fix, the elided label, and the show-the-bars-after-resetting-them ordering each fail their tests when reverted.

## Notes for review

- `FibsemProgressWidget.reset()` hides itself, so a start sequence that shows the bars and *then* resets them leaves them hidden for the whole run. Cost me one round trip; there is a test.
- The two placement paths deliberately differ — an image uses its own recorded geometry, the grid uses the live one — so it is not obvious they must share a base. That is what made the half-fix easy to miss.

author: sergeykuznetsov1995
body:
## Что и зачем

`dag_refresh_fotmob` (@continuous, ротация всех ~496 included-турниров) **ни разу не закрывал круг зелёным**: `complete` требует ноль ошибок во всех ~1600 операциях, а в каждом круге стабильно есть три независимых класса «ошибок», ни один из которых не является несобранной работой. Данные при этом реально льются (последний круг: 6888 запросов, 5364 success, бюджет израсходован на 46%).

Диагностика по 15 ранам `fotmob_refresh__*` (31.07–03.08), разбор 123 ошибок последнего круга:

| класс | шт | что это на самом деле |
|---|---|---|
| `terminal: leagues?id=N: unscoped transport absence (304)` | 5 | **#1070**: мёртвые записи каталога — `allLeagues` рекламирует id (Landesliga Австрия, промо «adidas Predator or F50», квалификации Марокко/Азербайджана/Коста-Рики), а `/leagues` отвечает литеральным `null` |
| `terminal: <team_id>: unscoped transport absence (304/200)` | 96 | тот же null-класс у команд: участники кубков из низших лиг и плейсхолдеры сетки (team id `-1`) без глобальной страницы `/teams`. Счётчик **монотонно растёт** по мере обхода экзотики (17→35→77→107→121→123 ошибок за 6 кругов) |
| `retryable: scope N incomplete; outstanding={'team_snapshots': K}` | 10 | следствие предыдущего: сумма outstanding = числу team-terminal (96 = 95+1, сходится до единицы). НЕ бюджет |
| `transfer pagination incomplete: unique=N source_hits=M` + `transfer stream incomplete` | 6+6 | **#1074**: источник сам врёт в своём счётчике `hits` на 1–2 события — все страницы скачаны и разобраны, дублей ноль |

## Что сделано

1. **#1070, каталог** (`service.discover_competition`): рекламируемая запись с доказанным null-body коммитится `EXCLUDED` (reason `dead_catalog_entry`, error_code `source_dead_catalog_entry`) и считается intentional absence — запись остаётся в каталоге, каждый круг перепроверяет её бесплатно (304-ревалидация кэшированного null).
2. **Мёртвые команды** (`sync_team_snapshots` + вызов в раннере): существующий путь «EXCLUDED без tombstone» (раньше только для исторических сезонов) распространён на latest-сезоны — гарантия та же: last-good снапшот не затирается. Reason-строки обобщены: `advertised_team_unavailable` / `source_team_unavailable` (были `*_historical_*`).
3. **#1074, трансферы** (`sync_transfers` + гейт полноты в раннере): при полностью исчерпанном потоке (страницы кончились, ни одной ошибки страниц) дефицит к `hits` в пределах `TRANSFER_SOURCE_HITS_TOLERANCE = 2` пишется в metadata `source_hits_deficit`, поток считается complete (и `record_competition_completion` фиксирует дефицит в coverage). Дефицит больше допуска или неисчерпанный поток — по-прежнему incomplete.

Fail-closed принцип сохранён: «unscoped» absence остаётся терминальной ошибкой везде, где нет доказательства (404/500/сетевые ошибки, неисчерпанные потоки, не-null тела).

## Тесты

- `tests/unit/scrapers/test_fotmob_service.py`: +3 новых (`dead_catalog_entry` → intentional; допуск дефицита ≤2 на исчерпанном потоке; дефицит >2 остаётся incomplete), 1 переименован/обновлён под новые reason-строки.
- FotMob-набор: 214 scrapers + 133 dags passed. Полный сьют: см. чек-ран CI.

## Деплой

Контур `-p fotmob-airflow` монтирует `/root/dpf-fotmob-930-runtime` — после мержа владелец делает `git -C /root/dpf-fotmob-930-runtime checkout --detach origin/master` (контейнер пересоздавать не нужно, раннер запускается подпроцессом). Приёмка: первый refresh-чанк после прокатки — ноль terminal-absence и ноль transfer-retryable; дневная волна 14:00 зелёная.

## Overview
This PR implements **KS-INT-03: On-Demand Container Image Vulnerability Scanning in MCP Server**.
It introduces a new tool `scan_container_image` to the Kubescape MCP server allowing AI coding and DevOps assistants to run on-demand vulnerability scans against container images directly from the MCP interface.

Features:
- Registers the tool `scan_container_image` in `cmd/mcpserver`.
- Accepts required parameter `image_name` (e.g., `nginx:alpine`) and optional registry credentials `username` and `password`.
- Connects to the underlying `imagescan.Service` to perform live image scanning using Syft and Grype.
- Returns a structured JSON payload containing:
  - `image`: Target image identifier.
  - `matches`: List of detailed vulnerability findings (`models.Match`).
  - `vulnerabilities`: De-duplicated list of distinct vulnerability models (`models.Vulnerability`).
  - `severities`: Aggregated severity counts (`map[string]int`).

## How to Test
1. Compile and build the Kubescape CLI: `make build` or `go build -v .`
2. Start the MCP server: `kubescape mcpserver`
3. Call the `scan_container_image` tool via any connected MCP client with argument `{"image_name": "nginx:alpine"}`.
4. Verify that the structured vulnerability findings, unique CVE list, and severity count mappings are returned in valid JSON format.

## Examples/Screenshots
Sample tool execution response structure:
```json
{
  "image": "nginx:alpine",
  "severities": {
    "High": 2,
```

author: aekdahl
body:
## Why
> My business account should pay for work stuff and store data in their GitHub; my personal should be paid by me.

A workspace had **one** GitHub connection, so every project pushed to / was stored under the same account. Now a project can be **pinned to a specific GitHub account**, so work repos live on (and bill to) the business account and personal ones on your own.

## Design (leaner than a connection-store rework)
Rather than making the GitHub connection store multi-account (a schema migration across memory/file/Postgres I couldn't verify locally), secondary accounts reuse the **multi-credential secret store** you just merged:
- A secondary account = a `github` credential (a fine-grained PAT + label). `CredentialProvider = ProviderId | "github"`; `github` is deliberately **not** a fleet provider (kept out of the runner catalog + provider-availability).
- **`Project.githubCredentialId`** picks the account; `null` → the workspace's default connection — **unchanged, zero migration**.

## Changes
- **Token resolution** (`githubService.projectToken`): a pinned project authenticates clone/push/PR/repo-list with *its* account's PAT; else the default connection. Safety policy still comes from the default connection.
- Orchestrator push + auto-clone pass the project's credential; `GET /api/github/repos?credentialId=` lists that account's repos.
- **UI**: Integrations → "Additional accounts" (add/list/remove PAT accounts); project header → a **GitHub** account picker.

## Verification
- Server + web typecheck clean; suite **515 passing** (also dropped a stale `reorderTask` coverage-allowlist entry — a simulation journey now references it on `main`).
- **Live** (screenshots): added Business + Personal accounts in Integrations; pinned "Work App" to Business; the project-header picker reflects it and the stored project carries `githubCredentialId=cred-github-…`.
- The real push/clone token-swap is wired + typechecked; a full remote push needs a real repo/token to exercise end-to-end.

body:
## Summary

Implements ADR-0164: replaces 36-char UUID session ids and the non-unique
`bg-N` background-job counter with a 15-char `<kind>-<epoch-seconds
hex><2-hex salt><3-hex counter>` scheme — `s-` sessions/agent handles, `j-`
background jobs, `r-` runtime-minted request/correlation ids.

- New `entanglement-core::id_gen` module: `IdKind`, the `IdGen` trait, and
  `DefaultIdGen` (a process-global monotonic `(second, counter)` pair, so a
  process never mints a duplicate id, and waits for the next second rather
  than repeating on the 4096/s counter budget).
- `EngineConfig.id_gen: Arc<dyn IdGen>` — a pluggable seam following the same
  shape as `model_resolver`/`aux_llm_resolver`/`SandboxResolver`
  (ADR-0079/0134/0154). `Holly::next_id(kind)` lets an in-process head mint
  through the engine's *configured* generator.
- `SessionId::new_uuid()` keeps its name for call-site compatibility but now
  mints the `s-` scheme, not an actual UUID; legacy UUID-form ids coexist
  indefinitely since `SessionId` is an opaque `String` newtype.
- `JobRegistry` (`bash`/`bash_output`) now mints `j-` ids through the same
  generator instead of a per-registry `AtomicU64` that restarted at 0 on
  every fresh registry (the non-uniqueness bug ADR-0164 retires).
- Scope is deliberately narrow: a `ToolCall.id` is provider-supplied on the
  wire and is never run through this generator — reformatting it broke
  Gemini (#444).
- Docs updated: `docs/architecture/engine.md` (new `id_gen` seam writeup),
  `docs/architecture/protocol.md`, `docs/architecture/heads-and-persistence.md`.

author: fahadaali
body:
## العطل

شاشة التحليلات تردّ ٥٠٠ عند فتحها وعند «سحب الآن» بعده.

**والسحب نفسه سليم.** `POST /api/metrics/sync` يردّ بنجاح — أعلى استعلام في مساره (`syncAllSources` + `computeAuto`) يرسل ١٣ رابطة. لكن `syncNow` يستدعي `loadMetrics()` بعده مباشرةً (`web/src/pages/Analytics.tsx:113`)، فتقع ٥٠٠ في القراءة وتحلّ رسالتُها محلّ «تم السحب» — فيُقرأ العطل سحباً وهو قراءة.

## السبب

`readLayer` بلا طبقة — وهي ما تقوم عليه `readBoard` واللوحة المختصرة، التبويبة الافتراضية — تسرد مفاتيح المؤشرات كلها:

```sql
WHERE period = ? AND period_start = ? AND metric_key IN (?, ?, … ×١١٦)
```

رابطةٌ لكل مؤشر في الدليل: **١١٨ رابطة**، وD1 يقف عند **١٠٠**. فالمحرّك يردّ خطأً قبل أن تُقرأ قيمة، وHono يردّ ٥٠٠ خاماً، فيعرض `api.ts:68` نصّ `خطأ (500)`.

الطبقة الواحدة تنجو (أكبرها ٢١ مؤشراً)، فبقيّة التبويبات كانت تعمل — وهو ما جعل العطل يبدو خاصّاً باللوحة.

## الإصلاح

الحدُّ على الطبقة صار انضماماً إلى `metric_definitions` لا سرداً للمفاتيح. القيمة تشير إلى تعريفها بمفتاحٍ خارجي أصلاً، فالانضمام يقول الشيء نفسه برابطتين أو ثلاث مهما كبر السجلّ:

```sql
FROM metric_values v JOIN metric_definitions d ON d.key = v.metric_key
WHERE v.period = ? AND v.period_start = ?  -- + AND d.layer = ? عند الطبقة
```

وسجلٌّ يكبر بمؤشرٍ واحد كان يكفي لكسر شاشةٍ تعمل — فالحدّ لم يعد مرتبطاً بعدد المؤشرات إطلاقاً.

## الاختبار

`test/metricsRead.test.ts` جديد: يبني القاعدة من ملفات الهجرة، ويحاكي حدّ D1 في غلافٍ يعدّ الرابطات ويرمي كما يرمي. محرّك SQLite المحلّي يقبل مئات الرابطات، فما يمرّ بلا محاكاة الحدّ يسقط عند النشر وحده — وهو ما وقع.

## ما جرى التحقّق منه

- `npx vitest run` — ١٠٨ اختباراً تمرّ (١٠٣ سابقة + ٥ جديدة)
- `npx tsc --noEmit` نظيف
- الاختبار الجديد يسقط قبل الإصلاح ويمرّ بعده: `2 failed` ← `5 passed`
- بعد الإصلاح: `readBoard → 10 rows`، `readLayer(all) → 116 rows`، `readLayer('reach') → 11 rows`

بنود «تعريف الإنجاز» البصرية (العرض في الاتجاهين والوضعين، ٣٧٥ بكسل، التنقّل بالمفاتيح) لم تُجرَ — التغيير في الخادم وحده، ولم تُمسّ واجهة ولا نصّ ولا أيقونة. ومسح الفرق لا يُظهر قيمة لون خام ولا خاصية اتجاه فيزيائية ولا إيموجي.

## ملاحظة خارج النطاق

`src/services/notify.ts:22` فيه النمط نفسه — `userIds` في `IN (…)`. عددُ الفريق اليوم دون الحدّ، لكنه المصدر ذاته لو كبر. لم يُمسّ.

body:
PR #46465: support wrapping any instruction with stream annotation

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/46465

📝 Summary of Changes
Generalize ExplicitStreamAnnotationAsyncWrapper to wrap any annotated instruction

Previously the pass only asynchronized instructions that were already kCall. This change extends it to handle any opcode by first wrapping non-kCall instructions in a CreateCallInstruction, then creating the async start/done pair as before.

case skipped:
- Skip instructions inside fusion or async computation bodies (wrapping there is illegal and causes HloVerifier failures due to nested async).
- Skip instructions that are already async (kAsyncStart/Update/Done, collective start/done like kAllReduceStart/Done, kAllGatherStart/Done, kCollectivePermuteStart/Done, and kCopyStart/Done) using IsNonFusionCollective from collective_ops_utils.
- Iterate computations in reverse post-order (callers before callees) and skip async computation bodies in the outer loop, so that ClearSchedulingAnnotations applied to a called computation's instructions takes effect before that computation is visited.

Frontend attributes are moved from the original instruction to the call wrapper so they remain only on the async start/done pair, not on inner ops.

author: mikelward
body:
Nu requires a space between a redirection operator and its target. The default `$env.vcs-auto-fetch` closure used `out>/dev/null err>/dev/null`, which nu (verified on 0.113.1) passes to the `vcs` binary as two literal arguments, so every `cd` printed `vcs auto-fetch: unknown flag: out>/dev/null` instead of fetching silently.

## Changes

- `config/nushell/config.nu`: use `out+err> /dev/null` in the default `$env.vcs-auto-fetch` closure, matching the existing spawn-silent form at line 99.
- `config/nushell/config_test.nu`: regression test that runs the default closure against a fake `vcs` on PATH and asserts it receives only the `auto-fetch` subcommand. It fails on the old syntax (the fake logs `auto-fetch out>/dev/null err>/dev/null`) and passes now.

The existing `maybe-background-fetch` tests override `$env.vcs-auto-fetch` with a recorder, so the default closure was never exercised — that's how this slipped through.

## Testing

`make test`: all suites green (407 nu tests, 78 vcs tests, 80 shrc_vcs tests). VCS timing check within budget (10× `vcs detect` in 44ms against a 200ms budget) — no perf change; the fix only corrects redirection syntax on the cd-triggered background fetch.

body:
https://liferay.atlassian.net/browse/LPD-88276

## What Is Being Fixed

The parent story LPD-85552 (Actions - Single Actions) asks for coverage of the single-item actions in the CMS Assets views: creating content from the OOTB structures, creating content from custom structures, editing an entry by clicking its title or through the row Edit action, and deleting an entry through the row Delete action.

An audit of the existing suite found all of those already covered, with one exception. Creating an External Video through the UI was not exercised anywhere. The only existing coverage asserts that External Video appears in the Space Summary creation dropdown and that an API-seeded entry renders a video preview, so no test had ever driven the creation form itself. Basic Document creation is covered end to end in the DXP folder-hierarchy suite, custom structure creation in the content editor suite, and both row actions in the content editor and All section suites.

## How It Is Being Fixed

Adds a single test to the All section suite that creates an External Video from the All section creation menu, fills the Title and Video URL fields, publishes, and then asserts the entry is listed with the External Video type and an Approved status.

Placing the test on the All section rather than on Files also closes a second gap, since no test previously drove an All section creation menu through to a saved entry. The creation menu there was only ever opened to assert that it offers no Folder option.

The final assertion checks that the submitted URL was parsed into the expected video, by switching to Cards view and matching the video id in the thumbnail src. It deliberately asserts the src attribute rather than the visibility of the thumbnail image, because asserting visibility would make the result depend on the remote image loading and would fail on a restricted network even when the product behaved correctly. The iframe preview used by the Files suite is not reachable here, since the All section offers only Cards and Table views while the iframe renders in the Files-only Gallery view.

Because the entry is created through the UI rather than through the API helpers, it is not covered by the automatic data cleanup, so the test deletes it explicitly in a finally block.

## Test Execution

```
cd modules/test/playwright && yarn test tests/site-cms-site-initializer/main/all.spec.ts --project site-cms-site-initializer.main -g "@LPD-88276" --reporter=list
```

author: jasadams
body:
Closes TRA-10013

## The bug

**A user who was never a member of a team got its name, icon and settings pushed into their store the moment anyone renamed it.** That is disclosure, not stale cache. And a user who *left* a team still got it back on the next rename — TRA-9963 closed only the removal trigger.

Bootstrap is membership-scoped (`list_teams(.., Some(user_id))`). Delta was not. Since `SyncStore::upsert_team` **appends when not found**, a workspace-visible TEAM `Update` didn't refresh a team the user had — it *added* one they never had.

Reproduced before any change: six tests failed on unmodified code.

## The fix

`get_entries_since` now requires membership for a TEAM row, putting bootstrap and delta back in agreement. **The tests assert that invariant directly** rather than enumerating the triggers that violated it.

## Deletes are exempt, and that is the whole of the difficulty

Both TEAM deletes are written when the membership row is **already gone**:

- `delete_team` cascades it away → requiring membership leaves a deleted team in every member's cache **forever**, which is worse than the bug being fixed.
- TRA-9963's eviction row is written *after* the member was removed → requiring membership **silently reverts TRA-9963**.

So membership is asked only of rows that *add or refresh* a team. Removing the exemption fails three tests, both traps firing exactly as predicted.

A delete reaching a non-member costs nothing: both writers pass `None`, so the row is a UUID and nothing else, and removing a team the client doesn't hold matches nothing. Review verified both the memory (`retain`) and IndexedDB (`.delete()` on a missing key) paths are genuine no-ops.

## Cost

Measured on a 200k-row `sync_log` with identical result sets, so only predicate evaluation differs. Every delta is at or inside the run-to-run spread.

Structurally, from `EXPLAIN` — review rebuilt a synthetic dataset and confirmed independently:
- **Postgres de-correlates it**: `hashed SubPlan`, the member set hashed **once per query**, not probed per row.
- **SQLite** probes per row but through the composite-PK **covering index** — no table access. No new index needed on either backend.

## The comment that was wrong twice

TRA-9963's eviction row **stays**, contradicting this ticket's own suggestion that it might be redundant. Removing it means the departing member keeps the team.

Its original comment said the row exists because the workspace-visible `Update` would re-add the team. That `Update` no longer reaches the departing user at all, so the claim became false.

**The first replacement was also wrong** — it said the `Update`/`Delete` ordering now decides the rejoin case. Swapping the two rows disproved it: only a row-order assertion failed, no behavioural test, because the rejoin's `Update` is a later transaction with a higher `sync_id` and applies last either way. That claim would have shipped if the mutation hadn't been run.

The comment now says the row survives because **a filter can only withhold rows, never retract what a client already cached** — so it is the only thing that can evict. Review checked every claim in the current text against the code and against the mutation's actual result.

## Scope: TEAM only, deliberately

Surveyed all 20 entity types. TEAM is the only reachable offender; the rest either agree already or are gated by their writers through `SyncAudience`. One latent near-miss (STATUS) is unreachable today because `create_status` has no non-test caller — filed as TRA-10015.

A general per-entity predicate registry would be speculative generality against a survey that found one instance, and would put a dispatch layer on the hot path to serve one row of a table.

## Tests

Row-presence checks cannot distinguish "never delivered" from "delivered then evicted" under this filter — both read as absent. So the tests model a real client (`bootstrapped()` + `catch_up()` per delta) and assert **end state**. `bootstrap_and_delta_agree_through_every_team_writer` also asserts users end holding specific **non-empty** sets, so a filter passing nothing can't satisfy it vacuously.

Four mutations, all reproduced independently by review. A `dual_backend_test!` covers both dialects — **Postgres suite: 13 passed, 0 ignored.**

## Gates

`cargo check`, both clippy gates, `cargo test --workspace` (507 passed), `check-tx-pool.py`, and the Postgres dialect suite — all exit 0.

## Follow-ups filed

- **TRA-10014** — `drain_delta`'s watermark lags under any visibility filter, so a user whose visible rows end below the head re-scans that tail on every delta. Pre-existing; this change adds another way to reach it.
- **TRA-10015** — latent STATUS bootstrap/delta divergence.
- **TRA-10016** — thirteen sync-log call sites pass a bare `None` instead of `SyncAudience`, bypassing the enum whose purpose is making that a deliberate choice.
- **TRA-10017** — `Team.member_count` is always 0 on single-team reads, so a member-list change reaches clients as "something changed".

### Variant B — live-manager path

- Expands manager lockdown to full compound alert plus both office guards deploying, while preserving all-seven-guards-eliminated as a guaranteed trigger.
- The manager locks the wooden door, arms himself, takes cover behind the desk, and begins an approximately ninety-second police-call sequence.
- Player fire may draw non-omniscient return fire through the destructible door; a quiet approach produces the safer stack.
- Tripper uses the Remington 870 / Serbu Super-Shorty breaching shotgun; Smoke readies and throws a stun grenade.
- Alerted entry order is Spook, Tripper, Smoke.
- Spook disarms and tackles the stunned manager, pins him on the floor, and conducts the altered breathless interrogation.
- `SEARCH` retrieves the keys from the manager's left jacket pocket.
- Spook calls `Smoke! Catch!` and tosses the key bundle to Smoke.
- Tripper zip-cuffs the manager to the adjacent desk.
- Alerted exit order is Spook, Smoke, Tripper.
- Police and Coast Guard response states depend on whether the phone call actually completes.

### Variant B — deceased-manager fallback

- Allows the manager to be killed through supported penetrating fire, destructive-door play, blast, fragmentation, explosive entry, or freeform premature entry.
- Manager death does not automatically fail the mission while the body and keys remain recoverable.
- Victor Two Bravo must still enter and clear the office.
- The player receives `SEARCH` on the deceased manager and physically recovers the complete N272BT key bundle from his left jacket pocket.
- No automatic key grant, reward, shortcut bonus, or cleaner objective state is created.
- The live interrogation is lost, and any completed police / Coast Guard response remains active.
- After SEARCH, the fallback uses Variant A's direct doorway handover and line: `You might wanna take these, Smoke.`
- The fallback does not use `Smoke! Catch!` or the Variant B toss.
- Tripper provides room and rear security but performs no restraint animation on a deceased manager.
- The mission then continues toward N272BT under the already-established alert and response state.

### Shared manager-handgun disposition

- In both live variants, Spook maintains positive possession until Tripper completes the restraint, then stashes the handgun securely on his person.
- In the deceased-manager fallback, Spook locates and secures any displaced handgun after the room is safe, then performs the same stow.
- The handgun remains a non-selectable narrative prop.
- It does not replace, unequip, or suppress `NOTHING`, which remains Spook's functional sidearm.
- No pickup banner, ammunition state, second sidearm slot, or later gameplay access is required.
- No loose or duplicate manager-owned handgun remains accessible in the office.

### Operator, aircraft, and key-bundle identity

- Names the fictional Goldberg-linked shell aerial-tour company `Ocean Blue Sky Tours, Ltd.`; `Ocean Blue Sky Tours` is the public-facing shortened form.
- Assigns the fueled north-jetty Found FBA-2C the fictional U.S. registration / tail number `N272BT`.
- Defines one shared tracked key-bundle prop across all paths:
  - up to four differently shaped keys;
  - a compact float-compartment drain / inspection-fitting mini wrench;
  - a scratched metal split ring;
  - a worn, slightly yellowed white writable tag marked `FBA-2C / N272BT`.

### Christiansted visual-reference package

- Records five exact owner-supplied image attachments by filename, dimensions, and SHA-256 hash.
- Uses photographs to guide tropical waterfront context, materials, weathering, vegetation, dock construction, and environmental atmosphere.
- Uses flight-simulator views only as secondary reference for broad spatial readability, aircraft-to-dock scale, and useful compositions.
- Keeps the KML and controlling mission sources authoritative for gameplay geometry, security placement, objective flow, and N272BT identity.
- Locks the owner-identified moored white floatplane image as the principal north-jetty visual reference.
- Extracts art-direction cues for the compact base footprint, green hillside and town backdrop, gray corrugated-metal operations building, exterior stairs, chain-link fencing, repaired apron, hard shoreline, floating docks, gangways, utility boxes, hoses, mooring hardware, and blue-green harbor water.
- Requires the daytime material character to be translated into the mission's after-dark stealth lighting rather than copied literally.
- Prohibits copying real operator branding, liveries, exact security layouts, or the reference aircraft in place of Ocean Blue Sky Tours and the fictional Found FBA-2C.
- Treats the visibly watermarked Shutterstock image and simulator renders as reference only pending rights clearance; final Project Warriors assets must be independently authored.
- Keeps third-party image binaries in a licensed/private production reference library while the repository records exact hashes and production findings.

## Why

The office encounter now supports stealth, alerted live capture, and destructive lethal player expression without softlocking the mission or flattening all outcomes into the same sequence. Live capture remains the intended and most informative route. The lethal fallback preserves continuity and freedom while retaining lost dialogue, room damage, and any earned external-response pressure as consequences.

The visual-reference package gives production a concrete environmental target without allowing stock photography or simulator reconstruction to override mission design. It preserves the compact working-harbor identity, tropical Christiansted context, north-jetty character, and practical waterfront material language while protecting canon hierarchy and third-party rights boundaries.

## Source authority and supersession

- The Variant B source supersedes earlier `Variant B pending` language.
- The deceased-manager fallback controls body SEARCH and the Variant A-style handover whenever the manager dies before live apprehension.
- The manager-handgun final-disposition addendum applies across both live variants and the deceased-manager fallback.
- The Ocean Blue Sky Tours / N272BT addendum controls company, aircraft, and key-bundle identity.
- The Christiansted visual-reference package controls the production findings derived from the five supplied images, while the KML and mission sources retain layout and gameplay authority.

## Validation

- Compared branch against `main`: visual-reference commits added on top of the existing manager-office workstream.
- No existing `main` source is overwritten by the new visual-reference source or audit.
- Cross-checked against the Christiansted geography, seven-contractor count, alarm / radio / CCTV state model, manager-office branches, north-je

author: alexanderz-band
body:
## Summary

Codex thought events (`reasoning`/`plan` items) were posting the literal
strings `(reasoning)` / `(plan)` to the room whenever the underlying item
had an empty summary/text — a real, live symptom on the backends E2E lane,
not just a theoretical edge case.

## Changes

- **Fix (INT-1148):** `_extract_thought_text` now returns `None` when a
  reasoning/plan item carries no informative text, and the caller skips
  emission entirely instead of falling back to a placeholder string.
  `_stringify_tool_output` (the shared "protocol payload -> display text"
  helper) now skips a list with nothing extractable rather than dumping it
  as `"[]"`.
- **Test coverage:** unit tests for dict-shaped reasoning summaries, empty
  reasoning/plan skip, and a `dynamicToolCall` result-list edge case; a new
  backends-lane E2E smoke (`test_codex.py`) drives a live Codex turn with
  `Emit.THOUGHTS` on and asserts the room never sees the placeholder
  strings (and, after review, that at least one thought event actually
  landed — otherwise the placeholder assertion would pass vacuously
  without exercising the fix). The smoke's joke-driving prompt asks for a
  harmless pun (not "a joke that might be badly interpreted") to avoid a
  safety-refusal false failure, while still demanding multi-step reasoning
  to reliably populate a real reasoning summary.
- **Follow-up cleanup surfaced by review:** the `item/completed` `"type"`
  vocabulary (`commandExecution`, `reasoning`, `plan`, etc.) was re-typed as
  bare string literals in ~5 places in `codex.py`. Added `CodexItemType`
  (StrEnum, `integrations/codex/types.py`) as the single source of truth,
  reused everywhere the vocabulary appears (gate sets, dispatchers, approval
  labels) — plus a test asserting the enum is fully and disjointly
  partitioned across the adapter's tool-like/thought-like/skipped-message
  buckets, so a new item type can't silently fall through all three.
  `_extract_tool_item` also returned a bare positional
  `tuple[str, dict, str]` and inlined all 7 item types in one ~95-line
  function; split into `CodexToolItem` (NamedTuple) + one small helper per
  item type. Same treatment for the two Codex approval RPC method strings
  (`CodexApprovalMethod` StrEnum backing `CODEX_APPROVAL_METHODS`, replacing
  6 re-typed literal checks).
- **Regression fix in the cleanup itself (caught by review):** three tool
  extractors (`_extract_mcp_tool_call`, `_extract_web_search`,
  `_extract_collab_agent_tool_call`) were switched to reuse
  `_stringify_tool_output` instead of hand-rolled `json.dumps`/`"completed"`
  logic — but that helper's list handling *skips* a non-text list rather
  than dumping it, so a real result like an MCP image/resource content
  block silently collapsed to the generic `"completed"` status instead of
  reporting the actual data. Added an opt-in `raw_fallback` mode to
  `_stringify_tool_output`: thought extraction and `dynamicToolCall` keep
  the skip behavior (avoids reintroducing placeholder noise), the three
  tool-output extractors now dump the raw list as JSON when it has nothing
  extractable as text. Covered by a new regression test per extractor.
- **Test-file cleanup:** extracted `events_of_type(tools, message_type)` and
  replaced ~30 duplicated inline
  `[e for e in tools.events_sent if e["message_type"] == ...]`
  comprehensions across `test_codex_adapter.py` with it.
- **Docs:** strengthened `AGENTS.md`'s Pre-Commit Checklist with an explicit
  self-review step for single-source-of-truth and intent-oriented-code
  violations — previously only stated as prose elsewhere in the file, never
  re-triggered at the point code actually gets checked before commit.
- **Docs (`.cursor` cleanup):** the branch carried an untracked
  `.cursor/rules/use-env-test.mdc` — a second, competing Cursor-rule
  mechanism alongside this repo's existing `.cursorrules`/`CLAUDE.md`
  symlinks to `AGENTS.md`. Folded its content (prefer `.env.test` over
  ad-hoc/.env/invented credentials, never print secrets) into `AGENTS.md`'s
  Environment Variables section and deleted the file, so the guardrail is
  visible from Claude, Cursor, and anything else reading any of the three
  symlinked names, with one copy instead of two.

A full `codex.py` -> package split (mirroring
`adapters/opencode/{adapter,approvals,config}.py`) was considered and
explicitly deferred as a separate, much larger-blast-radius effort (3200+
lines, 28 dependent files).

## Testing

- [x] `uv run pytest tests/adapters/test_codex_adapter.py -v` (191 passed)
- [x] `uv run pytest tests/ --ignore=tests/integration/ --ignore=tests/e2e/` (4381 passed, 85 skipped)
- [x] `uv run ruff check . && uv run ruff format --check .`
- [x] `uv run pyrefly check`

## Related Issues

Fixes INT-1148

author: codeitlikemiley
body:
Closes the gap flagged on #3. `companion.toml` listed the six crates a consumer names in its own manifest and stopped there, which under-describes what a consumer actually compiles.

## The problem

Four more path-local crates are reachable through those six — `wasi-authz-http`, `wasi-authz-testkit`, `wasi-http-metadata`, `wasi-http-policy-core`. All four must exist in the checkout for a `--locked` build to resolve.

One is not an implementation detail. `crates/leptos-wasi-authz/src/lib.rs:29` reads:

```rust
pub use wasi_http_metadata::{AuthContextV1, AuthStateV1, PrincipalV1, VerifiedAuthContext};
```

So a consumer handles `wasi-http-metadata`'s types by value while never naming the crate they come from. A manifest whose stated purpose is exact pinning of the companion surface was describing less of that surface than it claimed.

## The change

Every `[[crate]]` entry now carries a `direct` flag:

| | Crates |
|---|---|
| `direct = true` | `leptos-wasi-authz`, `wasi-authz-cedar`, `wasi-authz-client`, `wasi-authz-contract`, `wasi-authz-spicedb`, `wasi-http-authn` |
| `direct = false` | `wasi-authz-http`, `wasi-authz-testkit`, `wasi-http-metadata`, `wasi-http-policy-core` |

The distinction is load-bearing: a consumer should still name only the six. The other four are recorded so the closure is described, not so it is depended on.

**Derived, not hardcoded.** The indirect set comes from walking the resolved dependency graph of both workspaces and keeping path-local packages (`source == null`). A new intermediate crate cannot slip in unrecorded — the same property that makes the version fields trustworthy. Hardcoding the four would have reintroduced exactly the drift this manifest exists to prevent.

## Verification

- Generated output parses, contains 10 crates with correct `direct` flags and versions, and regenerates byte-identically (idempotent).
- The re-export claim was checked against source, not assumed.
- `docs/COMPATIBILITY.md` and `docs/CONSUMER_ALIGNMENT.md` §6 both updated to describe the two tiers.

## Note

`schema` stays at `1`. Nothing consumes this file yet — it landed in #3 — so adding a field breaks no reader. If a consumer starts parsing it before this lands, the flag would warrant a bump.

author: nissimmiracles
body:
## Thinking Path

> - Paperclip is the open source app people use to manage AI agents for work
> - The managed CLI runs an instance as a background service. It supervises that service with `paperclipai service` and diagnoses it with `paperclipai doctor`
> - Both surfaces decide "is this instance healthy?" from one HTTP probe against `/api/health`
> - That probe has a 2 second budget, and the readiness wait has a 60 second budget. Both are shorter than the time a healthy instance can take to answer
> - The result is a false negative. The CLI tells the operator that a running, serving instance is down
> - A false negative here is worse than a slow answer. It makes an operator restart or reinstall a service that needs no repair
> - This pull request moves the two budgets into named constants, and raises them to values that the observed response times support
> - The benefit is that `service status`, `service restart` and `doctor` report the true state of an instance that is slow to answer

## Linked Issues or Issue Description

Refs #10739 — the same managed-install session that produced that issue also produced these two false negatives.

**What happened:**
`paperclipai service status --instance <id>` reported `"health": { "ok": false, "error": "The operation was aborted due to timeout" }`. The instance was healthy. A direct `curl` against the same URL returned `{"status":"ok"}` seconds later. `paperclipai service restart` failed with `Paperclip service did not become healthy: fetch failed`. The restart had in fact succeeded. The instance answered about 100 seconds later.

**Expected behavior:**
The CLI reports an instance as healthy when the instance is healthy. The CLI waits for a restart for as long as a restart can legitimately take.

**Steps to reproduce:**

1. Install the managed CLI and onboard an instance with a database of significant size.
2. Run `paperclipai service install --instance <id>`. The first boot applies migrations.
3. Run `paperclipai service status --instance <id>` while the server warms up.
4. The command reports `ok: false`. A `curl` against `/api/health` succeeds.

**Paperclip version/commit:**
`2026.803.0-canary.4`; branch cut from `2c90cf0f2`.

**Deployment mode:**
`local_trusted` / `private`, loopback, embedded PostgreSQL, launchd service on macOS.

## What Changed

- Add `HEALTH_PROBE_TIMEOUT_MS` (10s) and `HEALTH_READY_TIMEOUT_MS` (300s) to `cli/src/utils/health-url.ts`. This is the module both health call sites already import.
- Use `HEALTH_PROBE_TIMEOUT_MS` for the `service` command probe in `cli/src/commands/service.ts`. It replaces the literal `2_000`.
- Use `HEALTH_PROBE_TIMEOUT_MS` for the doctor probe in `cli/src/checks/service-health-check.ts`. It replaces the second literal `2_000`.
- Use `HEALTH_READY_TIMEOUT_MS` as the `waitForHealth` default in `cli/src/commands/service.ts`. It replaces the literal `60_000`.
- Record the measured response times in comments next to each constant. A later reader can then see why the numbers are what they are.
- Add a regression test in `cli/src/__tests__/service-health-check.test.ts`.

The change does not add configuration, and it does not change control flow. Callers that pass an explicit `timeoutMs` keep their value.

## Verification

### Regression test

The new test starts a local HTTP server that answers `/api/health` correctly after 3s, which is what an instance does while it warms up. It then calls `serviceHealthChecks` **without** the injected `probe`, so the real probe and its timeout budget run.

The test fails on the code before this change, with the exact production symptom:

```
FAIL  src/__tests__/service-health-check.test.ts > reports a healthy instance that answers slower than the previous 2s probe budget
AssertionError: expected [ … ] to deep equally contain ObjectContaining{…}
    "message": "The operation was aborted due to timeout"
 Tests  1 failed | 7 passed (8)
```

It passes with this change applied:

```
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  8 passed (8)
```

Reproduce both directions:

```sh
pnpm exec vitest run cli/src/__tests__/service-health-check.test.ts
git stash && pnpm exec vitest run cli/src/__tests__/service-health-check.test.ts && git stash pop
```

### Field measurements

Measured on macOS 15 (Darwin 25.5.0), arm64, Node v22.22.3, against a 148MB instance:

| Observation                        | Old budget | Measured            |
| ---------------------------------- | ---------- | ------------------- |
| Healthy server, still warming up   | 2s probe   | 2.5s–3.1s to answer |
| Supervised restart                 | 60s wait   | ~100s to answer     |
| First boot after a payload upgrade | 60s wait   | ~250s to answer     |

The new values give headroom above each measurement. They stay below the point where an operator would think the command has hung.

### Type checking

```sh
cd cli && ../node_modules/.bin/tsc --noEmit
```

The changed files produce no TypeScript errors.

### Full CLI suite

`pnpm exec vitest run cli/src/__tests__` reports failures on my machine in `company-import-export-e2e`, `doctor`, `install-command` (3), `update-notice` and `worktree`. They reproduce on an unmodified checkout of `origin/master`, and none of them are in a file this pull request touches. The exact set is not stable between runs on this machine, so I treat CI as the authority on suite state rather than my local numbers. Please tell me if any of them are green in CI and red only here — I will investigate that separately.

## Risks

Low risk.

- A genuinely unreachable instance now takes 10s instead of 2s to report as unreachable. This is one probe, in commands an operator runs by hand.
- `service restart` now waits up to 300s before it declares failure. It still returns as soon as the instance answers, so a fast restart stays fast. Only a restart that was already failing waits longer.
- The new test adds about 3s of wall time to the CLI suite.
- No public API, schema, or migration is affected.

## Model Used

Claude Opus 5 (`claude-opus-5`), through Claude Code. Extended thinking was on. The session used tool execution: it read the repository, ran the test suite and the type checker, and measured the health endpoint against a live managed install on the machine described in Verification.

## Checklist

- [x] I have included a thinking path that traces from project context to this change
- [x] I have specified the model used (with version and capability details)
- [x] I have checked ROADMAP.md and confirmed this PR does not duplicate planned core work
- [x] I have searched GitHub for duplicate or related PRs and linked them above
- [x] I have either (a) linked existing issues with `Fixes: #` / `Closes #` / `Refs #` OR (b) described the issue in-PR following the relevant issue template
- [x] I have not referenced internal/instance-local Paperclip issues or links (only public GitHub `#NNN` / `github.com/paperclipai/paperclip` URLs)
- [x] My branch name describes the change (e.g. `docs/...`, `fix/...`) and contains no internal Paperclip ticket id or instance-derived details
- [ ] I have run tests locally and they pass — the files this PR touches pass. The suite has unrelated pre-existing failures on my machine. See Verification.
- [x] I have added or updated tests where applicable
- [x] I have updated relevant documentation to reflect my changes — no documentation states these values
- [x] I have considered and documented any risks above
- [ ] All Paperclip CI gates are green — to confirm after the CI run
- [ ] Greptile is 5/5 with no open P2s, recommendations, or follow-ups — Greptile returned 5/5 with no open items on the first commit; awaiting its pass on the test commit
- [x] I will address all Greptile and reviewer comments before requesting merge

author: s0x90
body:
Swaps the OpenCode integration for [coder/claudecode.nvim](https://github.com/coder/claudecode.nvim), since OpenCode is no longer in use.

## Changes

**Plugin swap** — `nvim/lua/plugins/opencode.lua` (137 lines of imperative config with hand-rolled WezTerm pane management) is replaced by a declarative `claudecode.nvim` spec, matching the direction of #14. It lazy-loads on `cmd`/`keys` rather than `lazy = false`, so no background server starts on a plain `nvim` launch.

**Stale-buffer fix** — added a `:checktime` autocmd in `autocmds.lua`. `autoread` on its own does not poll; it only reloads when something runs `:checktime`. Without this, a buffer went stale as soon as anything wrote the file outside nvim — the Claude Code CLI shelling out to `gofumpt`, `sed`, `git checkout` — and the next `:w` silently overwrote those changes.

Two non-obvious details, both found by testing rather than reading:
- `:checktime` cannot reload a buffer from inside an autocmd callback (textlock). Called directly it fires, passes every guard, and does nothing. It has to be deferred with `vim.schedule`.
- The `pcall` keeps a persistent failure from spamming an error on every `CursorHold`, but latches a single `vim.notify` — this autocmd is the only thing preventing the data loss above, so it must not fail silently.

**Cleanup** — dropped the unused OpenCode theme and its README sections, and documented the Claude Code install method actually in use (`~/.local/bin/claude`).

## Keybindings

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| `<leader>ac` | Toggle Claude split |
| `<C-.>` | Toggle Claude split (needs a terminal that sends CSI-u) |
| `<leader>af` / `<leader>ar` / `<leader>aC` | Focus / resume / continue |
| `<leader>ab` / `<leader>as` | Add buffer / send selection (or add file from nvim-tree) |
| `<leader>aa` / `<leader>ad` / `<leader>aq` | Accept / deny / close all diffs |

`<C-.>` is normal-mode only on purpose — a terminal-mode binding would apply to every terminal buffer and swallow the key before lazygit or NvChad's terminals see it.

## Testing

Verified: config loads with no startup errors; `:ClaudeCode` registered; 4 checktime autocmds active; buffer reload confirmed end-to-end (external write → `CursorHold` → buffer refreshes); failure path notifies exactly once across 5 consecutive failing fires; `<C-.>` absent from terminal mode; `lazy-lock.json` valid JSON.

Not verified — needs a human at a real terminal: the live integration (terminal spawn, WebSocket handshake, selection send, diff accept/deny), and whether WezTerm actually delivers `<C-.>`. `<leader>ac` works regardless.

author: domnic-alagappa
body:
Item 5 of the nurse-station flow: first poller converted, using the board-signal path from #4557.

## Why this one first

`QUEUE_REFRESH_MS = 5_000` drove five queries across `tv-displays.tsx` and `queue-tokens-tab.tsx`. That is roughly **3,600 requests an hour from a single display**, on the surface `DEVICE-CONSTRAINED-RULES.md` is strictest about ("bound the network", TV ≤120 MB). The board learned nothing between polls: a token is called by a person pressing a button, and the server knows the moment it happens.

## What changed

**Server.** `call_queue_entry`, `start_consultation`, `complete_queue_entry` and `mark_no_show` publish a board signal to the department after their transaction commits. All four already `RETURNING *` the queue row, so the department is in hand — no extra query.

**Signal kind.** `opd.queue.changed`, deliberately **not** a `ClinicalEventName`. That enum is the clinical audit taxonomy and a token being called is not a clinical fact. One kind covers every transition rather than four the client would have to map separately.

**Client.** `opd.queue.changed` → `opd-queue`, `queue-tokens`, `queue-state`. Those three refresh together or the screens disagree about who is next; there's a test pinning that.

## What did not change, on purpose

The poll is **not deleted** — it drops to 60s. A socket can drop and its reconnect can miss a frame, and a queue board showing the wrong token is worse than a board costing one request a minute. Event-driven is the update path; the poll is the backstop.

The registered-displays list moves to 5 minutes on its own constant. It changes when an administrator adds a display, not while a clinic runs — it should never have been on the queue cadence.

Net: ~3,600 → ~120 requests per hour per display, and the board now updates on the transition instead of up to 5s later.

## Gate

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo clippy` (opd) | pass, 0 errors |
| `board-signal-invalidations` (new, 3 cases) | pass |
| `opd_chief_complaint_test`, `opd_vitals_event_test` | pass |
| `pnpm typecheck` / `build` (web) | pass |
| `biome check` (touched files) | pass |
| `make check-api` | pass |

## Note

This converts the **web** TV-display views. The Android TV app in `apps/tv/` has its own data layer and still polls — it needs a WebSocket client of its own before it can use this, which is a separate piece of work.

author: irsoctierdt
body:
The `v1.0.0` tag exposed a pre-existing defect on the release workflow's **first real execution**.

## What happened

The archive step ran:

```
tar --exclude=.git --exclude=.venv --exclude=site -czf "EAODS-${GITHUB_REF_NAME}.tar.gz" .
```

`tar` was writing its output file *into the directory it was archiving*. It detected the growing archive inside its own input set and exited 1 with `tar: .: file changed as we read it`. Because the step failed, every subsequent step was skipped — PDF library, SBOM, and the GitHub Release itself. The tag exists; no release was published.

## Fix

Build the archive in `RUNNER_TEMP` and move it back afterwards, so the output is never inside the input set. The `--exclude` list and artifact name are unchanged.

This defect predates the v1.0.0 work — the workflow had never run, since the repository had zero tags and zero releases before today.

author: sourabhbilawadi-source
body:
🎯 **What:** The DOM XSS vulnerability fixed in the `loadAshwagandhaWidget()` function inside `dashboard.html`. The previously vulnerable code directly assigned an HTML template string interpolated with variables fetched directly from `localStorage` (`ashExtract` and `ashDose`) using `innerHTML`.

⚠️ **Risk:** The potential impact if left unfixed would be DOM-based Cross-Site Scripting (XSS). If an attacker could inject malicious content into those `localStorage` entries (e.g. through a different vulnerability, cross-site leak, or physical access), the payload could be executed as script nodes, compromising user data, executing unwanted commands, or altering the application state.

🛡️ **Solution:** The fix replaces the use of `innerHTML` with native, safe DOM API manipulations (`document.createElement`, `textContent`, `appendChild`). By utilizing `textContent`, all user inputs retrieved from storage are explicitly treated as literal strings and not parsed as executable HTML tags, thereby naturally sanitizing the code execution vector while preserving functionality and visual appearance.

author: hhavynn
body:
## Summary

- Adds a recording Supabase query-builder mock (`src/test-utils/supabaseMock.ts`), the missing foundation for **#291**. The existing global mock only knows `select/insert/update/delete/eq/single`, so it throws the moment any repository chains `.order()` — which is why there were no repository tests.
- Adds draft-content leak guards for **#292**, including a structural invariant over the whole `getPublic*` surface rather than case-by-case assertions.
- Adds route-level smoke tests for all 24 public routes for **#294**.
- Fixes a defect that made the repository's only app-level test vacuous.

### ⚠️ Two things to read before reviewing

**1. This branch carries three unrelated `chore:` commits.** The branch name is inherited from the session's designated branch, and I'm not permitted to push elsewhere without approval. The PR therefore also contains `.agent-handoff/` process artifacts and `scripts/audit-image-exif.mjs` from earlier work. **Only these files are part of this change:**

```
src/test-utils/supabaseMock.ts
src/data/repos/events.test.ts
src/data/repos/houseEvents.test.ts
src/routes/publicRoutes.smoke.test.tsx
src/setupTests.ts
```

Say the word and I'll split this into a focused branch containing only those five.

**2. A correction to a claim in commit `266f514`.** That commit's message asserts `/events`, `/leaderboard` and `/gallery` "render a completely empty `<main>`" against an empty database and calls it a degraded-mode defect. **That was wrong.** Those pages already handle empty, error, and Supabase-unavailable states correctly via `ContentUnavailableState` and `DegradedModeBanner`. The real cause was my own assertion sampling the DOM mid-flight while react-query was still resolving and the skeletons — which contain no text — were rendered. Corrected in `10fee9c`. There is no product defect here.

## Type

- [x] test
- [ ] feat
- [ ] fix
- [ ] chore
- [ ] docs
- [ ] refactor
- [ ] ci/build
- [ ] security

## The bug this fixes

Create React App sets `resetMocks: true`, which strips the implementation off every `jest.fn()` before each test — including the `window.matchMedia` mock installed in `src/setupTests.ts`. So `matchMedia` returned `undefined` in every test, `ThemeProvider` threw on `.matches` during render, and the `ErrorBoundary` rendered the error state instead of the app.

`App.test.tsx` renders `<App />` and asserts `expect(document.body).toBeInTheDocument()` — true whether or not anything rendered. **The only app-level test has been passing against a crashed app.** This is a concrete instance of the "test failures may be masked" concern in #290.

Fixed by installing `matchMedia` as a plain function, which `resetMocks` cannot strip. The `ErrorBoundary` stack traces that printed on every test run are now gone.

## Why the mock records queries

Recording the query chain is what makes the draft guard a real assertion instead of a replay of canned data. A mock that only returns rows the test supplied proves nothing about whether drafts are filtered.

For house events the guard is **structural**: six `getPublic*` methods must exclude drafts and `getAdminEvents` deliberately must not. The test discovers `getPublic*` methods by reflection and fails if any omits the filter — and separately fails if a new `getPublic*` method appears without a registered invocation. A future `getPublicFooBar` that forgets the filter cannot pass silently.

## A finding worth keeping

When a page component throws during render, **the outer `ErrorBoundary` never engages.** `Layout` wraps its `Outlet` in its own `<Suspense fallback={<PageLoader />}>`, so nav, `<main>` and footer render normally while the page area sits on "Loading…" indefinitely. Users see an eternal spinner, not an error.

That is why the smoke tests assert the page *settles* rather than merely that no error copy appears — the latter passes on a dead page.

## Tests added

| File | Tests | Guards |
|---|---|---|
| `src/data/repos/events.test.ts` | 10 | draft filtering, opt-in admin escape hatch, sort/pagination, interest counts, empty case, RLS denial → typed `DatabaseError` |
| `src/data/repos/houseEvents.test.ts` | 11 | `getPublic*` structural invariant, admin asymmetry, ordering, RLS denial surfaces rather than failing open |
| `src/routes/publicRoutes.smoke.test.tsx` | 24 | every public route mounts, settles, renders content, stays out of the error boundary |

Error-path tests construct a faithful `PostgrestError`. In `@supabase/supabase-js` 2.50.0 it `extends Error` and carries `code`/`details`, which is exactly what `withErrorHandling` sniffs for before routing to `normalizeSupabaseError`. A plain object would fall through to the generic "Unknown error occurred" branch and would have tested the opposite of what it claimed.

## Verification

- [x] `npm run build` — succeeds
- [x] `npm run lint` — clean
- [x] `CI=true npm test -- --watchAll=false` — **171 passed, 18 suites** (was 147 / 17 before this branch; no pre-existing test disturbed)
- [x] `git diff --check` — clean for all five files in this change. It does report trailing whitespace in two pre-existing `.agent-handoff/*.md` files from the unrelated commits described above.
- [x] Manual QA: not applicable — test-only change, no runtime behaviour modified.

### Mutation testing, both directions

Guards were verified to actually fail, not just to pass:

- Removing `.eq('is_published', true)` from `getPublicEventsForYear` → **fails exactly one test**, the right one, no false cascade.
- Injecting `throw new Error(...)` into the Events page → **fails exactly one test** (`/events`, by timeout), other 23 pass. Removing it returns the suite to 24/24.

An earlier iteration of the smoke suite passed under that second mutation. That negative result is what drove the current assertion design; it is documented in the test file so nobody weakens it back.

## Safety / Scope

- [ ] No unrelated files changed — **see caveat 1 above**
- [x] No secrets committed
- [x] No private/admin data exposed
- [x] No production Supabase mutation — all data is mocked; nothing touches a live project
- [x] RLS/storage/auth changes documented, if applicable — none made. Tests assert existing boundaries; no policy, grant, or auth behaviour is altered.

## Notes

Related to #290: `tsc --noEmit` currently reports 119 errors, **all** in `node_modules/zod` and **zero** in `src/`. TypeScript 4.9.5 cannot parse zod v4's `.d.cts`, and `skipLibCheck` does not suppress parse errors. The typecheck step #290 asks for cannot be added until TypeScript is upgraded.

Follow-up this does not cover: admin and protected route tiers, and per-page content assertions. Both belong in separate suites.

author: daniel-zint
body:
Selected by scanning the 1200 smallest of the 10000 raw Thingi10K meshes; 29 of those have non-manifold edges. These five give the widest coverage per byte, ~38 KB in total:

  file    #V   #F   non-manifold edges  boundary edges  non-manifold vertices
  49883    20   44                   4               0                      0
  91143    74  146                   2               2                      0
  188018  128  448                 224               0                      0
  229953  135  250                  18              32                      2
  314748  293  761                 101               5                      7

49883 is small enough to reason about by hand. 188018 is almost entirely non-manifold. 229953 and 314748 are the only two with pinch vertices, and both also have boundary, so they cover the mixed case.

314748 also carries one pair of identical triangles, so it is not a simplicial complex. That is kept on purpose: it is what pins down that an edge collapse merges only the duplicate faces it creates itself and leaves pre-existing ones alone.

Converted from the original binary STL by welding vertices on exact coordinate equality -- no tolerance, so the non-manifold structure is the file's own and not an artefact of snapping. Triangles with a repeated vertex after welding are dropped, as is any vertex left unreferenced.
