author: gnuzd
body:
## Summary

Adds **API-key authentication** and matches the TS SDK's realtime API to its docs; also renames the codegen CLI.

### 1. API keys (hardened)
- **Hashed storage**: only the SHA-256 digest of a key is persisted (`Lazypock.Settings`). The raw key is shown exactly once at generation, then cannot be recovered.
- **Scoped strictly to `GET /collections`**: an API key authenticates as a distinct identity, **not** a SuperUser struct — so it gets **no rule bypass** anywhere else. It can list collection schemas (the codegen path) but **cannot** `POST/PATCH/DELETE /collections`, read records, or reach superuser-only endpoints (verified 403).
- New endpoints (superuser-gated): `GET/POST/DELETE /api/settings/api-key`. General `GET /settings` masks the hash.
- Studio **Settings → API Keys** page: generate (raw shown once + auto-copy), regenerate, revoke.

### 2. TS SDK realtime (PocketBase-style)
- `collection(name).subscribe(callback, recordId?)` → returns unsubscribe fn; `unsubscribe(recordId?)`.
- Auto-connects the WebSocket on first use **without a token** → supports anonymous/rule-based realtime (honors list rules like PocketBase).
- `RealtimeMessage` / `RealtimeCallback` types.

### 3. Codegen CLI rename
- Primary bin `lazypock` (was `lazypock-gen`, kept as deprecated alias).
- `--api-key` flag + `LAZYPOCK_API_KEY` env (no login round-trip).

## Verification
- Backend `mix test` → **176 passed** (was 171; +5 new API-key tests).
- SDK `npm run build` / `typecheck` / `smoke` → all green.
- Studio `svelte-check` → **0 errors**.
- **Live E2E** (running server): API key → `GET /collections` 200, `POST /collections` 403, `GET /settings` 403, wrong key 403, no auth 403; `npx lazypock --url … --api-key …` generated `lazypock.types.ts` from live schemas ✓

## Notes
- Pending follow-ups (intentionally out of scope): realtime client-level convenience (`client.realtime.subscribe('collection:posts')` auto-connect) if desired; production key rotation/multiple keys.

Closes the open items in `HANDOFF.md`.

body:
# Program-specific roles

Realizes the master architecture prompt's **"roles are program-specific: a user may have different roles in different programs."** Additive — **no schema change, no security-gate change**; the membership-based RLS already scopes data per program. Verified against a live stack.

## What's added

- **`lib/program-context.ts`** — `getMyPrograms()` returns the caller's programs, each with **the role they hold in that program** (from `program_staff`, own rows readable under the existing RLS); founder/executive span all programs. `getActiveProgram()` reads a validated `active_program` cookie (defaults to the first membership).
- **`setActiveProgramAction`** — validates membership before setting the cookie.
- **`ProgramSwitcher`** (reuses the shadcn Dropdown from PR #14) in the dashboard header; the **sidebar role label now reflects the user's role in the ACTIVE program** (falls back to the global role).
- **Program-scoped pages** (ops dashboard, participants, transfers, master-schedule default) now read the **active** program instead of always the first one — switching program changes the data.
- seed: a second program where **pmgr is a Group Supervisor** (Manager in the first) to demonstrate one user with two roles.

## Verification (local stack)

`pmgr` shows **«مدير» (Manager)** in program A; switching to program B flips the sidebar label to **«مشرف مجموعة» (Group Supervisor)** and re-scopes the Participants / ops pages to program B. RLS scoping intact. typecheck / lint / build clean, no console errors.

## Scope note (safe + additive)

Data access was **already** correctly program-scoped by RLS membership (`is_program_staff` / `is_group_staff`), so this change surfaces the per-program **role** and **active-program context** without touching authorization. Capability gates still resolve on the global role — routing them through the active-program role is a clean **follow-up** if you want a user's *permissions* (not just their label) to change per program.

author: sanketsahu
body:
Fixes #77.

## Two gaps, not one

`POST /auth/v1/admin/generate_link` returned 404 — that's the reported bug. But while verifying the reporter's stated use case I found `/verify` only ever read `token`, while supabase-js sends **`token_hash`** for `verifyOtp({ token_hash })` — exactly the shape `generateLink` feeds it. Adding the endpoint alone would have returned a token nothing could redeem, so both are fixed here.

`hashed_token` is the same opaque one-time token the emailed link carries; tinbase stores one-time tokens verbatim rather than hashing them, so there's nothing to un-hash and the two keys mean the same string.

## Response shape

Flat — user fields alongside `action_link`, `email_otp`, `hashed_token`, `redirect_to`, `verification_type` — because supabase-js splits that shape into `{ user, properties }` client-side. A nested body would leave `data.properties` undefined, which is easy to get wrong and only shows up through the real client. The tests go through supabase-js for that reason.

## Shared internals, deliberately

Token minting moved out of `issueToken` into a shared `mintOneTimeToken`, so the mailed link and the returned link can't drift apart on expiry, replacement, or which `token_type` rows get written. Same lesson as #76 — a link `verify` can't redeem is worse than no link.

`redeemTypes()` is likewise now shared by `verifyToken` and `verifyLink`. Side effect: `signup`/`invite` links are redeemable, where before they matched no stored row and always failed. `recovery` stays scoped to `recovery`, so a login token still can't mint a password-reset session — there's a test pinning that.

## Scope

Supported: `signup`, `invite`, `magiclink`, `recovery`. `email_change_current` and `email_change_new` need email-change plumbing this handler doesn't have, so they return **400 with a clear message** rather than a link that would quietly verify as a plain login.

## Verified

- The literal `curl` from the issue now returns **200** with every documented property:
  ```
  HTTP 200
  action_link      : .../auth/v1/verify?token=5fC70...&type=magiclink&redirect_to=...
  hashed_token     : 5fC701IFfToo4LYevfXFEmVRJEdFQbcU
  email_otp        : 180992
  verification_type: magiclink
  ```
- 9 new tests through **supabase-js**, covering the reporter's flow end to end: generateLink → `verifyOtp({ token_hash })` → session; the `email_otp` path; `signup` with password + metadata; `recovery` requiring an existing user; a recovery token being rejected as a login; `action_link` redeeming via `GET /verify` (303 + `access_token`); service_role enforcement; and unsupported-type rejection.
- No email is sent — asserted against the inbox, matching GoTrue.

author: adityapainuli
body:
Sparse file detection in Builder is cfg-gated to Linux, Android, and FreeBSD, so macOS silently falls back to dense copies. The existing implementation already works on macOS unchanged: the non-Linux path probes fpathconf(_PC_MIN_HOLE_SIZE) before using SEEK_HOLE/SEEK_DATA, and APFS supports all three (libc exposes the constants for apple targets).

This PR adds target_os = "macos" to the three cfg gates in src/builder.rs and enables the writing_sparse size assertion on macOS.

I found this while debugging snapshot write amplification in qdrant (qdrant/qdrant#9858). Archiving a 32 MiB hole-backed file with 4 KiB of data via append_path_with_name:

- Linux (ext4): 9,728 byte archive, GNU sparse entry
- macOS (APFS), before: 33,555,968 bytes, dense regular entry
- macOS (APFS), after this change: 34,304 bytes, GNU sparse entry, extracted contents byte-identical

Same code, same file, the gate was the only difference.

Verified on macOS 15 (arm64, APFS): full test suite passes including all 5 sparse tests, and writing_sparse measures 37,888 bytes, the same 4k-block bound as ext4, so the assertion reuses the 37 KiB limit.

author: kiennguyen2403
body:
## What

Adds `GET /v1/models`, `GET /v1/models/{model}` and `POST /v1/chat/completions` (streaming and non-streaming) to the runtime.

## Why

An existing OpenAI client could not talk to a Kapsl runtime without writing a bespoke client first: the only inference route took a tensor packet keyed by a numeric model id. The OpenAI shim that did exist lived in the private enterprise gateway, so the Apache-2.0 runtime was not usable on its own — which reads as "the open part needs the paid part."

## How

A thin translation layer over the existing `ReplicaPool` paths. It inherits the same reader-scope auth, admission, runtime-pressure shedding and cancellation as `/api/models/:id/infer`.

- **Model addressing** — advertised name, `name:version`, or numeric id. Replicas resolve to their primary. An unmatched name lists what is actually loaded rather than a bare "not found".
- **Prompting** — a lone user message reaches the backend untouched, so GGUF models apply the real chat template embedded in the file. Multi-turn is rendered via `ChatPromptTemplate::render_chat`.
- **Streaming** — real per-token deltas, not a finished completion split after the fact. Client disconnect cancels generation.
- **Stream errors** — sent in band as `{"error": ...}`, never as `finish_reason: "stop"`, which would report a backend failure to the client as a successful empty answer.
- **Strictness** — `n > 1` and non-text content parts are rejected rather than silently ignored. Unknown OpenAI fields are accepted and ignored so clients that always send them still work.

## Performance

Additive: 1,499 insertions, 0 deletions. The only pre-existing files touched are `main.rs` (+12, route mounting) and `http/mod.rs` (+2, module declaration). `models/infer.rs` and `models/infer_stream.rs` are untouched, so existing clients cannot regress. The SDK rev bump is a content no-op beyond `render_chat` — `git diff` between the old pin and the intervening merge commit is empty.

Costs paid only by `/v1` callers: OpenAI chunk JSON is ~3–4× the bytes of the native stream event; a one-pass token estimate per request; stop scanning only when `stop` is supplied, bounded to the longest stop string.

## Testing

139 unit and route tests pass (was 126). Clippy clean on the new module.

Verified end to end on an RTX 4090 (CUDA 12.4, Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct Q4_K_M, layers confirmed on CUDA0): coherent generation, correct single-turn embedded template, multi-turn context preserved, 39 incremental stream deltas, stream and non-stream identical at `temperature=0`, stop sequences truncating in both modes, `max_tokens` honoured, 6 concurrent streams clean, no panics. `/v1` and native `/api/models/0/infer` returned identical text for the same prompt.

## Known gaps

Documented in `docs/openai-compatible-api.md` rather than left to be discovered: `usage` counts are estimates, `stop` is enforced at the API layer, multi-turn template family is guessed from the model name, and there is no tool calling, logprobs, embeddings, or `/v1/completions`.

## Notes for the reviewer

- **Merge after** kapsl-sdk#81, which this pins by git rev. If that merges under a new SHA, re-point the 14 rev strings in `kapsl-runtime/Cargo.toml` before merging here.
- **Unrelated pre-existing blocker found while verifying:** on a stock `nvidia/cuda:12.4.1-devel-ubuntu22.04`, `cargo build --features gguf-cuda` fails at link with `undefined symbol: ncclGroupStart` / `ncclAllReduce` from `llama_cpp_sys_2`. libnccl is present; the build script never emits `-lnccl`. `RUSTFLAGS="-C link-arg=-lnccl"` works around it. Not fixed here — it is outside this PR — but it should be fixed in the build script before any public launch, since anyone building the CUDA path from clean hits it.

author: dseif0x
body:
## Summary

Devices that can't do passkeys — Quest browser, TVs — can now join an existing sync account with no copy/paste and no typing on the bad keyboard.

### The flow (TV-activation style, typing happens on the *good* device)

1. On the Quest: Settings → **Link this device** → it shows a short code like `UMSY-BRSZ` plus a 5-letter verification word.
2. On an already-signed-in phone: Settings → "Link a device" → type the code → **Check** shows the same 5-letter word — confirm it matches → **Link device**.
3. The Quest picks it up within ~2 s and is fully signed in: settings arrive, and changes made there sync back like any other device.

### How it stays end-to-end encrypted

- The new device generates an **ephemeral ECDH P-256 key**; the signed-in device encrypts the data key + account name **to that public key** (ECDH → HKDF → AES-GCM). The server relays only ciphertext and never sees the DEK.
- The **fingerprint shown on both devices** is a hash of that public key — a server swapping keys mid-link would produce mismatched words.
- The server mints the linked device its own session when the bundle is claimed (claim is one-shot and sets the session cookie), so the device is a first-class sync participant with no passkey — "Sign out" works; re-joining means re-linking.
- Codes: 8 chars from a confusable-free alphabet (no 0/O/1/I), 10-minute TTL, one-shot, pending-flow cap; lookup + completion require a signed-in session.

### Also
- The sync section now appears on browsers without `PublicKeyCredential` (link-only — the passkey buttons hide), which was previously gating the whole section off on exactly the devices that need linking.
- Sync e2e suite grew a **two-browser-context** scenario (second context has no virtual authenticator, i.e. genuinely passkey-less): code displayed, fingerprints match across contexts, linked context signs in, receives the blob, and a change made there syncs back to the original. 24/24.

body: ## Bug and impact Several PostgREST-reachable gaps let authenticated users escalate tenancy, destroy clinical records, free doctor slots, or skip billing: 1. **Doctor self-management of clinical row** — `doctors_update` used `can_manage_doctor()`, which returns true for the owning clinician. A doctor could `PATCH` `hospital_id` / `profile_id` / `is_active` / specialty / department and self-transfer or rebind identity. 2. **Staff soft-delete frees a doctor slot** — Receptionists/doctors/hospital admins could `PATCH appointments.deleted_at`. The overlap exclusion only covers `deleted_at IS NULL` rows, so the visit vanishes while another patient can book the same window. (PR #7 only closed the patient path.) 3. **Hard-delete of completed consultation notes** — Assigned doctors could `DELETE` from `consultation_notes` after completion, permanently destroying the medical record the completion gate required. 4. **Fee bypass via `in_progress`** — No staff status machine: `pending`/`confirmed` could jump to `in_progress`, skipping check-in fee capture. Terminal statuses could also be rewound. 5. **Cross-hospital demographic writes** — `patients_update` used `can_access_patient()`, whose appointment branch lets Hospital B staff rewrite Hospital A’s master patient PHI. ## Root cause RLS is the security boundary (public anon key), but doctor-row and patient-update policies were broader than every legitimate app write path, and appointment lifecycle had no staff soft-delete / status-transition guards. ## Fix Migration `0030_lock_doctor_row_and_visit_transitions.sql`: - Restrict `doctors_update` to hospital/platform admins; freeze `profile_id`/`hospital_id` for non-super-admin JWT callers - Block appointment soft-delete for non-super-admin - Enforce the operational status machine (matches reception/doctor UI; `in_progress` only from `checked_in`) - Restrict `notes_delete` to super admin - Scope `patients_update` to owner or same-hospital non-deleted charts App defense-in-depth: - Shared `canTransitionAppointmentStatus` helper - `updateAppointmentStatus` / `completeConsultation` compare-and-swap on status ## Validation - Traced against admin `updateDoctor` / `setDoctorActive` / demote soft-delete, reception check-in UI, doctor start/complete UI, and patient profile self-update to confirm legitimate flows still satisfy the new gates - Confirmed distinct from open audit PRs #4–#7 (note/prediction ownership, soft-deleted doctor identity retention, patient/visit party rebinding, patient soft-delete + attachment destruction) - TypeScript check passed (`tsc --noEmit`) ## Not in this PR Open fixes still awaiting review: #4, #5, #6, #7.

author: korjavin
body:
Closes rc-4ou.1.

`internal/prog` is the data model for the visual programming language of design §10: what a rule is, how it serializes, and how it is validated against a blueprint. **Model and validator only** — evaluation is E3.2. Three new files plus a test, no dependencies, no changes anywhere else in the tree.

## What shipped

- **`program.go`** — `Program` (ordered `[]Rule`) / `Rule` (`When Condition` + `Then []Action`) / `Condition` (a `pred | and | or` tree with explicit grouping, §10.2 EBNF). `Encode`, `Decode`, and the shared structural check.
- **`catalogue.go`** — every predicate of §10.3 and every action of §10.4 as **data rows**, in the same style E1.1 used for the component catalogue. Adding a predicate is adding a row, not a switch case. `Language()` returns the whole thing ready to `json.Marshal` to the editor, so E6.1 renders its dropdowns from the server instead of keeping a copy that drifts.
- **`validate.go`** — `Validate(p Program, b sim.Blueprint) Result`, with `Errors` and `Warnings` in **separate slices** and `Result.OK()` gating the save.

Component awareness reads `sim.Blueprint.Has(kind)` and `sim.MemPoints`; there is no parallel hardcoded list of what has a radar.

## JSON schema (the contract for E3.2 / E6.1 / E6.2 / E6.3)

Versioned with `"v"` from day one. `Decode` accepts `v: 1` or an omitted `v`; anything else is a clean error.

```json
{
  "v": 1,
  "name": "component scavenger",
  "rules": [
    {
      "when": {"op": "and", "of": [
        {"op": "pred", "pred": "at_own_base"},
        {"op": "pred", "pred": "carrying_component"}
      ]},
      "then": [{"do": "deposit_component_at_base"}]
    },
    {
      "when": {"op": "pred", "pred": "health_below", "arg": 25},
      "then": [{"do": "move_to_own_base"}]
    }
  ]
}
```

- `when` node: `{"op":"pred","pred":<id>,"arg":<int>}` or `{"op":"and"|"or","of":[<node>,...]}`. Grouping is nesting; there is no precedence to get wrong.
- `then` entry: `{"do":<id>,"arg":<int>}`. `arg` is omitted when zero.
- `arg` is a **point index 1..3** (`sim.MemPoints`) or a **percent 0..100**, per the action's/predicate's `arg` kind in the catalogue. Actions that take no argument reject a non-zero `arg`.
- Signals are not a parameter: the four §10.3/§10.4 rows expand to the identifiers `received_come_here`, `received_avoid_here`, `broadcast_come_here`, `broadcast_avoid_here`. Keeps `arg` a plain int instead of an int-or-string union; adding a signal in E5 is adding two rows.

Catalogue wire format (`Language()`), abridged:

```json
{
  "v": 1,
  "predicates": [{"id": "carrying_component", "group": "self", "label": "Carrying a component", "arg": "none"}],
  "actions": [
    {"id": "move_forward", "group": "movement", "label": "Move forward", "arg": "none", "primary": true},
    {"id": "move_to_radar_target", "group": "navigation", "label": "Move to radar target", "arg": "none", "primary": true, "needs": ["radar"]},
    {"id": "save_visible_target", "group": "memory", "label": "Save visible target", "arg": "point", "primary": false}
  ]
}
```

`needs` serializes `sim.ComponentKind` **by name**, so the editor never sees sim's enum values.

## The locked action model

`primary` is the mechanism, not decoration. Exactly the 5 memory rows and 2 broadcast rows are `primary: false`; everything else is `primary: true`. A test asserts that count and that no non-memory/non-communication action is a side effect.

`Rule`'s doc comment settles execution order so E3.2 has nothing left to decide: **when a rule matches, every action in `Then` runs in slice order, and the primary action — wherever it sits in the slice — ends the tick.** A rule with only side effects runs them and evaluation continues down the list (design §10.8 rule 1 is exactly that shape). `Action.Primary()` is the accessor E3.2 wants.

## Errors vs warnings

Errors block the save:

| code | when |
|---|---|
| `unknown_predicate` / `unknown_action` / `unknown_op` | identifier not in the catalogue |
| `bad_argument` | point outside 1..3, percent outside 0..100, arg on an argless identifier |
| `empty_group`, `no_action` | malformed structure |
| `too_many_rules`, `too_many_actions`, `too_deep`, `too_large` | input caps |
| `multiple_primary` | more than one primary action in a rule |
| `missing_component` | the blueprint lacks the hardware the action needs — radar action without a radar, `pick_up_component` without a manipulator (§10.10) |

Warnings never block the save (there is an explicit test for that):

| code | when |
|---|---|
| `dead_predicate` | a predicate whose sensor the blueprint lacks — legal, just permanently false |
| `forward_only` | `move_forward` is the only movement/navigation action; the robot cannot turn |
| `unreachable_rule` | an earlier rule strictly dominates this one |
| `empty_program` | no rules; the robot idles |

The missing-component split is deliberate: an **action** you cannot perform is an error, a **predicate** you cannot satisfy is a warning. `has_weapon` declares no `needs` at all — false on an unarmed blueprint is the answer, not a mistake.

`unreachable_rule` is sound but deliberately incomplete: it recognises conjunction containment only (rule 5 = `A AND B` under rule 2 = `A`), which is what editors actually produce, and skips any tree containing an `OR` rather than guessing. Full implication is SAT and not worth it here.

## Safe failure on untrusted input (§10.5)

`Decode` never panics. Rejected cleanly: truncated JSON, bare `null`, wrong types, `[1,2,3]`, `{"when":null}`, `{"rules":[null]}`, unknown identifiers, unknown ops, negative and out-of-range args, empty groups, future schema versions, 200k-deep nesting, over-wide groups, oversized programs. Caps: 256 rules, 8 actions/rule, condition depth 16, 256 condition nodes/rule. The depth and node budget also stop `Validate`'s own tree walks from recursing without bound.

`Validate` deliberately continues past structural errors instead of bailing, so the editor can show everything at once; every catalogue lookup is guarded.

## Verification

```
$ gofmt -l .                      # (no output)
$ go vet ./...                    # clean
$ go build ./...                  # clean
$ go test ./... -count=2 -race
ok  github.com/korjavin/robocolony/cmd/server      1.026s
ok  github.com/korjavin/robocolony/internal/config 1.017s
ok  github.com/korjavin/robocolony/internal/prog   1.101s
ok  github.com/korjavin/robocolony/internal/sim    1.402s
?   github.com/korjavin/robocolony/web  [no test files]
```

Plus a 25s `FuzzDecode` run — 1,066,943 execs, 39 interesting inputs, zero crashes. Everything that decodes is also validated and re-encoded inside the fuzz target. The corpus is not committed; the seeds are the three worked programs.

Bead acceptance: the §10.7 scavenger, §10.8 scout and §10.9 defensive responder are encoded as fixtures, round-trip byte-identically, and validate **clean** (zero errors, zero warnings) against a plausible blueprint for each.

## Codex review — triaged

Two passes. All three findings were read at the source before acting.

1. **Accepted.** A side-effect-only rule was treated as a dominator by `unreachable_rule`. Real bug: under the locked model such a rule does not end the tick, so it pre-empts nothing — and §10.8 rule 1 is precisely that shape, so the design's own example would have thrown a false warning. Fixed; `warnDominated` now only considers rules with a primary action, and there is a test for it.
2. **Accepted.** Condition size was bounded by depth but not by width — one flat `and` with a million children passed. Added `MaxCondNodes` (256/rule) as a shared budget threaded through the structural walk, with a test at and over the limit.
3. **Partially accepted.** "Reject a side effect listed after a primary action as ambiguous." The ambiguity was real; rejecting it was not the right fix — it is a legal authoring order and an error there would be a bad editor experience. Resolved by *defining* the semantics in `Rul

author: m-szymanska
body:
## What

`MarkdownEditorSurface.init` registered its `.NSUndoManagerWillUndoChange` observer with `object: textView.undoManager`. At `init` the surface has no window yet, so `MarkdownTextView.undoManager` answers with its private `fallbackUndoManager` — not the window's manager the responder chain resolves to once the editor is hosted. The observer was pinned to a manager the user never undoes through, so `editorWillUndo` never fired on a real editor: every ⌘Z rewound the document while the AI session kept its opaque continuation, and the next completion was written as a continuation of text the user had just taken back.

The `textDidChange` / `isUndoing` path does **not** cover this — the new window-hosted pin fails on both paths without the fix.

## How

The observer drops the `object:` filter; the existing identity guard in `editorWillUndo` is the whole discrimination. It re-reads the *current* manager per notification, so a surface moving between windows is followed for free — no re-registration on `viewDidMoveToWindow`, and therefore no new teardown path across the detach/close seams the storage scrub guard (#29) already has to track. Removal stays where it was, in `deinit`'s `removeObserver(self)`.

## Pins (red → green)

Both fail on the pre-fix code, verified by reverting the source change and re-running:

- `testUndoInAHostingWindowInvalidatesOpaqueContinuation` — surface hosted in a window, type + ⌘Z; asserts the bytes were actually restored (so it cannot pass vacuously) and that the continuation is `.none`.
- `testUndoOnTheHostingWindowManagerReachesTheEditorHook` — the routing itself, no text edit in play; keeps the pin honest if a future text-change path starts invalidating on its own and would otherwise mask a dead observer.

The pre-existing `testNativeUndoRestoresExactBytesAndInvalidatesOpaqueContinuation` is the false green this bug hid behind: windowless, so both sides of the guard are the fallback manager. It stays green.

## Scope

Only the observer. No change to autocomplete logic, to the #29 undo scrubbing, or to close lifecycle.

## Gates

`make gates` green locally (test + test-scripts + lint + semgrep), and again on the pre-push hook.

author: programmerplus1998
body:
### Motivation and Context

The `mcp` dependency is pinned to `mcp>=1.26.0,<2.0`, which blocks the MCP Python SDK 2.x line. 2.0 introduced several breaking changes that the connector relies on, so the integration and its tests need to be updated before the pin can be loosened.

Fixes #14246

This takes the "upgrade to 2.x" approach (require the 2.x SDK) rather than trying to support both 1.x and 2.x at once.

### Description

Updates the MCP connector (`python/semantic_kernel/connectors/mcp.py`) to the 2.0 API and bumps the pin to `mcp>=2.0.0,<3.0` (both the main dependency and the `mcp` extra). `uv.lock` regenerated.

Server side (`create_mcp_server_from_kernel` / `create_mcp_server_from_functions`):
- The lowlevel `@server.list_tools()` / `call_tool()` / `get_prompt()` / `list_prompts()` / `set_logging_level()` decorators were removed. Handlers are now passed to the `Server(...)` constructor (`on_list_tools`, `on_call_tool`, `on_list_prompts`, `on_get_prompt`, `on_set_logging_level`), receive a `(ServerRequestContext, params)` pair, and return result models (`ListToolsResult`, `CallToolResult`, `GetPromptResult`, `EmptyResult`).
- The per-request session used to emit log messages now comes from the handler's `ServerRequestContext` (the removed `server.request_context` no longer exists).

Client side (`MCP*Plugin`):
- `streamablehttp_client` → `streamable_http_client`; it now yields a 2-tuple and no longer accepts `headers`/`timeout`/`sse_read_timeout`, so `MCPStreamableHttpPlugin` builds an `httpx2` client via `create_mcp_http_client` when those are set.
- `ClientSession(read_timeout_seconds=...)` now takes float seconds instead of a `timedelta`.
- Sampling callback context: `mcp.shared.context.RequestContext` → `mcp.client.session.ClientRequestContext`.
- `message_handler` now receives `ServerNotification | Exception` (no more `RequestResponder`); list-changed notifications are matched via `.method` directly.
- Session re-init check uses `session.initialize_result` instead of the removed `_request_id`.
- `McpError` → `MCPError` (raised with `code=`/`message=`).
- camelCase model fields → snake_case throughout: `input_schema`, `mime_type`, `tool_use_id`, `model_preferences`, `max_tokens`, `system_prompt`.

Removed in 2.0:
- The websocket transport (`mcp.client.websocket`) no longer exists, so `MCPWebsocketPlugin.get_mcp_client()` now raises a clear `KernelPluginInvalidConfigurationError` at connect time instead of failing at import. (Happy to drop the class entirely if preferred.)

Tests / assets:
- `tests/assets/test_plugins/TestMCPPlugin/mcp_server.py`: `FastMCP` → `MCPServer`.
- `tests/unit/connectors/mcp/test_mcp.py`: updated fixtures/mocks for the 2.0 shapes (`input_schema`, `streamable_http_client` 2-tuple, `initialize_result`), rewrote the server-handler assertions to the new `get_request_handler(method)` API, and replaced the websocket test with one asserting the removal error.

### Contribution Checklist

- [x] The code builds clean without any errors or warnings (`ruff check` + `ruff format` clean, `mypy` clean on the connector)
- [x] The PR follows the [SK Contribution Guidelines](https://github.com/microsoft/semantic-kernel/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) and the [pre-submission formatting script](https://github.com/microsoft/semantic-kernel/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#development-scripts) raises no violations
- [x] All unit tests pass, and I have added new tests where possible — 23 passed (unit), 1 passed (integration, real stdio MCP server) under `mcp` 2.0.0
- [x] I didn't break anyone :smile:

author: rohan-unbeg
body:
## Overview

1. This PR fixes part of #24933.
2. This PR does the following:
   - Adds a new `EntityTypeSelectorComponent` dropdown in `core/templates/pages/contributor-dashboard-page/entity-type-selector/` for choosing the target content type (All, Exploration, Skill) on the Contributor Dashboard.
   - Renames the selector label to **"Content Type"** and aligns the Topic, Content Type, and Language dropdowns in a single horizontal row on desktop, and hides it on the question lists and the accomplishments pages, which cannot be filtered by content type.
   - Plumbs the `target_type` parameter throughout the suggestion and opportunity frontend/backend services (`contribution-and-review.service.ts`, `translate-text.service.ts`, `contribution-opportunities.service.ts`, `opportunity_services.py`, `suggestion_services.py`).
   - Makes "All" mean every entity type on the suggestion list handlers. `/getreviewablesuggestions` and `/getsubmittedsuggestions` accept `all` as their `target_type`, and `suggestion.py` renders each suggestion using its own target type, so one response can carry several entity types. Asking for `all` with a question suggestion type is rejected, since a question always targets a skill.
   - Adds `ContributionAndReviewService.reviewTranslationSuggestion`, which picks the review endpoint from the suggestion's own target type, so neither `TranslationSuggestionReviewModalComponent` nor `ContributionsAndReviewComponent` branches on entity type.
   - Renames the single-entity request parameter from `exploration_id` to `entity_id`, the suggestion response key from `exploration_content_html` to `entity_content_html`, and `explorationId` to `entityId` through the frontend fetch chain, since all three now carry any translatable entity.
   - Renames `_build_exp_id_to_translation_suggestion_in_review_count` and the fetchers beneath it to entity-neutral names. The query only ever matched on `target_id`, so it always supported any entity type.
   - Takes an opened opportunity's entity type from the opportunity itself rather than from the dashboard filter, since the "All" filter lists several entity types side by side.
   - Fixes skill opportunity entity-type resolution and in-review suggestion counts so skill translation suggestions submit and track cleanly without backend errors.
   - Fixes an empty `topic_name` on `/getreviewableopportunitieshandlerv2` filtering out every opportunity that belongs to a topic. It now means "all topics", as the dashboard intends.
   - Fixes the review modal showing "undefined / undefined" for a skill translation suggestion, and a contributor's own accepted skill suggestion being labelled as deleted content.
   - Corrects the declared type of `skill_difficulty` on the skill review request from `string` to `number`. Every caller already passed a number and the backend expects a float, so the request itself is unchanged.
   - Spells out a skill's content types in the translation modal, so a contributor sees "skill description" rather than `skill_description`.

author: jefry16
body:
`/` gains a locale dimension and a lock. No new content, no new context, no migration.

The two land together because **the ordering between them is the load-bearing part**: the gate runs *before* locale resolution. Build either alone and that is a comment; build both and it is a test (`aLockedStoreRedirectsEvenForALocaleItDoesNotPublish`). Resolve locale first and a locked store 404s `/es` while redirecting `/fr`, which tells an anonymous visitor the store exists and which locales it publishes, from in front of the gate.

## Three things worth a reviewer's attention

**The spec was wrong about `javax.crypto`, and running it is what showed that.** It placed the unlock-cookie HMAC in `application/policy` as "pure JDK … which keeps it inside the application layer's allowlist". It does not — the allowlist is `com.vointika..` + `java..`, and `javax` is not a subpackage of `java`, so `application_depends_only_on_our_code_and_the_jdk` failed with four violations. The codebase's own answer applied unchanged (PATTERNS §8d): `UnlockTokenPort` + `HmacUnlockToken`. **No ArchUnit rule added, no exemption granted**, which was the slice's acceptance condition.

**`StorefrontPasswordController` was not an available name.** `touroperator` already owns one (the admin API that *sets* the password), and two classes with one simple name are one bean name — `ConflictingBeanDefinitionException` at startup, not a warning. All 21 storefront tests passed; only `VointikaApplicationTests.contextLoads` caught it. Renamed to `PasswordPageController` rather than given an explicit bean name: the collision was the signal that one of the two names described the wrong thing.

**One deliberate deviation from the spec.** It specified `GetHomePageUseCase(tourOperatorId, locale)`, which requires something upstream to have loaded the gate row and resolved the locale — either the controller calling the query port directly (against the precedent that use case's own javadoc sets) or a second use case whose only job is to feed the first. `execute(handle, pathLocale)` keeps gate → locale → content in one use case, leaves `LocaleResolver` a separately-tested pure function, and adds no class. The two-method port split the spec designed is unchanged.

Two additions the spec did not name but its own surface requires: `GetPasswordPageUseCase` (the page needs the shop name, which is on `StorefrontShopView`, not `StorefrontGateView`) and `StorefrontRateLimitRoutesTest` (found by the sweep — every other `RateLimitRuleRegistrar` has one).

## Verification

Suite **847 → 893**, clean `rm -rf target && ./mvnw -o test`, from Maven's own output. `ArchitectureTest` green at 8 rules, unchanged.

Mutation checks, one at a time:

| Mutation | Result |
|---|---|
| Remove the `HEAD` entries | `servesHeadAsWellAsGet` red in **both** controller tests — 401 |
| Move the gate after locale resolution | `aLockedStoreRedirectsEvenForALocaleItDoesNotPublish` red — **404 where 302 is required**, the leak itself |
| `MessageDigest.isEqual` → `String.equals` | **nothing red; suite stays green** |

That third answer is not a missing test but an untestable property — constant-time comparison has no observable behaviour, so unlike the `X-Storefront-Secret` header (same shape of finding, pinned to its literal) there is nothing to assert. The guard rests on the comment beside it and on review. Flagging rather than burying it.

Runtime, against the seeded `acme` over real Postgres (primary `es`, supported `{en,es,fr}`, one `es` translation row — read from the database, not assumed), with `curl -I` beside every `curl`:

- `/` renders the **translated** `es` title, `/en` the canonical one, `/fr` falls back to canonical with `lang="fr"` — nullable-wins-canonical, live. `/es` and `/de` 404. HEAD matches GET on all six routes.
- Gate on: **all five paths answer the same 302**, including the two that 404 unlocked.
- Wrong password re-renders at 200 with no `Set-Cookie`; the right one sets `storefront_unlock=…; Path=/; HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax` with no `Max-Age` and 302s to `/`. The cookie gets back in; a one-character edit does not.
- **Rotating the password through the admin API killed the outstanding cookie** — the property the derivation was chosen for, run rather than reasoned.
- `POST /password` 429s on the 21st attempt in an hour. `/api/**` on a locked storefront host is untouched by the interceptor (401/200, never 302).

**What I could not verify.** Docker was not run (I don't run it here) — the app was started on the host against the compose services instead, which still exercised Flyway and `ddl-auto: validate` against the live database, but the container image is unchanged and unbuilt. And `password_enabled` with a **null** password (trap 7) is not reachable through the admin API, which preserves the password across a disable; it is unit-covered in three places instead.

**One dev-data wrinkle to know about.** Enabling the gate for the runtime checks left `acme.storefront_password = 'hunter3'` where the seed had `NULL` — the admin API keeps the password on disable, so I could not revert that column through it. The gate is off and `password_message` is back to `NULL`, so nothing behaves differently; but if the gate is later enabled with no password typed, it will unlock with `hunter3` rather than being locked-with-no-way-in. Reset with:

```
docker compose exec -T db psql -U vointika -d vointika -c \
  "UPDATE touroperator.tour_operators SET storefront_password = NULL WHERE handle = 'acme';"
```

## Sweep

No `TODO`, no stub, no commented-out block, no orphan. Every new class has a caller or is an SPI `@Component`. The old `StorefrontShopQuery.findByHandle` has no remaining reference. The sweep's one find is the missing rate-limit test, now added.

Landed: `MAP.md` (storefront row, ledger, decision 6, the now-closed throttle debt, carried decisions), `PATTERNS.md` (§1 `application/policy`, §8d `javax`, §11 two new gotchas), `CLAUDE.md`. `STACK.md` untouched — no version-specific trap was hit. The spec file is deleted; it was SCRATCH.

author: julienmartel
body:
Perch has four install routes and, until now, no way to mention a new release. This ports trill's `UpdateCheck` (itself a port of pounce's `UpdateNudge`) — hourly poll of the latest GitHub tag, CalVer ordering, per-version dismissal, cohort detection off the rice's `perch.installed-from` marker and brew's Caskroom — and stops before the install.

**It stops there because perch is sandboxed.** `/Applications` is outside the container and a spawned `brew` inherits the same sandbox, so trill's self-swap would fail with nothing left running to report it. Every cohort gets advice instead:

| installed by | the button does |
| --- | --- |
| the nebelhaus rice | copies `haus update` |
| Homebrew | copies `brew upgrade --cask perch` |
| a Nix store path | copies `nix flake update perch` |
| dragging the release ZIP | opens the release page |

On a rice machine that is *identical* to trill's behaviour — its rice cohort copies a command too.

## Surfaces

Both passive, per the ask: a quiet strip along the bottom of the expanded shelf, and a row in the menu bar menu (plus a `Check for Updates…` item, since an accessory app has no ⌘-menu). No notification banner — perch asks for no permission it can avoid. The strip yields to a drag in progress and to the error banner; `✕` dismisses that version and no other.


## What this costs

One entitlement: `com.apple.security.network.client`, for one hourly unauthenticated GET to `api.github.com` carrying nothing but an IP and a user-agent. A Settings toggle stops it; DEBUG builds never run it. Documented at the declaration, in `docs/reference.md`, and in the README's permissions bullet — the "no telemetry" claim stays true but is no longer the whole story.

## Verified

`xcodebuild … test` green (13 new tests), plus a **signed, sandboxed** Debug build run with a back-dated `MARKETING_VERSION`:
- the fetch works through the sandbox (found `2026.08.01`),
- `/Library/Application Support/nebelhaus/perch.installed-from` and the Caskroom check are both readable from inside the container — the rice-theme-drop fallback in `detect()` is belt-and-braces for the day that changes,
- the strip lays out inside the 280pt panel both with tiles and on an empty shelf.

`isDevVersion` gained a rule trill doesn't need: anything not shaped like CalVer counts as a dev build. The project's placeholder `MARKETING_VERSION` (`0.1.0`) would otherwise sort below every release and nudge every debug build forever.

Docs: ADR 0003, ARCHITECTURE "Knowing there is a new release", `docs/reference.md` § Updating, PRD requirement + acceptance check 9.

author: tenphi
body:
**Do not merge as-is** — `@tenphi/tasty` points at a snapshot build. This exists to exercise the Tasty v3 release against a real design system before it ships, and to show what the migration actually costs.

Upstream: [tenphi/tasty#227](https://github.com/tenphi/tasty/pull/227) · [tenphi/eslint-plugin-tasty#38](https://github.com/tenphi/eslint-plugin-tasty/pull/38)

## Result

| | main | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| Tests | 1139 pass | **1139 pass** |
| Type errors | 13 | **13** (byte-identical, all pre-existing and unrelated to Tasty) |
| oxlint | clean | clean |

No style values needed changing. v3's stricter directional syntax — a group naming directions takes one value, so `padding: '2x 4x top right'` becomes `padding: '2x top, 4x right'` — **is not violated anywhere in this codebase.** I verified that by running the v3 ESLint plugin over `src/`, not by grepping.

## Migration

**`getCssTextForNode` → `getCSSTextForNode`** — test helpers and the ESLint-plugin probe. Mechanical.

**`Props` is no longer exported by Tasty.** It was never a Tasty concept, just `Record<string, any>`. Worth flagging: the UI Kit **re-exported it publicly**, so this would have been a breaking change for our consumers. It is now declared in `src/props.ts` and still exported from the package root, leaving our own API unchanged. 16 files repointed.

**`Text` declares its own `block` prop.** It was inherited from Tasty's `BaseProps`, which v3 dropped as an unconsumed prop — but the UI Kit *does* consume it, as a mod and in the `'ellipsis | block'` style branch. Declaring it locally preserves the behavior.

**`Title` declares its own `inline` prop, deprecated.** Same origin, but here the prop was genuinely dead: `TitleElement` has no `inline` mod and hardcodes `display: 'block'`, so forwarding it did nothing except risk an invalid DOM attribute. Kept on the type so the public prop surface is unchanged; no longer forwarded.

## Two things worth knowing

**The ESLint plugin stays on `^0.11.2`.** Its v3 canary cannot be published: npm trusted publishing for `@tenphi/eslint-plugin-tasty` rejects the snapshot workflow's OIDC token with a 404 on the final PUT, after the build and provenance signing succeed. Adding `environment: release` to match `release.yml` did not fix it, so the allowed-workflow list on the npm package needs updating. Once that lands, this PR needs one line changed.

The old plugin does not flag v3 code (it validates the v2 at-rule spellings, and v3's kebab-case keys fall through an unconditional accept), so lint is clean either way — it just isn't validating anything v3-specific yet.

**This PR found a regression in the v3 ESLint plugin.** An earlier version of `valid-directional-modifier` reported 20 errors here, every one a false positive: `verticalAlign: 'bottom'`, `textAlign: 'left'`, `transformOrigin: 'top center'`, `transition: 'left 0.2s, top 0.2s'`. Direction words are ordinary CSS *values* for a long tail of properties, so the rule's property gate turned out to be load-bearing. Fixed upstream, with all 20 cases added as regression tests. That is the payoff for testing on a real project rather than a fixture.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Minor semver API change for `Text`/`Title` props plus a major styling dependency bump and intentional bundle size increase; behavior is covered by new display tests but consumers must update usages.
> 
> **Overview**
> Upgrades **`@tenphi/tasty`** to v3 and **`@tenphi/eslint-plugin-tasty`** to v1, with the mechanical renames (`getCSSTextForNode`) and a local **`Props`** type in `src/props.ts` so the package still re-exports it after Tasty dropped it.
> 
> **Breaking API cleanup:** removes **`block`** on `Text` and **`inline`** on `Title` in favor of **`display`**; `Text` ellipsis still forces block display. Docs and **`display-prop.test.tsx`** cover the migration.
> 
> Registers **12 color tokens** in `tasty.config.ts` (were only in augment types), fixes Storybook **`inset`** to v3 comma syntax (`'2x bottom, 4x left'`), and **raises size-limit budgets** (~462 kB full / ~123 kB tree-shake) for Tasty v3’s larger bundle.
>

author: shiaho777
body:
## Summary

Follow-up fix to #440. The previous PR used `AiModel.contextLength` as the max_tokens ceiling, but that field **defaults to 4096** for custom models — which is *lower* than the old 32k hard cap, making truncation worse for reasoning models.

## Fix

1. Use `SavedModel.effectiveContextLength` instead of `AiModel.contextLength` — this respects the user's per-model context-length override in AI Settings.
2. When the configured context length is the 4096 default (likely unconfigured for custom models), fall back to **65536** instead of capping output at 4k tokens.

| Scenario | Before (#440) | After |
|---|---|---|
| Custom model, contextLength=4096 (unconfigured) | max_tokens=4096 ❌ worse than original | max_tokens=65536 ✅ |
| Model with user-set contextLength=128000 | max_tokens=4096 ❌ (wrong field) | max_tokens=128000 ✅ |
| Registry-known model with maxOutput | capped at contextLength | capped at effectiveContextLength ✅ |

## Test plan
- [x] `:app:compileDebugKotlin` green
- [ ] Manual: long reasoning turn with a custom model completes fully instead of truncating mid-sentence.

Fixes #429

Bočný panel sa dá zbaliť do úzkej lišty, v ktorej z každého modulu ostane len jeho ikona.

- Každá položka menu má vlastnú ikonu (`nav.ts`, povinné pole — nová záložka nemôže vzniknúť bez nej a v lište ostať neviditeľná).
- Prepínač nad menu; v zbalenom stave sa hlavičky priečinkov nevykresľujú vôbec a názov záložky sa ukáže bublinou pri prejdení myšou (`title` + `aria-label`, takže tlačidlo nikdy nie je bezmenné).
- Klikací cieľ v lište má 44 px — prepína sa rovnako ľahko ako v rozbalenom paneli.
- Voľba sa pamätá v `localStorage` (obe strany v `try`, zakázané úložisko appku nezhodí).
- Obsah vpravo sa roztiahne sám — `.main` je `flex: 1`, mení sa výhradne šírka panela.
- Priečinok zbalený pred zbalením panela nesmie v lište schovať svoje ikony (inak by k nim nebolo ako sa dostať) — pokryté testom.

Testy: 5 nových vitest testov v `Sidebar.test.tsx` (skrytie názvov, stav automatizácie v bubline, prepnutie záložky v lište, zapamätanie po obnovení, zbalený priečinok) + rozšírený e2e v `nav.spec.ts`, ktorý meria skutočné šírky panela aj obsahu pred a po zbalení a overuje stav po `reload()`. E2E je zámerne súčasťou existujúceho testu, nie nový súbor — každé ďalšie prihlásenie ide na zdieľaný `MAX_ATTEMPTS=10` rozpočet.

Ticket 190 sa zavrie ručne až po nasadení a živom overení.

author: kjfsm
body:
#113 で入れた **リグレッションの修正**です。マージ後のリリースワークフローが失敗しています。

## 何が起きたか

```
🦋  error Found changeset afraid-goats-share for package musescore-linter-plugin
        which is not in the workspace
```

#113 の S2 で `pnpm-workspace.yaml` からルート `"."` を外しました。しかし changesets は **ワークスペースのメンバーからしかパッケージを解決できません**。プラグイン本体のバージョンはルートの `package.json` が持ち、changeset もすべてルートを対象にしているため、`changeset version` が落ちます。

既存の 10 個の changeset すべてが該当するので、**リリース経路が完全に止まっていました**。

## なぜルートを外したのか、どう直したか

外した目的は turbo のタスク二重化の解消でした。ルートがメンバーだと、`build` のようにパッケージ側にも同名タスクがある場合に `//#build` と `musescore-linter-plugin#build` の両方が作られて同じスクリプトを 2 回実行し、さらに `musescore-linter-plugin#typecheck` が `turbo run` を再帰的に呼びます。

これは**ルートを外さなくても、ルートのスクリプト名がパッケージ側のタスク名と衝突しないようにすれば解決します**。

- ルートを workspace に戻す
- ルートの `build`（QML バンドル）を **`build:plugin`** に改名 — `apps/web` の `build` との名前衝突が二重化の原因でした
- ルートの `typecheck` を `tsc --noEmit`（ルート自身の `src/` と `scripts/`）にして通常の `typecheck` タスクに参加させる。`//#typecheck:root` は不要になったので削除
- `turbo.json` のルートタスク（`//#test` / `//#build` / `//#build:cli` / `//#package`）を通常のパッケージタスクに移動。いずれもルートだけが持つスクリプト名なので衝突しません

最後の点は、リポジトリ同梱の turborepo skill が「ルートタスクは本当にパッケージに置けないものだけに使う」としているのにも沿う形になりました。

## 検証

- `pnpm exec changeset status` がルートパッケージを minor として認識する（以前はここで落ちていた）
- `changeset version` はローカルでは `GITHUB_TOKEN` が無く changelog 生成で止まりますが、**パッケージ解決は通過**します
- turbo のタスク一覧に重複も再帰も無い（13 タスク、すべて実コマンドを持つ）
- クリーン状態の `pnpm pipeline` が 13 タスク成功し、`dist/bundle.js` / `dist-cli` / `apps/web/dist` / ZIP をすべて生成
- テスト 419 件・lint・knip・coverage（lines 96.07%）はいずれも変化なし

## 注意

`pnpm typecheck` はルート自身の `src/` と `scripts/` だけを見るようになりました。全体を確かめるコマンドは `pnpm pipeline` です（CI はこちらを使っています）。`.claude/rules/testing.md` にも記載しました。

author: d2fong
body:
Closes #639

`?installApp=` is now the single, repeatable install intent for both app kinds, and both prompt the user before anything is added.

## Why

Two parameters carried four asymmetries beyond the name:

| | `?installApp=` (React) | `?addserviceapp=` (service) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Multiplicity | `get()` — one value | `getAll()` — repeatable |
| User consent | none — installed silently | confirmation dialog |
| Validation | zod schema | none — raw cast |
| Origin gate | `appInstallAllowedOrigins` | none |
| Fetch deadline | 10s | none |

One parameter cannot keep them, so consolidating meant reconciling each one.

## Decisions

1. **Both kinds prompt.** This is the behavior change to `?installApp=`, which installed silently.
2. **React apps keep the origin allow-list, on top of the dialog.** A React app loads a remote `remoteEntry.js` as code in Cytoscape Web's own origin, so consent is not sufficient as the only gate. Checked before the prompt, so the user is never asked about an install that cannot happen. Service apps stay open to any origin — the dialog is their gate. (Open question 2 in the issue: the gate stays type-dependent.)
3. **Optional `type` field** in the React manifest, wired to the previously unused `AppType` enum. Optional with a structural fallback, because making it required would break every manifest already published on `apps-stage.cytoscape.org`. (Open question 1: it ships now so the App Store can emit it on its own timeline.)
4. **`?addserviceapp=` is removed**, not deprecated — it has no users.

## Classification

`classifyInstallPayload` (`src/features/AppManager/install/classifyInstallPayload.ts`), pure and framework-free like the rest of that directory:

```
1. Array                            → parseSingleEntryManifest    → client
2. Object, type === 'service'       → ServiceMetadataSchema       → service
3. Object, type === 'client'        → parseSingleEntryManifest    → client
4. Object, looksLikeServiceMetadata                               → service
5. Object, parseSingleEntryManifest([data]) succeeds              → client
6. otherwise                        → undefined, error toast
```

Rule 1 makes today's `?installApp=` behavior a strict subset of the new behavior. Rules 2–5 exist because the React example in #639 is a bare object with a stray trailing `]`, so the App Store may serve either shape — which is what makes the `type` field load-bearing for the single-object case.

## Validation

New `ServiceMetadataSchema` (`src/models/AppModel/serviceMetadataSchema.ts`) replaces the raw cast in `serviceFetcher`, so an unvalidated payload is no longer reachable from a link that looks like an app install.

Two exports with different jobs:

- `ServiceMetadataSchema` — validity, gates registration. Deliberately lenient: `.passthrough()` because the service-app spec ships with the paper and gains fields independently of this repo; `author`/`citation` accept `null` because endpoints send it; `parameters` defaults to `[]` because `updateServiceParameter` calls `.parameters.find(...)`.
- `looksLikeServiceMetadata` — discrimination, strictly narrower (schema *plus* a service marker).

Keeping them separate matters. The fixtures in `AppStore.spec.ts` register service apps with nothing but `{ name, parameters }`; folding the marker check into the validity schema breaks four passing tests and would reject real apps on `refreshAllServices`. A marker is how you tell the two payload shapes apart, not what makes metadata valid.

## Changed

**New**

| File | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `src/models/AppModel/serviceMetadataSchema.ts` | `ServiceMetadataSchema`, `parseServiceMetadata`, `looksLikeServiceMetadata` |
| `src/models/AppModel/PendingAppInstall.ts` | Discriminated union the `INTENTS` phase returns |
| `src/features/AppManager/install/classifyInstallPayload.ts` | The classification rule above |
| `src/features/AppManager/AppInstallConfirmationDialog.tsx` | The dialog |

**Modified**

- `src/boot/steps/runInstallIntents.ts` — the main rewrite. `getAll('installApp')`, fetch each under the 10s `AbortSignal.timeout` (service URLs now have a deadline; they had none), classify, origin pre-check for React apps, dedupe. Per-URL error isolation: one dead host does not lose the others. Installs nothing.
- `src/boot/steps/appShellBootContext.ts` — swaps `installApp`, now unused, for `appInstallAllowedOrigins`, which a plain async step cannot read from React context.
- `src/features/AppShell.tsx` — holds `PendingAppInstall[]`, renders the dialog, installs on confirm via `installApp` or `addService` with per-item toasts.
- `src/data/hooks/stores/AppStore.ts` — `serviceFetcher` validates. The Layout-menu action check is unchanged.
- `parseManifest.ts` / `AppCatalogEntry.ts` / `AppType.ts` / `AppModel/index.ts` — the optional `type` field and the `AppType` type alias + export.

**Removed**

`serviceAppUrlsToAdd` and its tests. It went dead once the pipeline deduped across both kinds; `normalizeServiceAppUrl` stays.

**Docs**

`ROUTING_SPECIFICATION.md`, `boot.md`, `bootPhases.ts`, plus `workspace-app-install-design.md` §7.2 (payload table, revised sequence diagram) and a new §9.1 explaining why service apps are gated differently.

## The dialog

Captured from the running app with both payloads passed in one URL:

```
┌─ Install into this workspace? ──────────────────────────┐
│ This link wants to add the following to Cytoscape Web:  │
│                                                         │
│ MCODE Web  (App)   v0.1.0 — Bader Lab, U. of Toronto    │
│ Finds densely connected regions of a network.           │
│ http://localhost:8899/manifest.json                     │
│                                                         │
│ Update tables example  (Service)   v0.9.0               │
│ Adds a new column, named 'test_col' by default, to …    │
│ http://localhost:8899/service.json                      │
│                                                         │
│ Only install apps from sources you trust.               │
│                            [CANCEL]  [INSTALL]          │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

Confirm is all-or-nothing. Cancel installs nothing and stays silent, as before. The dialog appears after `ROUTE` has stripped the params; the workspace-hydration precondition (§8.3) still holds because `PUBLISH` runs before `INTENTS`.

## Verification

**Unit** — 25 new tests across `classifyInstallPayload.test.ts` (one case per rule, driven by both real payloads from the issue), `serviceMetadataSchema.test.ts`, `AppInstallConfirmationDialog.spec.tsx`, and the `install intents` block in `runAppShellBoot.test.ts` (each kind, repeated mixed, disallowed origin, already-registered service, malformed payload).

`AppStore.spec.ts` passes **unmodified** — that is the guard on schema leniency.

`npm run lint` clean.

Full suite: 3332/3338. Five failures — `openDatabasePhase`, `SnackbarMessageList`, `TableColumnForm`, and two Vizmapper StyleManager specs — all pass in isolation, and the failing set changed between runs (3, then 5, 2 shared). Pre-existing flakes from the 1s global test timeout under worker contention; none in app-install code.

**Manual**, driven with Playwright against a local manifest and service endpoint:

```
CONFIRM toast lines: [ 'Added Update tables example' ]
CONFIRM persisted: {"serviceApps":["Update tables example"],"installedApps":["mcodeweb:active"]}
DISALLOWED dialog shown: false
DISALLOWED error toast: true
DISALLOWED app still booted: true
```

One dialog listed both apps; confirming registered the service app and installed + activated the React app; params were stripped before the dialog appeared. A manifest pointing at `https://evil.example.com/remoteEntry.js` produced an error toast and no dialog.

**Caveat:** any endpoint serving `?installApp=` must send `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` — my test server needed it before the fetch worked. This was already true, since `?inst

author: eugenelim
body:
## Summary

- Adds `repair-plan` and `repair-apply` subcommands to `workspace-status`, completing the five-command progressive CLI surface
- `repair-plan` runs exhaustive Type 2 reconciliation, builds a deterministic SHA-256-keyed plan, writes it to `.workspace-repair-plan.json` (and stdout)
- `repair-apply` verifies the fingerprint, re-reads each spec's status from disk, and writes atomically via `tempfile.mkstemp` with comment-preserving tomlkit
- Approved lifecycle invariant preserved — Approved entries are never automatically touched
- Pack version: `core 2.0.1` (patch — new skill subcommands, no breaking changes)
- agentbundle version: `0.27.3` (scaffold sync for `packs/AGENTS.md` tomlkit dependency record)

## Security hardening (24 Codex review rounds to convergence)

This diff was driven to convergence through 24 rounds of `codex review -c model="gpt-5.6-sol" --base main`. Key hardening themes:

- **TOCTOU** — fingerprint captured pre-`analyze()`; workspace path re-resolved under lock; both empty-ops and write branches re-verify confinement inside the lock
- **Path confinement** — `samefile()` for workspace.toml identity check (case-insensitive FS); `is_symlink()` guard on repair-plan write path before resolution (prevents clobber of in-root symlink targets); resolved path returned from confinement helper for all subsequent I/O
- **Parser parity** — `_parse_spec_status(text)` shared helper; both `extract_spec_status` and `extract_spec_status_with_fingerprint` are thin I/O wrappers; preamble boundary (stop at first `##`), code fence tracking (CommonMark: indentation + type + length), multi-line HTML comment state (including close+open on same line and fully-closed second comment in remainder)
- **Lock correctness** — `O_CREAT|O_EXCL` fail-closed (AC36); PID written for diagnostics; `OSError` from `O_EXCL` caught separately from `FileExistsError`; lock guards all branches including empty-ops
- **I/O error coverage** — every `read_bytes()`, `read_text()`, and `replace()` call wrapped to emit structured JSON; `written_bytes` returned from `_apply_operations` (no post-write re-read for digest)

## Spec + plan alignment

- `spec.md` Status: `Implementing` (two-step closeout: mark `Shipped` in follow-on after agentbundle 0.27.3 PyPI publication)
- `plan.md` Status: `Done`
- Deferred: `workspace.toml` work.active update (same follow-on PR)

## Test coverage

- 96 CLI tests (68 workspace-status + 28 others)
- New tests: `test_repair_plan_plan_file_is_symlink`, `test_repair_plan_stdout_emitted_on_plan_file_write_failure`, `test_repair_plan_plan_file_confinement` (updated), 12 pytest wrappers for `case_compute_repair_plan_*` functions
- `packages/agentbundle/tests/` suite (2983 tests): all passing

## Bundled fixes

- Scaffold sync: `_data/catalogue-scaffold/packs/AGENTS.md` synced to source after tomlkit dependency record added
- Changelog ordering corrected for `[core][2.0.1]` and `[agentbundle][0.27.3]` entries

## Follow-on

- Mark `spec.md Status: Shipped` + move spec from `workspace.toml [work].active` to `[work].shipped` after agentbundle 0.27.3 is confirmed published to PyPI

author: tetsuh
body:
## Summary

- accept ADR-0005 for five Sitometron-owned public Phase 0A capability ports;
- define the complete immutable logical JobJournal request and three-result logical commit boundary;
- define non-throwing postcommit Application and Session ownership handoffs plus throwable precommit Clock and identity generation;
- keep effect mapping, apply, ingress, responses, ACKs, timers, callback leases, and shutdown in Issue #12; and
- register the capability-port contract as Normative while its implementation and three deterministic fake-support checks remain Planned.

## Scope and maturity

This is a documentation-only Accepted ADR change for Issue #26.

- ADR-0005: `Accepted`
- `Core lifecycle capability ports`: `Normative | Planned`
- C++ implementation and named CTests: Planned for Issue #11
- complete logical-envelope orchestration: remains Issue #12-owned
- physical Journal durability: remains Phase 0B

The owner accepted ADR-0005 at reviewed head `04e42ec180353790708cc3a74f70ef5109d1fdaa` in [the acceptance record](https://github.com/tetsuh/sitometron/pull/27#issuecomment-5172327903). Commit `b6221d40f70579c5752212ec8ba82450106c1cd1` publishes the synchronized Accepted/Normative maturity without claiming implementation.

No Requirement ID, production header, C++ implementation, schema, dependency, standard-header authorization, CMake target, or link target is added by this PR.

## Design boundaries

ADR-0005 defines exactly these capability ports:

1. `ClockPort`
2. `JobJournalPort`
3. `ApplicationRunnerPort`
4. `SessionRetainerPort`
5. `IdentitySourcePort`

It explicitly excludes Timer, EffectExecutor, response, ACK, scheduler, callback, queue, thread, and generic service-locator/context APIs.

## Validation

- `git diff --check`
- `cmake -DSITOMETRON_SOURCE_DIR="$PWD" -P cmake/check_core_job_contract.cmake`
  - 209 event pairs
  - 22 command pairs
  - 324 reachable case vectors

body:
## Summary

Gives `mini_objects::Payload::Encrypted` its first real construction, closing roadmap #34 (Phase 4.6, "Storage privacy: cold storage, owner-only storage, encryption"). Every reader in the workspace has had a match arm for `Payload::Encrypted` since the object model's inception, but no crate ever constructed one with real ciphertext until this PR.

- **`mini-store::owner_seal`** (new module): `OwnerSealingKey`/`OwnerSealingPublicKey` + `seal_for_owner`/`open_as_owner`, implementing the NaCl/libsodium sealed-box pattern entirely from already-reviewed `mini-crypto` primitives (X25519 agreement, HKDF-SHA256, ChaCha20-Poly1305). The sealing keypair is deliberately independent of a device's Ed25519 KEL key rather than derived from it — full reasoning in the design doc.
- **`CacheTier::ColdArchive`** (wire tag 5): a sixth cache tier for content the owner wants retained indefinitely without treating it as "actively in use." Never advertised (same ceiling as `PrivateOnly`, preserving the frozen 2026-07-07 founder rule verbatim), set only explicitly via `Store::set_cache_tier`, never touched by `Store::note_view`.
- `mini-store` gains `mini-crypto` as a real dependency (was dev-only before).

See `docs/design/cold-storage-and-owner-only-encryption.md` and D-0434 in `docs/DECISION_LOG.md` for the full design, including honest limits (not KEL-bound/no recovery path, not a network transport, confidentiality only — not integrity/signature-bound, no eviction/pruning consumer yet).

## Does this touch a frozen domain?

- [x] This PR does **not** touch a Tier-F frozen invariant.

The frozen `CacheTier::PrivateOnly`-ceiling rule (2026-07-07) is preserved verbatim; `ColdArchive` sits at or below it, never above. No voice/value wall edge is introduced (P1, Directive 16).

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo fmt --all`
- [x] `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`
- [x] `cargo test --all --all-features` (two pre-existing, unrelated `mini-build-runner-wasmtime`/`mini-cli` timing tests flaked under full-workspace parallel load — both confirmed passing in isolation; neither crate is touched by this PR)
- [x] `Cargo.lock` unaffected (no new external dependency; `mini-crypto` was already a workspace member/dev-dependency)
- [x] New/changed behavior has a test that fails without the change: 11 new adversarial tests in `crates/mini-store/tests/owner_seal.rs` (round trip, wrong-key rejection, tampered ciphertext/AAD/ephemeral-key each fail closed, truncated/oversized bounds, ciphertext uniqueness, empty-plaintext, seed determinism) + 2 new tests in `crates/mini-store/tests/cache.rs` for `ColdArchive`

## Reviewer checklist (2-approval floor, D-0033)

- [ ] I reviewed this as a maintainer, not just skimmed the diff
- [x] No balance, stake, or payment appears anywhere in a vote/quorum/access rule
- [x] No new path lets any single key or party unmask a user, force an update, or act as an owner/admin
- [x] For any judgment call not covered by a spec or invariant: it holds up against `docs/FOUNDER_DIRECTIVES.md` (Directive 14, "simplicity is security" — cited explicitly in the design doc for why the sealing keypair is independent rather than derived from the existing Ed25519 KEL key via a second cryptographic transform)

author: shin1ohno
body:
## Summary

`bin/lint-cookbooks` に WARN tier を導入し、ファイルをまたぐ整合チェックを 3 本追加しました。

これまで linter の結論は「ビルドを落とす」の一択だったので、実在するが現状のヒットが既知・許容されている drift クラスは置き場所がありませんでした。全 PR をブロックするか、書かれないままかのどちらかです。findings を `violations`（exit 1）と `warnings`（独立ブロック、exit code に影響しない）に分割し、昇格は 2 つの配列間の 1 行移動で済むようにしました。既存 8 チェックの出力形式と exit code の挙動は変えていません。

追加した 3 本はいずれも複数ファイルにまたがる drift が対象で、既存の単一ファイルチェックでは原理的に見えなかったものです。

- **9 [FAIL] FLEET ↔ edge-agent config**: host-profile の `fleet` テーブルと `cookbooks/edge-agent/files/config-<label>.toml` を双方向で照合。config を持たない fleet label はそのホストが agent config なしで converge し、誰も解決しない label の config は死んでいるのに coverage に見えます。EXEMPT は `sh1-cloud`（linux.rb で guard 済み）と `es-N`（edge-agent の対象外）。
- **10 [WARN] hosts.json ↔ pve/*.rb ↔ FLEET**: orchestrator は hosts.json に載っているホストだけを converge するため、未登録の `pve/lxc-*.rb` は「recipe があるので managed に見えるが実際には一度も自動適用されない CT」になります。es-N の transport IP が 2 ファイルに手書きで重複している点も突き合わせます。EXEMPT は `pve/lxc-apm-server.rb`（`lxc_entry` を意図的に呼ばない documented opt-out）。
- **11 [WARN] `case node[:platform]` の else 欠落**: 未知の platform で fail せず nil を返し、path や package 名が未設定のまま「成功」してしまう形。

チェック 11 はインデントではなくブロック深さで走査します。fzf など `when` の下を字下げしない書き方があるためです。走査前に heredoc 本体をマスクします — `add_profile` の shell `if ... fi` は閉じないブロックを開いてしまい、実際 fzf の shell `else` は heredoc 内の 0 桁目にあるので、マスクなしではこれが case 自身の else 腕として読まれます。`end` に到達できなかった場合は黙って pass せず、その旨を自己申告します。

現状の WARN 7 件はすべて既知の drift で、`pve/lxc-es-memory.rb` は別 PR（registry 生成）が所管するため flagged のまま残しています。

## Test plan

`ruby -c bin/lint-cookbooks` → Syntax OK。`ruby bin/audit-cookbook-reachability` → 142/142 reachable, exit 0（変化なし）。

通常実行は exit 0、violations 0、WARN 7 件（zsh の case と es-memory の positive control を含む）:

```
cookbook lint (175 recipes scanned)

WARN: 7 warning(s) (advisory — exit code unaffected):
  cookbooks/dot-config-nvim/default.rb:61: `case node[:platform]` without else — returns nil on an unknown platform; add `else raise`.
  cookbooks/fonts/default.rb:3: `case node[:platform]` without else — returns nil on an unknown platform; add `else raise`.
  cookbooks/fzf/default.rb:39: `case node[:platform]` without else — returns nil on an unknown platform; add `else raise`.
  cookbooks/roon/default.rb:3: `case node[:platform]` without else — returns nil on an unknown platform; add `else raise`.
  cookbooks/speedtest-cli/default.rb:1: `case node[:platform]` without else — returns nil on an unknown platform; add `else raise`.
  cookbooks/zsh/default.rb:8: `case node[:platform]` without else — returns nil on an unknown platform; add `else raise`.
  pve/lxc-es-memory.rb:1: no cookbooks/auto-mitamae-orchestrator/files/hosts.json entry — this CT is never auto-converged, so cookbook changes reach it only on a manual apply. Add an entry, or list the recipe in bin/lint-cookbooks PVE_HOSTS_EXEMPT with the opt-out reason.
OK: no violations.
EXIT=0
```

チェックが本当に発火することを、4 つの一時的な drift を注入して確認しました（いずれも実行後に復元、`git status` は `bin/lint-cookbooks` のみ）。

`config-neo.toml` を退避（check 9 の FLEET→config 方向、FAIL tier なので `EXIT=1`）:

```
FAIL: 1 violation(s):
  cookbooks/host-profile/default.rb:62: FLEET label "neo" has no cookbooks/edge-agent/files/config-neo.toml. edge-agent selects its config by node[:profile][:label], so this host converges with no agent config at all. ...
```

`config-ghost.toml` を作成（check 9 の config→FLEET 方向、`EXIT=1`）:

```
FAIL: 1 violation(s):
  cookbooks/edge-agent/files/config-ghost.toml:1: no "ghost" entry in the host-profile FLEET table, so no host ever resolves this label — the file is dead but reads as coverage. ...
```

hosts.json の role を存在しない recipe に書き換え（check 10-i、WARN tier なので `EXIT=0` のまま）:

```
  cookbooks/auto-mitamae-orchestrator/files/hosts.json:15: role "pve/lxc-nonexistent.rb" (label "kibana") does not exist in the repo — mitamae-runner fails on this host every cycle.
```

FLEET の es-0 ip を書き換え（check 10-iii、`EXIT=0`）:

```
  cookbooks/host-profile/default.rb:67: FLEET es-0 ip="192.168.1.99" disagrees with cookbooks/auto-mitamae-orchestrator/files/hosts.json host="192.168.1.77". ...
```

チェック 11 の結果はファイルを直接読んで照合済みです。flagged 6 件は case レベルに `else` がないこと、unflagged（iperf3 / awscli / starship / jdk 等）は `else` を持つことを確認しました。fzf は heredoc マスクがなければ誤って unflagged になるケースで、`else` が `EOM` heredoc 内の shell コードであることを確認しています。

## Follow-up (this PR では触れていません)

`bin/lint-cookbooks` 以外は変更していないため、チェック本数を「8 checks」と書いている 2 箇所が古いままです — `CLAUDE.md` と `.github/workflows/test-setup.yml` の syntax-check job のコメント。CLAUDE.md は「linter 自身のヘッダコメントが canonical」と明記しているので実害はありませんが、別 PR での同期対象です。

author: hsk-hub
body:
이승원님이 `/predict/risk` 를 **예측 전용**으로 정리해 주셔서(콜드스타트 점수 계산 제거), 백엔드가 DB 점수 + ML 예측을 합치는 구조를 완성했습니다.

## 역할 분리가 끝났습니다

| 무엇 | 어디서 |
|---|---|
| 점수 (`riskScore`, `baseComponent`, `checklistComponent`) | **DB 함수** `fn_coldstart_assess` ← 정본 |
| 예측 (`topRisks`, `severityPrediction`) | **ML 서버** LightGBM |

채점 공식이 두 군데 있으면 어긋난다는 문제(체크리스트 20→835 교체 때 실제로 발생)를 **DB 한 곳으로 모아** 해결한 결과입니다.

## 동작

```
체크리스트 제출
   → fn_coldstart_assess 로 점수 계산            (method=COLDSTART)
   → /predict/risk 성공하면 raw_features 에 예측을 얹고  (method=HYBRID)
   → 응답에 topRisks / severityPrediction 노출
```

### `method` enum 질문에 대한 답

이승원님이 열어 두셨던 안건입니다. 이제 `/predict/risk` 는 순수 예측만 주지만, 백엔드가 **통계 점수와 함께 저장**하므로 `HYBRID` 가 맞습니다. ML 서버를 못 쓰면 `COLDSTART` 로 남습니다.

## ML 서버가 없어도 진단은 됩니다

예측 호출이 실패해도 **점수는 이미 DB 에 들어가 있으므로** 그대로 반환합니다. `topRisks`/`severityPrediction` 만 빈 배열이 되고 화면은 비지 않습니다.

## 확인 (제조업 / 5인 미만 / 부산)

```
method=HYBRID  score=72.81 HIGH  (base 32.81 + checklist 40.0)
top_risks: 업무상질병 0.212, 끼임 0.189, 넘어짐 0.111
severity : 6개월 이상 0.344, 91~180일 0.312, 29~90일 0.260
```

| 항목 | 결과 |
|---|---|
| `/predict/risk` 응답 필드 | ✅ `top_risks`/`severity_prediction`/`model_version` 만 (정리 반영 확인) |
| `raw_features` 저장 | ✅ `top_risks`, `severity_prediction`, `ml_model_version` |
| ML 서버 중지 시 | ✅ 점수는 그대로, 예측만 빈 배열 |
| 테스트 | ✅ 22건 통과 |

API 문서(`backend/docs/API.md`)도 갱신했습니다 — **점수와 예측의 출처가 다르다**는 점을 프론트가 알 수 있게 명시했습니다.

## 아직 남은 것 — 강주호님 확인 필요

`risk_score` NULL 허용 건은 **DB 에 아직 반영되지 않았습니다.** 이승원님도 README 에 같은 내용을 기록해 두셨습니다.

```sql
-- 현재: NOT NULL 제약 그대로, 함수도 NONE 매칭 시 0 으로 계산
ALTER TABLE risk_assessment ALTER COLUMN risk_score DROP NOT NULL;
ALTER TABLE risk_assessment ALTER COLUMN risk_grade DROP NOT NULL;
```

덧붙여, 현재 데이터로는 4개 업종 모두 베이스라인이 있어 **`NONE` 매칭 자체가 발생하지 않습니다**(폴백이 항상 `INDUSTRY` 에서 걸림). DB 변경이 들어오면 백엔드 응답을 nullable 로 바꾸고 프론트에 "통계 부족" 상태를 안내하겠습니다.

author: robbes
body:
## What

Run 94 (Postgres) failed at the Finish gate; run 95 (PGlite) was green. The drill passed in both. Here's the actual cause — and it isn't the drill.

**The Finish gate's precondition was timing luck.** It refuses over an item *"awaiting a decision"*, and an item only reaches that state after **`MAX_ITEM_ATTEMPTS` (5)** failed attempts. The workflow planted the second poison file, ran **one** pass, then let the gate poll for 200 s while the every-minute cron supplied the rest — but 200 s fits only **three** firings. So the gate needed 5 attempts and the step produced 4, passing only when the plant happened to land early enough in a minute for a fourth firing to squeeze in.

That coin flip came up green for months, and started failing when an unrelated step above it got **19 seconds slower** — the backup/restore drill merged today. Both failures died in `waitForUnresolved` at exactly 202 s (runs 92 and 94); run 95 is the same luck landing the other way.

**Fix:** the plant step now drives **five explicit synchronous passes**, so the item is provably at the threshold before the gate looks — no dependency on cron phase at all. The gate's timeout message now names the threshold and the reason, so the next person doesn't have to re-derive it from `MAX_ITEM_ATTEMPTS`.

## Status of the three failures

| Run | Backend | Cause | State |
|---|---|---|---|
| 92 | Postgres | My drill recreated the app without `compose.dev.yml` → `ENOTFOUND stalwart` | Fixed in #263 |
| 93 | PGlite | Nextcloud 500 on a source DELETE, *before* the drill | **Did not reproduce** in run 95 — flake, not a defect |
| 94 | Postgres | Finish gate's 5-attempt precondition vs 200 s cron window | Fixed here |

The backup/restore drill itself has now passed on both backends (runs 94 and 95), including the destroy-and-restore of a real volume and the post-restore idempotency check with the new failing-domain guard active.
