author: lesnik512
body:
## Why

`Container.resolve(dependency_type)` looked the provider up and then tail-called `self.resolve_provider(provider)`, paying a second Python frame on the by-type path — the one every `@inject` marker and framework integration takes.

Retires `planning/deferred/2026-08-01-resolve-by-type-inline.md`.

## Design

`resolve` now carries its own copy of `resolve_provider`'s body: closed check, memo hit, `resolver_for` fallback, resolver call, `RecursionError` conversion.

**The duplicated ~8-line body is the standing cost, and it is permanent** — both copies must be edited together. That is the trade this PR asks you to have made, and it is recorded in the code, in `architecture/performance.md`, and in the decision doc.

**What licensed it:** `resolve_provider` stopped being an interception seam when the compiled resolvers landed in 2.29.0. Resolvers call each other directly; its only callers are `resolve`, `resolve_dependency`, and the cycle back-edge thunk. A `Container` subclass overriding it records **1 call while resolving a 4-node chain** on `main` — it has never seen the graph. Full reasoning, including why this is deliberately narrower than `2026-08-01-scope-map-inline-declined.md` (which stands), is in `planning/decisions/2026-08-03-resolve-provider-not-a-seam.md`. The reviewer verified that central claim independently: 1 call on main, 0 on this branch, 1 by reference on both.

## Non-goals

- **`find_container` is untouched and remains a blessed extension point.** This rules on one method, not on `Container` subclassing generally.
- **No enforcement or deprecation** of subclass overrides; the decision records that the resolve path is free to bypass `resolve_provider`, not that subclassing is forbidden.

## Verification

`just test-ci`: 477 passed, 100% line coverage on **both** 3.14 and 3.10 (3.10 run under a local interpreter, twice, since it is the version that gates this change). `just lint-ci`: clean.

**Measured** with the repo's A/B/A harness (`ab_run.sh main HEAD g16_by_type`), CPython 3.14, three runs: **-18.57%, -20.10%, -22.21%** (~40 ns), by-reference control `g2_cached` flat at +1.13%. Naming the scenario and version because the size is shape-dependent — the reviewer measured a differently-built by-type case at -10.6% on 3.14 and -37.8% on 3.10.

### One thing I got wrong, and the review caught

I previously reported the 3.10 coverage blocker as "verified fixable in ~10 lines of test", and PR #416 recorded that in the deferred item (now deleted by this PR). **That verification was flawed** — I checked with `--cov=modern_di.container`, and the line records fine under narrow tracing. Under the real gate (`--cov=modern_di`) it does not.

My first fix was a `# pragma: no cover` on the production line, with a comment claiming the handler is "reached only by a by-reference cycle". The review refuted both:

- The claim is false. A **by-type** cycle re-enters `resolve_provider` through the back-edge thunk and hits that line six times.
- What actually changed is that the two tests reaching it *without* a stack overflow (`SelfRec.__init__` raises `RecursionError` directly, so the tracer survives) go by type, and now land on `resolve`'s copy.
- So the fix is a by-reference twin of that overflow-free shape, not a suppression. `test_by_reference_recursionerror_passes_through` restores genuine 100% on 3.10.

**No `pragma: no cover` on any production line in this PR.** The cycle test stays with a corrected comment: it contributes no coverage, but it is the only guard on `resolve_provider`'s own conversion — replacing that conversion with a bare re-raise kills that test and nothing else.

## Known follow-up, not in this PR

`docs/introduction/performance.md` and `benchmarks/README.md` quote the by-type surcharge (60/54/65 ns; "roughly 40 ns on top of `resolve_provider`"). This change invalidates those figures. They come from the generated comparative table, which is republished at release time — hand-editing generated numbers here would be wrong, so this is flagged rather than done.

---

### Before merging

- [x] **Behaviour changed?** `architecture/resolution.md`, `performance.md` (counts corrected four/three -> six/four, plus a note recording the duplication where a reviewer would look for it), `containers.md`, `concurrency.md`, `validation.md`.
- [x] **Rejected an alternative?** `planning/decisions/2026-08-03-resolve-provider-not-a-seam.md`.
- [x] **Found real work you are not doing now?** The stale by-type surcharge prose, flagged above as a release chore.
- [x] `just lint-ci` and `just test-ci` pass, on 3.14 and 3.10.

author: sunholo-voight-kampff
body:
Correction to the Gate-5 skill edit landed minutes ago in #570 — caught by running the check it added.

#570 told Gate 4 to pair the charter cheap tell with two controls: known-present `ITERATION <N-2>` and known-absent `ITERATION 999`. Verifying the landed record, the **known-absent control returned `1`, not `0`**.

Cause: the STATUS stamp #570 had just written *documents the control*, so `ITERATION 999` is now in the charter permanently. The charter is a file the loop **writes about itself**, so any literal named "known-absent" stops being absent the moment a record mentions it. And unlike the case-sensitivity bug it was added to fix, this one fails **silently in the safe-looking direction** — the control reads as firing while proving nothing.

**Fix:** keep the known-**present** control (the one that actually detects the failure mode: a broken instrument reads `0` on a healthy charter). Drop the known-absent literal. Where a structural second check is wanted, assert the rotation invariant `grep -c "^## STATUS 2026" == 3` — anchored to line-start, untrippable by prose.

Saved in the main checkout first (same inode via the `~/.claude` symlink, so it is live now) and mirrored here — no drift.

author: jeremyames-gmail
body:
Captured from ops #2524. Docs-only — deliberately **separate from #205** (the code fix), because #205 auto-deploys to CT 123 on merge and a learning shouldn't be gated on that decision. `.claude/` changes are in `paths-ignore`, so this one does not deploy.

**Mechanism:** Express runs middleware in registration order. A global `express.json()` ahead of the route-scoped `express.raw()` consumed the stream, so `req.body` was already a parsed object and `JSON.parse` stringified it to `[object Object]` and threw. Every well-formed delivery 400'd — measured three ways against the live service before the fix.

**The quieter half, and why it's worth an entry:** `validateWebhookSignature()` sits after the parse and was therefore **never reached**. The endpoint appeared to reject unsigned requests, but that was an artefact of the 400 — signed, unsigned, and forged all failed identically. An unreachable security control looks exactly like a working one, because both produce rejections.

**The trap in the obvious fix:** parsing earlier restores 200s while discarding the bytes the HMAC must be computed over — strictly worse than the bug, because it's silent. The suite asserts `rawBody` is a Buffer *and* that its length equals the serialized payload length.

author: jirathip-k
body:
Closes the last gap in the lifecycle. Implement opens drafts, review applies
`agent:approved` — and nothing lifted the draft, so an approved PR needed two
manual steps and GitHub refuses to merge a draft at all.

## Why deterministic rather than in the prompt

The reviewer already applies its own verdict labels, so adding `gh pr ready` to
its allowlist would have been the smaller diff. A workflow step is better here:
it derives the action from the label that was actually applied, so a
`REQUEST CHANGES` verdict cannot lift the draft even if the model misreads its
own instructions. `prompts/review-release.md` now tells the reviewer explicitly
not to do it itself.

## This is not auto-merge

Lifting a draft is a readiness signal. Branch protection and a human still own
the merge, and `AGENTS.md`'s "never add automatic merge behavior" constraint is
intact. One thing worth knowing: if a target repository has GitHub's own
auto-merge enabled on a PR, taking it out of draft is what lets that fire. That
is the target repo's configuration, not something this lane does.

## Verification

- `actionlint` passes with shellcheck enabled.
- Logic tested against 7 cases under `bash -e -o pipefail`: draft+approved lifts;
  draft+changes-requested, draft+blocked, draft+no-labels all leave it alone;
  already-ready is a no-op; multi-label including approved lifts; and
  `agent:approved-later` correctly does **not** match (substring trap).
- The `gh pr view --json isDraft,labels` output shape was checked against a real
  PR (#328).
- The step is `continue-on-error: true` and implicitly gated on the review step
  succeeding, so a failed review never lifts a draft.

## After merge

The `v1` tag must be moved to the new merge commit — target repositories consume
`@v1`.

author: aiden-jeon
body:
## 배경

`llmwiki publish add`에서 새 데이터베이스 생성 시 뜨는 **부모 페이지 선택 목록**이 Notion에 공유된 모든 페이지를 계층 구분 없이 평면으로 쏟아내 너무 길었다. 특히 프로젝트를 Notion DB로 관리하면 그 행 페이지들까지 전부 후보로 나와 목록이 감당이 안 됐다.

## 변경

- **depth 계산·정렬**: `listPages`가 search 결과 안에서 부모 체인을 따라 각 페이지의 depth를 계산하고 오름차순으로 정렬한다(최상위 먼저). `maxDepth`로 최상위+직속 자식(≤2)까지만 남긴다.
- **기본은 최상위만**: depth 1만 보여 목록을 짧게 유지하고, 자식이 있으면 `↓ 하위 페이지도 보기`로 펼친다.
- **제목 검색**: `🔍 제목으로 검색`을 목록 **맨 위**에 두고 Notion search query로 제목을 훑는다. depth 한계로 못 찾는 깊은 페이지도 찾을 수 있다. `maxItems`로 스크롤 창을 만들어 페이지가 많아도 화면을 뒤덮지 않는다.
- **DB 행 제외**: parent가 데이터베이스(`database_id`/`data_source_id`)인 페이지는 새 DB의 부모가 될 수 없어(Notion 새 DB는 `page_id` parent에만 생성 가능) 후보에서 뺀다. depth 계산 전에 걸러 조상 노릇도 못 하게 한다.

### 한계 참고
Notion `search` API는 각 페이지의 직속 parent만 주고 전체 조상 체인은 주지 않는다. 그래서 상위 페이지가 검색 결과 밖이면 depth가 정확하지 않을 수 있고, 이를 보완하기 위해 제목 검색을 함께 제공한다.

## 테스트

- `listPages`의 depth 필터·정렬, `excludeDatabaseChildren` 필터에 대한 단위 테스트 추가.
- 전체 스위트 통과(185 tests).
- 로컬에서 `llmwiki publish add` 실제 동작 확인.

This pull request and its description were written by Isaac.

author: magne
body:
Closes #253.

The map surface shared by the Geography tool and the Place record's Map tab said nothing about zoom and bounded it nowhere: MapLibre's 0–22 default applied while `tile.openstreetmap.org` only serves to z19, so a wheel gesture ran three levels past the last tile that exists and the canvas went blank. `fitBounds`' own `maxZoom: 15` was the only bound, and it bounds Fit alone.

## What the map does now

- **Bounded camera.** `minZoom: 1` / `maxZoom: 19` on the map from a new `ZOOM_RANGE` in `genealogy-ui`, plus `maxzoom: 19` on the raster source so MapLibre overzooms the last real tile instead of requesting tiles that 404. `fitBounds`' ceiling is now a named `FIT_MAX_ZOOM`, with a test asserting it stays inside `ZOOM_RANGE`.
- **A live zoom readout** (`z14.2`, one decimal, fixed-width tabular figures) beside the provider select in both toolbars. The mounted map reports its settled camera on `zoomend`, plus one measurement inside the `load` handler so the first reading is measured rather than assumed.
- **`NavigationControl`** (zoom buttons only, top-left) and a metric **`ScaleControl`** (bottom-left) — a pointer-free way to change zoom, and a statement of what the level means on the ground.

## How it is wired

The init script's single `dioxus.send` channel now carries tagged payloads (`{"click":[lng,lat]}` / `{"zoom":n}`), parsed by hand off `serde_json::Value` — the crate has `serde_json` but no `serde`, and a two-variant webview transport does not justify the dependency. Both emitters live inside the script's existing `!el.__geoMap` guard, so they cannot diverge from the map or from each other.

Zoom is a `Signal<f64>`, read only via `.peek()` at mount and written from the listener task, and the readout is its own `#[component]`: a subscribed surface would re-render on every gesture, and a re-rendered surface remounts, which rebuilds the map.

Every control string comes from the Fluent catalogue through MapLibre's `locale` option (ADR 0003 — MapLibre's English defaults are its own i18n), in `en` and `no`. `NavigationControl.ResetBearing` is deliberately not localized: `showCompass: false`, and an unused message is what `i18n-check` warns about.

## Tests

Written first, in this order: `clamp_zoom` over its range including non-finite input (`f64::clamp` panics on a non-finite bound, and `panic` is deny-level); the payload parser, including the `[lng, lat]` → `(lat, lon)` swap and refusal of untagged payloads; script-text assertions for both bounds, the source `maxzoom`, both controls being added *after* `load`, the locale table, and `zoomend` (with an assertion that no per-frame `zoom` listener exists — that would round-trip a whole gesture); readout formatting and the clamp-then-compare skip; and SSR tests for the readout's markup, accessible name and Norwegian text.

`tests/gui-pass/map-zoom.toml` covers what SSR cannot reach at all: pressing the map's own `+` moves the camera; tiles are still painted at the ceiling (`painted` at a calibrated `min_deviation`, against a blanked canvas measuring exactly 0); 60 further notches change nothing at either bound (`match`); and the readout's own rectangle changes with the camera and then sits still. The notch counts are measured, not guessed — one `xdotool click 4` is ≈0.167 of a zoom level, so a first attempt at 40 notches never reached the bound and compared two mid-gesture frames.

The readout widens the toolbar's right-aligned group, so the hardcoded coordinates in the five other map scenarios plus `map-view` moved 56px left and were re-measured from fresh shots. The toolbar stays on one row.

`cargo fmt --all`, `clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`, `nextest run --workspace --all-features --lib --bins --tests` (2033 passed), `cargo test -p genealogy-ui-dioxus --doc`, `cargo xtask check`, `cargo xtask gui-pass --reset` (13 scenarios passed), `cargo xtask issue-sync`, `prek run`.

Also still `manual-verify`: zoom smoothness and whether the readout lags perceptibly, since a still image has no frame rate.

author: barneychambers
body:
Follow-up to #129, which is its base. Raised under "Related" in #103.

## What

Deletes `src/crypto/dilithium/avx2/` — 43 files — and the one commented-out `CLEANFILES` line that referenced it.

## Why it is safe

The tree has never been buildable. **15 of its 43 files are zero bytes**, including `params.h`. Nothing in the build system referenced it; the only mention anywhere was a commented-out line.

Worth stating explicitly since the names collide: the `libbtq_crypto_avx2` target in `Makefile.am` is Bitcoin's SHA256 AVX2 code (`crypto/sha256_avx2.cpp`) and has nothing to do with Dilithium. It is untouched.

## Why delete rather than repair

AVX2 was evaluated and declined on its merits — roughly 2x on verification against no performance problem, since worst-case block verification is 0.23 s, or 0.38% of a 60-second block interval.

Beyond that, a second implementation of a consensus-critical primitive is a second thing that has to agree with the standard, and a place for the two to disagree. Now that #129 establishes what holding this primitive to the standard actually costs — reference vectors plus ACVP conformance vectors — adding a second implementation is a commitment to doing that twice. A broken copy bought none of the benefit and, as #103 put it, read as available capability.

It was also the one place BTQ sat behind upstream: `d35ba3f`, the stricter infinity-norm check from upstream issue #113, touches `avx2/sign.c` only, and the copy vendored here predated it. `ref/`, which production runs, already performs that check.

## Testing

- Rebuild clean.
- Full unit suite: 739 cases pass, unchanged.
- `./contrib/devtools/dilithium-kat.sh`: all three security levels still reproduce.
- No dangling `dilithium/avx2` references remain in any build file, script or doc.

## One note

Upstream's `README.md` and `Dilithium*_META.yml` in that directory still describe AVX2. They are upstream files kept verbatim as part of the vendored snapshot, so `PROVENANCE.md` says so rather than editing them and adding divergence for cosmetics. `PROVENANCE.md` also records the route back if AVX2 is ever wanted: re-vendor intact at a pinned commit and hold it to the same two known-answer tests as `ref/`.

author: ronmizrahi
body:
Adds a **Where the loops are** section between *The method* and *What ships with it*.

### Why

"Loop engineering" is the framing of the moment — Boris Cherny, June 2026: *"I don't prompt Claude anymore… my job is to write loops."* That framing answers **when a run starts**. It says nothing about **when it ends**, which is the entire subject of this plugin. The section names that split so the reader can place the tool.

### What it says

Three layers, usually conflated:

| Layer | Where it lives | Ends on |
|---|---|---|
| The outer loop — `/loop`, `/goal`, a routine, a CI hook | outside the graph | a schedule, a condition, or you |
| The graph's cycles — every retry path in one run | `edges.md`, each with a bound | its bound, then a stated behaviour |
| The deliberate exception — a human revising their own decision | same table, marked unbounded | the person |

> An outer loop wrapped around an unbounded inner one is the thing that runs all night and reports success in the morning.

### The data

Real numbers, read out of `superpowers-graph`'s own `edges.md` rather than asserted: **9 bounded cycles, 4 deliberately unbounded**, a **500-transition** global ceiling, and a six-row sample of the bounds table with exhaustion behaviour (`FIX_ROUND` ≤ 5 → `ADJUDICATE`, `DEBUG` ≤ 3 → `BLOCKED`, `INTEGRATE`→`DISCARD` ≤ 2 → `HANDOFF`).

Plus the three counter rules, each tied to the failure it prevents — per-item keying, never-reset, and keying by caller (`attempts["DEBUG:<return_to>:<item>"]`) so one caller cannot spend another's budget.

README-only, no new assets.

author: asigdel29
body:
Chunks are **generated rather than fetched**, and the streaming manager cannot tell the difference — it mounts and unmounts pieces without knowing whether one arrived over a network or was computed on the spot. That is the same boundary that let this world replace an exported island, and it is why the pivot cost a scene component rather than a rewrite.

Running: **52 fps, 27 draw calls, 59k triangles, 49 chunks, 25 colliders**, character grounded on a beach beside a lake.

### Four bugs, every one invisible to the tests

1. **Blank page.** The config failed validation, which throws at module scope — and it was right to. A step of a full block is taller than half the body, which the validator calls a wall rather than a stair. The reflex is to make the step a block, since a block is the unit of everything here. But that is not how this kind of world moves: **you step a half block and jump a whole one**, and conflating them gives a character who walks up walls.

2. **The fog rule was backwards** — and had never fired, because every world until now had `fog: null`. It demanded fog extend *half again past* the streaming edge, which guarantees a chunk arriving in air that is still clear: exactly the pop it claimed to prevent. Fog hides an arriving chunk only if it is already opaque at the distance the chunk arrives at. The rule **and its test** were written from the same wrong picture, which is how a test comes to agree with a bug.

3. **Nothing but fog.** The opening camera frames the whole world from outside, and this world's bounds are 768 units across — so it sat 832 units back, far beyond the fog. A world with no outside is *entered*, not surveyed; how a visitor arrives is now the world's own choice.

4. **Nothing at all, while collision worked perfectly** — grounded, 25 colliders registered, empty screen. A subtree named `colliders` means *simplified proxy geometry* and is hidden from rendering. That is right for a world whose collision is a cheap stand-in for expensive art, and exactly wrong here, where the blocks are already the cheapest possible description of themselves.

**Load radius is three, not five.** Five is 121 chunks generating 16,000 blocks each before the first frame: the world booted at 9 fps showing nothing, because it was still building. A generated world pays for its radius in *work* rather than in bandwidth — the opposite of a streamed one, and it needs a different number.

790 tests.

Closes #118

author: degoodman
body:
Closes #146. Phase 3 (inline Copilot-style suggestions) is split out into #277 and iceboxed, so this PR completes the issue.

Adds three RAG-backed advisory actions to the editor slash palette: `/challenge` ("Challenge this assumption"), `/gaps` ("What am I missing?"), `/contradictions` ("Find contradictions").

## The design decision that shaped this

Phase 1's commands transform text — they stream a replacement into the document. Phase 2's commands produce **critique**, and streaming a devil's-advocate argument into the note body would be wrong. So these render in an **inline advisory card** anchored near the cursor, with their cited sources. The document is untouched unless you explicitly click "Insert as quote", which makes the AC "accept/reject leaves the document in a clean state either way" true by construction rather than by careful rollback handling.

Routing is by an explicit `kind: "transform" | "link" | "partner"` discriminator on `SlashCommandDef`, set on all nine commands — not name-based special-casing at call sites.

## Backend

- `core/ai.py` — `EDITOR_PARTNER_COMMANDS`, folded into the existing `EDITOR_COMMANDS` validation; `build_writing_partner_prompt()` (pure) with `WRITING_PARTNER_CONTEXT_CHAR_BUDGET = 12000` and per-document truncation. Each action gets a distinct instruction; all three must cite retrieved notes by title and say plainly when the knowledge base doesn't support a point — `contradictions` in particular is told to report no conflict rather than invent one.
- Both existing endpoints gained a third branch rather than new routes, so the `AdminUser` gate and `ai_editor` rate limit are inherited. `EditorAssistResponse` gained `sources`; `result`/`suggestions` semantics are unchanged, so **Phase 1 clients in production keep working**.
- Retrieval reuses `_retrieve_documents_for_synthesis` from #166 at `top_k=6` rather than synthesis's 12 — this is focused critique of one passage, not a corpus-wide summary. **The current note is excluded from its own results** (fetch `top_k+1`, filter by `note_id`); a note contradicting itself is noise.
- **Zero-retrieval case**: when retrieval comes back empty, the LLM is never called. Returns a fixed honest message with `degraded: true` instead of asking a model to critique against nothing.

SSE contract: `sources` always first (so citations render before prose), then `token` deltas, then `complete`.

## Frontend

- `WritingPartnerCard.tsx` — positioned via the palette's `coordsAtPos` approach, then measured and clamped/flipped against the viewport on every content change so it can't stream itself off-screen. Escape and Dismiss both close it **and abort the in-flight stream**. Reuses `SourceList.tsx` from #166 — the backend's source shape was matched to it deliberately.
- Palette, wikilink dropdown, and card are mutually exclusive. Zen-mode Escape now checks for the card first, so one Escape closes the card rather than exiting zen.
- "Insert as quote" is the only path that mutates the document: a plain undoable dispatch at the original trigger position, each line prefixed `> `. Failure paths leave the document untouched — easy here, since nothing is inserted until you click.

## Testing

Backend: unit tests for the prompt builder (distinct instructions per action, `ValueError` on unknown command, truncation, empty context) plus integration tests for both endpoints — happy path, 401 unauthenticated, AI-unavailable, zero-retrieval, SSE ordering, current-note exclusion, and a regression test that Phase 1 transform and `/link` responses are unchanged.

Frontend: 26 tests in `slashCommands.test.ts` over the nine-command registry — `kind` assignment, prefix filtering, trigger detection unchanged.

`make test-backend` 621 passed · `make test-frontend` 117 passed · lint, typecheck, and `format:check` clean on both.

**Runtime-verified against the live stack:** non-streaming `gaps` returned the documented shape; streaming `contradictions` produced exactly one `sources` event (6 sources), 329 `token` events, then `complete`; the note under review never appeared in its own sources.

## Two caveats

- **The zero-retrieval degraded path was not live-verified** — dev Neo4j always returns something for similarity search, and forcing true zero-retrieval would mean emptying the shared dev knowledge base. It's implemented against the backend contract and covered by tests, but has not run end-to-end against a real empty corpus.
- In prod these commands go through the **Groq→Gemini chain** (`llm_use_api` routes all generation, not just embedding sync), which is known-flaky per #260/#263. The backend agent hit a real Groq 429 → Gemini 503 during verification and the degraded path handled it correctly — but expect occasional degradation in prod, same as the other AI features.

body:
## Что внутри

**Безопасность выкатки.** Проверка `--dest` в `nginx-apply.sh` была `case` по glob, где `*` совпадает и со слэшем — путь с `..` проходил мимо белого списка и писался от root, при том что sudoers даёт CI `NOPASSWD` на этот скрипт с любыми аргументами. `release.sh` и `rollback.sh` брали `--root` и `--version` без валидации и дальше делали `rm -rf` и распаковку. Пути канонизируются, проверка падает закрыто.

**Список изменений при релизе.** `bin/changelog` собирает его из git и отдаёт готовый фрагмент для Telegram. Зовут все три пути релиза: локальная выкатка и оба переиспользуемых workflow. Список едет в `version.json`, откуда его забирает агент статуса и показывает бот — включая команду просмотра по любому сервису или ферме.

Счёт в символах, а не в байтах: кириллица весит два байта, и байтовый лимит резал русские темы вдвое раньше английских. Ссылка на PR не отнимает место у текста. Генератор не может уронить выкатку — любой вход даёт код 0.

**nginx.** У metro и launcher слушался только IPv4 на 443, тогда как порт 80 отвечал по IPv6 и редиректил на https: клиент по IPv6 попадал в catch-all с `ssl_reject_handshake`. Плюс конфиг `die.samoy.love`.

**Откат.** `rollback.sh` молча пропускал reload nginx при провале `nginx -t` и всё равно печатал успех; ручной откат не откатывал systemd-юниты; после автоотката `previous` и `current` совпадали и следующий откат был невозможен.

author: supercapper
body:
## Summary
Fixes the generator writing a near-duplicate feedback paragraph per project when a portfolio has multiple projects in the same tech stack. `ReviewGenerator._format_context` now groups retrieved chunks by shared stack (`primary_language`, falling back to `tech_stack`) before building the LLM prompt. Same-stack projects are presented as one "Shared stack" block instead of N separate blocks, and paired prompt-template instructions tell the model to write one consolidated observation for that block instead of repeating itself per project.

## Issue
Closes #28

## Changes
- `rag/generator/review_generator.py`: add `_group_chunks_by_stack` and `_stack_label` helpers. `_format_context` groups same-stack chunks into a single numbered block: multi-project blocks get a "Shared stack: X -- N related projects" header plus per-project detail lines, and ungrouped/single chunks keep the original format exactly. Grouping happens inside the existing top-10-chunk retrieval limit.
- `rag/generator/prompt_templates.py`: `skills_feedback` and `projects_feedback` templates now instruct the model to consolidate observations for a "Shared stack" block rather than write one paragraph per project.
- `tests/unit/test_review_generator.py`: removed the `strict` `xfail` from the Week 8 reproduction test now that it passes for real, and added coverage for single-project (unchanged output), mixed-stack (no incorrect merging), missing stack metadata (graceful degradation, no crash), and the existing >10-chunk retrieval limit.

## Testing
- [x] Unit tests pass (`make test-unit`)
- [ ] Integration tests pass (`make test-integration`) -- not run; this change has no integration-level surface, it's pure data-shaping ahead of the LLM call
- [x] Linter passes (`make lint`)
- [x] Type checker passes (`make typecheck`, via the `pre-commit` `mypy` hook)
- [x] New/updated tests cover the changes

**Manual verification:** run this from the repo root to see the actual before/after shape of the fix:

\`\`\`python
from rag.generator.review_generator import ReviewGenerator

chunks = [
    {"metadata": {"source_id": "repo_1_todo-api", "primary_language": "Python", "tech_stack": ["Python", "Flask"]}, "score": 0.9, "text": "Flask REST API with SQLAlchemy models."},
    {"metadata": {"source_id": "repo_2_cli-tool", "primary_language": "Python", "tech_stack": ["Python"]}, "score": 0.9, "text": "Command-line tool using argparse."},
    {"metadata": {"source_id": "repo_3_data-pipeline", "primary_language": "Python", "tech_stack": ["Python", "Pandas"]}, "score": 0.9, "text": "ETL pipeline using pandas."},
]
print(ReviewGenerator._format_context(chunks))
\`\`\`

On `main`, this prints three independent `[1]`/`[2]`/`[3]` blocks -- the shape that made the LLM write three near-identical "Python skills" paragraphs. On this branch, it prints one `[1] Shared stack: Python -- 3 related projects` block with all three projects listed underneath. `tests/unit/test_review_generator.py::TestFormatContext` covers this and four related edge cases if you'd rather read assertions than run it by hand.

**Pre-existing failures (unrelated to this change):** `make test-unit` has 53 pre-existing failures on `main`, spread across unrelated modules (`test_bias_detector.py`, `test_resume_parser.py`, `test_review_service.py`, `test_pii_scrubber.py`, `test_skill_extractor.py`, `test_tech_detector.py`, and others), plus one in a file this PR touches only by association: `test_output_parser.py::test_json_array_fallback`, since `output_parser.py` itself is not modified here. I confirmed the same 53 failures exist before and after this change, with no new failures introduced. Separately, running `mypy` directly through the repo's local `.venv` hits an unrelated, pre-existing environment issue: a numpy stub uses `type X = ...` syntax that this venv's mypy version rejects before it can check any project files. The `pre-commit` `mypy` hook runs in its own isolated environment and passes cleanly against the changed files.

## Notes for Reviewers
One deviation from my own PLAN.md worth calling out: I originally planned to group primarily by `tech_stack`, falling back to `primary_language`. I flipped that precedence during implementation and grouped by `primary_language` first. Three projects that clearly share a "Python" stack in practice often have different exact `tech_stack` lists (e.g. `["Python","Flask"]` vs `["Python"]` vs `["Python","Pandas"]`), so grouping strictly by the exact stack list would have left them ungrouped and missed the case this issue is actually about.

I also considered the backstop dedup step in `output_parser.py` that PLAN.md flagged as a fallback option, but decided against it. This fix is deterministic and runs before the LLM call rather than just hinting at one in the prompt, and it's fully covered by unit tests at the `_format_context` level. A second heuristic dedup pass over LLM output would add complexity with no good way to test it in this suite.

author: rryles
body:
Follow-up to review on #238. Seven small things, no behaviour change on the device.

### The send_msg drop caveat reaches the last three pages

The pages converted by #219 all carry a paragraph saying `send_msg` posts with a **zero timeout** — a full queue drops the message — and that `make_msg` is the counterpart when the reply matters or you need to wait for room. The three pages converted by #238 didn't get it: Stopwatch said only "returning `false` if allocation or the send failed", Sensors said nothing, Files mentioned `make_msg` for replies but not the drop. That timeout is the one behavioural difference between the two calls.

Each page now states it in its own terms — the Stopwatch commands return the bool precisely so a screen can tell a press never left, while a lost *snapshot* needs no handling because the GUI re-requests one on start and resume; for sensor data the drop is the right trade, since the next sample is moments away.

### Two corrections on the same pages

- **`send_msg` was unqualified** in the Sensors guidance comments (7 places). Copying that doesn't compile in C++17: with no visible declaration of `send_msg` as a template the `<` parses as less-than, and ADL can't rescue a call with explicit template arguments until C++20's P0846. Now `SDK::send_msg`, as every other page writes it.
- **The "PressureValues is never sent" note** sat inside the code block a reader copies, and undersold the work — that branch hex-dumps the frame rather than parsing it. Now prose under the block, pointing at `SDK::SensorDataParser::Pressure` and the parse-then-send shape the other branches use.

Plus: the Stopwatch page showed `StopwatchState` without its constructors and then described one in prose. The snippet is now the struct verbatim from `Commands.hpp` (verified identical), and the prose says what delegating buys — the message type is named once.

### Fixed-width types finished in the Files tutorial

#238 widened `SetSettings::decimalCounter` to `int32_t` to agree with `SettingsValues` but left `activityType` and `displayMode` as plain `int` in both. These are `#pragma pack(4)` structs crossing a process boundary, and they're what a tutorial reader copies. `int` is 4 bytes on both the ARM target and the host simulator, so **no layout changes today** — it removes an assumption that doesn't belong in a wire struct. Call sites keep `static_cast<int>`: `int` is right for the locals and the JSON round-trip, and the conversion is exact.

Also in both tutorial headers: dropped the unused `<array>` (nothing in either `Software` tree names `std::array`, so it isn't a transitive dependency for anything downstream), and aligned the `StatsValues` constructor's second parameter line to its open paren per the SDK's `.clang-format`.

### One thing beyond the review

`Stopwatch-Architecture.md` was the **only** page under `Docs/Examples` missing from the Example Apps toctree in `index.rst`, so Sphinx built it as an orphan and no link on the site reached it — including from the page #238 had just rewritten. Added the missing line. Say the word if you'd rather that landed separately.

### Verification

Ran the CI builds locally in `xanderhendriks/stm32cubeide:16.0`:

| Build | Result |
|---|---|
| `Docs/Tutorials/Files` | `Files_0.0.0-dev.uapp`, 242784 bytes |
| `Docs/Tutorials/Sensors` | `Sensors_0.0.0-dev.uapp`, 535164 bytes |
| `Examples/Apps/Stopwatch` | `Stopwatch_0.0.0-dev.uapp`, 160736 bytes |

The 6 compiler warnings in the two tutorial builds are pre-existing and in files this PR doesn't touch (`Libs/Source/Fit/RecordingMarker.cpp`, `Libs/Source/Variant/VariantConfig.cpp`, and `-Wswitch` in each `MainView.cpp`); Stopwatch builds with none.

`sphinx-build Docs` exits 0 and goes from 212 warnings to 211 — the orphan-page warning is gone, and no remaining warning names any file touched here.

author: rubenvdlinde
body:
## What

Adds job-level `timeout-minutes` to the CI jobs on `main` that still had none.

A fleet-wide sweep bounded these repos' `development` branches. `main` carries an
older, separate copy of the same workflows that the sweep missed, so those jobs were
still running with GitHub's 6-hour default: a hung runner burns six hours of minutes
and blocks the queue before anyone notices.

| file | job | timeout |
|---|---|---|
| `.github/workflows/pull-request-lint-check.yaml` | `lint-check` | 15 min |

## Why these numbers

Measured from actual fleet run history (successful + failed executions only; skipped
records excluded, since they otherwise drag every median to zero):

| job | n | median | max | bound |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `lint-check` | 176 | 0.6 min | 1.4 min | 15 min |
| `validate` | 170 | 0.5 min | 3.2 min | 20 min |
| `check-source-branch` (Branch Policy Check) | 31 | — | 0.1 min | 10 min |

The bounds are deliberately loose — roughly an order of magnitude above observed max.
**A timeout that fires under normal contention is worse than no timeout**: it converts
a slow run into a phantom defect and trains people to re-run red checks. The goal is to
catch a hang, not to enforce speed. Please do not tighten these.

## What is deliberately NOT touched

Every other job in these repos' `.github/workflows` is a **reusable-workflow caller**
(`uses: ConductionNL/.github/...`). GitHub rejects `timeout-minutes` on such a job and
turns the whole file into a `startup_failure`, so those are bounded at source in
`ConductionNL/.github` (already merged). No job in this PR is a `uses:` caller.

## Verification

- Job list re-derived from `main` with `yaml.safe_load` rather than taken on trust.
- Per file: re-parsed after the edit, job set asserted unchanged versus base, each job
  asserted to carry its exact expected value, and every untouched job asserted byte-equal.
- Positive control: newly-bounded count per repo equals the expected count.
- Negative control: the same probe run against the unedited base file reports `None` for
  each target job, so it distinguishes bounded from unbounded rather than emitting a constant.
- `actionlint` on the edited files produces exactly the findings the base files already
  produce (only line numbers shift) — zero new findings.
- Diff is additions-only (`N	0` in `--numstat`, no deletion lines) and confined to
  `.github/workflows/`.

author: lukidzi
body:
## Motivation

Part of #17242, closes #17295. 3.0 replaces the standalone `ZoneIngress` resource with zone proxy listeners on `Dataplane`, so nothing may source cross-zone routing data from `ZoneIngress` anymore. `MeshZoneAddress` already carries the publicly reachable address of a zone proxy — reconciled from the ingress `Service` on Kubernetes, authored by the user on Universal — and `fillRemoteMeshServices` already preferred it, keeping `ZoneIngress` only as a fallback.

## Implementation information

`fillRemoteMeshServices` no longer takes `[]*ZoneIngressResource`: remote-zone endpoints for `MeshService` and `MeshMultiZoneService` destinations come solely from `MeshZoneAddress`. A zone without a `MeshZoneAddress` contributes no cross-zone endpoints.

`MeshZoneAddress` gains a validator (non-empty address, port 1-65535). It was previously only written by the Kubernetes controller and relied on kubebuilder markers, which don't apply on Universal where it is now user-authored.

The two `meshhttproute` golden entries covering "a zone reachable only through a legacy ZoneIngress" are removed along with their goldens — that configuration no longer exists. As a consequence the legacy-SNI branch in `pkg/plugins/policies/core/xds/meshroute/clusters.go` (`classifyMZMSEndpointZones`, the per-zone `transport_socket_match`) is now unreachable, since `ZonesWithMeshScopedProxy` is derived from the same `MeshZoneAddress` list that produces the endpoints. It is left in place here and should be removed with the rest of the legacy path (#17768, #17769, #17302).

`fillIngressOutbounds`, `BuildEgressEndpointMap` and `BuildCrossMeshEndpointMap` still read `ZoneIngress.AvailableServices` for legacy `kuma.io/service` routing and are untouched by this PR.

## Supporting documentation

`UPGRADE.md` documents the required `MeshZoneAddress` per mesh on Universal zones.

author: prabaltripathiofficial
body:
## Problem

Cloud replay renders a recorded pod's **init containers** as one-shot compose services (`restart: "no"`, the app `depends_on` them with `condition: service_completed_successfully`). Keploy runs the compose with:

```
docker compose -f - up --abort-on-container-exit --exit-code-from <app>
```

`--abort-on-container-exit` stops the whole stack the instant **any** container exits — including a one-shot init exiting **0**, which it *must* do for the app to start. Result: the app is torn down before it ever runs.

```
prepare-mongo-tls  exited with code 0        <-- init did its job (as designed)
Compose  Aborting on container exit...        <-- flag fires on that success
api-server  Stopping / Stopped                <-- app killed before it runs
→ "user application failed under --keep-app-alive: exit status 1"  (no report)
```

The flag has been correct for its intent (catch the **app** crashing) since #3256, but it's a blunt "any container" instrument. It became fatal once init containers started being rendered as one-shot compose services, because a one-shot init's success is indistinguishable from an app crash under `--abort-on-container-exit`.

## Fix

When the in-memory compose contains a one-shot init (detected by `service_completed_successfully` in the compose content), inject **`--abort-on-container-failure`** instead of `--abort-on-container-exit --exit-code-from <app>`.

- `--abort-on-container-failure` aborts only on a **non-zero** exit → the init's clean exit-0 is ignored, while a real app crash is still caught.
- `--exit-code-from` is dropped because it *implies* `--abort-on-container-exit`. There is **no** container-state polling on the compose path (`waitTillExit()` is skipped for `DockerCompose`), so after this change `--abort-on-container-failure` is the **only** signal that catches an app crash: it makes `docker compose up` itself exit non-zero, surfaced through `cmdErr` from `utils.ExecuteCommand`. Note that compose now returns its **own** exit status rather than the app's (via the old `--exit-code-from <app>`) — equivalent for pass/fail, but the specific code changes meaning.
- Only the **in-memory** compose path (`setupComposeInMemory` → `ensureInMemoryComposeFlags`) is switched. The user-provided-compose-file path (`modifyDockerComposeCommand`) passes `false`, so its behavior is unchanged.

~18 lines across `pkg/client/app/{app.go,util.go}`.

## Why this and not the alternatives

- **Two-phase (pre-run the init, then `up`)** was tested and *fails*: even with `--no-recreate`, compose re-runs the one-shot init as a dependency, it exits 0 again, and `--abort-on-container-exit` aborts anyway.
- **Detached + monitor** would work but keploy deliberately forbids detached mode (`isDetachMode`), so it's a larger lifecycle refactor.
- `--abort-on-container-failure` keeps the flag's original purpose (catch app crashes) while removing the only false positive (a one-shot init's success), with zero change to non-init flows.

## Verification

Reproduced against a real deployment whose recorded manifest carries a `prepare-mongo-tls` init, running the exact cloud-replay command with the stock vs. patched binary:

| | Stock | Patched |
|---|---|---|
| Injected cmd | `up --abort-on-container-exit --exit-code-from …` | `up --abort-on-container-failure` |
| `Aborting on container exit` | fires on init exit-0 | never |
| App | torn down, never ran | agent healthy, app booted, ran |
| Replay | catastrophic, no report | ran to a full report |

author: totalfrank
body:
## Problem

The WebSocket relay dials the upstream **before** accepting the client, so a
caller that gives up while that dial is in flight leaves `websocket.accept()`
reading a `websocket.disconnect` where it expects a `websocket.connect`.
Starlette reports that mismatch as a `RuntimeError`, which escaped the endpoint
and produced an unhandled ASGI traceback for every abandoned handshake.

Nothing leaked — the upstream exit was already owed unconditionally by the
existing `try/finally`, and that was verified rather than assumed. The cost is
noise: under load the tracebacks bury the single
`logger.warning("relay upstream unavailable")` that explains a *real* upstream
failure.

That is not hypothetical. A recent WebSocket relay capacity investigation spent
several rounds chasing a phantom ~430/500 connection ceiling, and this traceback
spam is part of what obscured the diagnosis. The root cause turned out to be a
capacity harness that attached an unconsumed `subprocess.PIPE` to the gateway's
stdout; once the pipe buffer filled, the gateway blocked in a synchronous write
inside the event loop and stopped accepting. The relay itself sustains 4000/4000
connections at 2 fd per connection with no fd leak. No capacity fix is needed or
included here.

Two smaller gaps surfaced alongside it:

- `_refuse` closed the client socket unguarded. Every refusal races a caller
  that may already have hung up, so a close-time error could replace the logged
  cause of the refusal.
- The dial guard catches `Exception`, which does not cover `CancelledError` on
  Python 3.12. Reviewed and deliberately left as-is, but the reasoning was
  nowhere in the code.

## Solution

Handle the abandoned handshake where it happens: catch `RuntimeError` /
`WebSocketDisconnect` scoped tightly to the `accept()` call, log at debug, and
return. The `finally` still runs, so the upstream is released on this path
exactly as before.

`_refuse` now closes through the existing `_quietly` helper, on the principle
that the reason for a refusal is worth more than the failure to transmit it.

The dial guard is unchanged. A cancellation there has nothing to unwind — the
context manager never entered, and the socket library releases its own transport
when its dial is cancelled — so widening it to `BaseException` would only turn a
cancelled worker into a refusal nobody is left to read. That reasoning is now a
comment rather than an open question a future reader has to re-derive.

Rejected: restructuring the handshake into a different async-context shape. The
existing `try/finally` already discharges the upstream on every path, which was
confirmed by driving Starlette's real `WebSocket` through the ordering; a
rewrite would carry risk without fixing anything.

## Validation

- New regression test `test_a_client_that_leaves_before_accept_still_releases_the_upstream`,
  driven at the ASGI seam because the condition under test is a message ordering
  a cooperating `TestClient` will not produce. Verified it **fails without the
  fix** with exactly `RuntimeError: Expected ASGI message "websocket.connect",
  but got 'websocket.disconnect'`, and passes with it.
- `tests/integration/test_relay_ws_route.py` — 40 passed.
- Full non-e2e suite — 587 passed, 1 failed.
- `ruff check` and `ruff format` clean on both changed files.

Not caused by this change, stated rather than hidden:

- The one non-e2e failure is `tests/architecture/test_ruff_lint_rules.py::test_ruff_formatting_passes`,
  from formatting drift in `src/gateway/community/spi/bot/_ports.py` — a file
  this PR does not touch. Left alone as out of scope.
- `tests/e2e` — 10 failed, 16 passed, all `httpx.ConnectError` from needing a
  live server. Identical counts on a clean tree.

Scale verification of this path is deliberately **not** claimed here. Generating
abandoned handshakes in volume needs the capacity harness, and that run is
tracked separately now that this fix and its unit coverage have landed.

## Compatibility and risk

No contract, schema, config, or migration impact. No client-visible behaviour
change on any path that previously worked: the handled case is one that
previously ended in an unhandled exception, and the endpoint's return value was
already discarded. Rollback is a straight revert of the single commit.

## Spec

`src/gateway/specs/2026-08-02-gateway-websocket-relay-domain/spec.md`

That spec defers concurrency limits under "measure first, then bound". The
measurement now exists and shows no wall below 4000 connections on a high-nofile
host, which supports keeping the limit deferred. No backpressure is added here.

Fourteen comments in this tree explained why some piece of work had *not* been done. Every one of those estimates has since been paid. A stale one is worse than no comment at all: it argues against the exact task the next person is holding a ticket for, and it does so in the authoritative voice of a comment that was true when written.

Applied per comment, not mechanically. Two kinds live here and only one can expire:

- A comment explaining why the **code is as it is** ("because X", "no Y required", "DO NOT use Z") encodes a constraint someone paid for. Preserved.
- A comment explaining why **work was not done** is an estimate of a cost. That is what expires.

Several of these were both — a load-bearing rule wrapped in a false tense. Those keep the rule and lose the tense, and where the rule was weak it now leads with DO NOT, names the forbidden alternative, and states the reason.

author: thijs-creemers
body:
Closes BOU-271. Found while building the `wagoe-migrate` skill, whose first step is creating a migration.

## The defect

`bb migrate create <name>` threw for everyone who followed `bb migrate --help`:

```
📝 Creating migration: add-widget...
ERROR … Failed to create migration {:name add-widget}
java.lang.ClassCastException: class clojure.lang.PersistentVector cannot be cast
  to class java.lang.String
```

`get-migration-config` sets `:migration-dir` to the discovered **vector** of every migration directory on the classpath. `up`, `status` and `rollback` accept that and have always worked; `migratus/create` casts it to String. Only `create` was affected — the command nobody scripts is the one that broke.

## Why it matters more than a broken convenience

The workaround is hand-writing `<id>-<name>.up.sql` and `.down.sql`. **BOU-256 exists precisely because that filename format is easy to get wrong and silently invisible to migratus.** So the broken command pushed people onto the path that had already caused a bug.

I hit this myself during BOU-265 and hand-wrote the migration rather than stopping to look. That was the wrong call — it took ten minutes to find once I did.

## Fix

`create-config` narrows the read config to a single directory string. It uses the project's own `migrations/` rather than the first element of the discovered list, so a dependency contributing a migration directory cannot decide where a user's migration lands.

## Verified end to end

Generated project, pointed at this checkout:

| step | result |
|---|---|
| `bb migrate create add-widget` | exit 0, files written |
| `bb migrate status` | **Pending 1** |
| `bb migrate up` | Applied 1, Pending 0 |
| `bb migrate rollback` | Applied 0, Pending 1 |

The `status` step is the one that counts. Creating files proves nothing if migratus cannot discover them — that is exactly how BOU-256 stayed hidden.

## An existing test had pinned the bug

`migration-operations-delegate-to-migratus` asserted:

```clojure
[:create config "add-users"]     ; config = {:migration-dir ["migrations/"]}
```

It expected `create` to receive the vector. So the test held the ClassCastException in place as intended behaviour, and my fix correctly broke it.

Updated, with the reason recorded in the test. **A test can hold a bug still as firmly as it can catch one** — a different failure mode from the ones this codebase has been finding lately, where tests couldn't fail at all.

New tests assert the shape `migratus/create` actually receives, and were proven to fire by reverting the narrowing.

## Verification

- `bb check` 14/14, `bb test:all` 5/5
- Migration lifecycle above, in a generated project
- All new assertions proven to fire

author: pavel-ptashyts
body:
## Problem

`AsyncHttpClientHandler` requested a read from both lifecycle callbacks:

```java
public void channelActive(ChannelHandlerContext ctx)       { ctx.read(); }
public void channelReadComplete(ChannelHandlerContext ctx) { ctx.read(); }
```

Netty's `HeadContext` already calls `Channel#read()` immediately after firing
either event whenever `autoRead` is on. AsyncHttpClient never clears `autoRead`
(no `ChannelOption.AUTO_READ` anywhere in the codebase) and Netty defaults it to
on, so that was the path for every connection: each read cycle traversed the
outbound pipeline and reached `doBeginRead` twice instead of once. The cost is
per read cycle, so it scales with how many reads a response takes.

## Change

Drive the read from the handler only when `autoRead` is off.

That is also a fix in its own right: a caller who disabled `autoRead` through
`setChannelOption` previously had the setting silently defeated by these two
unconditional reads, since the handler kept requesting reads regardless.

## Verification of the Netty behaviour

Checked against `netty-codec-http2` / `netty-transport` **4.2.16.Final**, the
version this project builds against, rather than assumed:

* `DefaultChannelPipeline$HeadContext.channelActive` and `.channelReadComplete`
  both call `readIfIsAutoRead()`, which is
  `if (channel.config().isAutoRead()) channel.read();`
* `DefaultChannelConfig`'s constructor initialises `autoRead` to `1`, so on.
* HTTP/2 stream channels inherit both behaviours:
  `AbstractHttp2StreamChannel$2 extends DefaultChannelPipeline`, and
  `Http2StreamChannelConfig extends DefaultChannelConfig` without overriding
  `isAutoRead`.

The last point matters because this is the shared base class of `HttpHandler`,
`WebSocketHandler` and `Http2Handler`, and neither of the two callbacks is
overridden by any of them, so the change applies to HTTP/1.1, WebSocket and
HTTP/2 stream channels alike.

## Verification of the build

`mvnw clean verify` - BUILD SUCCESS, 1371 tests, 0 failures, 0 errors,
19 skipped. Error Prone, NullAway and Revapi all clean.

The suites covering the paths most exposed to a change in read behaviour are
green: 168 HTTP/2 tests (`BasicHttp2Test`, `Http2MultiplexBugRegressionTest`,
`Http2StreamingBodyFlowControlTest`, `Http2StreamOrphanRegressionTest`,
`Http2ConformanceRegressionTest` and the rest) and 36 WebSocket tests
(`TextMessageTest`, `ByteMessageTest`, `CloseCodeReasonMessageTest`,
`WebSocketWriteFutureTest`, `ws.ProxyTunnellingTest`).

Caveat on the testing gate: `AGENTS.md` requires the build to run on JDK 11 and
no JDK 11 is installed on this machine, so it was run on **JDK 17** (also in the
CI matrix). The JDK 11 leg of CI on this PR is the real gate.

No public API change. Same review pass as #2300 and #2301.

body:
**PR-A2 of AIO-612.** Unblocks the cut. Depends on nothing; must merge before PR-B.

## Why this is a prerequisite, not cleanup

`validation/check-skill-library.mjs` (OGR09) reads `gui/server/skill-library/sources.json` through `scripts/lock-skill-library.mjs`. It runs inside `validation/validate-all.sh`, which the **required** `guard` check executes. The moment `gui/` is deleted, that throws ENOENT and reds a required check. This clears it ahead of the cut so PR-B is a pure deletion.

## Why deleting core's copy is safe

AIO-702 (gui repo PR #2, merged `fda6780`) ported all three programs into [`aiosbrain/aios-workspace-gui`](https://github.com/aiosbrain/aios-workspace-gui), alongside the `gui/server/skill-library/` data they operate on. Verified that repo genuinely **owns and runs** them, rather than holding a dormant copy:

- `package.json` scripts: `lock:skill-library`, `lock:skill-library:check`, `lock:marketplace`, `lock:marketplace:check`, `validate:skill-library`, `test:skill-library`
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` job `gates` runs `node validation/check-skill-library.mjs` on every PR and push to main — which transitively executes both lock scripts
- the data is there: `sources.json`, `index.json`, `marketplace.json`, `community.json`, `referenced.json` plus the vendored skill trees

Export parity checked symbol by symbol. The ported files differ from core's only by replacing inlined helpers with imports from `gui/server/skill-library-util.mjs`; no logic body was dropped.

In core, `scripts/lock-skill-library.mjs` had exactly **one** tracked importer — the validator being deleted in the same commit.

## Verification: the removal is a removal, not a silent skip

The failure mode worth guarding against is OGR09 degrading to a no-op that still prints green. So I diffed `validate-all.sh` output on a fresh scaffold, before and after, on the `Running` / `PASSED` / `FAILED` / `SKIP` / `✗` markers:

```
21,22d20
< Running OGR09 — Skill Library...
< OGR09 PASSED
```

Exactly two lines disappear. Nothing else changed, nothing became a skip, both runs exit 0.

## Deliberate deviation from the plan

The AIO-612 plan grouped `scripts/lock-marketplace.mjs` and ci.yml's "Marketplace lock check" step into this PR. **They stay for now.**

`test/skill-install-marketplace.test.mjs` imports `structuralCheck`, which exists **only** in `lock-marketplace.mjs` — `gui/server/skill-library-util.mjs` has `hashDir` but not `structuralCheck`, so there is no drop-in replacement. That test covers `gui/server/skill-library.mjs`, live code until the cut, and `marketplace.json` is still live data. Deleting the writer while both the data and the gate are live would weaken a real gate for one PR's duration and buy nothing.

Both move in PR-B, where the test, the data and the tree die in the same commit.

## Breaking change

`validate-all.sh` no longer runs OGR09. Workspaces vendoring the skill library run the check from `aios-workspace-gui`. The dropped line carries a comment saying where it went and why.

## Review

Adversarial Codex review at the exact head after CI goes green, per the AIO-612 review gate.

author: stn1slv
body:
## What

A deep review of the whole application (every source file read, each finding independently verified, plus three external review rounds) found 13 functional bugs and corner cases. This PR fixes all of them, in five logical commits:

**Engine / write pipeline**
- Runs are serialized: a new run cancels and awaits the previous task before reading, so a double hotkey press can no longer interleave with a run that is still typing or clobber its HUD. The run task owns the HUD lifecycle; Escape during the non-abortable typing phase keeps showing "Writing..." until the writer returns.
- `Task.checkCancellation()` in the pre-write context validation closes the last cancellation window before the first destructive keystroke.
- The previously-dead **Show HUD** setting now works: off hides progress states only, errors always show (Principle VI).
- Typed `AXError.modifiersHeldTooLong` replaces a misleading "app might not support Accessibility" message.
- `Selection.pid` is read from the AX element via `AXUIElementGetPid` (the frontmost-app lookup raced with dormant-tree recovery, which can take ~3.5 s).

**Providers**
- Escape during an OpenAI request is now a quiet cancel and timeouts map to `ProviderError.timeout`: both providers share `ProviderError.mapTransportError`.
- `GeminiProvider.extractText` skips `"thought": true` parts so model reasoning can never be typed into the document.

**Config**
- Tolerant decoding: missing keys with natural defaults no longer reset the whole config. A still-unreadable file is preserved as `config.json.invalid-<timestamp>` and surfaced via an alert instead of being silently replaced (and overwritten on the next save).

**Settings UI**
- Shortcut recorder redesign: recording always targets a temporary name, Cancel/Esc restore the previous state, and the create-flow ordering bug that left a brand-new action's hotkey dead until restart is gone. Verified against the vendored KeyboardShortcuts 1.15.0 source: unregistration is by shortcut value without refcounting, so every dismissal ends with a config-driven re-registration pass (commented quirk workaround).
- Providers tab gains a Kind picker; Gemini providers no longer require hand-editing config.json.
- Save/delete paths do fallible Keychain work first and roll in-memory state back if persisting fails.
- General tab: the Default Chunk Size and Default Delay fields were rendering their inner label inside the fixed frame, truncating the value ("100" showed as "10("); the labels are hidden and the fields widened.

**App / HUD**
- HUD panel: `statusBar` level, `canJoinAllSpaces` + `fullScreenAuxiliary`, `hidesOnDeactivate = false` — feedback is visible over fullscreen apps.
- Escape monitors are reinstalled via a polling timer once Accessibility trust is granted (monitors installed pre-trust never deliver events).

One suspicion from the review was refuted and intentionally not "fixed": deleted actions do **not** leave dead system-wide hotkeys (`removeAllHandlers()` unregisters Carbon hotkeys in 1.15.0).

## Why

These are user-facing correctness issues in the core pipeline (interleaved destructive writes, spurious error HUDs on cancel, silent config loss, dead hotkeys after creating an action) plus constitution compliance gaps (silent failures over fullscreen targets, a dead settings toggle).

## Verification

- `swift test`: 64 tests, 0 failures (baseline was 50; 14 new tests cover decoding defaults, transport-error mapping, backup naming, sanitizer quote guard, Gemini thought filtering).
- `rg NSPasteboard Sources/` returns nothing; `swift format lint` clean for changed code; `./scripts/build-app.sh` builds the release bundle.
- Pending manual acceptance (to record in `docs/compatibility.md` before release): double hotkey press during a slow run; Escape during an OpenAI request and during typing; Show HUD off with a forced error; new-action hotkey without restart; edit-then-Cancel shortcut revert; Gemini provider created from the UI; config with a missing key and a fully corrupted config; HUD over a fullscreen app; Escape-cancel after granting Accessibility without relaunch.

author: yahorbarkouski
body:
## What does this PR do?

Adds a new `git-worktrees` scanner that finds stale and orphaned git worktrees left behind by agents and local feature checkouts. These often contain full dependency trees and can reclaim tens of gigabytes, but were invisible to existing cache/`node_modules` scanners.

Discovery combines a deep home crawl with git worktree registries (so registered worktrees outside the crawl path are still found), plus dedicated agent roots (`~/.cursor/worktrees`, `~/.claude/worktrees`, `~/.codex/worktrees`).

The interactive picker and verbose scan output now show a detail column with relative age (`17d ago`) or `orphaned`.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [x] New feature (new scanner, command, or option)
- [x] Improvement to existing feature
- [ ] Chore / dependency update
- [x] Documentation

## Related issue

N/A

## Checklist

- [x] `bun run lint` passes
- [x] `bun run test` passes (no regressions)
- [x] `bun run build` succeeds
- [x] New tests added for new behavior
- [x] I've tested this on macOS locally

## Notes for reviewer

- Category is **risky** with `supportsFileSelection`, so cleanup requires `--risky` / `--unsafe` and can be narrowed per worktree.
- Stale = linked worktree directory `mtime` older than 7 days; orphaned = `gitdir:` target missing (always reported).
- Primary checkouts (`.git` directories) are never offered for deletion.
- Sizing uses `/usr/bin/du -sk` with a JS fallback for speed on large trees.

### Usage

```bash
mac-cleaner-cli scan -c git-worktrees --verbose
mac-cleaner-cli --risky
mac-cleaner-cli clean -c git-worktrees --unsafe --dry-run
```

## 症状

`mywant config env set TICKETMASTER_API_KEY --stdin` を端末で実行し、キーを貼り付けて Enter を押しても確定しない。

`io.ReadAll(os.Stdin)` は EOF まで読むので、端末では Ctrl-D を待ち続ける。しかもそのことをどこにも書いていないので、ハングしたようにしか見えない。

## 変更

端末のケースを独立させた:

| 入力 | 挙動 |
|---|---|
| 値を省略（端末） | **非表示のプロンプトで訊く。Enter で確定**（`x/term`） |
| `--stdin`（パイプ・ファイル） | これまでどおり EOF まで読む |
| 空のパイプ | 「stdin に何も来ていない」と言う（従来は「値が空」＝原因を取り違えた文言） |
| 引数 | これまでどおり |

非表示にしたのは、値がほぼ必ず API キーで、そうしないとコマンド終了後もスクロールバックに残り続けるため。

依存は `golang.org/x/term` を direct に上げただけ（`v0.43.0`、`x/sys` は据え置き）。

## Overview

This PR implements a new **Feed Scrolling Flow** that automatically scans the LinkedIn feed, scores posts based on user-defined criteria, and presents the top 10 scored posts for review.

## Features

### Two Search Modes
- **Job Search** — User provides experience interval (e.g. 2-3 years), job titles (e.g. Software Engineer, Python Developer), and skill set (e.g. Database Design, Development)
- **Post Search** — User provides freeform keywords/topics to match against

### Automated Scanning
- Configurable scan intervals: 1, 2, 4, 6, 8, 12, or 24 hours
- Self-rescheduling Celery tasks with ±15 min jitter
- Manual scan trigger button for on-demand scans
- Pause/resume functionality

### Regex Scoring Engine (0-100)
| Category | Weight |
|----------|--------|
| Job Titles | 35 pts |
| Skills | 30 pts |
| Experience Level | 20 pts |
| Keywords | 15 pts |

- Color-coded score badges (🔥 ≥80, ✨ ≥60)
- Shows matched terms for each post
- **Future-ready**: `ScorerInterface` protocol for easy AI scorer swap

## Changes

### Backend (12 files)
- **Models**: `feed_scroll_job.py`, `feed_scroll_result.py`

body:
## What changed

- Serialize replay callback dispatch across control-plane ports.
- Remove the cross-port replacement shortcut that bypassed callback draining.
- Keep the old sink/context registration alive until callback dispatch completes.

## Why

Cross-port sink replacement could return while another port was still executing the old callback, allowing its context to be released prematurely. The previous shortcut also left a cyclic drain-wait scenario unresolved.

The dispatch gate makes registration capture and callback execution a single lifetime-critical section, while the existing same-port reentrant path remains non-blocking.

- `./build/tests/test_control_plane_mutation`
- 78 tests passed, 0 failed.

author: gemshrine
body:
Fixes #6293.

The `> name` suffix validates the first character via `checkLowercaseStart`, but the `>> handle` path (`auto()`) only refused scope tokens and the cactus emoji, so an uppercase-first handle (`? >> H`, `? >> Foo`) or a digit-first handle (`? >> 1x`) was accepted even though the parallel `> name` rejects the same names.

The fix mirrors `named()` and calls `checkLowercaseStart` on a non-empty handle, leaving a bare `? >>` (empty handle) valid. Verified against `EoSyntax`:

```
? >> h   ? >>   -> ok
? >> H   ? >> Foo   ? >> 1x   -> error: name must start with a lowercase letter
```

Full `EoSyntaxTest` (1050 cases) stays green. Added the `auto-handle-lowercase.yaml` regression.

body:
# This PR contains

- Headless Pi Bridge JSONL v2 协议、候选与模型身份记录。
- Inspect 托管的双向工具 RPC、BFCL 单轮模型控制任务和 AgentBench OS dev 生产 Agent 任务。
- 候选仓库内生产 policy 契约、系统提示词与技能加载、激活证据和有效性门禁。
- 可复现采样配置、关键运行时配置和不包含样本内容的配对报告。

## Description

为 RongxinAI Issue #237 增加可复现的无头 Pi 测评桥接。Bridge 每个样本启动独立 worker，从指定候选 checkout 加载其 Pi SDK，通过显式环境变量连接 OpenAI-compatible 模型端点，并将有序事件、工具调用、结果、用量、候选身份和有效 HTTP idle timeout 写入 Inspect 轨迹。

工具执行权归 Inspect：BFCL 单轮任务使用 capture 模式保留结构化调用，只作为 Gemma/Pi 工具调用控制数据；AgentBench OS 使用 execute 模式在 Inspect sandbox 中执行 bash/python，才用于评估生产 Agent 能力。

AgentBench 的 baseline 与 candidate 都必须设置 `ZHIYUAN_CANDIDATE_POLICY_MODULE`，并从各自 checkout 加载生产系统提示词、技能和编排。Bridge 限制 policy 模块和技能目录不得逃逸 candidate root；每个样本必须记录 `evaluation_policy_loaded`，禁止 `evaluation_policy_bypassed`。单样本预检可进一步要求实际 Inspect 工具调用，完整评测则保留“不调用所需工具”为 Agent 能力失败。

聚合报告新增 `--require-production-agent` 和 `--expected-samples`，没有 policy identity、逐样本加载证据、实际 Inspect 工具调用、完整样本数，或出现 policy bypass 时拒绝生成生产 Agent 对比结论。报告不写出 benchmark prompt、target、answer 或 sample ID，并明确 approval UI、AskUserQuestion、MCP 和 subagent 尚未覆盖。

验证结果：

- `pytest tests/zhiyuan_bridge`：45 passed，2 个可选真实 SDK smoke 跳过。
- foundation 与 P2 分别使用真实 Pi 0.80.10 和本地伪模型完成 SDK/工具 smoke：各 2 passed。
- Pi loader 实测 foundation 与 P2 均加载 50 个候选技能，0 diagnostics。
- Ruff 全仓 check/format、mypy 和 `zhiyuan_bridge` autolint 通过。
- 全仓 autolint 仅保留与本 PR 无关的 `theagentcompany` 既有依赖声明失败。
- 完整 AgentBench baseline/candidate 对比等待内网模型与远程 Docker 链路恢复后执行，当前不声明 Agent 能力提升结论。

author: shlee9498-dev
body:
`mri-academy` **PR #109와 한 쌍**이다. PR #106 리뷰에서 나온 지적 1의 프론트 쪽 대응.

> ⚠️ **배포 순서** — `mri-academy` PR #109가 **먼저** 배포돼야 한다. 이 PR은 429를 받으면 자동 재시도를 1회 하는데, 서버가 아직 "차단된 요청도 버킷에 쌓는" 상태면 그 재시도가 **차단을 연장**시킨다. 카운트다운도 서버가 주는 `retry_after`에 의존하므로 #109 없이는 값이 오지 않는다.

## 문제

서버가 레이트리밋을 걸어도 화면이 그걸 구분하지 못했다.

| | 기존 동작 |
|---|---|
| `gdcup-confirm` | 429 전용 분기가 없어 `'처리 실패: too_many_requests'`로 떨어짐 |
| `gdcup-edit` | **HTTP status를 아예 안 읽음** (`.then(r => r.json())`). 429든 500이든 `'저장 실패'` |

둘 다 다시 누르게 만드는 문구다. 예전에 "재시도해주세요" 안내를 보고 4번 눌러 **40판이 중복 기록**된 적이 있다. 같은 흐름이 본선 당일 반복되면 대회 운영이 멈춘다.

## 변경

- `gdcup-confirm` / `gdcup-edit`에 **429 전용 분기** 추가. `gdcup-edit`은 HTTP status를 함께 읽도록 수정
- 429를 받으면 `rlHold()`가 **화면의 모든 버튼을 잠그고** 남은 시간을 초 단위로 센다. 잠그는 이유는 안내가 아니라 차단이다 — 안내만으로는 연타를 못 막는다
- **자동 재시도는 팀+동작 조합당 1회까지만.** 그 뒤에는 사람이 판단하도록 넘긴다
- 자동 재시도가 확인창을 다시 띄우지 않도록 `skipConfirm` 추가. 강제확정 사유도 이미 받았으면 재입력 생략
- `.catch`에 `rlClear()` 추가 — 네트워크 오류로 잠금이 방치되지 않게

원래 비활성이던 버튼은 `data-rl-locked` 표시로 구분해 건드리지 않는다. 잠금 해제 시 원상태가 유지된다.

## 문구 원칙

**"n초 후 다시 시도할 수 있습니다"** 상태 고지형만 쓴다. `'시도하세요'` 같은 행동 유도 표현은 넣지 않는다. **429 분기에 `alert`은 하나도 없다** — 팝업은 그 자체로 클릭을 유도한다.

## 검증

가짜 DOM 위에서 실제 로직을 그대로 실행했다.

```
[1] 429 시 버튼 잠금 + 카운트다운 + 복구
    배너 노출 / 자유 버튼 잠김                                  OK
    이미 비활성이던 버튼은 표시 안 함, 해제 후에도 그대로 유지     OK
    문구가 '초 후 다시 시도할 수 있습니다' 형태                   OK
    행동 유도 문구(하세요/해주세요/눌러주세요) 없음                OK
    카운트다운 종료 후 버튼 복구 + 자동 재시도 정확히 1회          OK

[2] 자동 재시도는 키당 1회뿐
    두 번째 429 → 자동 재시도 없이 수동 안내로 종료               OK
    그래도 버튼은 반드시 복구됨                                  OK

[3] 연타 시뮬레이션
    잠금 중 20회 클릭 → 서버 요청 0건                            OK
    복구 후에는 정상 클릭                                        OK

[4] rlClear() 즉시 해제                                          OK
```

인라인 스크립트 `node --check` 통과.

## 범위 밖 (의도적으로 손대지 않음)

429와 무관한 기존 재시도 문구 2건. 8/8 이후 대기열.

- 목록 불러오기 실패 시 `"잠시 후 다시 시도하세요"` — GET이고 리미터가 없어 재시도가 안전하다
- 솔로 데미지 조회 `🔍 재시도` 버튼 — 별개 기능

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

author: ajccarlson
body:
`font-family: Inter, ...` has been the interface font declaration since the beginning. There is no `@font-face` rule, no `@import`, no `<link>` in `index.html`, no `apps/web/public/` directory, and no `.woff2`, `.ttf`, or `.otf` anywhere in the repository.

So Inter renders for exactly those users who happen to have installed it. On a clean Windows machine — the primary target — the entire product renders in Segoe UI. The typographic voice was never chosen; it is whatever the reader already had, which is the opposite of an identity.

The stack now asks each platform for what it actually has, in a deliberate order rather than by accident. The display serif gets the same treatment: `Georgia, "Times New Roman", serif` is fine on Windows and macOS, but Georgia is absent on most Linux systems, where it fell through to Times New Roman — a different voice, and not one anybody picked. It now names the faces likely to be present before falling back.

A test pins that every `font-family` declaration ends in a generic family, so no future stack can fall through to nothing.

**Which face to self-host is deliberately left open.** Bundling a subset woff2 is the right end state and is recorded as such — but choosing the typeface is part of the identity direction, and picking one inside a fix for a lying font stack would quietly settle a decision that should be made on its own terms.

Full repository verification script green.

author: maldoteth
body:
The full-height panel down the middle of the dedicated post page on Osaka and Jungle — the blurred one **behind** the bentos. Not the bento itself; #93 removed that and this was still there.

## What it is

`[data-post-overlay-backdrop]` (`AppLayout.tsx:297`):

```jsx
<div aria-hidden data-post-overlay-backdrop
     className="fixed top-0 bottom-0 z-10 bg-black"
     style={{ left: POST_LAYER_LEFT, width: POST_LAYER_WIDTH }} />
```

`fixed`, full viewport height, explicitly sized to the middle column. Because of that `bg-black` it is caught by each theme's `#app-root` untagged-slab fill net and repainted as glass.

Measured on the deployed page, Osaka active, post opened from the feed:

| theme | computed on the backdrop |
|---|---|
| **osaka** | `rgba(17, 14, 28, 0.6)` + `blur(26px) saturate(1.65)` |
| **jungle** | `rgba(38, 28, 19, 0.86)` |
| cosmic / hazy / war | `rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)` |

`rgb(var(--osaka-slate) / 0.6)` and `var(--osaka-blur)` are that net's declarations verbatim.

`index.css:1124` already declares this element transparent for all eight canvas themes. It loses: the net is scoped under `#app-root`, carries an id, and beats a plain `html[data-theme] [data-hook]` rule no matter how many `!important`s are on the other side — the trap this repo documents. Osaka and Jungle are the only two themes with such a net, which is exactly why every other canvas theme looked fine.

## Why it survived several passes

- **The backdrop only exists on the feed-overlay path.** Opening `/app/post/:id` directly renders no backdrop at all, so a direct visit looks correct. Clicking a post from the feed — the normal way in — is the broken path.
- **`src/test/osaka-post-page-transparency.test.ts` asserts the `index.css` declaration exists.** It does, and always did, while the bug was live. The test passes and proves nothing, because it checks the losing rule.

## The change

Excluded from the nets rather than re-declared transparent: the net also sets `backdrop-filter`, and no plain `html[data-theme]` rule can outrank an id-scoped selector.

- **Osaka** — the exclusion list had no post-layer hooks at all, so `[data-post-overlay]` and `[data-post-drawer]` go in alongside the backdrop.
- **Jungle** — already had those two; only the backdrop was missing. It's the newest element in that layer and neither net was updated for it.

## Verification

Against the deployed page, not by reading the cascade. Both nets, exactly as they ship today, `element.matches()` the live backdrop; with the exclusions applied neither does:

```
osaka  before: true   after: false
jungle before: true   after: false
```

The new test asserts the nets exclude the post layer, since that is the thing that decides the pixel. Any future element added to the post layer needs adding to both lists — declaring it transparent in `index.css` alone cannot win.

Worth a look after merge: post opened **from the feed** on both themes (the path that was broken), and confirm the option/comment sheets and the mobile drawer still look right.

Removes shared Supabase Auth entirely and replaces it with a per-site credential system so each website on the same Supabase project has its own completely isolated admin account.

author: mspinola
body:
## Description

Adopts `2026-08-03-index-share.md`, the work order for the swap-dealer fragility weight. It was written as **cotdata#97** and committed to `cotdata/docs/handoffs/`, while its own header said:

```
Lives at: crowdmon/docs/handoffs/2026-08-03-index-share.md
Target:   Claude Code session, crowdmon worktree
```

It was a drop-off, not a home. **Paired with [mspinola/cotdata#98](https://github.com/mspinola/cotdata/pull/98)**, which removes the other copy. Land this one first: merging that one alone would delete the handoff with nothing tracking it.

## Why it belongs here, and it is not filing

The handoff orders analysis relating index flow to `w_SD`. `tests/test_boundaries.py` refuses an import of `crucible` precisely so a package cannot render a verdict on its own output, and cotdata's own brief already drew the line: *"Do not do the analysis. That is the companion handoff in `crowdmon`."* A work order for that analysis sitting in the producer repo invites it to be executed there, against the store rather than across the seam.

## What changed, and what deliberately did not

**The body is byte-identical** to what cotdata#97 committed. Verified by diff against `cotdata@b7004e8`.

Only the tracked front matter moved. `Status:` read *"blocked, do not start until cotdata CIT Supplemental ingestion is merged"*; that blocker cleared on 2026-08-03 when **cotdata#96** landed the CIT Supplemental report, so it now reads open and unclaimed. Moving a work order while leaving a false "blocked" on it means the next session opens it and stops.

**The body keeps its em dashes, against governance #8.** `docs/handoffs/README.md` overrides that explicitly: *"The work order is preserved verbatim, including anything the prose rules would forbid."* A handoff amended after the fact stops being evidence of what was actually asked.

## The README row

This is the **first OPEN entry in that table**, which makes the directory's own rule live for the first time: *"a handoff without a completion status will be re-executed by a future session."*

The row leads with the binding constraint rather than the question, because the constraint decides what can honestly be concluded:

- **13 agricultural markets, no metals.** Gold, silver and copper are outside Supplemental coverage permanently. Gold is the market that motivated *half the original question* (the swap dealer on the immovable side) and this report can never answer it.
- **Index Traders is a Legacy-taxonomy carve-out** and does not nest inside Disaggregated's Swap Dealer, so the two cannot be differenced.
- **Different bases**: Supplemental is futures-and-options combined, the Disaggregated store is futures-only, so no cross-report differencing.

Docs only. No package code touched.
