author: mablack01
body:
Closes Flip-Smart/flip-smart#1201

## Summary

`OfferStore.importRecords` assigned `nextOfferId = maxId + 1` from the largest id among the records it was handed. That set is routinely a **subset** of what the store held — the login reconcile drops terminal records past `TERMINAL_HISTORY_RETENTION_MS` and `MAX_RETAINED_TERMINAL_RECORDS`, and it runs on every world hop, not only at login.

So the counter regressed, and a fresh offer could take an id the backend still holds fills under. The method's own comment claimed re-seeding meant "subsequent offers cannot collide" — true within a single import, false once pruning is in the picture.

`apply()` already guarded the counter with `Math.max`; `importRecords` was the outlier. Raise rather than assign, so the counter only ever moves forward.

## Why it matters

The backend reconciles GE History rows per `offer_id`, and that path deliberately bypasses the item-level dedup window for precision. A recycled id corrupts it in both directions: a fresh offer inheriting an old id's fills is masked (data loss), and a renumbered position duplicates (profit inflation — observed live as 41,548 units recorded for a real 20,774-unit position, ~8M gp of phantom buy cost).

The backend-side containment for the duplication direction ships separately under the same issue. This change is the plugin-side half: stop generating bad identities in the first place.

## Scope

This does not make `offer_id` durable. A live position the offline reconciler re-mints still takes a brand-new id while the backend holds its fills under the old one — no choice of counter fixes that, which is why the backend cap exists. Server-side offer identity is tracked in epic #933.

The counter is still derived from the persisted blob at client start, so it can regress across a restart once records age out of retention. Closing that needs the high-water id persisted alongside the records; not done here.

## Changes

### 🐛 Bug Fixes
- `OfferStore.importRecords` now raises `nextOfferId` via `Math.max(nextOfferId, maxId + 1)` instead of assigning it outright, matching the guard `apply()` already had — the counter can only move forward, never regress on a lossy (partial) import.

## Testing

### Automated Tests
- `./gradlew test` — BUILD SUCCESSFUL, no failures.
- New test `OfferStoreTest.lossyImport_doesNotRecycleAnIdTheBackendAlreadyHoldsFillsUnder`, verified to **fail against pre-fix code**: it imports a subset with the highest-id record removed (simulating retention pruning), then places a fresh offer and asserts its id still exceeds the pruned one.

### Manual Testing
- [ ] N/A — this is an internal id-bookkeeping fix with no UI surface; coverage is via the unit test above.

## Token budget

`tools/token-budget.py`: **190,546** against the `.github/token-ceiling` of 191,750. The change is +6 counted tokens — the explanatory comment does not count toward the plugin-hub total.

## Checklist

- [x] Tests added/updated
- [x] Code follows style guidelines (Plugin Hub LOC/comment discipline — no issue refs in source)
- [x] Commits are clean and descriptive
- [x] No console.log / debug code left
- [ ] Reviewed by teammate

## Related Issues

Closes Flip-Smart/flip-smart#1201
Related to Flip-Smart/flip-smart#933

### 🩺 Codacy Quality Gate — fixed in this PR
- `b7b3c43` `PMD_category_java_errorprone_AvoidDuplicateLiterals` src/test/java/com/flipsmart/OfflineSyncPersistenceTest.java:273 — extracted the repeated `"nextOfferId_Zezima"` literal into a `NEXT_OFFER_ID_MARKER_ZEZIMA` constant, matching the existing `SYNC_MARKER_ZEZIMA` pattern in the same file.

### 🩺 Codacy Quality Gate — dismissed via API (noise)
- `PMD_category_java_multithreading_AvoidSynchronizedAtMethodLevel` src/main/java/com/flipsmart/trading/OfferStore.java:40 (`nextOfferId()`) — method-level `synchronized` is semantically identical to wrapping the whole body in `synchronized(this)`; not a real concurrency issue. The class already has 10+ other methods using this exact pattern (`addListener`, `bySlot`, `forItem`, `allRecords`, `export`, `importRecords`, `correctCreatedAt`, `correctActivityAt`, `completedAwaitingCollection`, `hasActiveSellOfferForItem`, `hasLiveBuyOfferForItem`); converting only the 2 new methods to block-level would make the file internally inconsistent for no functional benefit.
- `PMD_category_java_multithreading_AvoidSynchronizedAtMethodLevel` src/main/java/com/flipsmart/trading/OfferStore.java:49 (`raiseNextOfferId()`) — same rationale as above.

### 🤖 Codacy AI Reviewer — fixed in this PR
- `3f87ece` src/test/java/com/flipsmart/OfferStoreTest.java:255 — use simple `ArrayList` class name instead of fully-qualified `java.util.ArrayList`.
- `074c0f0` src/main/java/com/flipsmart/trading/OfferStore.java:148 — tightened Javadoc grammar ("would let" instead of "let") and capitalized "ID".

_(Both AI Reviewer threads were already resolved in the prior pass at head `074c0f0`; no new AI Reviewer comments landed on the two commits added since.)_

---

## Added after in-game QA

Three further changes, all verified against a live client rather than unit tests alone.

### The rescan was built for a state the game cannot reach

`maybeProactiveRescan` re-read the History tab every ~10s for as long as it stayed visible and posted every row each time, to "catch fills that land after the initial open". Those fills cannot land: an offer only enters the History tab once **collected**, and collecting requires the main GE interface, which *replaces* the tab. The tab's contents cannot change while it is visible.

Measured in-game at `inserted=0 deduped=40` on **twenty consecutive reads** — six full forty-row round-trips a minute per player sitting on the tab.

The rescan's real job is retrying a read that recovered nothing, since `WidgetLoaded` fires ahead of the clientscripts that populate the rows. It now stops once a read parses rows. New content arrives via re-opening the tab, which fires `WidgetLoaded` again — confirmed in-game by observing a read on re-open *with the rescan disabled*, where nothing else could have triggered it.

An earlier attempt used a content-signature check on the posted batch. That was ~30 lines solving a problem the gate solves in one, and it has been removed.

### High-water offer id is now persisted

`Math.max` in `importRecords` keeps the counter monotonic within a session, but the store derives it from the records it is given and retention pruning drops the oldest terminal ones. Across a **client restart** the surviving maximum is all that remains, so the counter still fell back. The mark is now persisted per-RSN and raised ahead of the reconcile — which is what mints ids for live slots no persisted record claims.

**Bug found during QA:** written unconditionally, it was clobbered with `1`. The store is transiently empty during the logout/hop transition and its counter reads 1, and the key was written as `1` against persisted records topping out at offerId 22 — destroying the mark in exactly the case it exists for. It is now written only when it would rise. Comparing, rather than testing for an empty store, keeps the guard independent of the order the counter is seeded in.

Verified end-to-end through a real client restart: with the stored mark seeded to **500** and records topping out at 22, fresh offers minted **500 and 501** rather than 25. A correct load and a broken load both yield 23 without that seeding, so the test was staged to distinguish them.

## Verified in-game

| Behaviour | Evidence |
|---|---|
| Backend cap blocks a stale-id duplicate | 6/6 reads, `offer_delta=20774 available=0` |
| Backend cap allows a genuine recovery | `inserted=1`, 20,774 units, no cap line |
| Rescan stops after first success | 1 read, then silence for 5½ min |
| `WidgetLoaded` fires per tab open | read observed with the rescan disabled |
| High-water id persists **and loads** | offers minted at 500/501, not 25 |
| Empty store does not clobber the mark | mark held throu

author: clauding-lab
body:
## What this does

EconDelta has an anomaly check that asks *"did this value move too much?"*. It has nothing that asks *"has this value stopped moving at all?"* — and that second question is the one that keeps catching us out.

The failure mode: a source page stops updating, or a parser locks onto a table that no longer moves. The fetch still returns HTTP 200. Nothing throws. The run is green. The number sits there being wrong for months.

Real cases, all found by hand rather than by any alarm:

| indicator | frozen for | at |
|---|---|---|
| the eight `food_*` retail prices | **93 days** | one `market.dam.gov.bd` page |
| `interbank_repo_data` | **33 days** | 5591.93 |

`utils/staleness.check_value_staleness` tracks how long each registry indicator has held the same value and alerts once that exceeds a cadence-derived budget. It runs at the end of `aggregate_latest`, right after the corridor coherence check, so one bad run reports both problems.

**Detect-and-alert only.** It never rejects a run and never mutates `data`. By the time it runs the values have already landed, and a frozen number is a reason to go look at a source — not a reason to throw away everything else in the bundle. The call is wrapped in a `try/except` so observability can never take down the aggregate.

## Validated against real data before it was written

Same discipline that killed the anomaly alarm proposal: the rule was replayed offline over **12,366 real `metric_history` rows** and the alerts counted before a line of production code was written.

**Result: 9 alerts today, all genuine** — the 8 food prices plus `interbank_repo_data`. No false positives.

Three design choices came directly out of that replay, and all three are load-bearing. They're documented as AGENTS.md landmine 40 so a future edit doesn't quietly undo them.

**1. Budgets are deliberately loose.** `daily` 14d, `weekly` 35d, `monthly` 75d, `quarterly` 200d, `fiscal_year` 400d. Re-printing the same value between releases is *normal* — a quarterly NPL is restamped daily at one value for ~90 days by design. And `bill_bond_rates` / `tbill_182d_yield` / `tbill_364d_yield` are nominally daily but really weekly auctions; they measured 6 days unchanged on a healthy day, which is why `daily` went from 10 to 14. Tightening a budget toward one publication period makes the alarm fire on healthy metrics every period — which is how an alert channel gets muted.

**2. The BB policy corridor is exempt, on purpose.** I originally told Adnan this alarm would have caught the stale policy rate. **That was wrong, and I'd rather say so here than let the PR imply it.** The repo rate sat at 10.00% for six years *legitimately*. No budget can distinguish "BB hasn't moved it" from "our parser is stuck", and any budget tight enough to catch the 65-day freeze would have cried wolf for the six years before it. That failure is caught where it's actually detectable — at the source (PR #100's homepage panel parser) and at the consumer (The Brief now ages event-cadence metrics off the restamp date, PR #142).

**3. Registry scope only.** Extending the rule to the other ~80 keys in the flat `data` dict fired **59 alerts on day one**, all restating already-known dead writers. A metric with no live writer is a missing-writer problem, not a stillness problem.

## Two incidental findings

- **`interbank_repo_data` has been frozen 33 days** at 5591.93. New — nobody was looking for it. Worth a separate check.
- **`debt_gdp_ratio` carries an `as_of` of `2031-12-31`** in `metric_history` from a mis-parse. A future date yields a *negative* age, which would make a metric permanently un-alertable — the quietest possible failure. `_parse_day` now rejects them.

## Warm-up behaviour (deliberate)

The tracker starts empty and learns by observation. Nothing can alert until a metric has held one value for its full budget *since deployment* — so the known freezes above re-surface on their own schedule rather than on the first run. That's the intended trade: the alarm earns its alerts from evidence it collected itself instead of inheriting a backfill whose provenance it can't check. State lives in `data/staleness_state.json`, is per-box, and is gitignored.

Alerts are **batched into one Discord message per run** with a 7-day re-alert quiet period. Eight identical-looking posts every morning for three months is the failure mode that guards against.

## Gates

```
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q        →  1105 passed, 5 skipped   EXIT 0
.venv/bin/python -m ruff check .     →  All checks passed!       EXIT 0
```

15 new tests in `tests/test_staleness.py`. Roughly half are false-positive tests — a moving value, a quarterly restamped for 91 days, the exempt corridor held 400 days, `None`/string/`bool` values, an unknown cadence — because an alarm that cries wolf is worse than no alarm.

author: cabapps
body:
MOTION SENSOR: back to counting. The amplitude thresholds were raised to fight walking, which they could never do -- they set how BIG a movement has to be, and a footfall is not small. All the raise achieved was dropping real reps: gentle ones, the end of a hard set, anyone not slamming the board. They are back near where they started, and walking is rejected purely on CADENCE, by the crossing-interval gate that was doing the work anyway. The refractory period goes 1200 -> 900 ms for the same reason. Two new tests: a gentle set at half the amplitude, and a brisk one at 1.4 s a rep.

SUPERSETS NEED A MATCHING NOTCH. Chest press against seated row looks ideal and is not: the notch that makes a press hard leaves a row light enough for twenty reps, because the back is stronger than the chest, so every round means getting up to move the pin. `typicalLevel` carries where each movement is normally done as a fraction of the rail -- derived from muscle group and the pulley, not tabulated by hand -- and pairs now require both within about two notches. The trainee's own logged levels override it, because "can I row as much as I squat" has no general answer, only theirs.

PROGRAMS THAT ADAPT. observedSecondsPerSet measures the trainee's real pace from elapsed session time over sets logged, absorbing everything the model cannot see. The ramp grows the plan only while it still fits the time they actually train for, so a session abandoned two movements short becomes a shorter plan next time rather than the same plan and the same abandonment. As they speed up, the room grows back. Derived, never stored -- same reasoning as the rotation.

STRENGTH GETS 45 MINUTES. Holding it to thirty did not produce a faster strength program, it produced one with the chest press deleted to make room: three minutes of rest IS the method. Someone who chose "get stronger" has opted into that, and is better told the session takes forty minutes than handed a shorter one that no longer trains half of them.

Rail-10 is no longer an open item -- back-solving angles from the resistance columns is the better source anyway, since those reproduce exactly and the printed angle column demonstrably does not reproduce its own table.

Templates re-fitted by tools/fit-programs.mjs, which is new and committed because the four constraints interact and I have now derived this pass by hand three times.

Verified: 205 xUnit, 226 vitest, 22 publish, 96 driver, 11 offline, 11 update.

author: raineorshine
body:
Partially addresses #4798

## The clone failure

Every `pull_request_target` run of BrowserStack failed at **Clone repository** with a bare `The process '/usr/bin/git' failed with exit code 1`, so no iOS test ran on a PR. Runs on `main` succeeded.

The step checked out `head.ref` — a bare branch name — which makes `actions/checkout` build a **wildcard** refspec (`+refs/heads/<name>*:refs/remotes/origin/<name>*`). A wildcard matching nothing makes `git fetch` exit 1 with an **empty stderr**, which is why the logs carried no diagnosis. Reproduced against this repo:

```
=== ref: main ===                          * [new branch] main -> origin/main   EXIT=0
=== ref: nonexistent-no-slash-xyz ===                                           EXIT=1
=== ref: claude/issue-4828-debug-83e64d ===                                     EXIT=1
```

Runs queue repo-wide and routinely started 30–50 minutes after being triggered — by which time the PR had merged and its branch was auto-deleted, leaving nothing for the wildcard to match. PR #4832: opened 03:07:27, run queued 03:08:48, **merged 03:19:43**, fetch ran 03:55:29. Every failing branch is deleted; branches whose PRs stayed open succeeded. `main` never gets deleted, which is why push runs were unaffected.

Checkout now pins `head.sha`. A SHA is fetched exactly, and GitHub keeps a PR's head reachable in the base repo via `refs/pull/<n>/head` after the branch is gone — verified for fork PRs too, which is why the `repository:` input is no longer needed.

## The concurrency rework

The same queue delay meant full suites ran against merged or superseded commits. Two requirements no single group can meet — repo-wide serialization must queue and never cancel, while commits to one PR must cancel and never queue — so both available levels are used:

- **Workflow level:** a per-PR group with `cancel-in-progress`, so a new commit supersedes that PR's earlier run whether queued or mid-suite. Non-PR runs get a unique group per run, so `main` pushes and the deliberate `workflow_dispatch` fan-out never cancel each other.
- **Job level:** the existing repo-wide `browserstack` queue (`cancel-in-progress: false`, `queue: max`), unchanged.

A merged or closed PR now cancels its own run in the first step after the gate admits it, rather than reporting green — no test ran, so nothing may report as passed. This cannot live in the job `if:`, which is evaluated when the run is created, while the PR is still open.

## Verification

- Failing fetch reproduced locally against this repo, and the fix verified — including fork PR head SHAs fetched from the base repo after their branches were deleted.
- The cancel step's three branches executed against live PR data (open / merged / closed-unmerged) with the cancel API stubbed.
- `queue: max` confirmed valid at job level: workflow-level and job-level `concurrency` `$ref` the same schema definition, which includes `queue`.
- actionlint reports the same three pre-existing findings before and after.

## Notes for review

- `pull_request_target` runs the workflow file from `main`, so **this PR's own BrowserStack run still uses the old workflow.** The change only takes effect for PRs opened after it merges.
- Partially addresses #4798: it removes superseded and already-merged runs from the queue, which is where much of the wasted wait comes from. It does not raise the session cap itself (#4816).
- Accepted tradeoff: a suite cancelled mid-run leaves its BrowserStack session to expire on the provider's idle timeout rather than closing cleanly.

author: mashkovd
body:
## Problem

`release-deploy.yaml`'s `bump` job ends in a bare `git push` — no retry, no rebase, and no `concurrency:` group anywhere in the file.

When two release-deploy runs overlap, the loser fails non-fast-forward **after** its image has already been pushed to GHCR. The tag bump never lands in `values.yaml`, so ArgoCD never sees a change and the deploy silently doesn't happen — while the build job reads green. The only symptom is a service quietly running an old image.

This is latent today (overlaps are rare), but it stops being latent immediately: `mctl-telegram` is about to dispatch **two** release-deploys from a single push to main — one for the server image, one for `agent-worker-preview` (same commit, different Dockerfile). Those two would race on every single push.

## Change

Replace the bare push with a bounded rebase-retry loop (5 attempts, jittered backoff).

Why rebasing is safe here: every bump commit rewrites exactly one `image.tag` line in one file. Concurrent bumps for *different* services never conflict textually, and two for the *same* service converge on whichever tag pushed last — which is the correct outcome. A genuine rebase conflict aborts and fails loudly rather than retrying into a mess.

Jitter rather than a flat backoff so two runs that collided once don't wake up together and collide again.

## Also in this PR

`platform-gitops/services/labs/agent-worker-preview/values.yaml` — comment only. Records that `image.tag` is auto-bumped by `mctl-telegram`'s `preview-deploy.yml` and must not be hand-pinned. It *was* hand-pinned until now purely because that workflow only ever dispatched a build for the server image, which left the running worker 4 commits behind `main` (including `fix(agent-worker): suppress adversarial prompt echoes`) with nothing surfacing it.

## Verification

`release-deploy.yaml` is on every mctlhq repo's release path, so this lands and gets confirmed on a normal single-dispatch release **before** the mctl-telegram side goes in. The retry loop must be a no-op on the happy path: first `git push` succeeds, loop exits immediately.

Extracted the step body and checked it with `bash -n`; both edited files parse as YAML.

author: metaspartan
body:
Builds on #26 (decode sub-tile warp2+signfold re-land). Decode-shaped forwards are unchanged; prefill-shaped forwards now also benefit from the sign-folded NVFP4 nibble decode.

## What changes

Instead of falling through to the stock launcher, forwards carrying more than 16 tokens run the same Triton kernel at the **stock geometry**: `BLOCK_SIZE_M` equal to the config's aligned block stride (64), Triton-default `num_warps=4`, `num_stages=3`. At that parameterization the kernel body is exactly the stock kernel's with `_e2m1_signfold` substituted for `_e2m1_inline`.

## Why no output bit can change

The fold is a per-element integer rewrite of the nibble -> fp32 decode — sign applied by ORing `(nibble & 8) << 28` into the integer bit pattern before the single bitcast instead of a float select. It is exhaustively bit-identical for all 16 nibble values, and per-element identity is independent of M. No shape, layout, tile geometry, K-loop, or reduction-sequence change at any batch size: same loads, same masks, same `tl.interleave`/`tl.trans` chain, same `tl.dot` tile shapes, same fp32 accumulation, same single bf16 rounding. This is the same identity argument the decode path carried through two ranked 128/128-exact runs (decode 1.0435 / 1.0401); only the launch shape it applies at broadens.

## Expected effect

Offline, the fold at nw=4 measured 1.02x the stock kernel per launch at decode shapes. The prefill-side fraction is smaller (MMA work grows with M while the B-decode ALU cost per tile is fixed), so this targets a modest prefill/TTFT gain on top of #26's decode gain.

Both launch paths log a one-time `ENGAGED` line, so candidate logs prove each really ran.

<!-- GITZILLA_SUMMARY -->
> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
>
> **Overview**
> This PR extends the NVFP4 sign-folded nibble decode optimization to prefill-shaped MoE forwards in `gainz-kernels` 0.4.0. Decode-shaped paths remain on the prior sub-tile warp2+signfold re-landing, while prefill-shaped forwards (more than 16 tokens) now run the same Triton kernel at stock geometry — `BLOCK_SIZE_M=64`, default `num_warps=4`, and `num_stages=3` — instead of falling through to the stock launcher. The change is concentrated in `Sources/kernels/gainz_kernels/moe_tile.py`, which adds the prefill routing and parameter selection, with a minor version bump in `Sources/kernels/pyproject.toml` and a small regeneration in `Sources/kernels/_build/gainz_backend.py`.

author: mohamedragab23
body: ## Problem The dashboard automatically logs into `https://eg.me.logisticsbackoffice.com` (Rooster) to keep the Cloudflare Access / Okta session alive for shift import, rider search, and the Live-3PL rider sync. When that session is fully dead, the last-resort recovery path (`recoverRoosterAuthFully()`, SRS-012 "Layer 3") performs a real Okta username/password login and reads the resulting email OTP automatically from Gmail. Reported symptom: the dashboard keeps logging in "one after another" and failing, even though the OTP codes correctly arrive on Gmail. ## Root cause `recoverRoosterAuthFully()` had **zero concurrency protection**. Whenever more than one caller hit the dead session around the same time — the "استيراد تلقائي من Rooster" button, the `rooster-keepalive`/`rooster-live-sync` crons, or even just several 401s in one sync's own per-page retry loop — **each caller independently started its own Okta login and triggered its own "send OTP" email**. Okta's `passCode` only validates against the exact `stateToken` of the login attempt that requested it, but the Gmail reader (`gmailOtpReader.ts`) has no per-attempt identifier to key off of (it just searches by sender + subject). So concurrent attempts raced for whichever OTP email happened to be returned first, read the *wrong* one, failed verification with an otherwise-valid, just-arrived code, and immediately retried — triggering yet another competing login and repeating the race indefinitely. This exact failure mode (Okta rate-limit/lockout risk from repeated automated logins) was flagged as **Risk #4** in `docs/SRS012_AUTH_RECOVERY_ENGINE_DESIGN.md`, with a documented mitigation ("single attempt per detected failure... and a cool-down before the next scheduled attempt") that was never actually implemented in code. ## Fix Added `lib/roosterLive/authRecovery/recoveryLock.ts`, reusing the same optional/fail-open Upstash Redis primitives already used by `lib/rooster/roosterCache.ts` and `lib/rooster/roosterQueue.ts` for the newer Rooster features: 1. **Cross-instance single-flight lock** — only one Layer-3 (full Okta + Gmail-OTP) attempt runs at a time. A losing caller waits briefly for the in-flight holder's result instead of starting its own competing Okta login. 2. **Post-attempt cool-down** — after any completed attempt (success or failure), a short window opens during which a new Layer-3 attempt is skipped outright. This throttles rapid *sequential* retries too, not just truly concurrent ones — implementing the Risk #4 mitigation that was missing. Wired into `authRefresh.ts`'s `smartRefreshRoosterAuth` via a new `runGuardedFullRecovery()` helper. Layers 1 (cheap `dhh_token` mint) and 2 (silent Cloudflare Access session replay) are untouched, since they're already idempotent/safe under concurrency — only Layer 3 (the one with the real password + OTP + Gmail race) is guarded. Fail-open by design: with no Upstash Redis configured, behavior is unchanged from before this fix (single-instance/local dev is unaffected). ## Testing - `npx tsc --noEmit` — clean, no errors. - Added `lib/roosterLive/authRecovery/recoveryLock.test.ts` (`node:test`, run via `npm run test:rooster-recovery-lock`) — mocks the Upstash REST wire protocol in-memory (no real Redis/Okta/Gmail needed) and covers: single-flight lock exclusivity, reusing an in-flight holder's cached outcome, waiter timeout without blocking forever, cool-down activation, cool-down natural expiry, and fail-open behavior when Redis isn't configured. All 6 pass. - No existing tests or call sites needed changes — `smartRefreshRoosterAuth`'s external signature/behavior is unchanged except for the new concurrency guard around Layer 3.

author: gdevenyi
body:
`sdoc upgrade` and the daily auto-update both overwrite the CLI in place. That is right for an installed copy and wrong when the code being run is a git working tree.

Running a development copy as `sdoc` means pointing the install path at the clone:

```
~/.sdocs/bin/sdoc -> ~/.sdocs/cli/bin/sdocs-dev.js
~/.sdocs/cli      -> ~/dev/smalldocs/cli
```

`isUrlInstall()` realpath-resolves both sides, so that reports as a URL install and `upgradeCommand()` returns `curl -fsSL .../install | sh`. install.sh then replaces `$SDOCS_HOME/cli` with a fresh tarball, symlink and all. The npm branch is no better from a plain checkout: `npm i -g sdocs-dev@latest` installs a second copy that shadows the one being worked on.

Neither is recoverable by re-running sdoc, and with `autoInstallUpdates` on neither asks. npm is ahead of a working tree most of the time, so the daily check finds an update on nearly every run, self-upgrades, and re-execs.

## Change

`checkoutRoot()` in `cli/lib/update-check.js` looks for a `.git` at or above the realpath-resolved package root, as a file as well as a directory, so worktrees and submodules count. Realpath first, or a symlinked `~/.sdocs/cli` is judged by the symlink rather than by where the code lives.

Every path that would write over the checkout then declines:

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| daily check | prompts, or silently reinstalls | returns silently |
| `sdoc upgrade` | runs the installer | prints `git -C <repo> pull` |
| `sdoc setup` | asks to enable auto-install | skips the question, records `false` |
| `sdoc auto-update on` | records consent | declines, explains why |

The daily check stays quiet rather than printing a notice, because the published version is ahead of a working tree most of the time and the only action it could offer is the one that breaks the copy.

```
$ sdoc upgrade
sdoc 1.15.0 is running from a checkout at /home/gdevenyi/projects/smalldocs
Upgrade it with git, not the installer:
  git -C /home/gdevenyi/projects/smalldocs pull

To replace this copy with the published one, remove the checkout
from your install path first, then run `curl -fsSL https://smalldocs.org/install | sh`.
```

An installed payload has no `.git` above it, so nothing changes for real users. If some unusual layout does put one there, the cost is a refused auto-upgrade, which fails safe.

Five tests in `test/test-update-check.js` cover the repo layout, a worktree `.git` file, npm and install.sh payloads, the symlinked-install-path case, and a missing package root. Full suite passes (1090).

author: sykk
body:
Closes #371. Branches from `main`, independent of #369 and #370. Test and docs
only — no production code changes.

`ircx-plugin`'s permission tests give the sandbox a fetcher with no network
behind it; `ircx-net` has its own loopback tests. The seam is
`network_for_plugins`, and `docs/manual-verification.md` had it down as the last
thing in the plugin section nothing exercises.

**What the seam carries** that neither side can be asked about alone is the
policy's default:

```rust
let policy = FetchPolicy {
    timeout: request.budget.max(Duration::from_millis(1)),
    ..FetchPolicy::default()      // allow_local_addresses: false
};
```

A plugin granted `network-requests` **with `127.0.0.1` in its host list** still
cannot reach the machine it is running on, because the guard is on the resolved
address rather than the grant. That was a security property resting on a struct
update and one `..`. It is now asserted against a port something is really
listening on — a refusal against a dead port would pass for the wrong reason —
and again for a private address.

**The success half** dials `example.com`, `#[ignore]`d like `libera.rs` and
`sasl_probe.rs`, and the body comes back through the sandbox into the plugin's
return value. First time those two have run together.

**No test for the budget against a slow socket**, and the file says why in a
comment rather than leaving a hole. The guard refuses every address a test could
stand a server on, so a server that accepts and never answers is refused before
it can fail to answer. My first draft asserted it anyway and passed in ten
milliseconds — the shape of a test that proves the opposite of its name. The
budget stays covered by `ircx-plugin`'s own tests, against a fetcher they can
make slow.

Four tests run in `cargo test --workspace`; the fifth needs `--ignored`.

author: mohammedali-770
body:
Store-readiness gaps in the app config. **No new dependencies**, so the native module graph is unchanged.

## 1. The app declared push — and could prompt for it — while push is dormant

CLAUDE.md §7 keeps the push stack dormant: the `push`/`expo` integration row is disabled and no credentials exist, so **nothing server-side can deliver a notification**. The app nevertheless shipped the `expo-notifications` config plugin, so the binary carried the iOS push entitlement and Android notification permissions, and Profile → Notifications could request OS permission for it.

Two problems:

- It is a store-review question we cannot answer ("what notifications does this send?" — none, ever).
- An iOS denial is **sticky** (`canAskAgain: false`). Prompting today permanently costs the customer's opt-in for whenever push actually ships.

The plugin is removed and the card is gated behind a new `PUSH_CLIENT_ENABLED` constant. **Nothing is deleted** — the implementation stays whole, so enabling push is a flip + the server row + the plugin, in one change. A test tripwire spells out all four steps so the flip can't be a silent one-liner.

Two design notes:
- The gate is a **build-time constant, not a read of the server flag**: `integration_settings` is fully revoked from the API so the client cannot see the real row, and a network-dependent gate would fail **open** on a timeout — the wrong direction for this decision.
- It's a **hook-free wrapper** around the card, not an early return inside it, so the condition never sits above a hook call.

## 2. Two iOS settings that stall or widen review

| Setting | Was | Now | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ios.config.usesNonExemptEncryption` | absent | `false` | Every TestFlight/App Store upload otherwise stalls on export compliance |
| `ios.supportsTablet` | `true` | `false` | Committed us to an iPad review pass and iPad screenshots for a phone-only layout |

## 3. English-only iOS strings in an Arabic-first product

Adds `expo.locales` with `ar`/`en` Info.plist strings, so the on-device app name and the location prompt appear in Arabic on an Arabic device. The Arabic brand name is the one already in the app ([strings.ts:357](apps/mobile/src/i18n/strings.ts#L357)). Core Expo config — no new package.

## 4. A dead scaffold config shadowing the real app

The repo root carried an `app.json` and `eas.json` that were **not** the real ones (`apps/mobile/` holds those). The root copy had:

- a different slug — `spicy-meal-app` vs the real `spicy-meal`;
- a placeholder EAS projectId — `"spicy-meal-delivery-pos-eas-project-id"`;
- `NSCameraUsageDescription` **and the Android `CAMERA` permission**, for a capability the app does not have — verified, no camera API is used anywhere in `apps/mobile/src` (the only "camera" hits are the map-camera metaphor).

Running `eas` from the repo root would have picked this up. Nothing references either file (checked `package.json`, `.github/workflows/`, `vercel.json`, `vite.config.ts`), so both are deleted.

## Deliberately not included

`usesCleartextTraffic: false` requires the `expo-build-properties` package, which is **not installed**. Adding a native-build plugin cannot be validated without an EAS build (owner-approval-gated), and Android defaults this to `false` from API 28 anyway. Tracked for the store-submission change.

## Verification

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| mobile typecheck | clean |
| web typecheck | clean |
| `npm test` | **1606/1606** (1 new) |
| production build with new config | succeeds |

⚠️ **The native entitlement changes are not verified here.** Only an EAS build exercises iOS entitlements and the Android manifest merge; that is owner-approval-gated. Please run one `preview` build before submission to confirm the push entitlement is genuinely gone.

author: devabdullahs
body:
## Symptom

The Rainbow Six card shows the same fixture twice — once correctly, once as an opponent-less blob:

> **CAG by VARREL** VS **Fnatic** — 14:00
> **CAG by VARREL vs Fnatic** — 15:00 ← ghost

## Cause

Official schedule tabs give a match as a single `Match` cell (`"CAG by VARREL vs Fnatic"`), split on a v/vs token. The pattern was:

```js
raw.split(/\s+v(?:s\.?)?\s*/i)
```

The trailing `\s*` makes the closing whitespace optional, so a bare `v` can match mid-word. `" VARREL"` matches before `" vs "` does:

```
"CAG by VARREL vs Fnatic"  ->  ["CAG by", "ARREL", "Fnatic"]   // 3 parts
"Twisted Minds vs Team Vitality" -> ["Twisted Minds", "Team", "itality"]
```

Three parts fails the `length === 2` check, `splitPair` returns null, and the row hits the placeholder branch — `teamA` becomes the whole label, `teamB` becomes `"Lobby"`.

That pair never matches a tracked fixture in `normalizedOfficialPair`, so the feed inserts a **new** match rather than updating the real one.

## Blast radius

18 live rows, every one a V-initial team, across four tournaments:

| team | tournaments |
|---|---|
| Team Vitality | MLBB WI, MLBB MSC, Honor of Kings, Rocket League |
| Natus Vincere | MLBB Women's International |
| TEAM VAMOS | MLBB Mid Season Cup |
| CAG by VARREL | R6 Siege at EWC 2026 |

None carry `match_details`, so they are pure duplicates.

## Fix

Require whitespace on both sides. `vs.` keeps the loose form — the dot already closes the token and the sheets write `"Weibo Gaming vs.Twisted Minds"` with no space:

```js
raw.split(/\s+(?:vs\.\s*|vs?\s+)/i)
```

A bare `v` now needs real whitespace after it, so `"VARREL"` and `"Vitality"` cannot start a separator. `"Team V.Pro vs X"` is also safe — the dot branch requires `vs.`, not `v.`.

`OFFICIAL_PARSER_VERSION` 11 → 12 so every workbook is re-read once instead of waiting for an unrelated edit.

## Tests

`npm test` — 886 pass, 0 fail. New regression test uses the real R6 rows and asserts no row degrades to a `Lobby` placeholder; the existing Overwatch layout test already covers `vs.` with and without the trailing space.

## Not included

The 18 existing ghost rows are not removed by this change — the fix alters their external id, so the feed writes a correct row and leaves the old one behind. They need a separate cleanup.

author: erichare
body:
## Summary

- commit API-key usage tracking and legacy hash backfill at the authentication-owned transaction boundary, releasing SQLite's writer lock before downstream handlers open an independent write session
- roll back and clear state from failed native/external credential attempts before API-key fallback so bookkeeping cannot commit unrelated authentication state
- cover hashed and legacy keys with tracking enabled/disabled, plus real file-backed SQLite catalog-policy PUTs authenticated only by API key

## Root cause

API-key validation updated usage metadata and only flushed it. On SQLite, that kept the authentication session's write transaction open through the request. Catalog-policy PUT then opened a second write session in the same request and waited on the lock held by the first session, producing a self-deadlock/timeout.

## Transaction semantics

Successful API-key authentication owns and durably records its usage bookkeeping before request handling continues. Failed prior credential attempts are explicitly rolled back and their auth contexts cleared before any fallback that can commit.

## O que o Paulo viu (03/08, com o extrato na mão)

A declaração estava saindo como *"Prestação de Serviços, exceto para o exterior — Não sujeitas ao fator 'r' e tributados pelo Anexo III, **com retenção/substituição tributária de ISS**"* (atividade 15), com o total de R$ 14.174,86.

> "Continua com a MSG acima, e leva errado pro SIMPLES."

Ele tem razão: entrega ao PGDAS-D não se desfaz, e declarar natureza falsa é pior do que não declarar pelo app. O comportamento provisório (transmitir como ISS retido + avisar) **virou bloqueio**.

- `bloqueiosDoPayload` (puro): receita marcada **ISS fixo (SUP)** sem o código oficial da atividade cadastrado **impede** a emissão, com a ação prática — usar **🔎 Atividades declaradas** numa competência já declarada para descobrir o código e, enquanto isso, entregar a competência pelo e-CAC.

- O aviso de SUP saiu (virou bloqueio); o de receita **imune** continua como aviso.

body:
Закрывает #368.

## Проблема

`/privacy` и `/eula` отдавали 200, весь текст был в HTML — и не читался. У корневого `<main>` не было **никакого** `color`: заголовки, абзацы и ячейки таблиц наследовали начальное значение браузера (`canvastext`, чёрный) и давали к фону `#05010f` контраст **1.02:1**. Это ровно те два адреса, которые открывает модератор Маркета.

Причина — оболочка «тёмный бренд» была описана дважды: лендинг задавал её у себя, юридические страницы **повторили половину** (фон через `bodyAttrs` взяли, цвет текста — он живёт в разметке, не в `useHead` — нет).

## Сделано

- `app/config/landingShell.ts` — один источник фона и переднего плана. Пара «фон + текст» неразделима по построению; полупрозрачные варианты фона для шапки лендинга (`/85`, `/95`) переехали сюда же.
- `SHELL_VARS` — мост карты цветов в разметку (инлайн `--legal-*`); `LegalDocument.vue` читает **только** его.
- `tests/landingShell.test.ts` — два гарда: структурный (кто берёт фон, обязан взять и передний план) и численный (контраст по WCAG считается из **отгружаемой** палитры b24ui).

## Замечания разбора, устранённые здесь

| # | Находка | Как проверено |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Тест читал стоковую `tailwindcss/theme.css` — палитру, которой приложение не отгружает (b24ui переопределяет её целиком: стоковый `slate-500` = 4.33, отгружаемый `#93a0b4` = 7.79) | Палитра берётся из темы b24ui через объявленный подпуть `exports` |
| 2 | `SHELL_COLORS` — мёртвая конфигурация: компонент хардкодил цвета мимо неё | Мутация «переписать все цвета на непроходящие» проходила при зелёных тестах; после моста — краснеет |

body:
Hardens `obot::persist`: it returned early for any existing symlink, so a link whose target no longer exists (replaced pool volume, or a link outliving its state) was never repaired, and writes through the dangling link failed with a bare `Permission denied` naming the link rather than the missing target.

Verified against the published image: with $HOME/.codex symlinked to a missing target, `codex:0.146.0` fails with `mkdir: can't create directory '/home/agent/.codex': No such file or directory`; with this change the entrypoint logs `points at missing state; recreating` and proceeds to configure the model. Files are still left alone deliberately.

**Correction to the original description:** I first attributed a crash-looping Codex sandbox to this. That was wrong. Inspecting the actual pool volume showed its persisted state was written by an earlier image whose `agent` user was **uid 1001**, while the current wolfi images use **uid 1000** — so `.codex` existed but was not writable (`drwxr-sr-x 1001`, `config.toml` mode 0600). The symlink was not dangling, and this change does not repair that pod. It remains a real robustness fix on its own merits.

body:
Footer
------
The two link lists were nested inside one grid cell, which stacked them into a single tall column at lg — the reason it read as one long line of links. They are now columns of the footer grid in their own right (four across), and the newsletter has its own full-width row underneath.

Email
-----
Enquiries now send through Resend when RESEND_API_KEY is set, falling back to the SMTP details in secure_settings when it is not. Addresses still come from Settings so the owner can change who is notified without a deploy; where nothing is set they default to info@mistymeadowsresorts.com.

Both transports go through one `deliver()` that never throws — an enquiry is written to the database before mail is attempted, and a mail outage must not lose it or fail the guest's submission. The Resend SDK reports failures in the payload rather than by throwing, so that branch is checked explicitly. The dashboard now says which transport is live.

Offers
------
Gallery takes the Offers slot in the menu. An offer ticked "announce" opens in a panel a moment after any page loads instead, with a link to the enquiry form; /offers stays, linked from the footer and the panel.

The dismissal is keyed on the offer's slug AND a new `announce_version`, so closing it means closing it — while publishing a different offer, or adding one to the version, brings it back for guests who had already dismissed the previous wording. Only the first announced offer still inside its validity window is shown, so an expired one stops appearing on its own.

It is a real dialog: focus moves in, Escape closes, focus returns, and Tab is trapped while it is open. Every localStorage access is guarded — Safari in private mode throws on write, and the fallback is simply to show it again.

Facilities
----------
`facilities` had no `image_id`, so there was no way to put a picture on one. Adds the column, the admin field, and renders it in both the home-page cards and the facilities grid, with the icon carrying the card when there is no photograph. Seeded for the four on-site facilities.

Videos
------
A `videos` content type: upload a file or paste a YouTube/Vimeo link, pick whether it plays on the home page, the gallery, or both. Nothing loads until the guest presses play — an embed's iframe is not in the document at all before then, which matters on a hill-station connection.

The link parser is in `src/lib/video.ts` rather than the client component because its output goes into an `iframe src`; `scripts/check-video-links.mjs` asserts the accepted shapes work and, more importantly, that anything else (including `javascript:`) is rejected and rendered as a plain link instead.

Also: a check-constraint violation on a video with neither source now explains itself, and a missing column reports that a migration has not been run rather than showing raw PostgREST.

author: lorenzhs
body:
## Rationale for this change

Found a few places where untrusted alignments from input files are not properly validated and can lead to excessive allocation sizes / OOMs.

Alignments in the file format are a power-of-two exponent in a `u8`, and `try_from_exponent` only rejects exponents that would overflow a `usize` shift. Satisfying an alignment can require copying the buffer into an allocation of `len + alignment` bytes, so an exponent of 40 on a 4-byte buffer asks the reader for 1 TiB.

This cannot be contained by the caller: Rust aborts via `handle_alloc_error` when an allocation fails rather than unwinding, so it is a process abort rather than an error. Fuzzing the reader found it from two directions, array-tree buffer descriptors and footer segment specs, with exponents from 32 to 61.

- Related: #8819

## What changes are included in this PR?

- `Alignment::MAX_UNTRUSTED` (64K) and `Alignment::try_from_untrusted_exponent`, which rejects anything above it.
- Use it wherever an exponent comes from a file or message: array-tree buffer descriptors, footer segment specs, postscript segments, and IPC buffer messages. The IPC path used the panicking `from_exponent`.
- Regression tests for the array-tree and footer-segment paths, and for the constructor's bounds.

## What APIs are changed? Are there any user-facing changes?

`Alignment` gains a public const and constructor. Reading a file that declares a buffer or segment alignment above 65536 now errors where it previously succeeded. 64K is what some ARM chips use as page alignment, but larger alignments aren't useful here.

I used Claude Code to investigate this and draw up the initial fix and write the tests. The issue itself was found using a libFuzzer-based harness.

author: fkloosterman
body:
Closes #2.

CI has never been green, so `smoke-apply` — the job that actually applies the migration — has never run. It depends on `lint`, and `lint` was failing.

## Lint

Four ruff findings: an unused `# noqa`, a chain of `or s.startswith(...)`, a `[:-1]` that should be `removesuffix`, and a shebang without the executable bit. The `_skip` prefixes are now a tuple constant so the per-prefix comments survive.

## Baseline

Two problems, both found once `smoke-apply` could run:

- The dump has a bare `CREATE SCHEMA tiger;`, but `postgis/postgis:16-3.5` — which CI pins, and which most people run locally — already creates `tiger` and `topology` with `postgis_tiger_geocoder`. A first apply against that image died on "schema tiger already exists".
- Rollback dropped the two tables but left `update_score`, so rollback then re-apply died on "function already exists".

Rather than hand-edit the 3.8 MB dump, `_rewrite()` adjusts two statement kinds as it is replayed: `CREATE SCHEMA` → `CREATE SCHEMA IF NOT EXISTS`, and `CREATE FUNCTION` → `CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION`.

Rollback now also drops `update_score`. It still leaves the PostGIS extensions and the `tiger`/`topology` schemas alone — they are shared infrastructure, and dropping postgis to undo a data load would be disproportionate.

## Verified

Against `postgis/postgis:16-3.5`, the image CI uses:

| | result |
|---|---|
| apply | `ridescoredc` 13834 rows, `crashes_dc` 2005 rows, SRID 4326, `update_score` present |
| rollback | tables and function gone, postgis intact |
| re-apply | 13834 rows, `update_score` present |

### Proposed Changes
Ensures all ReactiveSearch components function correctly under React's `StrictMode` (in development mode) by making Redux component registration resilient to double-mounting cycles:

1. **Mount Safeguard (`componentDidMount`):** Added a validation step in `ComponentWrapper.js` and `DynamicRangeSlider.js` that checks if a component is registered in the Redux store. If missing (e.g. unmounted/removed due to StrictMode double-rendering), it automatically re-registers and re-binds watchers.
2. **Fixed Unmount Cleanup Typo (`ComponentWrapper.js`):** Corrected a typo in `componentWillUnmount` (`this.$timestamp` -> `this._timestamp`), resolving component leaks in the Redux store on real component unmounts.
3. **Map State to Props:** Added `components` state map in `DynamicRangeSlider`'s `mapStateToProps` to enable mount-time existence checks.

### Linked Issues
- Fixes #2314 (`bug: components fail to function properly when wrapped in StrictMode`)

### Checklist
- [x] Describe the proposed changes and how it'll improve the library experience.
- [x] Please make sure that there are no linting errors in the code.
- [x] Add a demo video/gif/screenshot to explain how did you test the fix.

### Improvements to the Library Experience
- **StrictMode Compatibility:** Resolves the critical development-mode bug where keystrokes fail to fire queries, URL parameters vanish, and results fail to display when components are wrapped in React's `<StrictMode>`.
- **Zero Resource Leaks:** Ensures Redux store properly cleans up components and queries on genuine unmounts by fixing the timestamp property typo.

- The build block still gave `go build -o den ./cmd/den` and a hand-written `-ldflags` line with a
  `v0.1.0` that never existed. Replaced by `make build`, with why it is the only documented way.
- The "stale artifacts" section warned that `HANDOFF.md` claims Plan 2 is unexecuted — that HANDOFF
  was rewritten in #32, so the warning had outlived what it warned about. Replaced by what is
  genuinely stale now: the **dated** handoffs and the reports under `.superpowers/sdd/`, several of
  which still assert `sbx` is not installed on this machine.

## `internal/nest/resolve.go` — the same assertion, in live code

The comment on `configDirToken` justified leaving spec §14.1's hypothesis **A11** (that sbx mounts a
workspace at the same absolute path inside the VM as on the host) unverified with "it cannot be
settled here (sbx is not installed on this machine)".

`sbx` is installed — `/opt/homebrew/bin/sbx`, v0.35.0, three real smokes. A11 is open because no
smoke has aimed at workspace mount paths, which is a different reason and the honest one. The
hypothesis itself is untouched: this corrects why it stands, not whether it does.

`make test` green (699 functions, 13 packages), `make lint` clean. `TestHandoffNamesThePortsArgumentAsImplemented`,
which locks `HANDOFF.md` against `den ports`' declared argument, still passes.

## The tag intentionally predates this commit

`v1.0.0` points at `e964606`, one commit before this one. So a checkout of the tag reads the
**pre-tag** entry points: a `CLAUDE.md` whose build block still shows the old `-ldflags` line, and a
`HANDOFF.md` §0 that says *"v1 n'est pas taguée"*.

That is deliberate and stays. Issue #10's first acceptance criterion is about the **README**, and
that fix is inside `e964606` — a checkout of `v1.0.0` builds with `make build` and answers
`den v1.0.0`. `CLAUDE.md` and `HANDOFF.md` are agent-facing *current state* documents, not release
artifacts, and HANDOFF's own preamble already establishes that everything but the spec describes the
state on its date. Moving a pushed tag would cost more than the inconsistency it removes.

## On the three issues closed by hand

#21 and #30 were verified against their commits. **#27 was verified against the shipped code**,
since it is the only one of the three that changed behaviour rather than a message: `internal/cli/sh.go:57-76`
passes `stopped` through to the gate rather than re-deriving it, with the comment naming why the
stopped branch waits instead of reading once, and `sh_test.go` carries
`TestShWaitsForTheGateWhenItStartsAStoppedSandbox` and
`TestShPollsRatherThanReadsOnceWhenItStartsAStoppedSandbox`. A citation would not have shown that.

author: thedarkphantom
body:
## Problem

The v2 sidebar row folded two different things into one `Merging` label:

```ts
: isMerging || prState === "merged" || prState === "closed"
  ? { label: "Merging", icon: "merging", ... }
```

`isMerging` is correct — it only fires while a source-control action is actually in flight. The two `prState` disjuncts are the bug: a PR that has *finished* merging, or was closed unmerged, read as still merging for the rest of the thread's life. The branch also sat above `working`, so a settled outcome masked live activity.

## Fix

Split the branch three ways. In-flight keeps `Merging` with the branch icon. A merged PR reads `Merged` (violet, git-merge icon) and a closed one reads `Closed` (red, pull-request-closed icon), matching the colours `settledPrHoverColorClass` already uses for those states.

Both settled labels drop below `Working` and below an unseen completion, so an outcome no longer outranks activity. An in-flight action still wins over a previous PR's outcome, because a thread that landed one PR and is pushing the next should show the live action.

The decision moved out of the JSX ternary into `resolveSidebarChangeRequestStatus` in `Sidebar.logic.ts`, which is pure and tested.

## Notes

v1 is unaffected: `resolveThreadStatusPill` never emits `Merging` at all, so the `Merging` entry in the shared `ThreadStatusPill` union and `THREAD_STATUS_PRIORITY` is vestigial. Left alone rather than widened with labels nothing constructs.

## Verification

`vp test run apps/web/src/components/Sidebar.logic.test.ts` (110 passed, 5 new), targeted lint, and `tsgo --noEmit -p apps/web/tsconfig.json`.

author: syynth
body:
Part of #2080 — the mount only, per the issue's 2026-08-03 ruling scope fence (see below for what's not reachable yet).

## What / how

`#2080`'s ruling found the issue's original framing (a virtual/embedded module tree distinct from tree-is-universe discovery) was solving a problem `Environment` (#1306) had already solved: it generalizes `the-tree-is-the-universe` to `the-environment-is-the-universe` (`{ local module tree } + { resolved external module set }`), addressing sources by string key into a hash-addressed manifest — so native module identity derives from those keys with no bespoke resolution needed.

This PR is the whole mechanism the ruling describes:

- `Project::load` (`crates/internal/brink-environment/src/lib.rs`) now calls a new `mount_stdlib` after assembling a project's own sources, merging a small embedded `STDLIB_SOURCES` table (currently just `std/conventions/screenplay.brink`) into the same manifest/content-store every project source lives in.
- The source is embedded at **compile time** via `include_str!` (not a runtime filesystem read), because `@brink-lang/web`'s wasm build has no filesystem — the ruling's explicit instruction.
- A project source already present at the same key wins over the embedded copy rather than being silently clobbered (defensive; `std/` is a reserved-by-convention path so a real collision isn't expected).
- The stdlib ships as **source** in the manifest, not as a `resolved_deps` entry — that field stays reserved for #1093's compiled per-module artifacts (the ruling's explicit correction).
- No `FileId` question arises — `FileId`s are downstream of the manifest, minted the same way regardless of which key contributed a given source.

## Scope fence — what is and is not reachable

This is the **mount only**. After this PR:

- Every compiled `Environment` (native or ink entry alike) has `std/conventions/screenplay.brink`'s real source present in its manifest, and it participates in native module resolution exactly like any project file at that path (`brink_db::modules::native_module_path` mints its identity the same way).
- **Not reachable yet:** nothing in the mounted module is marked `pub`, and no confinement rule scopes what a project's own `use` may reach into it. A real `use std::…` importing an item out of this module still needs **#1582**'s pub marker and **#2167**'s closure-scoped confinement — neither built here.
- Also untouched: the same 2026-08-03 ruling separately records `[project] elements` → `conventions` as an owed (breaking) config rename, needing its own deprecation path and reader sweep — out of scope for this PR, tracked as a distinct, larger piece of work.

Docs updated in this PR to reflect the mount landing: `std/README.md`, `docs/prose-dialect-spec.md` §3.5, `docs/native-feature-status.md`, and a new `docs/decision-log.md` entry.

## Tests

Added to `crates/internal/brink-environment/src/lib.rs`:
- `stdlib_screenplay_preset_is_mounted_into_every_environment` — the mounted text is present and looks right.
- `stdlib_mount_is_present_for_a_native_and_an_ink_entry_alike` — mounts unconditionally regardless of entry dialect.
- `a_project_source_at_the_stdlib_key_wins_over_the_embedded_copy` — the override-safety rule.
- `mounted_stdlib_compiles_cleanly_alongside_an_ordinary_native_project` — exercises the actual `brink_environment::compile` production path (not just the manifest), proving the mounted module introduces zero diagnostics.

Updated 4 existing tests whose exact `source_keys()` assertions the new unconditional mount key affects (`identical_content_is_stored_once_but_keyed_twice`, `source_keys_are_sorted`, `native_universe_is_the_whole_tree_excluding_config`, `ink_universe_follows_the_include_graph`).

**Regression-tested per house rule 20a**: reverted the `mount_stdlib` call, reran `cargo test -p brink-environment --lib` — all 6 new/updated tests failed as expected (verified output), then restored the fix and confirmed all 36 tests green again.

## Reachability

The real, sole production compile path (`brink_environment::compile`, used by both `brink-cli/src/main.rs` and `brink-web/src/compile.rs`) now sees the mounted stdlib source on every call to `Project::load` — proven end-to-end by `mounted_stdlib_compiles_cleanly_alongside_an_ordinary_native_project`, which drives a plain native project through `compile()` and asserts the mounted module introduces no diagnostics. There is no user-facing `use std::…` surface yet (see scope fence above) — this PR's reachable surface is "every compiled project's `Environment` now contains the stdlib source," not "a project can import it."

## Gate (ref e44f1fab3, shared `CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/tmp/pump-cargo-target-brink`)

```
cargo fmt --all -- --check                              # clean
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings    # clean
cargo nextest run --workspace                            # 7547 tests run: 7547 passed, 11 skipped
cargo test -p brink-test-harness --test oracle_snapshots -- --nocapture
  CASES: 366 pass / 8 fail / 398 total
  EPISODES: 5608 pass / 1010 mismatch / 2 missing
```

`RATCHET_EPISODE_COUNT` read directly from `crates/internal/brink-test-harness/tests/oracle_snapshots.rs` at this branch's merge-base (origin/main @ 4b4862788) is **5607**, not 5608 as an earlier briefing claimed — verified by reading the file, not trusting the quoted number. The observed 5608 pass is unaffected by this PR: `oracle_snapshots.rs` drives its own harness (`brink_test_harness::corpus::compile_and_explore_from_ink`) directly through `brink-driver`, never through `brink_environment::compile`, so this PR's mount cannot move that count in either direction — 5608 is origin/main's pre-existing baseline, ratchet holds (5608 ≥ 5607).

Changeset: `@brink-lang/web` patch (`.changeset/issue-2080-stdlib-manifest-mount.md`) — every wasm compile now sees one extra mounted source key, compiled as an ordinary native module.

author: 2600hz-oscillator
body:
## The red row, and what it is not

`main @ 7d048c01` ([run 30842128606](https://github.com/2600hz-oscillator/patchtogether.live/actions/runs/30842128606), shard 1/6):

```
Error: analogLogicMaths: every drivable input perturbed the observed output
  analogLogicMaths.attB_cv (type=cv) → sum (type=cv): NO observable delta —
  C(rms=0.137±0.053 zc=0±0 cent=95±5Hz crest=1.18±0.58)
  P(rms=0.137±0.073 zc=0±0 cent=95±4Hz crest=1.18±0.57)
  | Δμ(rms=0.000 peak=0.004 …)
```

> **This did not make main red.** `behavioral-coverage` is `continue-on-error: true` and is in neither the `ci` umbrella's `needs:` nor its failing `if`. The umbrella failed on `webgl-attest: cancelled` — a 5-minute job timeout — fixed separately in #1335.

**It is not #1330.** That signature requires control and perturbed to be identical *including their ± dispersion*. Every failing row here differs on every dispersion figure (`±0.053` vs `±0.073`, `±5` vs `±4`, `±0.58` vs `±0.57`) and `peak Δμ = 0.004 ≠ 0`. Distinct buffers — the perturbation landed.

**It is not the module.** All four ports perturb `sum` reproducibly, 3/3 locally. And `sum = tanh(a·attA + b·attB)`, so `attB_cv` scaling `b` cannot be a no-op while `b` carries signal.

**It is the instrument.** The sweep could not resolve the effect it asserts.

## Root cause

ALM is a pure CV utility, so `buildContextEdges` fans `BUGGLES.smooth` into every primary cv input not under test — **the control's entire observable output is a random walk** — and the generic `cv` test source is *a second BUGGLES*. Both sides randomized.

BUGGLES seeds its PRNG from the node id, so the value *sequence* is deterministic; but the woggle scheduler runs off `setTimeout`, so **which** values are in effect during the 5 reads is pure main-thread timing. The walk's correlation time (~1/0.6 Hz ≈ 1.7 s) is **30× longer than the 50 ms scope window**, so each window's rms samples the walk's position rather than a property of the module.

This mechanism is already written up in this file on `BEHAVIORAL_PORT_TEST_SOURCE['adsr.release']`, including its CI symptom — a Δμrms straddling the floor across ~35 main runs. ALM is the same class.

The signature in the CI log: the **control arm**, which contains no test input and is identical in construction, read `rms = 0.058 / 0.078 / 0.079 / 0.096 / 0.137 / 0.164 / 0.166 / 0.175` across attempts. Locally it is `0.086` or `0.166–0.175`, reproducible to 3 dp across 7 runs including under load. The instrument's *zero point* is environment-dependent — "the instrument reads differently here", not "the result is genuinely different here".

And the failing port **moved between two consecutive attempts on the same commit in the same job** (`.a` → `.attB_cv`), which is what a coin flip near a floor looks like.

## The measurement that settled it — and the worse bug it found

The perturbation edge is now omittable via `BEHAVIORAL_NEGATIVE_CONTROL=1`, which re-runs the control patch as *both* arms, so every printed Δ is the instrument's own control-vs-control scatter.

`BEHAVIORAL_DECIDING_METRICS` already *instructs* you to take exactly this measurement ("measure the control-vs-control spread per metric, then name only the metrics whose floor sits ABOVE that spread") — but the harness offered no way to take it, so those numbers had to come from hand-editing the file, and the sandwich could not be re-checked later.

Run against `analogLogicMaths` on main, it caught something worse than the red row:

```
attB_cv, NO perturbation present → Δμ(rms=0.0104) → FIRED the 0.01 rmsMean floor → PASS
```

**A false positive in a coverage gate** — "this port perturbs the output", asserted about a patch with no perturbation in it — and nothing in the ordinary output distinguishes it from a real pass. 1 in 12 rows, on an idle machine.

## Fix

Replace both random sources with deterministic ones:

- **CV context → an 80 Hz sine.** ~4 full cycles inside every 50 ms read, so the window statistics are the same no matter *when* the window opens — load-independent by construction rather than by tuning. This is the CV-domain form of CLAUDE.md's "count frames, don't wait ms": the defect is a source whose correlation time exceeds the observation window. Added as a **module-level** `BEHAVIORAL_PORT_CONTEXT_SOURCE` entry, with a module-level fallback in the lookup matching the existing `thresholdsFor` / `decidingMetricsFor` idiom.
- **Test source → a DC** (square LFO at the 0.01 Hz rate floor = constant for 50 s), the same remedy `adsr.release` / `tomtom` / `clap` already use.

`+1 V` not `−1 V` on the attenuverter CVs on purpose: −1 V makes `a·attA + b·attB` cancel exactly and the output degenerate to digital silence. Bigger delta, worse test — every metric on a `0.000` buffer is trivially "different", which is indistinguishable from the module having died.

**No exemption is added.** `attB_cv` is a live port and stays gated.

## Measured (local, N=3 each; `rmsMean` floor = 0.01)

| port | control rms ± range | Δμrms | margin |
|---|---|---|---|
| **before** | | | |
| `a` | 0.086 ± 0.067 | 0.075 / 0.074 / 0.074 | 7.4× |
| `b` | 0.086 ± 0.074 | 0.026 / 0.026 / 0.023 | 2.3× |
| `attA_cv` | 0.166 ± 0.144 | 0.023 / 0.024 / 0.029 | 2.3× |
| `attB_cv` | 0.166 ± 0.144 | 0.017 / 0.017 / 0.017 | **1.7×** ← noise reached 0.0104 |
| **after** | | | |
| `a` | 0.333 ± 0.006 | 0.167 / 0.163 / 0.165 | 16.5× |
| `b` | 0.334 ± 0.006 | 0.165 / 0.163 / 0.165 | 16.4× |
| `attA_cv` | 0.576 ± 0.010 | 0.145 / 0.146 / 0.145 | 14.5× |
| `attB_cv` | 0.576 ± 0.010 | 0.145 / 0.144 / 0.147 | 14.5× |

Control dispersion falls **11–14×** (from ~0.8× the mean to ~0.018×) and the asserted deltas rise 2–8×. The two populations are a real sandwich now, not adjacent.

## Negative control, both directions

| | rows | result |
|---|---|---|
| perturbation present | 12 | **12/12 PASS**, Δμrms 0.144–0.167 |
| perturbation removed | 12 | **12/12 "NO observable delta"**, Δμrms 0.000–0.001, suite correctly RED |

Zero false positives, zero false negatives — against 1 false positive in 12 before.

## Load

Under 8 CPU burners on a 10-core box the fixed harness reads control `0.334±0.006` / `0.576±0.010` — **unchanged from idle to 3 dp**. Honest caveat: that synthetic load did *not* reproduce the original red (the old harness still passed under it, with visibly more scatter: attA_cv Δμrms 0.029→0.044). Shell busy-loops are not a 10-shard CI runner's starvation profile. The load-dependence evidence is the CI control-arm spread above plus the in-file `adsr.release` precedent, not this experiment.

## Verification

- typecheck: 3241 files, **0 errors**
- `behavioral-observation-window.spec.ts`: 7/7
- `scripts/test-ledger.test.ts`: 6/6 · `behavioral-smoke-subset.test.ts`: 3/3
- attest hashes **unchanged** — collab `e81297bc…`, webgl `ec6f221a…`, both still resolve to their committed attestations
- `analogLogicMaths` is **not** in the required `behavioral-smoke` subset → informational lane only

CI wall-time delta: **none** (same spawn/read plan, same port count).

Labelled `behavioral` so the otherwise-skipped full sweep runs on this PR.

Refs #1330 (a different bug — this is not an instance of it).

author: suchanek
body:
`.mcp.json` serves `dockg` and `pycodekg` MCP servers, which need those CLIs on `PATH` — but neither package was declared anywhere in this repo. A fresh clone got dead MCP servers with no hint why.

## Why a Poetry group and not an extra

They are tools this repo *runs*, not libraries it imports — nothing under `src/` imports `doc_kg` or `pycode_kg`.

Extras are **published metadata**: putting siblings in `[project.optional-dependencies]` means `pip install memory-kg[...]` pulls sibling KG packages into a stranger's environment, and couples the whole fleet's dependency resolution together. A Poetry group is maintainer-facing — locked and installable, but never written into the wheel.

```
poetry install --with kg      # dockg / pycodekg CLIs into .venv/bin
poetry install                # default: group is optional, skipped
```

## Verification

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Wheel `METADATA` vs. previous build | **byte-identical** — zero `Requires-Dist` / `Provides-Extra` changes |
| `poetry install --with kg` | installs doc-kg 0.21.1 + pycode-kg 0.21.4 |
| `poetry install` (default) | both skipped |
| `poetry check --lock` | passes |
| Tests | 393 passed |

**No version bump or release needed** — the published artifact is unchanged, so a release would ship a version differing in nothing a consumer can observe.

author: abhattacherjee
body:
Patch release. Scope is a single issue: **#287**.

## What ships

**`/dev-test` works from any project again.** It resolved its script through the caller's cwd (`cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"` then `./scripts/test-dev-skill.sh`), so invoking it from any repo other than obsidian-brain — the normal case, since you install the dev plugin while working on something else — resolved *that* project's root and failed. It now locates the checkout explicitly and prints which one it used:

1. `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`, if that toplevel carries the sentinel `scripts/test-dev-skill.sh`
2. the registered directory-source install from `known_marketplaces.json`
3. a loud failure naming both routes

The plugin cache is deliberately not a fallback: `test-dev-skill.sh` derives its source tree from `dirname "$0"`, so a cache-resolved script would copy the cache onto itself — a no-op that prints a full success transcript.

**Seven failure modes in `scripts/test-dev-skill.sh` that reported success while doing nothing, or narrated an outcome that did not happen.** Full detail in the changelog; the two that could destroy data:

- `restore` promoted a partial or corrupt `.bak` over a healthy cache and printed `Original vX.Y.Z restored.` at exit 0 — reproduced during review destroying two real skill files. Backups are now built out of place and renamed into position only after the copy completes, so a `.bak` that exists is complete by construction.
- A checkout with an **empty** `skills/` passed the sentinel check, leaving the install loop's glob unmatched: it narrated a copy that never happened, created a directory literally named `*` in the plugin cache, published a `.bak` that blocks the next install, and exited 0.

`install` and `restore` now return distinct exit codes for distinct states, and `/dev-test` branches its reporting on them rather than unconditionally announcing success.

## Version

No bump in this release — `plugin.json`, `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json`, and `docs/architecture/architecture.json` already declared `3.4.1` from develop's post-3.4.0 pre-bump. This commit only stamps the changelog heading. All five version surfaces verified in agreement.

## Verification

- Suite **2306 → 2409** on this branch's scope; green locally and in CI.
- Every guard mutation-tested — deleted or inverted, re-run, and confirmed a *named* test fails for the right reason. Ten defects were found this way that had passed the entire suite.
- Reviewed to convergence by four Claude dimensions over four rounds, then an adversarial Claude↔Gemini pass: 7 findings, 7 cross-model confirmed, 0 unconfirmed, 0 rejected.
- Dogfooded end-to-end from two foreign repos with the live plugin cache checksummed before and after — unchanged.

## Milestone

**v3.4** closes at 1/1 with this release. #214 (vault-doctor resumed-session false positives) was moved to the backlog as it is not in scope here.

## Deferred

**#293** parks three residuals reviewers explicitly judged non-blocking: a concurrent-install `mv`-nesting TOCTOU, and two unpinned test paths.

author: kanylbullen
body:
CI builds and smoke-tests but has never linted. That is how 36 violations accumulated unnoticed — and it means #79 invited contributions into a repo that could not tell a newcomer whether their code was clean.

Turning lint on outright fails every PR until the backlog is cleared. Clearing the backlog myself would empty the `good first issue` label we just filled ([#80](https://github.com/kanylbullen/xupersplit/issues/80) is exactly those violations). So neither.

## The baseline

`eslint --suppress-all` records today's violations in `eslint-suppressions.json` — 36 across 12 files, `react-hooks/set-state-in-effect` and `react/no-unescaped-entities`. The run passes. **Anything new fails.**

Verified three ways, not assumed:

| Scenario | Exit |
|---|---|
| New error in a file with no baseline entry | **1** |
| A 15th unescaped apostrophe in a file baselined at 14 | **1** |
| Untouched baseline | 0 |

Warnings (9 today) stay advisory and don't gate — matching how the repo already treats them.

## Placement

The step runs **before** the build, so a lint failure costs seconds instead of the full Playwright cycle. It sits inside the existing `build-and-smoke` job rather than as its own, so current branch protection covers it with no settings change. Split it out later if you want it reported as a separate check.

## For contributors

`CONTRIBUTING.md` now explains that the baseline is a baseline and not a pardon, and that fixing a suppressed violation means running `npx eslint . --prune-suppressions` and committing the result — otherwise the entry lingers and silently re-permits the same mistake.

author: nibsbin
body:
Closes #1180.

## What was wrong

An island's payload was reachable from no op channel: `text` carries one `ISLAND_SLOT` per island and nothing more, `lines` the `Island` kind, `marks` neither. So an island changed exactly two ways — cascade removal, and whole-value `install` — and every table or image edit took the second. `install` is field-wide value semantics, so it dropped every identity anchor in the field, including anchors on prose the edit never touched. The anchor guarantee that motivates the op vocabulary held for every edit except the one class the vocabulary could not express.

This is not a new principle. `LineOp::SetContinues`'s own doc already says a hard break "is unreachable op-wise and falls back to a whole-`install` (losing that edit's identity anchors)", and that this is why the op exists. Islands are the same argument at the scale of a table.

## What this adds

**`IslandOp`, two ops.** `Set { island }` replaces the entry its `id` names, in place. Not props-only: `island_type` and `loss` move with it, so the write path can state the loss class a props edit changes rather than silently carrying a stale one. An `id` no island carries is `UnknownIslandId`, never a silent no-op — swallowing it would leave the store on the old value with the caller believing it committed, which is the defect the issue opens with. `Insert { at, island }` places the slot and its backing entry in one op, so the orphan the text channel rejects (`IslandSlotInInsert`) is unrepresentable here rather than caught after the fact. Removal keeps working through the delta's cascade and needs nothing.

**A pinned stage order.** delta → islands → lines → marks, and it is a coordinate contract. The issue said the ordering "falls out of the existing rule"; it does not. `LineOp::SetKind { kind: Island }` validates the kind against the segment as it stands, so the slot must exist before line ops run — which forces islands *between* the delta and the lines, not merely somewhere before the terminal `normalize`. A block island is consequently one bundle of three channels: the delta's `\n` opens the line, the island op fills it, `SetKind` tags it. `LineOp::Split` cannot open that line, since line ops run later.

**The errors the issue named none of.** `UnknownIslandId`, `IslandIdCollision`, `EmptyIslandId`, `IslandInsertOutOfRange` — the op-time twins of the invariants `normalize` does not repair, on the same pattern as `AnchorIdCollision` / `EmptyAnchorId`.

**`ChangeBundle` replaces the three positional op arguments** on `Content::apply_field_change`, `Card::apply_body_change`, and `Card::apply_field_richtext_change`, so channel five would be additive at every call site. `change_bundle_from_value` returns it in place of its tuple. `Default` means a caller names only the channels it uses.

On the WASM surface the channel is purely additive: `applyChange` gains an optional `islandOps`, and a bundle that omits it behaves as before.

## Deliberately not here

- **No validate gate on the island an op carries.** Cell-mark ranges and props depth in a caller-supplied island can produce content failing `validate()` — but `install` and `MarkOp::Add { kind: Unknown { attrs } }` already carry opaque caller payload unchecked, so gating only this op would be inconsistent with its siblings rather than a fix. Worth one decision across all three doors.
- **Cell anchors stay out of scope**, as `Invariant::AnchorIdCollision`'s doc already declares. Value semantics over the island entry means a cell edit drops any anchor inside a cell — this issue's defect one level in, now a written boundary rather than an oversight.
- **`loss` is still authored, not derived** (#903, #1050). The op carries it rather than deriving it, matching `install`, so the deferral is unchanged rather than deepened.

## Docs

`DOCUMENT_STORAGE.md` § Island-id determinism gains the edit-time minter: `IslandOp::Insert` carries a caller-supplied id, and the never-ambient rule binds that producer too — continue the positional `isl-{n}` sequence, never a UUID or a clock reading. Import purity is untouched, since export drops island ids. The unreleased migration guide and its index row cover the `ChangeBundle` break and the new channel.

## Verification

- `cargo test --workspace`: 50 test binaries, 0 failures. 8 new unit tests in `crates/content/src/ops.rs` and a new property (`apply_island_ops_preserves_validate`).
- `./scripts/build-wasm.sh --ci` then `vitest run`: 224 passed, including two new `applyChange` island tests; `.d.ts` typechecks clean.
- Clippy warning count unchanged from baseline (58, all pre-existing).
