author: johnnymo87
body:
A peer session (W2a) established that `bun:sqlite`'s busy-wait runs on the serve's **main JS thread**, so `busy_timeout=5000` means a contended write freezes the event loop for up to 5 s. That isn't merely *similar* to the "alive but frozen" wedge signature this canary exists to catch — it's a mechanism that produces it exactly.

## Why this wasn't already covered

At first glance it was: the canary already captured `/proc/PID/wchan` **and** per-thread wchan. But it captured a **snapshot**, and a snapshot of a wait channel can't discriminate. Sampling a healthy serve by hand returns `0` (running) or `do_epoll_wait` depending purely on when you look — I hit both in five samples.

What discriminates is whether the loop *ever* returns to epoll across a window:

| main-thread wchan across ~2 s | reading |
|---|---|
| `do_epoll_wait` | loop free — an HTTP stall is request **serialization**, not a blocked loop |
| `hrtimer_nanosleep`, never returning to epoll | SQLite busy handler spinning |

The peer measured the second case directly: `hrtimer_nanosleep` continuously from 0.2 s to 3.4 s of a 4 s contended write, never once back to epoll.

## Change

Sample the main thread **20× at 100 ms** into `wchan-series`. **Zero added wedge-time** — it runs inside the 2 s window `cpu-io-split` was already sleeping through.

`/proc/<tid>/syscall` would be richer, but yama `ptrace_scope=1` on this host makes it unreadable; `wchan` is readable. Worth knowing before reaching for the wrong file.

## Two incidental fixes, same spirit as the rest of this spine

- The block printed `interval=2s` as an **asserted constant**. Real elapsed is **~2.11 s**, and the utime/stime delta is divided by that number. Now measured and emitted.
- The loop uses a plain shell counter rather than `seq`. `coreutils` is on the canary PATH, but `lbe2` was a silent no-op caused by exactly one assumed-present binary — cheapest fix is to depend on nothing new.

## Verification

Against the **built artifact**, not the Nix source: `systemctl cat` → `ExecStart` → grep the store path. `nixos-rebuild` rebuilt only the canary derivation; serve pool `NRestarts=0`, all four members still active. Already deployed.

author: esaugomez31
body: > ### Stacked on the contacts PR > > This branch sits on top of `fix--contact-transactions-self-custodial`, because it reuses the `useSelfCustodialTransactionFragments` hook introduced there. Review that one first. ## Summary The home screen only ever fed the unseen-transaction badge with custodial data: `transactions` came from `me.defaultAccount` and the seen state was keyed by the custodial account id. A self-custodial account has no `me` behind those, so `useTransactionSeenState` saw an empty list, `hasUnseenBtcTx` and `hasUnseenUsdTx` stayed false, and a received payment produced no bubble on the currency pill and no amount under the balance. This sources both inputs per account type, and stores the seen state where a self-custodial account can actually keep it. It also fixes the badge announcing the same payment again on every launch, reported on this PR after the first round of review. The seen state was only written once the display window had elapsed, so closing the app before that lost the write and the next launch announced the same transaction again. Closes blinkbitcoin/blink-wip#925 ## Changes **Feeding the badge** - `app/components/unseen-tx-amount-badge/use-unseen-tx-badge-state.ts` (new): owns everything the home screen needs for the badge. It builds the custodial list from the home query, maps the wallet's transactions through `useSelfCustodialTransactionFragments` for a self-custodial account, and returns the badge, the auto-seen wiring and the visibility flags. Mapping also primes the Apollo cache, which is what lets the transaction detail behind the badge load when it is opened from home. - `app/screens/home-screen/home-screen.tsx`: calls that hook once instead of assembling the badge from five separate hooks inline. The screen was already at the `max-statements` ceiling, and this keeps it under it. **Persisting the seen state** `txLastSeen` is a client-only Apollo field, and the cache persistor only restores from disk when there is an auth token (`app/graphql/client.tsx`). A self-custodial account resolves that token to `""` by design, so its seen state was never restored: on every cold start `lastSeenBtcId` was `""`, the newest transaction always compared as unseen, and the badge fired again for a payment that could be weeks old. - `app/store/persistent-state/tx-last-seen.ts` (new) plus schema 16 (`txLastSeenByAccountId`): the same per-account device store already used for display currency, language and quiz progress. - `app/hooks/use-transaction-seen-state.ts`: custodial keeps using the Apollo cache; self-custodial reads and writes the device store. It also stops falling back to the cached custodial home query, which for a self-custodial account is another account's data. - The hook now takes an explicit `isSelfCustodial` from its caller rather than deriving it, so the flag that picks which transactions are fed in is the same one that picks where they are stored. Deriving it internally meant a second, looser predicate (`accountType` only) that could only agree with the caller's `useActiveWallet().isSelfCustodial` (`accountType` + wallet status) by accident. - `transaction-history-screen.tsx` and `transaction-detail-screen.tsx` move to the same signature. Both derived their `accountId` from `me.defaultAccount.id`, which is `""` for a self-custodial account, so without this they would have keyed the seen state differently from home and marking a transaction seen in the history would not have cleared the badge. **Announcing a transaction once** Marking seen used to be deferred to the end of the display window, 5000ms plus the 180ms exit animation, and the effect cleanup cleared both timers. Any exit before that point cancelled the write: losing focus, unmounting, or closing the app. On a self-custodial account the window effectively started later still, because the transaction list only arrives once the SDK has synced, so a short visit was enough to never persist anything. - `use-incoming-badge-auto-seen.ts`: marks the transaction seen the moment the badge reaches the screen, and holds what it announced until the exit animation has played. Marking seen empties the unseen state the badge is derived from, so the announcement is what the screen renders from while it is up. The guard is keyed by transaction rather than by currency, so the one already shown never comes back while a second receive in the same wallet is still announced, and a live announcement is never overwritten: with both wallets unseen, each waits its turn instead of the second replacing the first a frame later. - `use-unseen-tx-badge-state.ts`: resolves the badge amount, id and direction from the announcement while one is live, keeps the announced currency reading unseen so the wallet row dot stays lit for the whole window, and parks the outgoing badge behind an incoming one, which would otherwise run its cycle unpainted and still mark its own transaction seen when it hid. - `use-unseen-tx-amount-badge.ts`: exposes `navigateToTransaction(txid)` instead of a press handler bound to the newest unseen transaction, which by the time the badge can be pressed no longer exists. ## Test plan - `yarn jest` on the badge hooks plus the home screen: 117 passed, **100% statements, branches, functions and lines** on the two hooks this rewrites - Self-custodial coverage exercises the real logic, not mocks: cold start with an empty store, a stored id treated as already seen, marking seen on device instead of the cache, and never reading the custodial cache - Each fix is pinned by a test that fails when the fix alone is reverted, so none of them pass by coincidence - `__tests__/screens/home.spec.tsx`: integration cases that differ only by `allTransactions`, asserting the badge appears for a received self-custodial transaction and stays absent when the wallet has none - Scoped run over the transitive consumers (hooks, home, transaction history, transaction detail, persistent state, contacts): 14 suites, 227 passed - `yarn tsc --noEmit` and `eslint` on the changed files: clean - Device (Android), against the exact scenario reported here: received 100 sats on a self-custodial account, the badge appeared with `+$0.06` and the white dot on the Bitcoin pill, the app was killed within 2 seconds of it appearing, well inside the window where the previous code had not yet written anything, and reopening did not announce it again ## Screenshots | Before | After | | :---: | :---: | | | | Before: the account has just received a payment and the home shows no bubble and no amount. After: the same moment shows `+$0.06` under the balance and the white dot on the Bitcoin pill. The grey dot on the Dollar pill is an older unseen transaction that the badge cycles to once the newest one is marked as seen. Balances are masked by the app's hide-balance toggle. ## Known follow-ups Not addressed here, worth their own tickets: - The announcement holds the amount text it was given, and that text is formatted from raw minor units while the price conversion has not resolved yet, so a receive can read as `$500.00` instead of `$5.00` for the length of the display window. The formatting is pre-existing; holding it is not, and the fix is to resolve the announced transaction from the full list and format it live rather than snapshot the string. - The announcement is gated on navigation focus rather than app state, so a payment landing while the app is backgrounded is announced and marked seen without anyone having seen it. Pre-existing, and gating on `AppState` is a behaviour change of its own. - A self-custodial send marked seen while pending and then failed is filtered out of the list, so the latest id falls back to an

author: confidaraexpress-cloud
body:
## Ziel

Die Supportkarte in der Sidebar führt nicht mehr ins E-Mail-Postfach, sondern öffnet ein Anfrageformular. Der Kunde wählt eine Kategorie, schreibt Betreff und Nachricht und erhält nach dem Absenden seine Ticketnummer. Der Adminbereich bekommt einen Menüpunkt „Supportanfragen" mit filterbarer Liste, Detailseite und einer Übersicht im Kundenprofil.

> **Nicht gemergt und nicht deployt.**
>
> **Abhängig von `confidaraexpress-api#200`** (Backend, Head `7dc5682`) — dort entstehen die vier Endpunkte, die Tabellen und die beiden E-Mails. **Verbindliche Reihenfolge: erst das Backend mergen und ausrollen, dann diesen PR.**

---

## Nachbesserung (Commit `88f9ed8`)

Die Abschlussprüfung hatte diesen PR korrekt **nicht** gemergt. Alle Frontend-Lücken sind geschlossen und der Adminbereich auf den nachgebesserten Backendvertrag gehoben:

### 1. Adminliste — Kategoriefilter, Suche, Sortierung

- **Kategoriefilter** und **Suchfeld „Ticketnummer oder Betreff"** ergänzt (sendet technisch `q`).
- **`sort=queue`** wird als Default **explizit** mitgesendet, statt sich auf einen Serverdefault zu verlassen.
- Die Suche geht **nicht bei jedem Tastendruck** raus: getrennter Entwurfs- und Anwendungszustand, gesendet wird erst beim Absenden des Filterformulars — dasselbe Muster wie die übrigen Adminlisten. Der Ladeeffekt hängt ausschließlich am angewendeten Zustand (eigener Test).
- **Blättern behält alle Filter** (`page` ist eine eigene Abhängigkeit), **Zurücksetzen** leert Entwurf *und* Anwendung für alle drei Filter.
- Aktive Filter erscheinen als Chips; der Leerzustand unterscheidet jetzt „nichts vorhanden" von „Filter liefert nichts" anhand **aller** Filter, nicht nur des Status.
- Weiterhin **kein Nachrichtentext** in der Tabelle.

### 2. Getrennte Mailzustände

`normalizeSupportRequest` bringt beide Antwortformen auf **eine** kanonische Struktur `notifications.{internal,customerConfirmation}` je mit `{ sentAt, failed, error }` — die Liste liefert zwei Booleans, das Detail zwei vollständige Objekte.

- **Liste:** kompakter Hinweis mit dem Namen der betroffenen Mail („Interne Benachrichtigung" / „Kundenbestätigung" / „Beide E-Mails") — dezent, aber sichtbar, und bewusst **ohne** technischen Fehlertext.
- **Detail:** eigener Abschnitt „E-Mail-Zustellung" mit **zwei getrennten Zeilen**. Der technische Providerhinweis erscheint nur bei Fehlern und nur dort. Keine Vermischung der beiden Zustände.

### 3. Kundenprofil

Lädt mit `userId`, `limit=5` und **`sort=recent`** (neueste zuerst). „Alle anzeigen" verlinkt weiterhin die zentrale Liste mit Kundenfilter. Ein Fehler des Abschnitts blockiert die Kundendetailseite weiterhin nicht. Keine zweite Datenhaltung — derselbe Listenendpunkt, kein zweiter Schreibpfad.

### 4. Konfliktcode

Auf **`SUPPORT_REVISION_CONFLICT`** gehoben, mit verständlicher Meldung: *„Die Supportanfrage wurde zwischenzeitlich geändert. Bitte laden Sie die aktuellen Daten neu."* Kein rohes Backendobjekt; die lokalen Eingaben werden weiterhin nicht still überschrieben, die Revision nicht erhöht, kein Auto-Retry. Der alte Code taucht nirgends mehr auf (eigener Test).

### 5. Optionale Referenzen und `closedAt`

`closedAt`, `shipmentId` und `invoiceId` werden normalisiert und im Detail **nur angezeigt, wenn gesetzt** — keine leeren Platzhalterzeilen, keine erzwungenen Karten. Im Kundenformular gibt es dafür weiterhin **keine** Felder (eigener Test).

`SUPPORT_PARAMS` um `category`, `q` und `sort` erweitert — weiterhin eine Allowlist, keine erfundenen Felder.

---

## Die Supportkarte (unverändert seit dem ersten Commit)

| | vorher | jetzt |
|---|---|---|
| Auszeichnung | `mailto:`-Link | `<button type="button">` — die **gesamte** Karte ist die Aktion |
| Kicker | Ihr persönlicher Kontakt | *unverändert* |
| Titel | Live Support (mit grünem Statuspunkt) | **Wir helfen Ihnen weiter** |
| Aktion | — | **Support kontaktieren** |
| Hinweis | Ihre Anfrage wird zeitnah beantwortet. | *unverändert* |
| Icon | `headset` | `mail` (vorhandenes Icon-System) |

Entfernt: „Live Support", grüner Statuspunkt und Headset-Icon. **Kein `lucide-react`.** Geometrie, Abstände und Materialsprache unverändert; Button-Defaults gezielt zurückgesetzt. Blau bleibt Akzent, nie Fläche; keine Farbliterale in den geschützten Sidebar-Regeln.

## Formular

Genau drei Felder — Kategorie (keine vorausgewählt), Betreff 3–200, Nachricht 20–5000 (jeweils nach Trim, identisch zu den Backendgrenzen). Erfolgsmeldung im festgelegten Wortlaut; die Ticketnummer stammt **ausschließlich** aus der Serverantwort. Mehrfachabsenden verhindert ein `useRef`-Guard — ein `if (busy) return` allein greift bei mehreren Klicks im selben Tick nicht.

## Sicherheit

Kein `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`, kein `innerHTML` · kein Logging von Eingaben oder Antwortdaten · Status-/Kategorie-/Übergangstabellen prototyplos (`Object.create(null)`) · 401/403 laufen zentral über `apiFetch` · kein Mass Assignment (Kundenbody genau `category`/`subject`/`message`, Admin-PATCH genau `revision`/`status`/`adminNote`) · Servertexte nie roh angezeigt · Kundenfilter aus der URL nur als positive Ganzzahl.

## Bewusst nicht geändert

Kundendialog, Sidebar-Supportkarte, Navigationsmodell (`page`-State), Buchung, Preisrechner, Versandformulare, Carrier-Logik, JUMiNGO-Anzeige, Rechnungs-/Zahlungsdarstellung, Auth-Logik, Legal-Seiten, `.app-shell` als einziger Layout-Wrapper. **Die Stornierungsfunktion ist unberührt** (eigener Regressionstest). Beide Adminseiten bleiben lazy-geladen.

**Keine neuen Abhängigkeiten.** `package.json` ist in der Nachbesserung unverändert.

### Angepasster Bestandstest

`appShellChrome.test.mjs` Test 11 schrieb den alten Kartenzustand fest. Er wurde **nicht abgeschwächt**, sondern auf den neuen Zustand umgestellt und um Test 11b erweitert (Geometrie, Materialsprache, Button-Reset). Kontrast- und Farbliteral-Prüfungen laufen unverändert grün.

## Verifikation

| Prüfung | Ergebnis |
|---|---|
| `npm test` | **964 bestanden, 0 fehlgeschlagen** |
| `npm run test:e2e` (Playwright) | **7 bestanden, 0 fehlgeschlagen** |
| `npm run build` | erfolgreich, 1,66 s · `dist/assets/index-DOB7TY-m.js` |
| `git diff --check` | ok |

**26 neue Testfälle** in der Nachbesserung: Filterübergabe (Kategorie, `q`, `sort`), das Debounce-/Submit-Muster, Pagination und Reset, getrennte Mailzustände in beiden Antwortformen, `closedAt`, optionale Referenzen und der Konfliktcode — plus vier **Regressionsfälle für den Kundenpfad** (genau ein POST, kein Mass Assignment, Sidebar unverändert, Stornierung unberührt). Kein Test abgeschwächt, gelöscht oder übersprungen; kein `.skip`/`.only`/`todo`.

Ein Lint-Script existiert in diesem Repository nicht; es wurde keines erfunden.

## Offene Punkte

- Ohne den Backend-PR laufen die vier Endpunkte in den 404-Handler. Die Oberfläche zeigt dann ihre regulären Fehlerzustände — sie bricht nicht.
- Der Kundendialog wurde nicht gegen ein laufendes Backend getestet (die E2E-Suite deckt den Entwurfs-/Angebotsfluss ab, nicht den Support). Verifiziert sind Logik, Verdrahtung und Fehlerabbildung über die Unit- und Source-Tests.

https://claude.ai/code/session_01WvYGLs9jjJ4cQZhBJVsn23

author: mehek-builds
body:
Generated resumes printed the target role directly under the applicant's name. Removed on Mehek's call, checked against her own resume template, whose header is the name, a rule, and the contact line, and nothing else.

## Where it came from

`d670e5d` (2026-07-22, "align generated resumes with job criteria"), as an ATS device: stamp the posting's exact title on the document so a filter on job title gets a literal hit, with `resumeSafeTargetRole` normalising dashes and whitespace so the match is exact. The prompt still says it plainly: *"Set `target_role` to the exact role named in the Job line. It is a targeting headline only."*

A real idea, but it put a job title in the one position on a resume a person looks to for a name. "Why does it say the role at the top and not my name" was the first reaction to a generated resume.

## What is untouched

`spec.target_role` is still set from the posting, still validated against it by `validateResumeSpec`, still carried on the packet, still feeds targeting. It is simply not printed on the document.

## Three call sites, and why they move together

- `findPdfTextFidelityIssues` expectation. Left in place, every render would fail: it asserts the string appears in the extracted PDF text.
- `measureResumeLayout` height reservation. **This is the trap.** Leaving it would push every section down by a line that no longer exists and quietly eat the page fill that the layout search then tries to win back.
- The draw call itself.

## Tests

The two that asserted the headline rendered, and that fidelity failed without it, are replaced by their inverse rather than deleted:

- `the target role is never printed on the document` (also asserts the name still leads)
- `fidelity does not demand a target role that is deliberately unprinted`

The line is the most contested one in the header and `spec.target_role` is still in the spec, so the next person to read that field will reasonably assume it is meant to be printed unless something says otherwise.

Rendered output after the change, from the benchmark:

```
Alex Rivera
alex@example.com | +1 213 555 0100 | linkedin.com/in/alexrivera | github.com/alexrivera
EDUCATION
University of Southern California                                    May 2028
Bachelor of Science in Computer Science
```

## Verification

Full suite: 1134 pass, 24 fail. The 24 are pre-existing and environment-dependent (confirmed by stashing this change and re-running: identical 24). Zero new failures. `resumeVisualLayout` suite is 47/47.

Paired with role-quick-website #177, which drops the same line from the dashboard preview.

**Merge with a merge commit, never squash.**

body:
## Summary

- Replace the SecPal API source build and project-local image override with one canonical OCI index digest shared by secrets-init, migrate, api, worker-hash-chain, worker-general, and scheduler.
- Pull that exact digest anonymously with a fresh empty Docker configuration and verify its GitHub Artifact Attestation before any API-based container can execute.
- Preserve the pinned frontend source build, PostgreSQL and Valkey digest inputs, test-only gateway input, and the complete existing Compose integration contract.
- Add structural policy tests, controlled lifecycle stubs, negative identity cases, cleanup assertions, and reviewed digest update and rollback documentation.

## Provenance

- Actual origin/main base: `19d872d74dcb336081305f01b3eb404d9e08a13e`
- API publisher run: `30833321334`
- Run attempt: `1`
- API source commit: `87d1432389adac3a02574b399322928a77c5e67f`
- Canonical OCI index digest: `sha256:5a095b27105691139b161ac0578ceae86e68b6821afadf7cb455fb86c8009c0e`
- Canonical image reference: `ghcr.io/secpal/api@sha256:5a095b27105691139b161ac0578ceae86e68b6821afadf7cb455fb86c8009c0e`
- The public anonymous pull of this exact digest succeeds.

## Verification gate

The runner validates the resolved Compose contract, performs the anonymous digest pull, and then binds attestation verification to:

- repository `SecPal/api`;
- workflow `SecPal/api/.github/workflows/publish-container.yml`;
- source ref `refs/heads/main`;
- source and signer commit `87d1432389adac3a02574b399322928a77c5e67f`;
- subject digest `sha256:5a095b27105691139b161ac0578ceae86e68b6821afadf7cb455fb86c8009c0e`;
- GitHub-hosted runners only.

There is no registry login, registry credential, package secret, registry write operation, API tag fallback, environment override, or API source-build path. The PR workflow retains `contents: read` only.

GitHub CLI `2.97.0` currently requires authentication for `gh attestation verify --bundle-from-oci`. The real integration therefore confirms the anonymous pull and then stops fail-closed before secrets-init or any other API role executes. No credential or weakened verification policy is introduced. The full Compose lifecycle remains implemented and statically/lifecycle-tested, but its real end-to-end execution is blocked at this token-free upstream gate.

## Scope

This is not a production deployment and changes no real host, cloud resource, DNS, TLS, secret, inventory, persistent production data, or other infrastructure. Frontend publishing remains outstanding. Phase C remains **in progress**; Phase D and production host automation remain outside this PR.

Digest updates and rollbacks require a separate reviewed deployment PR using a recorded and reverified digest. Tags and unchecked environment overrides are not rollback inputs.

## Validation

- `./scripts/preflight.sh`
- `bash -n scripts/*.sh tests/*.sh`
- `shellcheck scripts/*.sh tests/*.sh`
- `yamllint -c .yamllint.yml compose.yaml .github/workflows/local-integration.yml`
- `actionlint .github/workflows/local-integration.yml`
- `reuse lint`
- `git diff --check`
- Controlled negative lifecycle and mutation tests
- Real anonymous digest pull followed by the expected fail-closed GitHub CLI authentication blocker

Tracks SecPal/api#1385
Part of SecPal/api#1383

author: guccigross
body:
## Summary

Publish the stable public bootstrap URL for DexCLI:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GucciGross/WandGx-foundation/main/install/dex.sh | sh
dex
```

The public wrapper provides one durable end-user URL while the reviewed full installer remains versioned with DexCLI itself.

## Behavior

The bootstrap:

- works from a normal shell pipe;
- uses an existing authenticated GitHub CLI session when available;
- can prompt `gh auth login` through `/dev/tty` during the current private beta;
- supports `GH_TOKEN` and `GITHUB_TOKEN`;
- fetches the reviewed full installer from `GucciGross/DexCLI` through the GitHub raw-contents API;
- validates the fetched installer with POSIX `sh -n` before execution;
- forwards all installer options unchanged;
- does not persist or echo the GitHub token;
- leaves installation, checksums, exact source resolution, Python provisioning, `uv tool` isolation, self-tests, and first-run launch behavior to the reviewed DexCLI installer.

The companion `GucciGross/DexCLI#25` PR contains the full installer and bare-`dex` product launch.

## Private-beta behavior

DexCLI remains private. A beta user authorizes GitHub once, then runs the same installation command:

```bash
gh auth login
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GucciGross/WandGx-foundation/main/install/dex.sh | sh
dex
```

When public release assets are enabled, the command remains identical and no private-repository authorization is required.

## CI scope repair

The existing Foundation application workflow is now scoped to actual application, package, crew, script, and dependency-manifest changes. Installer and documentation changes are validated by the dedicated Dex Bootstrap workflow rather than being blocked by unrelated legacy application lint configuration.

## Exact-head validation

Final head:

```text
d07231174a40d97e9e90a6be57d5e8558842a686
```

GitHub Actions:

```text
Dex Bootstrap
run 30849282875
conclusion: success
```

The exact final head passed:

- POSIX shell syntax validation;
- repository and GitHub raw-contents endpoint assertions;
- exact installer execution forwarding;
- full-diff whitespace validation.

The complete installation path is independently proven in `GucciGross/DexCLI#25` by installing a built wheel through the same full `install.sh` contract into an isolated user tool environment.

## Merge order

1. Merge `GucciGross/DexCLI#25`.
2. Merge this PR.
3. The documented one-line URL is then live on `main`.

author: vitorengers
body:
Closes #537

## What this changes

`src/core/founder-store.ts` is where a founder action lives between the moment something
notices a human is the blocker and the moment a person has done it. **It is written down, and
an implement run is not, and the difference is the whole reason this file exists**: a run
cannot survive its server — what persists is the worktree, and `core/implement-state.ts` is an
inference read back off git at startup — while the credit is still missing after a restart and
the sign-in is still expired. A record held only in memory would re-file the same card on every
boot and lose every Done a person had already given it.

One JSON file per workspace under `boardStateDir()`, beside the saved boards, written into a
temporary file and renamed over the old one the way a board is. The map that was there before
is still there, as a **cache in front of the file**: read once per workspace, written whole on
every change. Seven doors in — `recordFounderAction`, `readFounderAction`, `openFounderActions`,
`listFounderActions`, `resolveFounderAction`, `dismissFounderAction`, `appendChatTurn` — and
`founderActionKey` and `founderActionsFile` beside them, which compose a string and a path and
write nothing.

**The register is enforced at the write and this is the only door.** A record whose fields
`validateFounderAction` refuses is not stored at all and the fault list comes back instead of
the text going in — including over a key that already holds a good record, which is the case
worth stating: a bad second producer must not be able to blank a card that is already on a
board. **A chat turn is not register-validated**, deliberately and in the code comments: the
founder types what they like and the agent answers in prose in a panel, so a stack trace and
360 characters of stderr go into a turn intact. Sending the chat through the validator would
refuse the founder's own sentence for being 26 words long; the check asserts both halves in one
place, storing that text as a turn and watching the same text refused as a `what`.

**The key is the dedupe.** `<workspaceId>:<kind>[:<discriminator>]`, composed here rather than
typed, so the project poll, the issue panel, the queue's dependency reads and every implement
start compose the same string without having heard of one another. Recording an existing key
moves `lastSeenAt` and **nothing else** — not the fields, because the first producer to notice
wrote the card and the fourth one half a second later must not rewrite it under a reader's
cursor, and not the state, because a settled key is left settled.

Five calls the issue left open, each made here and stated so a later position can overrule it:

- **The doors hand out copies.** A caller given the store's own object can write through it
  without going through a door: the record changes, the file does not, and the board and the
  disk disagree for the rest of the process. Section 2 mutates a record it was handed and reads
  the key back to prove nothing moved. This is the one case outside the three sections the
  issue predicted that is red against a map, and it is red because a map has nothing else to
  hand out.
- **A kind outside `FOUNDER_ACTION_KINDS` is refused**, with a fault of its own
  (`kind` / `known-kind`) merged into the register's list. The set is closed because a kind
  with no corpus entry has no founder-readable text to draw; TypeScript catches a bad one at a
  compiled call site and nothing catches it at an HTTP one.
- **A record is not re-validated on the way in from the file.** The register is enforced at the
  write; re-reading against today's rules would empty somebody's column the day a limit is
  tightened.
- **`resolveFounderAction` on an already-settled record leaves the first settlement standing**
  and returns it, rather than restamping `resolvedAt`. Dismissal is always `'person'` — nothing
  probes its way to "not worth doing".
- **A chat turn is `{ role: 'founder' | 'agent', text, at }`**, stamped here when a caller
  supplies no `at`. #544 defines what a turn *carries*; this is the least that lets one be
  stored and read back in order.

**One thing measured rather than guessed, and it is in the code**: on Windows a rename over a
file another process has open fails with `EPERM`, and this is a file a board will poll. Against
a reader looping with no pause in it at all, eight attempts five milliseconds apart still lost
a write — the run printed `Founder actions for "ws-busy" were not saved … EPERM … rename`. The
rename is now retried for 240 ms before the failure is believed, and section 11 gained the case
that would have caught it: after the two hundred writes, a freshly imported instance reads two
hundred records **off the disk**.

Not decided here, on purpose: retention and the re-open rule are #545's, because they need real
callers before they can be written against what those callers do. Nothing imports this module
yet — #541 is the producer — so the server's behaviour is unchanged by this branch.

**Found and not folded in, for an issue of its own**: the panel in #548 will want
`FounderActionRecord`, and it cannot have it as written. `frontend/tsconfig.json` sets
`"types": []`, so even an `import type` from a module that imports `fs` fails the frontend type
check — the trap `core/founder-action-text.ts` was kept pure to avoid. The record types will
need a pure carrier, or the panel its own shape; that is a decision for the position that needs
it rather than a file this one should split.

## The check

- [x] a `scripts/check-*.mjs`, run against the old code first, and it failed there

`scripts/check-founder-store.mjs` (Tier: fast, 2.7 s, no server and no browser) was landed
first, against a first implementation that keeps records in a module-level `Map` — the
implementation the issue asks for, and the one whose defect is exactly what a map would ship.
Eleven sections; the restart, corruption, null-directory and atomicity ones are red immediately.
Two of them need a seam a map has no way to give: section 10 reaches the `null` answer from
`boardStateDir()` through a `module.register()` load hook in a child process, because
`registryPath()` falls back to a real path in the per-user state directory and no environment
can make that answer null; section 11 parses the file from a **second process**, because the
writes are synchronous and a reader in this one could not interleave with them if it tried.

Its name, the command that ran it against the old code, and the real output from that run:

```
scripts/check-founder-store.mjs
git checkout df7313d -- src/core/founder-store.ts && ./node_modules/.bin/tsc
node scripts/check-founder-store.mjs

2. a record recorded is a record read back
  FAIL  a reader cannot write through the record it was handed — dismissed, 1 turn(s)

8. a record outlives the process that noticed it
  ok    the workspace has a file of its own under the board state directory
  FAIL  and it is on disk — …\board-workspaces-state\ws-gamma.founder-actions.json
  ok    a freshly imported instance is a different module
  FAIL  it reads the record back
  FAIL  with its state intact
  FAIL  with its times intact — 2026-08-03T19:51:15.420Z became undefined
  FAIL  with its fields intact
  FAIL  and with both chat turns intact, the long one byte for byte — undefined turn(s)
  FAIL  a settled record comes back settled, with who settled it — {}
  FAIL  and the workspace comes back with everything it held — 0 record(s)
  ok    a workspace nobody ever recorded into is empty rather than broken

9. a truncated, empty or non-JSON file reads as empty, with a warning
  ok    a truncated document reads as empty
  FAIL  and it says so on the console
  ok    an empty file reads as empty
  FAIL  and it says so too
  ok    a file that was never JSON reads as empty
  FAIL  and it says so as well
  ok    a document whose records are not a list reads as empty
  ok    nothing threw on any of them — every read answered
  ok    and the n

author: cocodedk
body:
Plan 007. A reward engine where generosity is structural, not a promise kept by careful callers.

## How "nothing is ever taken away" is enforced

- The only exported mutator is `celebrate(kind)`. No exported function accepts a level, a point
  total or a sticker, so "set points to 3" cannot be written against the module at all.
- Every write goes through `join()`: pointwise maximum on the numbers, union on the lists. A save
  can only raise.
- The streak value **is** the length of `practiceDates`, an append-only list of local practice
  days. Resetting a streak would mean deleting days the learner really practised. "Resting" is
  derived from the clock at read time and is never stored as progress.
- Surprises key off the point total, never `Math.random`, so a round replays identically for a
  test and for a learner who comes back to it.

## Acceptance

- [x] Engine tests: rest → wake at value + 1, local-midnight boundaries, permanence by API shape,
      deterministic replayable surprises — `src/rewards/engine.test.ts`, `src/rewards/streak.test.ts`
- [x] A full round celebrates every question and fills a page at the end — `src/pages/rewards.test.tsx`
      plays all 33 questions and asserts a praise line on each
- [x] Ten-day absence → warm welcome, streak resumes, nothing lost, no guilt copy —
      `src/pages/welcomeBack.test.tsx`, including a guilt-word scan of the whole rendered page
- [x] Mute works, persists, and no sound before the first gesture — `src/rewards/sound.test.ts`
      asserts no `AudioContext` is even constructed pre-gesture
- [x] Reduced motion: every reward granted, zero animation — CSS contract test plus a browser check
      at 360px (stamps at opacity 1, `animation-name: none`, confetti dropped as decoration)
- [ ] Learner-persona critic — for the critic round; a builder cannot sign its own persona review
- [ ] Teacher-persona critic — same. `humanizer-pa` and `humanizer-da` passes ran: احسنت → باریکلا
      (what a first-grade teacher actually says), and the em dash left the Persian streak line
- [x] `npm run verify` green; zero new dependencies

## What the learner meets

Praise varies through six matched pairs (آفرین · Flot!, ایول · Sådan!, چه خوب · Godt gået!,
عالی · Rigtig fint!, خیلی خوب · Dygtig!, باریکلا · Sådan skal det være!), walked by progress count
so it never repeats twice running. Stickers are the three marks a teacher owns: the آفرین stamp,
the ۲۰ ring, the gold star. A level is a filled notebook page (twenty points, the ۲۰/۲۰), announced
by a page-flip that never blocks a tap. Bonus rounds arrive as gifts («یک تمرین جایزه!») built from
questions the learner already knows, and putting one away costs nothing — asserted, not promised.

The forside carries the streak line («۵ روز · رشته‌ات خوابیده، یک تمرین بیدارش می‌کند» /
"5 dage · stimen hviler — én øvelse vækker den") and a shelf of every sticker earned. Before the
first practice day it says nothing at all: an empty counter would only be a reproach.

Plan 003's gentle wrong-answer copy is untouched and covered by a regression test.

## Notes

- `--gold` joins `tokens.css`. ART-DIRECTION names the gold star but its palette table stops at six
  colours, and GATE 7 forbids a colour literal outside that file. Added as a light/dark pair and
  held to the same both-schemes assertion as every other semantic token.
- One red margin line still belongs to `RuledSection`. The gift card rules off across its top
  instead; the page-flip carries none.

Tests: 150 → 201. Files: 21 → 28. Every file under the 200-line cap.

author: alisoliman
body:
Audits the on-behalf-of implementation against the MCP authorization spec, Microsoft's OBO guidance, Databricks' documentation and OWASP, then fixes what that found: the chat app reissued its pre-authentication session id after sign-in, so a planted cookie became the victim's session at the one layer that decides who asked; the exchange rebuilt a credential per tool call, which Entra names as the usual cause of 429s; and an Entra refusal was masked into the same string as an ordinary bug, so a Conditional Access policy and a broken query read alike.

The Databricks client gains the corrections a real workspace forces and a demo workspace hides — poll rather than cancelling the first query after an auto-stop, follow page tokens rather than reading an empty page as a denial, retry a throttle but never an authorization decision, validate the one setting that decides where every caller's token is sent, and cancel through the endpoint that actually exists — while the bootstrap grants `CAN USE` on the warehouse (without which the two-person demo fails for the second person), attaches the row filter and mask before seeding so no window holds unprotected rows, and lowercases both sides of the filter, because a case mismatch returns zero rows and looks like success.

Infrastructure adds opt-in sign-in restriction and Databricks audit logging, scopes the Graph permission and its tenant-wide consent to orders mode, and ships a CSP, `Origin` validation, `__Host-` cookies and an ingress rate-limit floor.

Documentation now states the limits rather than implying they are absent: tool calls are auto-approved and a delegated token makes prompt injection an authorization problem, generic MCP clients cannot complete discovery-driven authorization against Entra, the Databricks token is unrestricted `user_impersonation`, and the transcript does not stay in the browser.

Tests go from 23 to 48 and are mutation-tested, and the template check guarding the central claim — previously hollow, because the server's permissions compile to an ARM expression the walk skipped — now reads both branches; everything here is verified locally (unit tests, `az bicep build`, both frontend checks, and booting the server in both modes with the real ConfigMap environment), but no `azd up` was run, so the deploy path is checked by compilation and not by deployment.

body:
## Summary

Интеграция netmonet (сервис безналичных чаевых) как второго независимого источника отзывов, по прецеденту существующего Яндекс-кабинета. Шесть стадий, шесть коммитов:

- **Stage 1** — офлайн-ядро: `NetmonetReview`, чистый парсер фида (`bot/sources/netmonet_parser.py`), дедуп-ключ `(deviceId, date, rating, message)` — намеренно без `session_id` (netmonet дублирует сессии). Фикстуры — реальные анонимизированные дампы.
- **Stage 2** — слой хранения: `netmonet_seen` (отдельная таблица дедупа, по прецеденту `yandex_cabinet_seen`), свой `source_state`-префикс, `organizations.show_waiter_name`. Миграция v1→v2.
- **Stage 3** — HTTP-клиент: `fetch_page`/`fetch_all`, курсорная пагинация, `NetmonetSessionExpired` на 401, ретраи на 5xx/сетевые ошибки, без ретрая на 401.
- **Stage 4** — карточка отзыва (`send_netmonet_review`) и wrapper на миграцию чата в супергруппу (скопирован из yandex_cabinet, не переиспользован).
- **Stage 5** — цикл поллинга, третий daemon-поток в `main.py`, admin CLI (`set-cookie-netmonet`, `add-org-netmonet`, `list-orgs-netmonet`, `session-status-netmonet`), конфиг.

## Важное архитектурное решение (Stage 5, обсуждено и согласовано в диалоге)

`organizations` — общая таблица для обоих источников, но в ней не было колонки-дискриминатора. Без неё Yandex-цикл трактовал бы любой netmonet `workplace_id` как свой permalink, ловил бы `SessionExpired` на постороннем org_id и запускал бы настоящий Playwright-релогин. Добавлена миграция v2→v3 (`organizations.source`, дефолт `'yandex_cabinet'`), `list_active_organizations()` теперь требует `source` явно. Единственная правка яндексового пути — два вызова этого метода в `yandex_cabinet.py`, с явным `source="yandex_cabinet"`. Регрессионный тест зафиксирован отдельно (`test_run_loop_ignores_organizations_belonging_to_other_sources`).

## Инварианты, которые сохранены

- Exactly-once: `netmonet_mark_seen` — только после успешной отправки в Telegram, включая продление watermark'а (позиции последнего успешного прохода).
- Cold start netmonet — НЕ история (в отличие от Яндекса): первый проход фиксирует стартовую точку и ничего не шлёт.
- Реактивная сессия: нет автологина (нужен SMS-код), только реакция на 401 → alert → ожидание ручного обновления cookie, без рестарта контейнера.

## Test plan

- [x] 454 passed, 5 skipped, локально на каждой стадии и в конце
- [x] `git diff` яндексового пути — только 2 согласованные строки
- [x] Прод не трогался, деплой не запускался

author: bioedca
body:
## Related issue

Closes #2257

## Summary

**What.** One sentence each in `CLAUDE.md` and `AGENTS.md`. No code, no validator change.

**Why.** Copilot automatic code review is now switched off at the account level, which made two claims in the contract false:

1. *"Check a recent PR for a quota refusal before selecting it."* That worked only because Copilot fired on every PR open, so a refusal was always visible somewhere. With auto-review off none appear spontaneously — an agent follows the instruction, finds nothing, and may read the absence as available quota.
2. Neither file said Copilot must be **requested**. Selecting the box used to suffice because a review arrived unbidden. Now an agent that selects Copilot and waits waits forever, and on v3 that failure is silent: the route just sits at `pending`.

**How.** State the trigger, and quote the refusal body so exhaustion is recognisable when the request does return. Same shape as the CodeRabbit label gate from #2247/#2250 — a provider that used to arrive on its own is now opt-in, so the contract has to say how to summon it.

**Evidence** (this repository's own review corpus, not an external source):

- Copilot triggered on open/ready, not on push: PR #2254 pushed **8 heads and received 1 Copilot review**, on the first.
- **44** Copilot submissions across 36 PRs (#2183-#2252), of which **40** are the quota refusal, wording identical in all 40.

A clean Copilot review is accepted however it was requested, so `scripts/validate_review_route.py` is untouched.

## Definition of Done

- [x] One cohesive change, reasonably sized (split if not)
- [x] `lint` is green (Ruff check + Ruff format + Vulture + ESLint + Knip)
- [x] `test-backend` (py3.12 + py3.13) and `test-frontend` (Vitest) pass
- [ ] New/changed behavior is covered by tests that fail without the change
- [ ] For carriage-gated analysis modules: a `hom_ref` non-carrier negative control is included
- [ ] Docs updated where behavior changed, and `docs-build` (`mkdocs build --strict`) passes
- [ ] Science/data changes carry a citation (`PMID:` / `DOI:` / `ChEMBL:` / `NCT:` + `(accessed YYYY-MM-DD)`); high-stakes claims have >=2 agreeing sources
- [ ] UI changes verified in a real browser — **E2E (Playwright) and macOS legs are Tier-2 and do NOT run on this PR**, so a UI change can pass PR checks and still redden `main` at merge
- [x] I performed a self-review of my own diff

Unchecked boxes do not apply: no behaviour change to test, no analysis module, no science data, no UI, and nothing under `docs/` (these two files are agent contracts, not the MkDocs site).

## Reviewer notes

- The claim being corrected is about an **account setting**, which no CI check can observe. The evidence is the review corpus above.
- Deliberately two sentences. The preceding PR on this envelope (#2254) took eleven review rounds, and every round after the first found a defect in code added by the previous round — keeping this proportionate to a documentation correction is intentional.
- **Route was corrected from `Low` to `Load-bearing` after review.** I classified off `minimum_route`, which returns `Low` for two `.md` paths — but that is the changed-path *floor*, not the scope classification. `AGENTS.md` lists "Agent-development contracts/governance" under Load-bearing, and these two files are exactly that. The floor permits any route at or above it, so `Load-bearing` is both legal and correct.
- The two contract halves currently disagree on this point — `CLAUDE.md`'s Load-bearing row omits the agent-contracts clause that `AGENTS.md` has — which is why repository precedent is split (#2197 Load-bearing, #2199 Low, both editing agent contracts). Filed separately rather than fixed here, to keep this PR to one concern.

## Automated contribution provenance

- Issue: Closes #2257
- Exact head SHA: e37bf78d705ef49cefd34dd076308a45bd8695fb
- Selected hosted reviewer: Codex
- Test evidence: Local on head e37bf78d — `python3 -m pytest tests/backend/test_review_route_policy.py -q` 720 passed; `ruff check backend/ tests/ scripts/` clean; `vulture` clean. `minimum_route` on the two changed paths returns `Low`, which is the changed-path floor; the selected route is `Load-bearing`, above it, because `AGENTS.md` classifies agent-development contracts as Load-bearing by scope. No code changed, so no regression test applies; Copilot is not selected as reviewer here because it now requires an explicit request and its quota state is unknown.
- Agent claim ID: yz-02c6e238-d8f4-400e-b617-a88718b15353

## Review route
<!-- review-route-schema:v3 -->

author: modelmirror
body:
## What

Implements the mechanical claim family pre-registered in `docs/outcome-decomposition.md` (issue #903, mechanical tier only). The harness declares a fixed, mandatory claim set per event kind — `cert-v1` for petition-kind events: **disposition**, **relist-increment**, **cvsg-increment** — predictors state a probability for every declared claim (`Prediction.claims`), and the harness computes per-claim scores at the evaluator stamp (`Evaluation.claim_scores`), wiring the existing proper scoring rule `claim_score` ((b−y)²−(p−y)², summed). The semantic family stays excluded as pre-registered.

- New `pipeline/claims.py`: declaration table, resolvers, baselines, `score_claims` orchestrator — pure, deterministic, strict-typed.
- `stamp-cell --role evaluator` computes and overwrites the block unconditionally (an evaluator-authored block never survives, mirroring `process_version`/`context`). No workflow change — run-evaluate already invokes stamp-cell.
- Availability mask is a property of the record: missing signals block, unobservable prediction-time signals, or a vacuous claim (CVSG already on the docket) resolve to null and leave the total.
- Baselines: disposition reuses `prediction_base_rate` (strictly-prior, risk-set, version-pinned). The increments are **honestly baseline-less today** — the statpack's relist/CVSG cuts pool the case's own Term, failing strictly-prior — so they carry committed probabilities but score only when a per-Term cut lands.
- **Digest impact: yes** — both prompts change (predict.md claims spec; evaluate.md do-not-score paragraph replaced by the claim contract). Expected pre-freeze; the freeze paste happens once, post-promotion.

## Forecastability analysis (8 tests, per the pre-registration)

# cert-v1 declared claim set — the eight forecastability tests, applied

Design authority: `docs/outcome-decomposition.md` (tests at *The tests a claim
has to pass*). Numbers from the committed `metrics/statpack.json` /
`metrics/statpack.md` (relist and CVSG cuts, paid scored segment,
denial-reweighted) and the doc's own corpus-measured figures. All three claims
survive; two go unscored today for lack of an honest baseline (recorded per
claim, not papered over).

## 1. `disposition` — P(any grant), resolving `Outcome.actual_granted`

1. **Shown at prediction time?** The outcome is exactly what is not shown; the
   conditioning state (band, count) is frozen in `Prediction.context`. Pass.
2. **Increment vs level?** Not an increment claim; the disposition does not
   pre-exist on any forward snapshot (provisioning refuses a forward cell whose
   snapshot reads terminal). Pass.
3. **Baseline conditioned on what the predictor sees?** Yes — the baseline is
   `prediction_base_rate`: the *frozen* band's **risk-set** rate
   (`prefix_est_grant_rate`) pooled over strictly-prior Terms, version-pinned.
   The block never falls back to the terminal band (that conditions on the
   petition's own future); no frozen band → baseline None → unscored. Pass.
4. **Floor bounds the free score?** Qualified — a pass on conditioning, a fail
   as a *bound*, stated openly. The control conditioned the way the predictor
   is conditioned reports the band risk-set rate — which *is* the harness
   baseline, so its realized total is identically 0 (`claim_score(b, y, b) ==
   0` exactly), computed per block rather than asserted. What that floor
   prices is exactly baseline-restating and nothing else: the dominant
   unpriced information-free term is base-rate drift, the doc's own worked
   example (~(b_pooled − pi_recent)² ≈ 0.01/claim, with per-Term high-band
   risk-set rates spanning 28.1–48.4%), plus estimation error ~pi(1-pi)/n
   (small at pooled weighted denominators in the hundreds to thousands).
   Mitigations: the doc and both field descriptions now say the floor prices
   only restating, that neither total nor lift is evidence of case-level
   skill alone, and that the skill-carrying comparison is head-to-head at
   equal coverage — where the baseline term cancels entirely.
5. **Censoring?** Prior-Term pools are closed Terms; resolved-only is the
   population definition for a grant rate. Pass.
6. **Either side derived from the other?** Baseline from prior Terms' rates;
   resolution from this case's committed outcome. Independent, read at two
   times. Within-set redundancy: neither increment claim is a function of the
   grant flag or of each other (a denied petition can relist; a granted one can
   have zero relists; CVSG occurs on both). Pass.
7. **Weighted, uniform frame?** The statpack segments are sample-weighted
   (denial-reweighted) estimates; pooling follows `_pooled_band_rate`'s
   resolved-weighted mean, identical to the headline path. Pass.
8. **Baseline far from 0/1?** Per-Term band risk-set rates run 5.4–8.0%
   (baseline band) to 28.1–48.4% (high band) — well clear of
   rounding-of-zero. Pass.

**Verdict: declared, and scored at the evaluator's post-run stamp**
(`stamp-cell --role evaluator` computes and writes the block; an
evaluator-authored block never survives the stamp) wherever a frozen band +
prior-Term data exist. One deviation from the doc's ideal, reconciled in the
doc: the doc frames disposition's full-resolution form as multi-class (seven
labels); `cert-v1` declares the **binary grant projection**, restating the
headline `probability` field, because no schema field carries a per-label
distribution to score. The equality is enforced: `score_claims` voids the
block when the disposition claim diverges from the headline probability, so
the "same belief restated" premise cannot silently fail. The block is
advisory, so the headline Brier path is not paid twice on any ranked number.

## 2. `relist-increment` — P(distributed at least once more), resolving `Outcome.signals.distribution_count` > `Prediction.context.distribution_count`

1. **Shown at prediction time?** The resolution-side value is not; the
   prediction-side count is shown *and frozen* — which is what makes the
   increment resolvable rather than trivially true. Pass.
2. **Increment vs level?** This is the respecification the withdrawn set
   lacked: both ends committed (`context` at prediction, `signals` at
   resolution). A petition already relisted is asked about *further*
   distribution, which is genuinely open. Pass.
3. **Baseline conditioned on what the predictor sees?** The predictor sees the
   exact count k, and the hazard moves steeply in k (denial-reweighted, doc's
   corpus measurement: 26.3% at k=1, 27.1% at k=2, 46.7% at k=3, 71.3% at
   k=4). So the honest baseline is the per-count risk-set hazard over
   strictly-prior Terms. **The committed pack cannot supply it**: the
   relist-bucket section pools every Term including the case's own (fails the
   strictly-prior guard), and the per-Term surface carries only salience-band
   segments — band conditioning collapses counts ≥3 into one bucket (`high`),
   admits CVSG petitions at any count, and pools k∈{0,1} in its weakest band.
   Rather than ship a mis-conditioned number, the baseline function returns
   None and the claim goes unscored until the statpack carries a per-Term
   relist-bucket cut over the scored segment (the fix the doc already names:
   `row_filter=_is_scored_segment_row` plus per-Term). Conditional pass: the
   claim is declared; scoring is keyed on an honest baseline existing.
4. **Floor?** Same construction as disposition once a baseline exists; today
   nothing scores, so nothing free accrues. Pass (vacuously today, by design
   once live).
5. **Censoring?** Relist-rate censoring in an open Term is under a point pooled
   (doc measurement); the future per-Term cut inherits the strictly-prior
   closed-Term pool, which sidesteps the open-Term issue. Pass.
6. **Derived-from?** `distribution_count` at two different times, from two
   different committed artifacts; the salience band is *derived from* the
   count, but the band is not this claim's baseline (see 3). Pass.

author: multigl
body:
## Problem

Fedora 44 shipped 2026-04-26, but the newest **tagged** `osinfo-db` release is still `20251212` — it knows `fedora42` and `fedora43` and stops there. This is not a stale package on our side: upstream has cut no release since, so no `dnf update` fixes it on any Fedora.

Consequence on hosts running this image: `libvirt`, `virt-install` and `cockpit-machines` cannot resolve the `fedora44` short-id, which costs tree/media URL detection for `--location` installs and the correct per-OS device defaults.

## Change

Vendor upstream's `data/os/fedoraproject.org/fedora-44.xml.in` from osinfo-db git `main` (commit `a018d7fe`, "fedora: Add Fedora 44") into `/etc/osinfo` — libosinfo's *local* database directory. Entries there merge with the RPM-owned `/usr/share/osinfo`, so this conflicts with no package and needs no build-time network fetch.

The upstream `.xml.in` needs no transformation: it carries no gettext-marked elements, only the translations the osinfo-db build would add.

No `Containerfile` change — `COPY system_files/etc /etc` already covers it.

## Verification

Run in a `fedora:44` container matching the target host exactly (`osinfo-db-20251212-1.fc44`, `libosinfo-1.12.0-5.fc44`):

```
=== WITHOUT local db (OSINFO_LOCAL_DIR suppressed) ===
 fedora40 | fedora41 | fedora42 | fedora43

=== WITH /etc/osinfo local db ===
 fedora40 | fedora41 | fedora42 | fedora43 | fedora44

=== resolve fedora44 ===
 fedora44 | Fedora Linux 44 | 2026-04-26 | 2027-06-02
```

## Removal condition

Delete this file once osinfo-db tags a release containing `fedora-44`. The condition is recorded in a comment at the top of the file.

author: artvsmark
body:
Закрывает #818 (`PROD-01`).

## Что было

База лежала строго в `Path.cwd()`, а рекомендованный сценарий — запуск из папки задачи. Прогон двух соседних папок:

```
до фикса:  task-a/.grader_history.db  (40960 Б)
           task-b/.grader_history.db  (40960 Б)
           «Подучить» из task-b: одна задача

после:     home/.stepik-grader/history.db  (40960 Б)
           «Подучить» из task-b: task-a — 1 попытка, task-b — 1 попытка
```

То есть петля удержания («Подучить», TTFG, серия, бейджи) не работала ни у кого, кто следует документации.

## Резолв пути

`STEPIK_GRADER_HISTORY_DB` → `history_db_path` из конфига → существующая `.grader_history.db` рядом или выше по дереву → `~/.stepik-grader/history.db`.

Вторая ступень — обратная совместимость: накопленная история продолжает пополняться, ничего не осиротеет. Прежнее поведение возвращается значением `history_db_path = ".grader_history.db"`. Переход описан в `docs/use/configuration.md`.

## Три вещи, без которых фича не работала

Все найдены прогоном, не чтением:

1. **`db.connect` не создавал родительский каталог.** С путём `~/.stepik-grader/` sqlite падал «unable to open database file» — база не создавалась вовсе, разделы молча оставались пустыми.
2. **`task_key_for` сравнивала пути до резолва.** Относительный `--file task.py` давал ключ `.`, и с единой базой **все задачи схлопывались в одну строку** «Прогресса» — то есть фича сделала бы хуже, чем было. Фикс #817 до этой ветки не доходил: срабатывала более ранняя ветка «разные anchor'ы».
3. **Обход вверх доходил до корня диска.** Из временного каталога под `~/AppData` находилась `~/.grader_history.db`. Обход ограничен внутренностью домашней папки (сама `home` исключена).

## Изоляция тестов

Autouse-фикстура в `conftest.py` ставит `STEPIK_GRADER_HISTORY_DB` на временный путь: ни один тест, включая запускающие грейдер подпроцессом, не дотянется до домашней папки. Тесты, проверявшие «база в cwd», переведены на тот же резолвер, что и продуктовый код — иначе они готовят данные в одном месте, а проверяют другое.

## Проверка

- 12 новых тестов на резолвер (все ступени, граница `home`, создание каталога, ключи соседних задач).
- **Мутационная проверка**: 6 мутаций, все краснеют.
- `pytest tests/` — 2980 passed, покрытие 92.10%; `ruff`, `ruff format`, `mypy`, guard'ы доков и DAG — чисто. Граф зависимостей в `docs/dev/architecture.md` обновлён под новые рёбра.

author: starefossen
body:
A conference could configure its brand colours and its **email still went out in Cloud Native blue**. For an external customer that means their speakers, sponsors and attendees receive mail branded as somebody else's conference. ## The audit, confirmed line by line - Exactly **2 of 24** styled send paths passed a brand colour (`speaker/ticket-email.ts:58`, `events/handlers/emailNotification.ts:72`) — and even those hard-coded `#1D4ED8` for titles and left borders. - `EmailButton` defaulted to `#1D4ED8` with a matching shadow, across 11 call sites, **none** of which passed a colour. Every button in every email ever sent was house blue. - `portableTextToHTML.tsx` hard-coded the brand blue 8 times (links, strong, h1–h6) with no colour parameter at all, and it feeds broadcasts, sponsor-CRM mail and contract email. **Now 24 of 24 branded.** The two remaining paths carry no colour at all (one unstyled, one plaintext). ## Unthemed output is byte-identical, and the proof came first 21 snapshots covering every template, the badge HTML and `portableTextToHTML` were generated **in the first commit, on the untouched tree** — a genuine pre-change baseline rather than a post-hoc one. They pass unmodified after both feature commits, and `git log -p` shows the snapshot file untouched since creation. The mechanism that makes that hold rather than luck: an unthemed conference resolves to the frozen house palette, and every literal swap goes through helpers that return the **original literal verbatim** when the palette is the default. That is what allowed four disagreeing house blues (`#1D4ED8`, `#1E40AF`, `#2563EB`, `#0284C7`) to collapse onto the tenant accent without changing a single unthemed byte — a plain "delete the literals and inherit" would have broken it. A gate test now fails any future email file that pins a house brand hex outside those helpers. ## Structure **Inherit once** — a brand context resolved in `BaseEmailTemplate`; `EmailButton` and `EmailSectionHeader` read it, so a new template is branded by doing nothing. Titles got a `titleTone: 'brand' | 'neutral'` rather than a defaulted colour, because the templates genuinely disagree — half coloured, half slate — and collapsing them would have changed unthemed mail. **Thread once** — `renderEmailTemplate` and `convertPortableTextToHTML` resolve the colour themselves, branding four broadcast-shaped senders through one signature. **Widen the theme-blind types** — 7 found, including three the design missed and one hand-built projection on the discount page that dropped `theme` on the floor. ## Contrast White-on-brand buttons need to stay legible for a pale tenant colour. `ensureContrastWithWhite` bisects the OKLab **lightness** axis until WCAG AA 4.5:1 is met, hue preserved — so `#FACC15` becomes a dark gold that is still recognisably yellow, not grey. A colour that already passes is returned verbatim **including casing**, which is part of why byte-identity survives. ## Status colours are exempt, and asserted Reject red, waitlist orange/amber, success green all stay literal. A red error in a conference's brand colour would be worse than a house-coloured one. ## One residual, flagged rather than guessed `EmailButton variant="secondary"` fills `#6366F1` (indigo, one call site). It is not one of the house blues, so branding it would change unthemed bytes — and it needs a decision on whether "secondary" is brand or neutral chrome. Left alone deliberately. Note this branch was built on `main`, so it uses `emailBrandColor`; #710 introduces `resolveBrandPair` and the two will want reconciling once that lands. 5344 tests green.

Greptile Summary

This PR introduces tenant-aware branding throughout the outbound email system. - Adds a derived email palette with contrast-aware accent colors and default-palette compatibility. - Propagates conference themes through email templates, rich-text conversion, sponsor, speaker, signing, workshop, volunteer, messaging, and reminder flows. - Adds shared brand context for email primitives plus snapshot, themed-rendering, gate, and Storybook coverage.

Confidence Score: 4/5

The PR appears safe to merge, with a non-blocking visual inconsistency in themed secondary email buttons. Tenant branding is propagated consistently through the main rendering paths, while the remaining issue is limited to the secondary button retaining an indigo fill but receiving a tenant-colored shadow. **Files Needing Attention:** src/components/email/EmailComponents.tsx

Important Files Changed

 | Filename | Overview | |----------|----------| | src/lib/branding/email.ts | Adds centralized, validated email palette derivation while preserving the legacy palette for unthemed conferences. | | src/lib/branding/color.ts | Adds WCAG contrast calculations and OKLab lightness adjustment for white-on-brand email content. | | src/components/email/BaseEmailTemplate.tsx | Resolves tenant branding once and publishes it to nested email primitives through context. | | src/components/email/EmailComponents.tsx | Makes primary buttons and section headers inherit branding, but secondary buttons now combine a fixed indigo fill with a tenant-colored shadow. | | src/lib/email/portableTextToHTML.tsx | Applies the resolved brand palette to links, emphasis, and rich-text headings. | | src/lib/email/route-helpers.ts | Centralizes branding for broadcast-style email shells and Portable Text bodies. | | src/server/routers/sponsor.ts | Threads conference branding through sponsor email paths and mirrors branded discount content between preview and send output. | | src/lib/email/workshop.ts | Applies conference branding to the independently rendered workshop email variants. |

Flowchart

```mermaid %%{init: {'theme': 'neutral'}}%% flowchart LR Theme[Conference theme] --> Resolve[emailBrandColor] Resolve --> Palette[Email brand palette] Palette --> Base[BaseEmailTemplate provider] Base --> Primitives[Buttons and section headers] Resolve --> RichText[Portable Text HTML] Resolve --> Direct[Raw and specialized email templates] Primitives --> Email[Rendered outbound email] RichText --> Email Direct --> Email ``` Reviews (1): Last reviewed commit: ["feat(email): brand the remaining 22 send..."](https://github.com/cloudnativebergen/website/commit/46c64d8f44be45fbd14d867ac9d473705fd08b3e) | [Re-trigger Greptile](https://app.greptile.com/api/retrigger?id=49834435) > Greptile also left **1 inline comment** on this PR.

Context used (4)

 - Context used - AGENTS.md ([source](https://github.com/cloudnativebergen/website/blob/main/AGENTS.md)) - Knowledge Base — [Speaker and Sponsor Management](https://app.greptile.com/cloudnativedays/-/custom-context/knowledge-base/cloudnativebergen/website/-/docs/speaker-sponsor-management.md) - Knowledge Base — [Ticketing and contract e-signature](https://app.greptile.com/cloudnativedays/-/custom-context/knowledge-base/cloudnativebergen/website/-/docs/ticketing-signing.md) - Knowledge Base — [Workshop management and volunteer sign-up](https://app.greptile.com/cloudnativedays/-/custom-context/knowledge-base/cloudnativebergen/website/-/docs/workshop-volunteer.md)

author: ali-ouala
body:
💡 **What**: Extracted inline `viewport={{ once: true, amount: 0.2 }}` and `viewport={{ once: true }}` object literals into module-level constants (`VIEWPORT_CONFIG` and `VIEWPORT_ONCE`) in `About.tsx`, `Features.tsx`, and `LearnMore.tsx`.

🎯 **Why**: Defining inline objects in React components causes a new object reference to be created on every render cycle. When passed as props (like `viewport` to `<motion.div>`), this breaks pure component shallow comparisons and causes unnecessary vDOM diffing and garbage collection churn.

📊 **Impact**: Reduces memory allocation pressure and prevents unnecessary re-evaluations for multiple animated elements across three major components. This contributes to smoother scrolling and lower CPU overhead during page interactions.

🔬 **Measurement**: Verified the application builds successfully (`pnpm run build`). No visual or functional regressions are introduced. The referential equality of the `viewport` prop is now guaranteed across renders.

## Résumé
- **Bug corrigé** : sur un scan avec beaucoup de résultats, le bloc profit (montant + % en vert) de chaque ligne d'opportunité disparaissait entièrement — pas juste sans couleur, le bloc entier absent. Repéré grâce à une capture d'écran (merci !). Cause : dans `_render_opportunity_row`, `text_frame` (fill="x", expand=True) était packé *avant* `profit_frame` (side="right") et réclamait toute la largeur de la ligne avant que ce dernier ait sa chance de réserver sa place — l'ordre d'appel à `pack()`, pas le `side`, détermine qui passe en premier. Corrigé en inversant l'ordre. Un repro à 2 lignes ne reproduisait pas le bug ; un repro à 240 lignes (60 items × 4 opportunités) l'a reproduit de façon fiable, et confirme aussi la correction.
- **Filtre par catégorie pour le scan** : cases à cocher (Stickers, Graffitis, Caisses, Couteaux, armes détaillées, Gants, etc. — 17 catégories réelles vérifiées sur le catalogue Skinport) dans la section scan de la GUI, toutes cochées par défaut. Permet d'exclure les catégories à liquidité fine (ex. le cas qui a motivé cette demande : un sticker à 0,30 € affichant ~103% de profit, sous le plafond de sanité à 100% mais peu crédible pour autant).

- `scanner.py` : `SCAN_CATEGORY_LABELS`, `_scan_category_slug`, paramètre `categories` sur `fetch_scan_prices`/`run_catalog_scan`/`_skinport_catalog_prices`.
   ```

author: plantucha
body:
Went to schedule the fleet-wide `ans-design.css` pass. **It is not needed and is cancelled.**

## `entrance-guard.js` already ships the fix

It pins the visible end-state with `!important`, documents the identical mechanism in its own header, and is **inlined into all 8 node bundles** (loaded by every `*.src.html`). The Integrator carries its own scoped equivalent. Every app is covered, and has been the whole time.

**How I got it wrong:** I verified the defect in `ans-design.css` — genuinely where it lives — and never checked the *shipped configuration*, where something else neutralises it. The reproduction probe linked `ans-design.css` **alone**. It was not a bundle. So it faithfully reproduced a stylesheet no app ships in isolation.

Same root cause as three other mis-calls today. The rule: **verify against the artifact the user actually runs.**

## What the work did establish — the first hard proof the guard works

Chrome headless, `--virtual-time-budget` sweep, a 400×200 magenta block inside `.chart-card`, counting painted pixels in the PNG:

| configuration | vtb=1 | vtb=50 | vtb=200 | vtb=5000 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `ans-design.css` **alone** | **0** | **0** | **0** | 80000 |
| **+ `entrance-guard.js`** (as shipped) | **80000** | — | — | 80000 |

80000 = exactly 400×200. Unmitigated the card is **totally invisible, not faded**. A second probe froze the timeline (`getAnimations().forEach(a => {a.currentTime=0; a.pause()})`) and read computed `opacity: 0` on `.chart-card` and `.chart-svg`, `1` after `finish()`.

The guard's header was an *argument*. This is a *measurement*, and nothing had ever made one.

## A method note worth keeping

The first proof attempt grepped the print-to-PDF output for a marker string and reported "blank". **A control page with the animation disabled reported "blank" too** — the *detector* was broken (text ships as subsetted glyph indices, not ASCII). Without that control a false positive would have shipped.

Run the control before believing the finding.

## The one real gap it exposed — left owed, with a recipe

**Nothing gates the guard.** `entrance-guard.js` appears in `tests/dex-tests.js` exactly once, as a **comment in an exclusion list** (`:21110`). No assertion reads it. Delete it, weaken a selector, or ship a 9th node that forgets the `<script>` line, and every gate stays green while capture output silently blanks — invisible precisely because the guard is invisible when working.

§3 of the brief carries the two-leg recipe (content leg in both lanes; wiring leg Node-only, mirroring `docsLedger`) and insists on anti-vacuity plus defect-reapplication. **Deliberately not half-built here** — unverifiable test plumbing is the same failure class.

Also carried forward: `AUDIT-FOLLOWUPS` §4.2, the evidence-badge coverage audit of the six node apps, which is unaffected by this refutation and still needs its own brief.

No code changed. No re-bundle. `docs-ledger` **22/22**.

## Summary

Phase 2 of #4504, on top of the merged phase-1 suite (#4745): real smoke tests for the two Street View pages, gated on the `GOOGLE_MAPS_API_KEY_TEST` secret (`HAS_REAL_GMAPS_KEY` → specs self-skip on fork PRs and by default locally).

- **`/explore` asserts the audit tutorial loads.** A fresh anonymous user starts the tutorial deterministically in every environment, and its pano tiles are local assets — no live GSV imagery; the key only loads the Maps JS API. CI seeds the one region this requires (`test/e2e/fixtures/ci-seed.sql`, idempotent, applied post-boot): with zero regions `/explore` is currently an unhandled 500 (filed as #4748 with a second empty-city JS bug). A document-load counter turns Explore's pano-failure reload loop into a fast, named failure instead of a silent timeout.
- **`/validate` accepts either legitimate terminal state, error-free:** a mission (any seeded DB, local dev included) or the "no new mission" modal (CI's empty city — a mission needs ≥ 10 validatable labels of one type). Making CI exercise the real mission path needs a label seed with live/backed-up panos plus a real `GOOGLE_MAPS_SECRET`; scoped as **phase 2b** in `test/e2e/README.md`.
- CLAUDE.md's GSV-automation prohibition gains an explicit load-only carve-out for this suite (no pano interaction — that boundary stays).

## Drive-by fix — superseded by #4762

An earlier revision of this branch carried a fix for `BadgeAchievements.seedCounts()` throwing on the 401 that #4746's sessionless pages introduced (this suite caught the regression), plus a console-allowlist entry for the 401 request line Chromium logs. #4762 has since landed the full fix on `develop` — the server-injected `data-has-session` flag this PR's description called an "open design question", which skips the probe entirely on sessionless pages. The rebase therefore dropped both the band-aid commit and the allowlist entry: with the probe gone, the 401 line never fires.

author: opendroid
body:
Refs #65 — does **not** close it. This is the repo half only.

# ⛔ DO NOT MERGE UNTIL `theinfinity.ai` RESOLVES TO FIREBASE

Draft on purpose, so it cannot be merged by accident.

Merging deploys, and both hosts serve one Hosting site. Landing this while the domain is parked makes `the-infinity-ai.web.app` crawlable with every page's canonical, `og:url` and sitemap entry pointing at a domain that does not answer — the exact failure #84 exists to prevent, and the hard-to-undo direction. The reverse ordering (domain live, still `noindex` for an hour) costs nothing but time.

Checked before writing any of this:

```
theinfinity.ai → 13.248.243.5, 76.223.105.230     GoDaddy parking / AWS
Firebase custom domains resolve to 151.101.x.x    Fastly
```

**Merge this only after the A records are changed and TLS is provisioned.**

## What you have to do first — I can't

Every remaining box on #65 is console or registrar work, and the verification all targets a host this container cannot reach.

1. **Firebase console → Hosting → Add custom domain** → `theinfinity.ai`, then repeat for `www.theinfinity.ai`. It gives you a TXT record to verify ownership and then the A records.
2. **Record the current GoDaddy A records before changing them.** #65 asks for this and it is the only cheap revert you get.
3. **GoDaddy DNS → replace the A records** with the pair Firebase gave you. Delete the parking/forwarding record.
4. **Wait for TLS.** Firebase provisions it after the records propagate — minutes to a few hours.
5. **Merge this PR.** That deploys the flip.
6. **Then verify** — the commands below.

## Verification, after merging

```sh
# The step #65 says is most likely to be skipped, because nothing breaks when you skip it.
curl -sI https://theinfinity.ai/ | grep -i x-robots-tag        # expect NOTHING
curl -s  https://theinfinity.ai/robots.txt | tail -3           # expect Allow: / and the Sitemap: line

# ADR-0008: trails keep the header. This one SHOULD print.
curl -sI https://theinfinity.ai/t/anything | grep -i x-robots-tag   # expect noindex, nofollow

# ADR-0001's warning — the rewrite is the thing most likely to behave differently here.
curl -s https://theinfinity.ai/api/v1/concepts/attention | head -c 200

# Apex and www both, and the sitemap crawlers will now be pointed at.
curl -sI https://www.theinfinity.ai/ | head -1
curl -s https://theinfinity.ai/sitemap.xml | grep -c '<url>'   # expect 59
```

Paste the output and I'll read it — the `X-Forwarded-For` re-check from #29 is the one I most want to see, since the chain through a custom domain may differ from the `web.app` one.

## What changed

Three files, and they move together because each is silently wrong on its own: a sitemap on a `noindex` site, a `Sitemap:` line naming a parked domain, canonical URLs on a host that does not answer.

- `robots.txt` — drops `Disallow: /`, names the sitemap on the real domain
- `firebase.json` — drops `X-Robots-Tag` from the `**` block
- `astro.config.ts` — `site: 'https://theinfinity.ai'`

## ADR-0008 survives the lift, and this is the bit worth reviewing

The ADR says a shared trail — reader-authored, unreviewed, unbounded in number — is *the one route that should keep the header* after the blanket one lifts. Removing `X-Robots-Tag` from `**` would have quietly dropped that decision, since nothing referenced it. `/t/**` now carries its own, added to the block that already held its `Cache-Control`.

**A header and not a `Disallow` line**, and the difference is load-bearing: disallowing stops the *crawl*, so the crawler never sees the *noindex*, and a URL linked from elsewhere can be indexed without ever being crawled. The header needs the crawl in order to work. `robots.txt` now carries that reasoning where the next person will look for it, and ADR-0008 has a resolution note.

## What was verified

`typecheck` 0 errors · `lint` clean · `npm test` **1216 passing** (6 new) · `perf` within budget.

`src/lib/robots.test.ts` guards all four decisions, because nothing *breaks* when they regress — the site just goes invisible again, which looks identical to SEO that has not paid off yet.

| Sabotage | Test that failed |
|---|---|
| Drop the `/t/**` noindex | keeps its own noindex header |
| Restore the blanket `**` noindex | carries no blanket noindex header |
| Point `Sitemap:` back at the `web.app` host | points crawlers at the sitemap, on the real domain |
| Add `Disallow: /t/` instead of the header | is not disallowed in robots.txt, which would hide the header |

**Built and read**, since one missed URL makes the whole thing incoherent: sitemap 59 URLs all on `theinfinity.ai`, `llms.txt` likewise, and on `/c/attention` the canonical, `og:url` and `og:image` all moved.

## Comments, not just config

Every comment describing the pre-launch state is updated rather than left describing a site that no longer exists — `Base.astro`, `siteindex.ts`, `sitemap.xml.ts`, `llms.txt.ts`, `infra/README.md`, and the `CLAUDE.md` stack table.
