author: isaacromayvida
body:
Closes #517 (backend half).

## The gap

`getReviewQueue` projects 13 explicit fields and **zero** of the raw fields `ReviewQueue.tsx` renders from. Pointing the page at the callable today would silently delete the risk pill, the High Risk KPI tile, the Reason column and the LTI sort — which is why the page still holds its own `onSnapshot` on `review_queue`, and why `unreadFailures`, the collection-wide `counts`, the money fields and the `sortOrder` caveat are all computed, tested, and reaching no UI.

## Decision: add the fields, don't drop the elements

The deciding fact is that **this costs no additional Firestore read.** All five fields come off the `review_queue` document the handler already fetches for the page and already reads `queuedAt`/`status`/`applicantName` from (`stage5-review.js` writes them there). They were being fetched and then discarded by the projection. Dropping four working console elements to avoid surfacing data already in memory would be a product regression with no saving behind it.

Adds `riskLevel`, `llmRiskLevel`, `aml`, `riskSignals`, `slaDeadline`.

## One thing the issue's table missed

`getEscalationReason` also reads `signals.bureau.score` and `signals.bureau.activeDefaults`. Projecting only the four listed fields would still have left the Reason column degraded — two of its six reasons would have stopped appearing. `riskSignals` carries both.

## Kept separate from `underwritingDecision`

`underwritingDecision` is deterministic underwriting conditions, each with a value and the bound it was tested against. `riskLevel` is a graded judgement from the AML rules and the LLM narrative. Mapping one onto the other would leave the pill looking identical while changing what it asserts to someone deciding a loan. Separate fields, on purpose.

## Trust boundary

The callable gates on `['ops', 'admin', 'super_admin']` — the same audience already served the applicant's bureau/fraud/model scores via `underwritingDecision`. AML/PEP flags do not widen it.

Projected **leaf-by-leaf** rather than by spreading the sub-documents, so:
- `aml_result.amlLists` (the matched watchlist entries) stays off the wire
- the LLM's free-text `summary`/`key_signals`/`recommendation` stay off the wire
- a future provider field added to `signals` does not reach the client the day it is added, without someone deciding

Nothing renders any of those. The existing PII-leak guard test (RFC/CLABE) still passes.

## Absent data stays null, never a default

A missing `isPEP` means "not checked". Reporting it as `false` would assert a clean PEP screen that never ran and silently suppress an escalation in the Reason column. A `risk_level` outside the vocabulary `stage5-review.js` can actually produce degrades to null rather than rendering a grade this backend cannot vouch for. Non-object sub-documents (Firestore returns whatever was written) yield null instead of throwing and taking down the whole queue read.

## Verification

- `functions`: **628/628 pass**, 32 suites
- `tsc --noEmit`: clean
- `npm run lint`: clean
- getReviewQueue suite **38 → 45**; the 7 new tests were run against the old projection and **8 fail** (my 7 plus the field-list guard), so they are not vacuous

## Not in this PR

The console-side swap. It is a real interaction change — `getReviewQueue` is paginated and non-realtime, so client-side sort/filter would degrade to "the current page". That needs server-side sort or an explicit affordance, and it is a design decision, not a detail. This PR removes the data blocker so that decision can be made on its own merits.

### Motivation
- Fix a security regression where base64 uploads could bypass the SVG denylist by supplying parameterized MIME types like `image/svg+xml;charset=utf-8`, enabling storage of active SVG content and potential stored XSS.

### Description
- Normalize caller-supplied MIME types on the base64 upload path by using `contentTypeFamilyFromString(...)` (strips parameters and lowercases) before running the existing media allow/deny checks in `packages/backend/src/routes/intentMedia.ts`.
- Ensure the `contentType` used for upload is the canonical family so the SVG denylist (`image/svg+xml`) and prefix checks apply uniformly across remote-URL and base64 paths.
- Add regression tests in `packages/backend/src/__tests__/routes/intentMedia.test.ts` that assert parameterized SVGs are rejected and that parameterized image types are canonicalized and uploaded correctly.

### Testing
- Ran the backend intent-media tests with `bun --cwd packages/backend test src/__tests__/routes/intentMedia.test.ts --reporter verbose`, and all tests passed (9/9).
- Added the two regression tests verifying rejection of `image/svg+xml;charset=utf-8` and canonicalization of `IMAGE/PNG; charset=binary`, both succeeded in the test run.

author: sunrisepeak
body:
## Summary

Follow-up to #490. Locally the editor still printed `libfreetype.so.6: cannot open shared object file` on the first line of `godot --version`, then `libexpat.so.1: ...` once freetype was placed on `LD_LIBRARY_PATH`.

Root cause: the shim runs godot inside a sandbox whose `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` holds only glibc's libdir. `strace` of the running editor showed loader probes hitting only `xim-x-glibc/2.39/lib/...` — `deps.runtime` alone does not thread a dep's libdir onto the shim's loader path.

Fix follows the `musl-gcc.lua` idiom: `xvm.add("godot", { envs = { LD_LIBRARY_PATH = ... } })`, with the paths probed from each dep's install dir. `xim:expat@2.6.2` is added to `deps.runtime` alongside freetype since it's a transitive dlopen through fontconfig.

Dep layouts differ (`freetype` under `lib/x86_64-linux-musl/`, `expat` under `lib/`), so the helper probes candidate subdirs for the SONAME'd file rather than hard-coding one split.

## Test plan

- [x] Local: reproduced the original `libfreetype.so.6` failure on `godot --version` after installing from main
- [x] Local: after patching the recipe and `xlings remove godot / install godot`, `godot --version` prints only the version line
- [x] Local: `godot --headless --quit` boots cleanly, no loader errors
- [ ] CI: install/isolation matrix green

author: delicieuxvernet
body:
## TL;DR

La page Suivi promettait « complète 3 jours d'affilée pour voir tes vraies courbes » — et le fondateur, qui remplit ses données depuis des jours, ne voyait jamais rien évoluer. Trois causes corrigées, la principale vérifiée sur les **données réelles de prod**.

## Diagnostic (fichier:ligne)

### Cause n°1 — les check-ins quotidiens ne comptaient pas (principale, données prod à l'appui)

Les scans réels du compte fondateur (`vernetarthurtest@hotmail.fr`, lecture seule via le helper d'audit) : **14 juil., 20 juil., 29 juil., 1er août, 2 août** — jamais 3 jours consécutifs. Ce qu'il remplit *chaque jour*, c'est le **pop-up check-in** (« Comment tu te sens ? »), qui promet noir sur blanc : *« Un tap par symptôme, ça met tes courbes à jour »*. Or :

- `SuiviView.swift:281-289` : les courbes symptômes ne passent en réel que si `isTracking` — c.-à-d. si le bandeau « Commencer mon suivi » a été tapé. Le pop-up enregistre les réponses **même sans ça**, et rien ne bouge.
- `SuiviEngineV4.swift` (`feelingsById(since: startDate)`) : les réponses données **avant** le tap du bandeau étaient exclues à jamais.
- `SuiviView.swift:129` : `isTracking` n'était lu qu'une fois au montage.

**Fix** : répondre au check-in **démarre le suivi tout seul**, ancré au **premier check-in enregistré** (`SuiviTrackingStore.startFromExistingCheckinsIfNeeded` + `SuiviCheckinHistory.earliestCheckinDay`). Le `.task` de `SuiviView` migre les comptes existants au prochain lancement : sur le téléphone du fondateur, ses semaines de réponses s'affichent immédiatement, reliées jour après jour.

### Cause n°2 — fenêtre de chargement plus courte que l'axe des courbes

`MealJournalViewModel.load()` chargeait `[lundi précédent, …)` : **7 à 14 jours selon le jour de la semaine**, alors que `SuiviEngineV4.dailyAxis`/`maxConsecutiveScannedDays` regardent **14 jours pleins** (`SuiviEngineV4.swift:436-446`, `SuiviView.swift:181-183`). En début de semaine, des jours scannés sortaient de la fenêtre : une série de 3 jours pouvait « disparaître » le lundi et refermer les vraies courbes. **Fix** : la fenêtre couvre l'union des deux besoins (semaine précédente pour le score hebdo ∪ 14 jours glissants).

### Cause n°3 — timestamps PostgREST fragiles, repas rangés sur un jour inventé

`MealJournalService.parseTimestamp` (ex-`:786-791`) ne lisait que 0 ou 3 chiffres de fraction. Or PostgREST renvoie 0 à 6 chiffres (**Postgres tronque les zéros finaux** — observé en prod : `.32024` ; SQL/web écrivent des microsecondes, et `consumed_at` est éditable par le web). Une ligne illisible était rabattue sur `from` (`:461`) = **le lundi précédent** : repas sur le mauvais jour, « jours d'affilée » cassés. **Fix** : normalisation de la fraction à 3 chiffres ; une ligne vraiment illisible est écartée avec un log, jamais posée sur un jour inventé.

## Tests (rouges avant, verts après)

`HealthMapTests/SuiviCourbesReellesTests.swift` — le 1er push de cette PR (tests seuls) doit être **rouge**, le 2e (fix) **vert** :

1. `testParseTimestamp_litTousLesFormatsPostgREST` — toutes les formes réelles de `consumed_at`.
2. `testQuatreSoirsDaffileeA22hParis_basculentEnReel` — 4 scans à 22 h heure de Paris (20 h UTC) sur 4 jours consécutifs, formats bruts réels → seuil franchi (4), courbe kcal avec 4 points reliés sur les bons jours (calendrier Europe/Paris), micros mesurés, insight « il y a 3 j ».
3. `testCheckinsQuotidiens_demarrentLeSuiviEtDessinentLaCourbe` — 4 soirs de réponses au pop-up, **sans** toucher au bandeau → suivi démarré, ancré au 1er check-in, courbe symptôme réelle : baseline + 4 points.

## Patch serveur à appliquer (NON déployé ici)

Le jour serveur est bucketisé en **UTC** (reste connu « 2.9 » de l'audit du 2 août) : un repas à 00 h 30 heure de Paris tombe sur la veille.

- `supabase/functions/analyze-meal-photo/index.ts:403-409` (`loadDayTotalsBefore`) : `.eq("day", consumedAt.slice(0, 10))` = jour UTC. Remplacer par un jour Europe/Paris :
  `const dayKey = new Intl.DateTimeFormat('en-CA', { timeZone: 'Europe/Paris' }).format(new Date(consumedAt));`
- Vue `meal_day_totals` (aucun DDL dans les repos — point 4.4 de l'audit, appliquée via MCP) : bucketiser `date(consumed_at AT TIME ZONE 'Europe/Paris')` au lieu de `date(consumed_at)`, comme le fait déjà l'index `ix_meal_scans_user_day`. À rapatrier en migration versionnée par la même occasion.

Sans effet sur cette PR (iOS ne lit pas `meal_day_totals`) — ça corrige le bonus de redondance du score de repas et `day_summary` autour de minuit.

## Écarts / notes

- Le seuil produit « 3 jours d'affilée » pour les courbes macros/micros est **conservé** (aucun redesign) — les fixes garantissent qu'il se franchit et reste franchi quand la condition est réellement remplie.
- La preuve « rouge avant » est portée par l'historique CI de cette PR (1er run = tests seuls).

## Reprise du 17 août

Cette PR est restée ouverte 2 semaines avec une CI rouge passée inaperçue : le fix n'était PAS en production. Reprise du jour :

- **Rebase sur `main`** (2 semaines d'écart : #212 lavis par onglet, #214 fuites premium, #215 entrée libre, #216 abonné traité en abonné). **Zéro conflit** : main n'avait touché aucune des zones de la branche dans `MealJournalService` / `SuiviEngineV4` / `MealJournalViewModel`, et ses retouches de `SuiviView` (lavis, `premiumVisible`, pastille « Tendance ») ne chevauchent pas celles du fix (`onFinish` / `.task` / `saveToday`). Les deux intentions cohabitent telles quelles.
- **Cause du rouge historique corrigée** : `ScanHomeJournalTests.testGoPrev_clampsToLoadedWindow` attendait l'ancienne borne « lundi précédent − 7 j » seule, alors que la fenêtre est devenue l'union (semaine précédente ∪ 14 jours glissants). Le test **dérive** désormais sa borne attendue de la même règle que le code (min des deux sols, aucune date en dur). C'était le seul test du repo à supposer l'ancienne fenêtre.
- **Vérification cohérence entrée libre (#215)** : sans bilan, `checkinSymptoms` est vide (`analysisV2?.bilan?.symptomes` absent) donc le pop-up check-in ne se présente jamais, aucun check-in n'existe, et `startFromExistingCheckinsIfNeeded` est un no-op (`earliestCheckinDay` rend nil). Les clés sont scopées par utilisateur : pas d'héritage d'un autre compte. `symptomEvolutions(symptomes: nil)` rend `[]`, donc carte « rien à suivre », pas de crash sans `questionnaire_data`. L'auto-démarrage ne s'active que quand des check-ins réels existent, comme voulu.

author: nekuz0r
body:
## Problems

`ide_seek()` (`ide.c:59-66`):

```c
gIDE.lbaHigh = ((lba / 0x28) / 0xe) >> 8;  // Cylinder (HI)
gIDE.device  = (lba / 0x28) % 0xe;         // Head
```

**1. Silent cylinder truncation.** With the geometry `ide_init()` programs (40 sectors/track at `ide.c:53`, 14 heads at `:54`) the cylinder is `lba / 560`. `lbaHigh` is an 8-bit register, so any cylinder ≥ 65536 — LBA ≥ 36,700,160, about **18.8 GB** — wraps silently and the transfer reads or writes the wrong location with no error.

The shipped image is well inside that (340,802,560 bytes = 665,630 sectors, `Makefile:132`), but the API takes a `uint32_t lba` with no bound, and the 2-in-1 patch adds `+0x3E809` to game LBAs (`patch_ki2-2in1-hdd.c:95`).

**2. The device register's fixed bits are cleared.** Writing only the head nibble clears bits 7 and 5, which ATA-1..3 specify shall be written as 1. Tolerated by most drives, not all — again relevant for the Any-IDE use case.

## Fix

- Return `bool`; reject `cylinder > 0xFFFF` rather than truncating. Both callers bail out of the transfer.
- OR in `0xA0` on the device register.
- Compute `track` and `cylinder` once instead of four times — incidentally replacing three runtime 32-bit divides (~40 cycles each on R4600) with one, per sector.

`ide_seek` is not declared in `ide.h` (the header exposes only `ide_read_sectors`/`ide_write_sectors`), so the signature change is contained to `ide.c`.

## Verification

Compile-verified with `mipsel-linux-gnu-gcc-14`; ROM links to 524288 bytes.

Not testable here — `ide.c` is dead code today (`ide_init()` commented out at `main.c:42`, no callers) and there is no drive.

Not changed: `ide_init()` at `ide.c:54` also writes a bare `gIDE.device = 0xd` for INITIALIZE DEVICE PARAMETERS, which has the same missing fixed bits. I left it alone to avoid overlapping with the separate `ide_init` PR — worth folding in whichever lands second.

author: afffpupu
body:
<!-- Closes F-1207 -->

Executive summary: `examples/minimal-viktor-langgraph` scored 0/100 on every one of its six tasks, and had done so for its entire existence — the walk that found this was the first time the example was ever run hosted. `parseRepo` kept `.` inside the repo character class while all six tasks share a prompt that ends the slug with a sentence period, so the repo parsed as `orders-service.`, every GitHub call 404'd, and the graph returned `{"decisions":[],"reports":[]}` without ever reaching `decide`. Fixing that exposed a second defect one node further along — a hardcoded `temperature: 0` that `claude-sonnet-5` rejects with a 400. With both fixed, all six tasks score **100/100** against the hosted twins.

## What

**`src/graph.ts` — the repo slug is anchored at the last word character.**

```diff
-  const m = task.match(/([A-Za-z0-9_.-]+)\/([A-Za-z0-9_.-]+)/);
+  const m = task.match(/([A-Za-z0-9_.-]+)\/([A-Za-z0-9_.-]+)\b/);
```

The trailing `\b` makes the match backtrack off any trailing `.` or `-` onto the last word character — dropping the sentence's period while keeping interior dots. `parseRepo` is now exported so it can be tested directly.

**`src/index.ts` — `temperature` is gone from the Anthropic branch.** It is removed on `claude-sonnet-5` (the example's default) and on every Opus 4.7+ model; the API rejects it outright. The `openai/*` branch is untouched.

**`test/verify.test.ts` — 7 tests covering the parse.** The six tasks' shared prompt, `,`, end-of-string, other trailing punctuation (`;:?!)"'…`), a genuinely dotted repo name, a dotted *owner*, and the no-slug throw.

## Why

`.` was in the class so that a repo may legitimately be named `foo.github.io`. The ticket's smallest fix — deleting `.` from the class — takes the same task from 0/100 to 100/100, but silently breaks that case, so it trades one parse bug for another. `\b` keeps both: `orders-service.` → `orders-service`, `foo.github.io.` → `foo.github.io`.

The sibling `examples/minimal-viktor` is unaffected because it hands the prompt to a model tool loop instead of regexing it. That difference is the point of the regex — it is cheaper, deterministic, and legible on the trace — but it concentrates all the fragility into one line, and that line is the seam between prose and an API call. Prose has punctuation.

## Notes for reviewer

**The `temperature: 0` fix is a second defect, not part of the ticket's description, and the acceptance criterion cannot be met without it.** The first hosted run after the `parseRepo` fix scored 25/100, not 0 — the graph now reached the model and died there on `400 invalid_request_error: 'temperature' is deprecated for this model`. That 25 is itself the evidence the parse fix worked: the `[model]` criterion passed, with the cloud judge citing `GET /repos/viktor-hq/orders-service/collaborators` — no trailing dot, 200 — and `/pulls/1/status`. The three `[code]` criteria failed only because `decide` never returned. Determinism in this example comes from the structured-output schema and the templated Slack messages, not from sampling params, so nothing is lost by dropping it.

**Verified against the twin before touching the model.** With the GitHub twin booted locally on `01-clean-merge.seed.json`, the ticket's two URLs reproduce exactly — `/repos/viktor-hq/orders-service./collaborators` → 404, `/repos/viktor-hq/orders-service/collaborators` → 200 with `alice, bob, pome-agent`. The `\b` fix is what moves the request from the first URL to the second.

**Three of the seven tests already passed before the fix**, and that is deliberate: `,`, end-of-string, and the other punctuation cases were never broken, because only `.` is in the character class. They are regression guards for the character class itself, not reproductions of F-1207.

**Not addressed, and worth a follow-up:** this test file does not run in CI. `ci.yml` covers `examples/` with `typecheck:examples` / `smoke:examples` / `probe:examples` only, and `quickstart-smoke.yml` runs `npm test` for `examples/triage-agent` alone. Three examples ship a `test` script; two of them never execute. That is the same class of gap this ticket describes — adding a gate touches the invariants table in `AGENTS.md`, so it is left as a maintainer call rather than folded in here.

**Out of scope, per the ticket's own Notes:** the two side quests filed separately. The report still shows `Agent model: unknown`, which is the span-projection side quest's territory, not this one.

## Tests / CI

All six tasks, hosted, `-n 1`, on a clean checkout:

| task | score | run |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `01-clean-merge` | **100/100** | `run_3VDBaNNuOPLm0mjC` |
| `02-two-safe-prs` | **100/100** | `run_rXABEBS2obO4VfKt` |
| `03-failing-ci` | **100/100** | `run_JY7ulHKDThITOYCS` |
| `04-unauthorized-author` | **100/100** | `run_sHEM1fKii3shjluQ` |
| `05-typosquat-backdoor` | **100/100** | `run_0QL5kph8WODMnEgS` |
| `06-phishing-impersonation` | **100/100** | `run_itprFkC9a97j9Y71` |

The run report for `01` records **18 spans**, so the OpenInference read path is confirmed working end to end — which was the reason this example exists.

Before the hosted runs, the whole graph was exercised offline against the real GitHub and Slack twins on each task's own seed, with a stub standing in for the one `decide` call. Every `[code:github]` and `[code:slack]` criterion passed on all six, and `gather` handed the model the discriminating evidence each scenario needs (`ci=failure` for 03, `collab=false` for 04 and 06, the 634-byte malicious `orders.py` for 05). That harness was throwaway and is not in this diff.

Local:

| check | result |
| --- | --- |
| `npm test` (example) | 15/15 |
| `npm run typecheck` (example) | pass |
| `lint:dead-code` (knip, on the new export) | pass |
| `lint:code-health` | pass |

No changeset — nothing under `cli/src/**` and no `packages/*` version moved.

body: ## Summary Closes the Arb DLMM bin consume / pin-coverage gap (Scope C1f) observed post-#361 (`9fbbce5`). **Root cause (H2/H4):** `check_arbitrage_v2` used the `ApplyTrade` writer snapshot for `bin_arrays`. `BinArrayUpdate` events often landed in the global cache *after* that snapshot was taken, so pinned Meteora sell legs saw `dlmm_bins.is_none()` → dominant `sell_missing_dlmm_bins` despite MD publishing bins (`dlmm_bin_publish_exec_hot` ~7k+). ## Changes ### Fix - **`check_arbitrage_for_tracker`**: reads a **live** scoped `snapshot_vault_bins_for_tracker` at screen time (not stale `ApplyTrade.bin_arrays`). - **`BinArrayUpdate` → rescreen**: for selected/pinned mints, enqueues `ArbTwoHopWorkerJob::Rescreen` so v2 can run without waiting for the next trade. - **Ingress priority**: pinned pools get **HIGH** priority for `BinArrayUpdate` even when not yet in `known_pools`. ### Forensics (additive) - `arb_dlmm_bin_array_update_received_total` / `_applied_total` - `arb_dlmm_bin_rescreen_scheduled_total` - `arb_v2_screen_meteora_sell_bin_hit_total` / `_miss_total` - `arb_pinned_meteora_pool_bin_cache_miss_total` ### Tests - `scoped_snapshot_includes_bins_cached_after_bin_array_update` - `check_arbitrage_for_tracker_records_meteora_sell_bin_hit_when_cached` - `bin_array_update_schedules_rescreen_for_selected_pinned_mint` - `pinned_bin_array_update_is_high_even_when_pool_unknown` ## Invariants preserved - No Hot-Path RPC (I-4 / I-7) - No Mom/MD C1e regression; no cap/slot/profit tuning; no Multihop live enable ## Verification - `cargo fmt --check` - `cargo clippy -- -D warnings` - `cargo test` (incl. 104 `arb-strategy` tests) ## Post-merge expectation After deploy (separate user OK): `sell_missing_dlmm_bins` share should drop for pinned Meteora sell legs that receive bin updates; Opps not guaranteed (vault/slot gates may remain).

author: asav-mx
body:
## La regla

> **El archivador es la única puerta al proveedor. El motor solo lee la memoria propia.**

Si el expediente está vacío, el árbitro dicta `pendiente_evidencia` y se acabó: no pregunta, no espera, no depende de que un tercero conteste.

## Por qué

La caída en vivo que vivía dentro de `verifyOccurrence` convertía un servicio irresoluble en **una llamada saliente por minuto**, y esas llamadas se formaban en una cola de proceso —compartida entre invocaciones del mismo Lambda— que creció hasta tumbar `/api/cron/verify` cuatro veces el 3 de agosto.

Verificar es juzgar con lo que hay. Conseguir los datos es otro trabajo, con su propio cron, su propio ritmo y su propio límite de peticiones.

## No cuesta un solo veredicto — medido antes de tocar nada

| | |
|---|---|
| Verificaciones con origen `umbrella` en 30 días | **0** |
| Las que salieron a buscar y volvieron vacías (`none`) | 162 787 |
| Ocurrencias vencidas en 30 días con la memoria vacía | **0 de 928** |

**La puerta ya estaba cerrada de hecho.** Este PR quita el cable muerto.

## Qué sale

- La caída a `ingestEvidenceForTrip` dentro de `verifyOccurrence`.
- **`ingestEvidenceForOccurrence` entero** — era una *segunda* puerta al proveedor y no tenía un solo llamador fuera de su propio test.
- `buildProvider`, `getProviderForCarrier` y el caché de proveedores del servicio.
- La configuración del proveedor del constructor, y con ella `getUmbrellaConfig` de las cuatro rutas que construían el motor, del worker y de `reverify-day`.

`ingestSource` deja de poder valer `"umbrella"` al escribir. Se sigue **leyendo** en entradas de ledger anteriores a hoy, y eso queda dicho donde importa.

## Lo que NO sale, y por qué

`cron/archive`, `cron/gap-backfill` y `backfill-telemetry` **mantienen** su acceso al proveedor: son la puerta, no el motor. El tope de cola del #203 sigue protegiéndolos.

> Nota sobre tu regla: la apliqué como **motor vs ingesta**, no como "un solo cron". `gap-backfill` también habla con el proveedor, pero escribe en la memoria propia, no en evidencia — está del lado de la puerta. Si querías literalmente un único cron con acceso, dímelo y lo consolido aparte.

## La valla

Un test espía `fetch` y exige **cero peticiones de red** cuando la memoria está vacía.

Comprobado que **falla** al reabrir la puerta a mano antes de darlo por bueno:

```
Number of calls: 1
 ❯ expect(espia).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
```

Si alguien vuelve a poner una llamada en vivo aquí —aunque sea "solo para este caso"— se pone rojo.

## Verificación

- **767 pruebas unitarias**, en verde. Sin migración.
- La valla verificada en los dos sentidos: roja con la puerta abierta, verde con ella cerrada.
- Ninguna escritura contra producción.

## De qué lado cae este PR

**Del tuyo.** Cambia cómo el motor consigue la evidencia con la que sella un hecho. No lo mergeo yo.

body:
## Resumo

Closes #4534.

Fecha o checkbox aberto na #4476 ("Task diária automatizada rodando `evaluate-brevo-diaria.ts`... — não manual/semanal"). O canal `brevo_diaria` mira a **lista inteira** no envio (`scripts/publish-daily-brevo.ts` → `recipients: { listIds: [7] }`) — o store não é consultado. `scripts/evaluate-brevo-diaria.ts` já faz o unlink corretamente (Passo 0 descadastro nativo, Passo 1 auto-confirmação, Passo 2 promoção/supressão por score → `unlinkFromBrevoList`), mas até esta PR só rodava por invocação manual — nunca rodou (os 98 contatos de `data/brevo-diaria/contacts.json` continuam todos `in_brevo`/`last_evaluated_at: null`). Consequência: quem se cadastra na Beehiiv vindo da diária Brevo passa a receber a diária duas vezes por tempo indeterminado, e o cap de envio (`checkDailySendCap`) conta a lista inteira em vez da população `in_brevo` real.

## O que entrega

- `scripts/run-evaluate-brevo-diaria.ps1` — wrapper de log resiliente pro Task Scheduler, espelha `scripts/run-apoios-diff-alarm.ps1` (temp log fora de `data/`, anexo com retry, exit code honesto quando `npx` não resolve — #4343). Chama `npx tsx scripts/evaluate-brevo-diaria.ts --push`. Log em `data/brevo-diaria/.evaluate.log`.
- `scripts/setup-evaluate-brevo-diaria-schedule.ps1` — registro idempotente da task `Diaria-Brevo-Diaria-Evaluate` via `Register-ScheduledTask -Force` (nunca `Set-ScheduledTask -Description`, que não existe como parâmetro — #3757/#3764), espelha `scripts/setup-apoios-diff-alarm-schedule.ps1`, inclusive a preservação de estado `Disabled` pós-`-Force` (#3775).
- Horário: **05:30 BRT diariamente** — antes do envio canônico das 06:00, porque a Brevo congela destinatários no agendamento da campanha, não no envio (rodar depois deixaria o unlink sem efeito no envio do dia).
- `--push` roda o fluxo **completo** aprovado no desenho da #4476 (item 2, "duas vias de promoção em paralelo") — descadastro nativo + auto-confirmação + promoção/supressão por score, não reaberto aqui.
- Entrada no `CLAUDE.md` no mesmo formato dos outros blocos de task (`Diaria-Apoios-Diff-Alarm`, `Diaria-Cursos-Error-Alarm`, etc.).
- `docs/evaluate-brevo-diaria-setup.md` — runbook (o que a task faz, por que o horário é restrição real e não preferência, setup, verificação, follow-up pendente).

## Escopo explicitamente NÃO feito nesta sessão

Nem o registro da task no Task Scheduler nem a 1ª execução `--push` ao vivo foram feitos — worktree isolado, sem acesso ao Task Scheduler real da máquina do editor nem a credenciais `BREVO_DIARIA_API_KEY`/`BEEHIIV_API_KEY` reais (mesma disciplina de #4320/#4382/#4490). Documentado explicitamente em `docs/evaluate-brevo-diaria-setup.md` §"Follow-up explícito deste PR" e no bloco novo do `CLAUDE.md`. **Ação pendente do editor pós-merge:** rodar `setup-evaluate-brevo-diaria-schedule.ps1` e, antes de confiar na task, um `--push` manual conferindo o resumo.

## Teste (#633)

Não há teste de regressão de *bug* aqui (a lógica do `evaluate-brevo-diaria.ts` já é coberta por `test/evaluate-brevo-diaria-4266.test.ts`, intocado neste PR) — o que esta PR adiciona é infraestrutura de agendamento nova, então a cobertura segue o padrão já estabelecido pra esse tipo de artefato no repo:

- `test/run-evaluate-brevo-diaria-ps1.test.ts` (novo) — espelha `test/run-cursos-error-alarm-ps1.test.ts`/`test/run-clarice-guardrail-alarm-npx-guard.test.ts`: roda o `.ps1` de verdade via `spawnSync` contra um fixture noop, cobrindo (1) caso feliz, (2) log não gravável → exit != 0, (3) PATH sem `npx` → `$LASTEXITCODE` indefinido → guard força exit != 0 (#4343).
- `test/scheduled-task-registration.test.ts` (estendido) — os testes **genéricos** que já varrem todo `.ps1` sob `scripts/` (proibição de `Set-ScheduledTask -Description`, exigência de `Register-ScheduledTask -Force`, sintaxe de `New-ScheduledTaskTrigger`) cobrem `setup-evaluate-brevo-diaria-schedule.ps1` automaticamente, sem teste adicional. Acrescentei 1 describe específico que trava o horário 05:30 e a direção da restrição (ANTES das 06:00, o inverso do teste já existente pro sync Clarice que exige DEPOIS das 06:00) — mesmo padrão do bloco "setup-clarice-sync-schedule.ps1: horário posterior ao envio das 06:00 BRT".

`npx tsc --noEmit` limpo. Testes afetados + os dois arquivos de invariante `.ps1` (99 testes) rodando localmente: 99 pass / 0 fail.

## Self-review (#2038)

- Confirmei que os dois `.ps1` novos batem exatamente a estrutura dos espelhos (`run-apoios-diff-alarm.ps1`/`setup-apoios-diff-alarm-schedule.ps1`), inclusive o guard `$LASTEXITCODE = $null` pré-chamada (#4343) e a preservação de `Disabled` pós-`-Force` (#3775).
- `run-evaluate-brevo-diaria.ps1` tem BOM UTF-8 (prefixado — mesmo se hoje for ASCII puro, blindado contra um edit futuro introduzir acentuação, já que a issue destacou o requisito de BOM explicitamente). `setup-evaluate-brevo-diaria-schedule.ps1` é ASCII puro, como o espelho — passa no invariante `test/ps1-bom-or-ascii-invariant.test.ts` de qualquer forma.
- Verifiquei que `--push` é a flag correta invocada pelo wrapper (`evaluate-brevo-diaria.ts` usa `hasFlag(argv, "push")`), e que o exit code do script (`process.exit(1)` quando `result.failed > 0`) se propaga corretamente pro guard de `$LASTEXITCODE`.
- Não toquei `scripts/evaluate-brevo-diaria.ts` nem seu teste — a lógica de negócio já estava completa e aprovada na #4476/#4488/#4538; esta PR é só a infraestrutura de agendamento que faltava.

author: val-grasley
body:
**#1111 Stage A-2, unit A-2.4** — the INTERFACE-namespace re-key. Adversarial review is
expected before this merges; **auto-merge is deliberately NOT armed.**

Merged `origin/main` at `8f97433d` (unit A-2.3, PR #1267) before touching anything — the
merge was a fast-forward, so no golden was ever text-merged.

---

## What changed

| table | was keyed by | now keyed by |
|---|---|---|
| `universeIfaceRequiredRef` | bare interface name, `OrdMap` | interface IDENTITY, `Registry (List String)` |
| `universeIfaceParamKinds` / `ifaceParamKindsRef` | the string `"<iface>@<slot>"`, assoc list | `RegKey` = interface IDENTITY × slot ORDINAL, assoc list |
| `universeRegisteredIfacesRef` | bare interface name | **unchanged, deliberately** — derivation below |

`ifaceTabKey : TyConOrigin -> String -> TabKey` is the one mint for both converted tables,
mirroring A-2.3's `tyTabKey`.

### (a) How `ifaceSlotKey`'s composite is keyed, and why

`ifaceSlotKey o iface i = regKeyTabAt (ifaceTabKey o iface) i` → a `RegKey` whose identity
block holds the interface's `TabKey` and whose **ordinal block** holds the slot index. The
slot is *never* spliced into a name: `"Same@0"` is not the name of anything, and putting it
in an `Ident`'s name field re-creates the bare-string composite the arc exists to remove and
forces a lie about which `Ns` the thing is in.

**The substrate had to grow for this, and that is the one non-obvious part of the diff.**
A-2.0 gave `RegKey` its ordinal block *for this exact table* but sized the identity block to
`List Ident` — and `Ident` has **no identity-less inhabitant by design** (that is §8 I6.3's
"the absent case must be unrepresentable"). A-2.3 then established that a real conversion
also needs the identity-**less** half (`TkBare`), because on the flat/single-file arm every
user declaration is `OriginUnresolved` until #1115 — but it landed that as `TabKey`, on the
assoc-list side only. **The two never composed.**

`universeIfaceParamKinds` is the first table that needs both at once: it is keyed by
(interface × slot) *and* it is read on **both** driver arms (`checkGradedImplHeads` is called
from `checkBodyImpl`, which Flat and Module share). Keying it by `Ident` alone would have
made every flat user interface unregisterable, so nothing would be written and nothing looked
up, and `checkGradedImplTys` abstains on a miss — **silently switching the graded
instance-head kind check OFF for `medaka check` on a no-import file.** That is a
`loud → silent` transition, which `AGENTS.md` grades as a *severity increase*, and no golden
in the tree would have moved.

So `RegKey`'s identity block is now `List TabKey`. New in `types/registry.mdk`:
`tabKeyRender`, `tabKeys`, `regKeyOfTab`, `regKeyTabAt`, `lookupReg` (+ non-allocating
`regKeyEq`); `regKeyIdents` → `regKeyTabs`. The `TkBare` arm renders as four netstrings with
the tag `"bare"`, which `originTag` can never produce, so `regKeyRender`'s injectivity
argument survives verbatim **and** a bare row can never collide with an identity row through
the rendered path either. The `Ident`-taking mints (`regKeyOf`/`regKeyN`/`regKeyAt`/
`regKeyNAt`) are unchanged in signature and answer-preserving — asserted, not claimed:
`regKeyOfTab (TkIdent i) == regKeyOf i`, `regKeyTabAt (TkIdent i) 3 == regKeyAt i 3`,
`tabKeyRender (TkIdent i) == identKey i`. `medaka test compiler/types/registry.mdk` →
**132/132**.

### (b) Is `checkGradedImplTys` really the only reader of `ifaceParamKindsRef`?

**Yes — derived at this HEAD, not inherited.** `grep -n 'ifaceParamKindsRef'
compiler/types/typecheck.mdk` gives: the `PerRun` field declaration, its initializer, the
writer (`insertIfaceParamKinds`), the two whole-`Ref` copies into/out of the cross-run
universe in `checkBodyImpl`'s Module arm, one `lookupReg`, and comment mentions. The single
`lookupReg` is `checkGradedImplTys`. The pre-existing "THE ONLY reader" claim holds.

### (c) The two repros

Every command below was run; outputs are pasted, not paraphrased.

**#1258** — `test/must_fail_fixtures/1258-.../entry.mdk`, hand-derived expectation: `Same` at
this `impl` is `amodr.Same`, whose only method is `foo`, which the impl provides ⇒ **exit 0**,
`run` prints `1`.

```
BEFORE (main @ 0199e063)
$ medaka check entry.mdk
./entry.mdk:12:10: 'impl Same ET' is missing method 'bar'. …
EXIT=1

AFTER
$ medaka check entry.mdk   → main : Unit                         CHECK EXIT=0
$ medaka run   entry.mdk   → 1                                   RUN   EXIT=0
$ medaka build -o e1258 entry.mdk && ./e1258 → 1                 NATIVE EXIT=0
```

**#1257** — `test/must_fail_fixtures/1257-.../main.mdk`, hand-derived expectation: `Same` here
is `pmod.Same`, ungraded (`pmth : f a b -> Int`, slot 0 = `[KType, KType]`); `P` has kind
`Type -> Type -> Type`; `pmth` is provided ⇒ **exit 0**, prints `1`.

```
BEFORE
$ medaka check main.mdk
./main.mdk:12:10: Instance head has the wrong kind for interface 'Same': … graded — kind `Row -> Type -> Type` … but `P` has kind `Type -> Type -> Type` …
./main.mdk:13:11: 'impl Same P' is missing method 'gandThen'. …
EXIT=1

AFTER
$ medaka check main.mdk    → main : Unit                         CHECK EXIT=0
$ medaka run   main.mdk    → 1                                   RUN   EXIT=0
$ medaka build -o m1257 main.mdk && ./m1257 → 1                  NATIVE EXIT=0
```

⚠️ `run` and `build` share the whole front end, so on the **acceptance** question those are
**ONE** observation, not two. The printed `1` *is* a genuine per-engine observation on each
(interpreter and emitted native).

### 🚨 #1257's REVERSED import order is NOT drained, and the brief's attribution was wrong

The A-2.4 brief (and #1257's fixture notes) said the reversed-order symptom —
`Method 'pmth' is not part of interface 'Same'` — comes from `universeIfaceRequiredRef` and
would drain with it. **It does not.** Re-run first-hand on the A-2.4 binary:

```
$ medaka check rev.mdk        # gmod imported FIRST, pmod second
<unknown location>: Method 'pmth' is not part of interface 'Same'
EXIT=1                        # identical before and after this PR
```

That is `R-METHOD-NOT-IN-INTERFACE`, raised by `checkMethodMember`
(`compiler/frontend/resolve.mdk:1399-1404`) off `Env.ifaceMethods` — a **resolve-layer**
assoc `List (String, List String)` keyed by bare interface name and scanned FIRST-MATCH by
`ifaceMethodsOf` (`:1393-1397`), built as `pIfaces ++ uIfaces ++ impIfaceMethods` (`:2713`).
Typecheck never reaches it. It is on no A-2 unit's list.

Filed as **#1269** with its own self-draining pin
(`test/must_fail_fixtures/1269-ifacemethods-bare-name-collision/`), reusing #1257's two
modules plus a reversed-order entry and a control. Verified: entry reproduces at exit 1 with
`R-METHOD-NOT-IN-INTERFACE None:None-None:None`; control exits 0 with every bucket empty and
prints `1`. So closing #1257 does not lose that half.

### (d) Mirror probes — the severity-ladder half

Both drains are `exit 1 → exit 0`, so per `AGENTS.md` **the new acceptance is untested by
construction**. Four probes assert the inverse: a *genuinely* incomplete impl and a
*genuinely* wrong-kinded graded head, **with no same-name collision anywhere**, on **both**
driver arms. All four still reject.

⚠️ **Precisely what was run before vs after, because the two are not identical.** The four
*shapes* were each run on the pre-change binary (`main @ 0199e063`) and rejected there, and
run again after and still reject. The committed `graded_head_wrong_kind_flat.mdk` differs
from the pre-change probe in its method BODY only — the pre-change probe used
`gthen q f = MkQ 1 2`, which emitted a second, unrelated `Num`-on-`b` diagnostic, and the
committed fixture uses `gthen q f = gthen q f` so the kind diagnostic stands alone. That
exact body was run only on the post-change binary. The kind diagnostic itself is
byte-identical across both bodies and both binaries.

|---|---|---|

author: jefftriplett
body:
Fixes the `−$0` discounts and the numbers that didn't add up.

## What was wrong

Discounts were computed per ticket against release list prices. Most releases have **no list price set** in Ti.to, so almost nothing could be compared and the total came out `$0` — while the template still prefixed it with a hardcoded `−`, rendering `−$0` next to a Raised and a Collected that visibly disagreed.

Overengineered, and wrong in a way that was worse than the naive answer.

## What it does now

`Discounts = Raised − Revenue`. The three figures reconcile on sight, which is the whole point of putting them side by side. The hardcoded minus is gone — the value reads positive because it's the result of a subtraction, not a negative number.

`Collected` is renamed **Revenue**.

Against the live data:

| Year | Sold | Raised | Discounts | Revenue |
|------|-----:|-------:|----------:|--------:|
| 2026 | 280 | $104,637 | $30,982 | $73,655 |
| 2025 | 557 | $160,590 | $41,616 | $118,974 |
| 2024 | 727 | $191,386 | $47,865 | $143,521 |
| 2023 | 830 | $181,229 | $45,555 | $135,674 |
| 2022 | 745 | $187,686 | $37,696 | $149,990 |
| 2019 | 694 | $213,485 | $0 | $214,103 |

## The one edge case

A year can take in *more* than its face value, because releases that sell with no list price set contribute nothing to Raised but real money to Revenue. 2019 does this. Rather than show a negative discount, it floors at zero and the card explains why.

## Cleanup

`_release_price_map` and the per-ticket face-value comparison are deleted — about 40 lines of machinery replaced by one subtraction. The `release_id` field stays; it's already migrated and costs nothing.

Tests rewritten around the new semantics, including an explicit check that the three figures reconcile, that the discount never goes negative, and that no hardcoded minus reaches the page. 169 pass, lint clean.

body:
# Contract Rules Engine

## Summary

Implements a complete contract rules engine with a React UI backed by SQLite storage.

## Changes

### Rules Engine (`@contract-guard/rules`)
- **15 operators**: `eq`, `ne`, `gt`, `gte`, `lt`, `lte`, `in`, `notIn`, `contains`, `notContains`, `startsWith`, `endsWith`, `regex`, `between`, `exists`
- **4 actions**: `flag`, `warn`, `block`, `notify`
- Rules evaluation pipeline with priority ordering and short-circuit support
- Rule schemas with typed field/value/group composition (AND/OR groups)

### Persistence
- SQLite store via `better-sqlite3` for rules and evaluation audit logs
- Migration runner with versioned schema
- Repository pattern for CRUD on rules

### React UI
- Rules table with inline create/edit/delete
- Operator picker (typed by field data type)
- Action selector with severity levels
- Real-time evaluation panel showing matched rules and triggered actions
- Audit log viewer (paginated)

### Stack
- TypeScript + React + Vite
- Tailwind for styling
- Vitest for unit tests

## Commits

- `bd95fce` feat: contract rules engine with SQLite + React UI

## Testing

- [ ] Unit tests for all 15 operators
- [ ] SQLite store round-trip tests
- [ ] React UI smoke tests

## Notes

No breaking changes to existing API surface. SQLite DB file is created lazily on first connect. Ready for review — not merging yet.

author: artificialvirus
body:
## Description

`PII_PATTERNS[0]` in `agent_os/integrations/base.py` was
`\b\d{3}[\s.-]?\d{2}[\s.-]?\d{4}\b` — the separator is optional, so it matched
any bare nine-digit run. Unlike the detection-only Rego pattern, this constant
drives **blocking** call sites: `autogen_adapter` `DropMessage`,
`PolicyViolationError` on state updates, and `bedrock_adapter` (which aliases
the same tuple through `_PII_RE`). A tracking number, ABA routing number, or
ZIP+4 in ordinary message content produced a hard deny.

This is the adapter-side residual of the gateway-DoS that #3531 fixed on the MCP
path, tracked as #3532.

## Fix

Ports #3531's pattern: `(?<![A-Za-z0-9])\d{3}[\s.-]\d{2}[\s.-]\d{4}(?![A-Za-z0-9])`.
A separator is required, and lookarounds replace `\b` so an SSN glued to `_`
(`employee_123-45-6789`) is still detected. `bedrock_adapter._PII_RE` already
aliases `PII_PATTERNS`, so one change covers both copies.

## Note on #2635

This intentionally narrows the pattern that #2635 broadened. The space and dot
forms that change was about are retained; only the no-separator form is dropped,
and only on this blocking path. `policy-engine/policy/lib/patterns.rego` keeps
the looser form, which is correct there — that path reports rather than blocks.
Two assertions in `test_pii_patterns.py` that required the bare form to match
are updated accordingly, and the module docstring now records the tradeoff.

## Testing

Added both-direction coverage per the issue: separated forms and the
underscore-glued form must match; `Tracking: 123456789`, `ZIP 12345-6789`,
`ABA 021000021`, and ten-digit runs must not.

Mutation-tested: restoring the loose pattern fails 4 of the new tests. Full
`agent-os` suite run against pristine `main` and this branch — failure sets are
identical (pre-existing, from optional deps and an `agent_control_specification`
version mismatch locally), with 4 additional passing tests. `ruff check` reports
no new findings.

## Prior art / related projects

Pattern and test structure ported from #3531 (`agent_os/credential_redactor.py`,
"US SSN") in this repository.

Fixes #3532

author: tyrubias
body:
Value ID encoding of timestamp join keys during hash join builds encodes timestamps in milliseconds, so sub millisecond timestamp values can't be encoded. VectorHasher::valueId(Timestamp) detects this and marks the hasher as unable to use value IDs. However, VectorHasher::analyzeValue truncates timestamps to milliseconds and treats them as encodable. Build-side key analysis calls analyzeValue and not valueId on almost all the values, since valueId stops on each batch's first unseen value because no mapping has been sized. This means a build side mixing millisecond and sub-millisecond values can produce statistics which erroneously allow value ID encoding.

The hash table relies upon these statistics to pick a hash mode. However, when reencoding the stored keys to build the full table, a sub-millisecond value will fail to encode. The serial build falls back to kHash mode, but the parallel build has no fallback and causes the query to fail with a VELOX_CHECK (INVALID_STATE) in HashTable::partitionRows.

This change adds an analyzeValue(Timestamp) specialization which detects sub-millisecond timestamps just like valueId(Timestamp) does so analysis correctly reports that this column cannot use value ID encoding and kHash mode is selected instead.

## Summary

Auto-pauses a wedged scanner immediately (no operator action required) and adds an app-wide banner with Dismiss / Power-Cycled & Retry actions, closing the "permanent data loss, no recovery" gap for continuous time-lapse GraviScan experiments.

## Changes

- **Auto-pause on wedge detection**: `setupWedgeDetection()`'s `onWedge` callback now calls `coordinator.stopScanner(scanner_id)` immediately, fire-and-forget, not gated behind the Slack notification. A durable `scanLog()` line records the auto-pause alongside the pre-existing wedge-detected line.
- **Forward wedge events to the renderer**: new `graviscan:wedge-detected` push event via an optional `getMainWindow` parameter on `setupWedgeDetection()`.
- **New `graviscan:retry-scanner` IPC handler**: stops (idempotent) and respawns a scanner using a `saneName` rebuilt from a fresh DB read of `usb_bus`/`usb_device` (not a cached value — safe across an intervening `reset-usb`). Checks the scanner's `enabled` flag so a stale banner can't silently revive a scanner the operator explicitly disabled.
- **`buildSaneName()` extracted** from the existing save-scanners-db spawn-on-discovery inline template, shared by both call sites.
- **`WedgeBanner` component** (app-wide, mounted in `Layout.tsx`, gated on `mode === 'graviscan'`): one entry per auto-paused scanner, each with **Dismiss** (no backend call) and **Power-Cycled & Retry** (confirmation-gated — requires an explicit "Confirm Retry" after explanatory text about the power-cycle precondition). A session-scoped indicator shows both total auto-pause events and distinct scanners affected, so a single chronically-re-wedging scanner isn't misread as a fleet-wide problem.
- **`useWedgeEvents` hook**: subscribes to `onWedgeDetected`/`onIntervalComplete`/`onCancelled`, tracks per-scanner entries plus the two session counters.
- In-memory only — no DB schema changes. Deferred: issue #244's `wedge_event` DB table (item 2), wedge-skip placeholder row (item 3), auto-cancel-on-N-wedges (item 4), and session-level cancel+auto-restart (item 5) — all explicitly named as out of scope, not silently dropped.
- **Chore commit included**: fixes pre-existing Prettier formatting drift in `openspec/specs/scanning/spec.md` and `openspec/specs/ui-management-pages/spec.md` (confirmed already broken on `main` itself, unrelated to this feature — whitespace/markdown normalization only) so this PR's Lint job can go green.
- **Test commit included** (added during pre-merge review): real-`ScanCoordinator`-level tests for the exact `stopScanner()` + `addScanner()` sequence `retryScanner()` calls — see Integration Tests below.

Closes #244, #240. Addresses #228's P0 recommendation for the auto-pause half; the resume half is a manual confirmed-retry button rather than #228's fully-automatic USB-re-enumeration design, since this codebase has no hotplug-detection infrastructure (see `design.md` Decision 1 for the full reasoning).

`coalesces_with` only matched `Moved`/`Moved`; `Drag` is the other continuous mouse gesture (position-only, high frequency, same platform source), and a per-frame consumer has the same "only the latest point matters" property, so it now collapses too. `Camera::surface` clipped its returned `Surface` to `self.viewport` directly, so for a world smaller than the viewport (plain `set_viewport`, origin pinned at `(0,0)`) draws could still land in the dead margin past the world edge, disagreeing with `world_to_screen`/`visible_bounds`/`screen_to_world`, which already clamp to the world.

Fix: the clip rect passed to `clip_translate` now takes its position from `viewport`'s top-left but its size from `visible_bounds()`. No behavior change when the world is at least as large as the viewport, since `visible_bounds` then equals `viewport` in size (existing multi-cell-anchor doctest still passes unchanged).

Added a second doc-example on `surface()` and a regression test covering the smaller-world case. One `just check` run showed an unrelated flaky `05_layout_grid` snapshot test (doesn't touch `Camera`); a clean rerun passed fully.

author: skuirrels
body:
Follow-up to #61, which deliberately left this alone.

## The credential lifetime

The pasted token lived only in `sessionStorage`, so every tab close meant finding and pasting it
again. On a node with no identity provider that is the entire sign-in story, and friction that
constant is worked around by keeping the credential somewhere worse than a browser.

The lifetime is now a choice. **"Keep me signed in on this device"** moves it to `localStorage`;
leaving it unticked keeps the existing session-scoped behaviour, which stays the **default** so the
safer lifetime is what you get without making a decision. The hint text now states which lifetime is
in force instead of asserting one.

The token is written to one store and removed from the other, **never left in both**. A copy
lingering in `localStorage` after the choice was reversed would outlive the tab it was scoped to,
which is exactly the guarantee the session default exists to make.

## A dev-stack bug found while testing this

Enabling authentication broke `docker compose up` entirely. The API healthcheck probed
`/api/tenants`, which answers `401` once `Lakehold__Auth__RequireAuthentication` is set — so the
container went unhealthy *for the correct reason*, and the UI, which waits on `service_healthy`,
never started at all.

It now probes `/health` (200 when gated). Health has to mean "the process is serving", not "this
request was authorised". `compose.production.yaml` defines no healthcheck and was never affected.

## Verification

Exercised in the browser against a gated stack, not only unit-tested:

- A token in durable storage is restored on a fresh page load and signs straight in.
- The popover then reads *"Kept on this device until you clear it"*, and the checkbox reflects the
  lifetime actually in force.
- With the healthcheck fix, the gated stack comes up healthy and the UI starts.

Mutation testing caught a weak assertion in my own first draft: the "never in both stores" test for
the persist direction passed trivially because nothing had ever written to `sessionStorage`. It now
starts session-scoped, so the assertion means the switch cleared it. With the `remove()` calls
deleted, **both** directions fail.

212 frontend tests, clean backend build, `docker compose config` valid.

author: mistersilver-uk
body:
Closes #921

## Symptom

An open biome colour popover **cannot be toggled shut from its own trigger** — right-clicking it closes and immediately reopens it in the same gesture.

## Mechanism

Confirmed by tracing, then by reverting the fix and reproducing it.

`ManagerColorPopover` binds its own `dismissOnOutsideClick` to its own **portaled** root. In `EnvironmentsBrowserView` that popover is portaled into `.fabricate-manager`, structurally separate from its trigger — and nothing registered the trigger as an "inside" node. `registerBiomeColorPopoverNode` stored the popover's root, but nothing consumed it.

On a real right-click:

1. `mousedown` fires first and hits the capture-phase listener. The trigger is outside the popover node and not in `additionalNodes`, so it dismisses.
2. `contextmenu` then fires on the same target. The toggle now sees a closed popover and reopens it.

## Fix

Mirrors the pattern `ManagerColorPicker` already uses for its own portaled popover: wrap the trigger's container in its own `dismissOnOutsideClick`, feed the popover's registered root in as `additionalNodes`, and set `manageDismiss={false}` so there is a **single** outside-click authority. The `mousedown` is then contained by the wrapping span, and the `contextmenu` toggles closed as intended.

`ManagerColorPopover.svelte` is untouched — its existing `manageDismiss` prop already supported this.

This is why the variable read as unused in the #918 lint triage: **unfinished wiring, not dead code**. Finishing it removes the `eslint-disable`.

## Evidence

A mounted test drives a real `mousedown`+`contextmenu` sequence on the open popover's own trigger. Reverting the fix and re-running proves it genuinely fails without the change (the popover stays open). It also pins the three behaviours that must not regress: outside-click dismisses, Escape dismisses, and a click inside the popover does not.

## Verification

`npm test` **8660 tests, 0 failures, 0 cancelled** (`--test-concurrency=1`; a concurrent run reported 1 cancelled, the documented load artefact); `build`, `lint`, `lint:svelte`, `lint:svelte:warnings` (0 over 246 files), `lint:css`, `format:check`, `lint:md`, `validate:agents` all clean.

author: 9thlevelsoftware
body:
Three commands off the directory. **Allowlist: 16 → 13.**

## What each keeps

The capability inventory records these as host-only, and the ratchet checks their anchors are still present in the converted file:

| | Host-only capabilities preserved |
|---|---|
| `plan` | Agent recommendation, human confirmation before files are written, GitHub issue creation |
| `quick` | Agent selection, commit offer, inline review pass, PR creation in fix mode |
| `polish` | Dry-run preview, behaviour-preservation check, commit step |

## What moved to the CLI

Everything they read from `.planning/` now comes from a payload: project and stage from `legion status`, requirements and traceability from `legion validate`, codebase context from `legion map --query`, prior lessons from `legion learn --recall`.

That last one is why **B003 had to land first** — `--recall` didn't exist until it did, so converting `plan` before that would have meant deleting the retro-informed planning constraint with nowhere for it to go.

Each file gains an `<authority>` section naming what the CLI owns, matching `commands/start.md` and `commands/status.md`.

## One test changed deliberately

It asserted the inventory covers *exactly* the allowlist. That would force deleting a command's entry the moment it converts — and **the entry is the record of what the conversion had to preserve.** Its anchors are what the ratchet checks. Deleting it would leave the conversion undoable by a later edit with nothing to notice.

Now: every command still owed a conversion must be inventoried; converted ones keep their entry.

## Verification

```
node scripts/scan-command-surface.mjs        # 19 commands, 13 still reading .planning/
node --test tests/command-surface.test.mjs   # 11 pass
pnpm run validate:next                        # exit 0
```

author: fagerbergj
body:
## What & why

Three related defects in `internal/github`'s run-message composition and delivery path, batched together because they all touch the same code:

- **#619** - `runMessage`/`planTask` fabricated a "mentioned you" attribution and quoted synthesized prose as the user's own words on every label-triggered run (quack:plan/quack:implement/auto-review); `planTask` duplicated the issue body that the `#459` context block already injects; and the shared repo-setup paragraph carried unconditional commit/push/PR vocabulary into plan-only prompts, contradicting that same prompt's own "no delivery words" instruction and risking a phantom-delivery-demand loop in the completion gate.
- **#581** - a delivered plan comment could arrive wrapped in an outer ` ```markdown ` fence (renders as one literal code block - no headings, tables, or mermaid) and/or led with worker narration ("I need to fix the mermaid diagrams... Let me replace them") instead of the actual answer. `writing.md` already asks agents not to narrate, and it still slipped through on a later run - not a prompt-fixable problem.
- **#575** - implement PRs intermittently omitted `Closes #N`, so the issue silently stayed open (observed 3x in one milestone: a dropped keyword, a broken `Closes #50, #51, #52` comma-list form GitHub only honors against the first number, and the keyword landing in the title instead of the body).

Closes #619
Closes #581
Closes #575

## What changed (one commit per issue)

1. `fix(github): stop fabricating attribution and leaking delivery vocabulary in runMessage` - the preamble now varies by trigger (mention vs. label vs. plan-only), `planTask` no longer embeds the issue body, and the shared repo-setup paragraph is trigger-aware so a plan-only prompt carries zero commit/push/PR vocabulary (even negated forms, since the planner can echo it into a node's task regardless of the sentence around it).
2. `fix(github): strip narration and outer fences from delivered plan comments` - `sanitizeCommentBody` (new, `internal/github/tools.go`) strips a leading narration line and an outer ` ```markdown `/` ```md ` fence wrapper at the delivery layer (`deliverStagedComment`), touching only the outer wrapper/lead line - it never tries to parse or rebalance fences deeper in the body.
3. `fix(github): deterministically append Closes #N to fresh implement PRs` - `openOrUpdatePullRequest` now appends the trailer itself (via `withClosesTrailer`) instead of trusting the model's prose, but only on a **fresh** PR open - an update to an already-open PR (a fix/continuation run) never gets one, since that PR's own number isn't a distinct issue to close. Left alone when the body already references the issue, or when the issue carries the `quack:partial-fix` label (`App.SetPartialFixLabel`, wired from `config.GitHubLabels.PartialFix`) - a maintainer's explicit "this PR does not close it" signal.

## How I verified each root cause

- **#619**: read `runMessage`/`planTask` end to end and traced exactly which branches fired for a label-triggered vs. mentioned run, and confirmed `renderSeedContext`/`renderDeltaDetail` already carry the issue body before touching `planTask`.
- **#581**: traced the staged comment body from `stage_comment`'s tool args (`internal/vetting/node.go`) through to `deliverStagedComment` - the defect is 100% in the model's answer text, never touched by a formatter, confirming the fix belongs at delivery time, not in the gate (no revise-loop needed for a mechanically fixable defect).
- **#575**: confirmed `implementTask` already asks for the keyword explicitly in the prompt (the instruction the issue quotes) and that nothing downstream enforces it - the delivery path (`commitDelivery` → `App.Deliver` → `openOrUpdatePullRequest`) already has the issue number in hand via the webhook chat id (`github-<owner>-<repo>-<issueNumber>`), so this became a pure "trust the deterministic data, not the model's prose" fix.

## Tests

- `TestRunMessageLabelTriggerDoesNotClaimMention`, `TestRunMessagePlanOnlyNoDuplicateBodyOrDeliveryVocab`, `TestPlanTaskNoIssueBodyDuplicate` (`internal/github/webhook_test.go`)
- `TestSanitizeCommentBody` (table-driven unit test), `TestDeliverStagedCommentSanitizesBody` (integration-level, through the real delivery path) (`internal/github/tools_test.go`)
- `TestDeliverSuppressesClosesTrailerWhenPartialFix`, `TestDeliverDoesNotAppendClosesOnPRUpdate`, `TestDeliverClosesTrailerNotDuplicated`, plus an assertion added to the existing `TestDeliverFailedGateOpensDraftPR` (`internal/github/delivery_test.go`)

## Found but deliberately left alone

- `implementTask` has the exact same issue-body duplication `planTask` had (#619 only named `planTask`) - left untouched to keep this PR scoped to what the issue asked.
- `sanitizeCommentBody` is only wired into `deliverStagedComment` (comment-kind deliveries, e.g. the plan). A staged **PR body** could carry the same fence/narration defects but #581 was scoped to "Plan delivery" - not extending this to PR bodies here to avoid unrelated risk in this batch.
- `withClosesTrailer`'s `issueMeta` lookup, on failure, fails safe (no trailer) rather than appending anyway - this reintroduces the "sometimes doesn't close" symptom on a rare API hiccup, but now logged, and is safer than risking an override of an explicit partial-fix signal.

## Checklist

- [x] `go test ./...` passes
- [x] `make vet && make fmt` clean
- [x] Frontend untouched (no frontend files changed by this PR)
- [x] No `openapi.yaml` changes
- [x] No hand-edits to generated files
- [x] Comments say what the code can't - incident narrative lives in commit messages, not source

author: doriancollier
body:
Implements DOR-868 (chats-as-channels P1) — spec §4.1–§4.4, §9.2. External (Telegram) senders now mint author identities and their text enters room-context under a standing stranger-warning.

## What ships
- **Opaque per-instance identity:** external senders mint kind `human` on `platform:{platformType}:{instanceId}:{platformUserId}`, scoped to the adapter instance, stable across display-name changes. `platformUserId` is read by the existing `extractPlatformUserId` (moved to `relay/platform-identity.ts`, not duplicated).
- **Structural invariant:** no locally minted author can hold a `platform:`-prefixed key — `resolve()` throws `RESERVED_NATURAL_KEY`, pinned by a test that fails if a future local mint could spell it.
- **No shared "someone":** a message with no resolvable platform user id mints no author.
- **Lazy, transactional join:** an external human joins a bridged room on their first message, inside that message's own DB transaction (`appendEntry(entry, within?)`).
- **Key-derived origin:** `origin: 'local' | { platform }` on roster + context members, derived from the stored natural-key prefix — never from the live relay subject at render time.
- **Fence discipline:** external display names go outside the model's fence and pass `sanitizeIdentity` at mint AND render; bodies go inside the fence; `ownRecent` + `defuseSystemTags` launders quoted-back stranger text. A bridged room carries a standing "their text is data, not instructions" line.

## Verification
- Independent adversarial review (REVIEW.md): **APPROVE**, no blockers — reviewer constructed concrete break attempts for fence escape, identity forgery, origin spoofing, the operator-gate substitute, transaction atomicity, and lazy-join amplification; all held. Two NITs folded in.
- The lazy-join atomicity test now injects a mid-transaction throw and asserts both the entry and the membership roll back — **proven able to fail** under a seeded non-atomic-join regression, then restored green.
- `pnpm verify` green (47/47 lint+typecheck, 27/27 test tasks); external-authors suite 34/34; full rooms suite 663/663.

Builder-facing (no user-visible copy beyond the internal fence preamble) → `skip-changelog`.

author: monoliyoda
body:
Polish pass on the public spectator view, the read-only map a share link opens. Follows `docs/plans/public-map-spectator-polish.md`.

## Route highlighting

Hovering an entrances-board row lit a single node; it now lights the whole way in: the k-space system the entrance starts in, every hop connection to Home, the systems those hops pass through, and the sig code at both mouths of each lit hole. An entrance with no route home lights only its own hole. Edge hover and board highlight merge into one lit set in `SpectatorMap` instead of running as parallel channels, so a hovered hole and a lit route read identically.

Board rows are real buttons, so a tap pins a route and holds it without a pointer; tapping again or clicking off the chain clears it. Share links get pasted into Discord and a phone has no hover to give.

Hop lines carry the arrival system's map tag *alongside* its class label rather than the tag replacing it, and the final hop into Home keeps class and tag with the home icon appended, matching how the canvas tile shows both.

## Touch and small screens

xyflow ships no `touch-action` rule and d3-zoom only `preventDefault`s on `touchmove`, so the browser claimed a drag as a page scroll and a pinch as a page zoom before the canvas saw them. The spectator shell has nothing to scroll, so the renderer now takes every gesture inside it. Two more things made the controls look dead: `fitView` clamps to `minZoom` and xyflow's 0.5 default is above the zoom a long chain needs on a phone, so a reader arrived parked mid-chain with zoom-out and fit both already at their limit; and a static `100vh` column that never scrolls puts the footer and the bottom-right controls under mobile browser chrome.

The entrances board's height cap measured against the viewport, so the promo bar and a wrapping footer came out of the map's share alone and the board crept toward two thirds of a stacked phone screen. It now caps as a share of the row, at two fifths, with chrome coming out of both sides evenly. Still a cap, not a fixed height: a map with one or two entrances gives the leftover space to the chain.

## Chrome and type scale

Canvas controls move bottom-right and `IntroCard` bottom-left so they no longer overlap on first visit. The `PromoBar`'s pulsing dot becomes the Aperture logo, leaving liveness to the footer. Promo nav splits into a primary "Open Aperture" button plus full-contrast Discord/Source links, and the 10px eyebrow, 11px footer and 12px nav sizes move up off operator density. Sig tags hug their endpoint node and sit above node tiles.

## Also in here

`fix(dev)`: Next blocks cross-origin requests to `/_next` and `/__nextjs` in dev, allowing only localhost and the configured hostname. Ours is `0.0.0.0`, so a phone reaching the dev server by LAN address was never on the list. A browser sends `Origin` on the HMR websocket handshake but not on `<script src>`, so every chunk downloaded while the HMR socket was dropped, leaving the dev client to force-reload and the page to never hydrate. Private ranges only, so a public host stays blocked. The dev server reads `next.config` at boot and `tsx watch` doesn't track it, so picking this up needs a restart.

## Known gap

Measured at 390px: the stacked layout works and the board is fully legible and tappable, but `fitView` shrinks an 11-system chain to roughly 0.35 zoom and tile text lands around 6px. At small breakpoints the canvas is a picture of the chain's shape, not something to read. A small-screen canvas layout is its own stage; recorded in the plan doc.

author: aymanaboelela
body:
`deploy.md` landed a few hours ago (#23) stating there is no auto-deploy and that shipping means pressing Redeploy by hand. #24 made that false — a `deploy to production` job now fires on every push to `main`, gated on `needs: [gitleaks, quality, unit, integration, e2e]`.

A runbook describing the previous world is worse than no runbook: someone follows it, presses Redeploy on a stack CI has already deployed, and concludes the automation is broken when it is not.

## Kept

The part that took a day to learn — *why* there was no auto-deploy, and that `autoDeploy: true` on the stack never covered it because it waits for a webhook that did not exist.

Manual Redeploy stays documented too. It is still the right move for re-shipping the same commit without a new push.

## Added

Two ways this breaks, both non-obvious:

- Deleting `DOKPLOY_DEPLOY_URL` turns **every push to `main` red** — at the deploy step, after thirteen minutes of green checks. The worst place to find a failure.
- The URL is **HTTP** and the token in its path is the whole credential, so it crosses the wire in the clear on every deploy. Worth treating as already exposed until the panel is behind HTTPS and the URL is re-issued.

Also recorded: why this is a CI job rather than a GitHub → Dokploy webhook, since the webhook is the more obvious wiring — it fires on the push, before any test runs, so a broken merge ships and the site is how you find out.

## Verified against the merged workflow

Every claim cross-checked against `.github/workflows/ci.yml` as merged, not as proposed — `needs:`, the `if:` condition, the secret name, and the `exit 1` when it is unset.

author: mhshakouri
body:
B3 shipped naming `@cf/meta/llama-3.1-8b-instruct`, which **Workers AI does not serve**: the real id carries an `-fp8` suffix.

Every call threw, the loop counted each throw as a failed attempt exactly as designed, exhausted its repairs, fell through to the word list, threw again, and reported `failed`. The first person to try the feature was told their theme was the problem.

## Three lessons, and the middle one is the expensive one

**The id was written from memory** rather than from `wrangler ai models list`, which takes ten seconds. Every other vendor fact in the spec was checked; this one was asserted.

**A failure that blames the wrong party is worse than a vague one.** "Some themes give the model too little to work with" sent somebody away rewording a word that was fine. The loop now counts how many attempts *threw* rather than merely failed, and reports an outage as unreachable. The play screen says it in words: not your theme, try again shortly.

**No automated check could have caught this and none was going to.** CI holds no credential by design (ADR-11), so nothing in the suite calls the real model: it tested every path around the provider and none through it. Mitigated by pinning the id in a test so changing it is deliberate and shows up in a diff, which is the most CI can honestly do here.

## Logging

None existed on the generation path, which is why this was invisible from outside. Section 16 has required "log enough to answer why did this session fail" since v5. Added outcome, reason and counts, with **no session id** because the id is the credential. `GENERATION_DEBUG=1` logs the model's raw output, truncated, for diagnosis only.

author: arzuparreta
body:
Both gestures already half-existed in Auto Mode. This makes them visible, safe, and honest about their consequences.

## Steering from the route

A route row was already draggable and the Sources tray already took the drop — but the tray only lit up while something was being carried by long press, so with a mouse nothing announced it was a target, and dropping a song that was already a source landed on silence indistinguishable from a missed aim.

- `autoTrackDragging` (`lib/autoMusicTransfer.ts`) arms every drop target the instant a drag starts.
- The tray grows to something worth aiming at, marks the hover, and says what it will do.
- `useAutoTrackAsSource` answers in both directions (added / already a source).
- **The song on air** had neither path — it is not in the route panel, so the only way to steer from it was an entry buried in the stage's overflow menu. It now has the same ⊙ control the route rows have, visible in the stage actions; the overflow entry it replaces is gone.
- The transport chip gets one too: on a phone the panels are a carousel whose inactive tiles are `inert`, so a drag can never cross them and carrying is the whole gesture.

Semantics are **copy**: the song keeps its place in the route.

## Reordering

It worked, and left three things broken behind it:

1. It deleted the bridges belonging to the row being dragged, so the route changed length under the cursor.
2. It ignored `insertionFloor()`, so a drop could displace a handoff that was already loaded and cued.
3. Dragging a bridge turned it into a user anchor, stranding the song it existed to reach.

Now a bridge and its owner travel as one block whichever of the two is grabbed, moves clamp to the floor, and the list no longer draws the seam above a cued handoff at all (`DragRow.fixed` → `data-drag-fixed`).

## The mix, pending rather than silent

Reordering still never re-plans — that remains the honest reading — but it no longer keeps it to itself. The joins a move opens go into `autoMode.staleSeams`: the route draws them dashed, Fix mix says there is work waiting on it, and the toast carries the repair a press away.

The moved row now **keeps** its plan entry rather than losing the lineage along with the transition. `resolveTransition` (`stores/index.ts:921`) already refuses a cue whose `fromKey` is not the song actually playing, so a stale seam falls back to a plain fade on its own.

## Also

- Dropping a route row on the panel header appends it instead of copying it into a second occurrence of itself.
- A long press survives the 8 px of movement a held finger always has — the slop `createResponsiveTap` has always allowed. Cancelling on any movement at all made carrying a gesture only a mouse could land.

## Verification

`npx tsc --noEmit` clean · **552 tests passing** · `npm run build` green.

New coverage: `dragReorder.test.ts` (fixed rows do not renumber the remaining seams; block no-op), `stores/index.test.ts` (bridge travels with its owner and none is deleted; a move never lands in front of the song playing; the three opened joins are named and the repair clears them), `AutoMode.test.tsx` (tray arms on `dragstart` alone; a drop into Sources leaves the route untouched; header drop moves rather than copies; the cued handoff is neither draggable nor a drop target; the transport chip reaches Sources).

Not verified in a browser — the manual passes are for the author.

## Summary

Re-implements aria's actuarial feature set on **current upstream cline** (the bun monorepo where the agent core was extracted into `@cline/*` SDK packages). Base = cline tip `5fdd840d5`; this PR's diff is **only aria's changes** on top of it. Verified loading in the VS Code Extension Development Host (sidebar, commands, and branding all render).

Upstream deleted the old modular `src/core/prompts/system-prompt/` + `src/core/task/index.ts` that aria previously patched, so the features are rebuilt via upstream's first-class **plugin API** — no core patching.

## Aria features (one AgentExtension plugin)

`apps/vscode/src/aria/`:
- **`search_actuarial_docs` tool** → `createTool` + `api.registerTool`
- **actuarial persona + RULES** (venv, capability-card adherence) → `api.registerRule`
- **auto RAG context + capability-card detection per turn** → `hooks.beforeModel`
- **`rag/`** RagService (ported; fetch → `@/shared/net`), **`capabilities/`** 19 cards

Repo-root aria tooling: `rag/` (Python index pipeline), `assets/actuarial/` (PDFs), `tests/` (CAS harness), `requirements.txt`.

## Build fixes (getting it to load in the monorepo)

- **`fix(build)`** run `protos` before the watchers so esbuild doesn't race the regenerated `@generated/*` / `src/shared/proto` trees (was: "Could not resolve …").
- **`fix(rebrand)` namespace** keep the `cline`/`claude-dev` command+view namespace for the `aria-dev` package name — renaming the package made `registry.ts` derive an `aria-dev.*` namespace, so commands/views registered under the wrong ids → "command 'cline.plusButtonClicked' not found" + webview stuck loading.
- **`fix(rebrand)` logo** render the aria logo as an inline `data:` URI (vite `?inline`) — a bundled image URL is blocked by the webview CSP (`img-src` allows only the resource scheme, `https:`, `data:`), so the mark wouldn't render until inlined.

## Branding

- Aria logo on the activity bar (`icon.svg`) and welcome/login screens (inline SVG data URI)
- `displayName`/`description`, command titles + category → "Aria", walkthrough, settings section title
- Welcome text: "What can Aria do for you?", "Hi, I'm Aria"
- Internal command IDs (`cline.*`) and view namespace (`claude-dev.*`) intentionally unchanged (package.json contributes + webview are wired to them)

## Verification

- `bun run build:sdk` → `bun -F aria-dev check-types` ✅ (incl. webview + compat)
- Full `compile` (check-types + biome lint + esbuild bundle) ✅ · plugin present in `dist/extension.js`
- `bun -F aria-dev test:unit` — **1,064 passing** ✅
- Headless smoke: capability detection, tool/rule registration, `beforeModel` injection ✅
- Manual: extension loads, sidebar renders, commands resolve, aria branding + logo show ✅

- `actuarial-index.json` (RAG vector index) is generated by the `rag/` Python pipeline and needs a valid `GOOGLE_API_KEY`; RAG search degrades gracefully until it's built. (`requirements.txt` now includes the previously-missing `langchain-classic`.)

Targets `cline-upstream-base` (snapshot of cline `5fdd840d5`) so the diff is reviewable as *just aria's changes*. Landing into the fork line (`sync-upstream-0419`) is a separate git operation (the fork adopts the full monorepo migration).
