author: jerseycheese
body:
## Description

Collapses the app shell from three surfaces to two. `getSurfaceMode()` returned `default | workshop | manuscript`, and `AppSurfaceShell` picked between a top header, a 288px left rail with its own contextual header, and the chrome-free manuscript. Now it returns `app | manuscript`: one chrome everywhere outside play, and the manuscript surface for play, untouched.

The rail's justification expired. It arrived in #1071 when three design systems needed to feel like three products, and ADR-013 deleted two of them. What survived was two shells serving the same three destinations, drifting apart — `/worlds/[id]` shipped two Play buttons in two colours 71px apart, both going to the same route; four nav components carried four different control sets; one hamburger opened one of two drawers with different keyboard contracts depending on the route; and the rail's section label sat at 3.9:1.

What changed:

- **One header everywhere outside play.** `/about` gets the same chrome as `/worlds`. Content resolves to the 1200px `--content-max-width` column, so the 11 former workshop routes widen by ~190px, and `.page-layout-description` caps at `70ch` so prose keeps its measure while tables and grids use the full width.
- **The header absorbs the rail's CTA**, with suppression extended from `/worlds` alone to every route that owns the play or create action inline. That's the double-Play fix. Play switches to the `success` variant so it stops being the one Play control in the app rendered in slate.
- **Breadcrumbs suppress on `/characters` and `/settings`** too — they're top-level destinations now. Exact match, not a prefix, so `/settings/providers` and the detail routes keep theirs.
- **The mobile drawer is a real modal dialog** — `role="dialog"`, `aria-modal`, a Tab trap, and focus handed back to the hamburger on close. It covered the page while announcing itself as a plain navigation landmark and let Tab walk out behind it.
- **~350 lines of shell CSS deleted**, including the DS3 `:root` block that gave the rail its uppercase-mono console voice and the 3.9:1 label. `workshop.css` no longer contains a workshop, so it's `app-shell.css`.
- **Canon added**, which is the part that stops this recurring: an `AppShell` Storybook story showing the header's four CTA states side by side, and a DESIGN.md `Surfaces` section.

**This reverses [#1432](https://github.com/jerseycheese/Narraitor/issues/1432) F7**, which looked at the same header-to-sidebar jolt during v1.0 QA and kept the rail because it was "well-differentiated across DS (folio / bento / console)". ADR-013 then removed the two systems that differentiation was for, and the decision was never revisited. The reversal holds because its stated reason no longer exists.

## Related Issue

Closes #1655

<!-- Merging to develop rather than the default branch, so this won't auto-close. Closing manually post-merge. -->

## Type of Change

- [ ] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [ ] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected)
- [x] Refactoring (code improvements without changing functionality)
- [x] Documentation update
- [x] Test addition or improvement

## TDD Compliance

- [ ] Tests written before implementation
- [x] All new code is tested
- [x] All tests pass locally
- [x] Test coverage maintained or improved

Not TDD in the strict sense — this is mostly deletion, and the shape of what survives was already specified in the issue. Tests moved with the code rather than ahead of it. Net new coverage: an `AppSurfaceShell` suite (there was none), four `HeaderNavigation` cases for the CTA and breadcrumb rules, and two `MobileNavigationMenu` a11y cases. 2400 passing, up from 2393.

## User Stories Addressed

As a returning player, I cross `/dashboard` → `/worlds` → `/worlds/[id]` without re-learning the chrome twice before reading a line of prose.

As a screen-reader user, no view announces two controls with the identical name "Help & Tutorials", and the mobile drawer tells me the page behind it is inert instead of presenting itself as ordinary navigation I can Tab straight out of.

## Flow Diagrams

N/A

## Component Development

- [x] Storybook stories created/updated
- [x] Components developed in isolation first
- [x] Visual consistency verified

New `04-Templates/layouts/AppShell` story with four stories — `NoWorlds`, `WorldsNoneActive`, `ActiveWorld`, `CtaSuppressed` — seeded through the sanctioned `withStores` decorator. This is the artifact that was missing: Storybook had a story for `HeaderNavigation` and nothing for the rail, the contextual header, or the shell, and the Workshop layout pattern lived only in an archived HTML file. The two shells drifted precisely because nothing ever put them side by side.

## Implementation Notes

**Two things the issue asked for that turned out to be no-ops.** The CTA state rules (active world → Play, no worlds → Create Your First World, worlds but none active → nothing) were already what `HeaderNavigation` did; only the variant needed changing. And the modifier-click guard doesn't need porting — the header's nav links are plain `<Link>` with no `onClick`, so cmd-click already opens a new tab. Porting the guard would have meant first adding `navigateWithLoading` to links that don't have it.

**A behaviour delta worth naming:** navigating to `/worlds`, `/characters`, or `/settings` no longer shows the loading message the rail showed, because the header's links are plain `<Link>`. This is already how the header behaved on `/dashboard` and `/about`, so it's a consistency gain, but it is a visible change on 3 routes.

**`/worlds/[id]` still ships two solid buttons** — `View Characters` in accent and `Play in World` in green. Suppressing the header CTA removes the *duplicate Play*, not the two-solid-accents finding that DESIGN.md's usage rule calls out. That one needs a separate look at the page's own action group.

**`.default-surface-*` renamed to `.app-surface-*`** rather than left alone. 17 touch points across 3 files, two of which this PR rewrites anyway; keeping `.default-surface-inner` next to `.app-surface-app` would have left the surface named two ways at once, which is the exact drift this closes.

**The mobile drawer keeps its three CTA states**, including "Create New World" where the header shows nothing. That's deliberate — a drawer is a menu, not a header CTA, and the extra affordance earns its place there.

**#1076 (route groups) shrinks to almost nothing** now that there are two modes and manuscript is play-only. Worth a comment on that issue rather than a change here.

**A randomized visual crawl over the six changed routes** (six breakpoints per route from 375px to 1920px, light and dark, live DOM rather than screenshots) found four things worth a follow-up commit, three of them caused by this PR:

- **The breadcrumb band was 1248px wide against the other two bands' 1200px.** `.breadcrumbs-inner` never got the `box-sizing: border-box` its two siblings declare, so the gutter landed outside the max-width. Under the 1200px cap the parent constrains it and nothing shows; past the cap the left edge staggers a full 24px off the header and content. That shipped on every detail route at desktop width, directly under a comment claiming all three bands share an edge. The visual suite missed it because `maxDiffPixels: 10000` swallows a text row moving one gutter - worth knowing that budget is wide enough to hide a full-gutter shift.
- **`--color-success-hover` didn't exist**, so `.button-success:hover` fell back to its own resting colour. Survivable while success was a card-only variant; this PR made it the header's primary CTA, which left the most prominent button in the app the only one that doesn't answer a hover. Light darkens, dark lightens - success flips its on-color between schemes.

body:
## Summary

Self-hosting the published image failed at account creation for almost everyone.

Better Auth rejects any request whose `Origin` is not trusted, and `CLIENT_URL` defaults to `http://localhost:8080` — correct only when browsing from the Docker host itself. Reaching a Pi, a NAS, a VM or a VPS by IP or domain gave:

```
POST /api/auth/sign-up/email 403 (Forbidden)
{message: 'Invalid origin', code: 'INVALID_ORIGIN'}
```

Pages and health checks kept working, so it presented as a rejected password rather than a configuration problem. Five of the six realistic deployments were broken out of the box:

| Scenario | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `localhost:8080` on the Docker host | ✅ | ✅ |
| LAN IP — Pi, NAS | ❌ 403 | ✅ |
| LAN hostname | ❌ 403 | ✅ |
| VPS by domain, plain HTTP | ❌ 403 | ✅ |
| Behind a reverse proxy with TLS | ❌ 403 | ✅ |
| Tailscale / VPN address | ❌ 403 | ✅ |

## Related Issues

None.

## Type of Change

Bug fix, security-relevant. Changes a default: `TRUST_HOST` is on unless set otherwise.

## Changes

### `TRUST_HOST` (new, default `true`)

An `Origin` is accepted when its host matches the host the request arrived on. `CLIENT_URL` still applies and is **additive**, so any existing configuration keeps working, and `TRUST_HOST=false` restores the previous strict behaviour exactly.

**CSRF protection is unchanged.** A browser always sets `Host` to the server it is talking to, so a page on `evil.com` arrives as `Origin: https://evil.com` with `Host: notes.example.com` — the hosts differ and it is refused. An attacker cannot make a victim's browser send a forged `Host` without already controlling DNS for that name.

> **Note for review.** This was first implemented with Better Auth's dynamic `baseURL` and `allowedHosts: ['*']`. That is wrong and dangerous: it expands to the literal entries `https://*` and `http://*` in the trusted list, which match **every** origin and disable CSRF protection outright. The test matrix caught it accepting `Origin: https://evil.com`. The shipped implementation uses a `trustedOrigins` callback that binds trust to the request's own host, and `origin.ts` carries a comment explaining why the other approach must not be used.

### Session cookies could lose `Secure` over HTTPS

`baseURL` was `BETTER_AUTH_URL ?? CLIENT_URL[0]`, and Better Auth infers the `Secure` flag from that URL's scheme. So a perfectly reasonable `CLIENT_URL=http://localhost:8080,https://notes.example.com` served **session cookies without `Secure` to HTTPS users**, silently.

Now derived from the declared public address, and startup warns when `TRUST_PROXY` is set without an HTTPS address configured.

### `X-Forwarded-Host` was trusted unconditionally

Better Auth defaults `trustedProxyHeaders` to `true`, so the header was believed even with no proxy in front. Now tied to `TRUST_PROXY`.

### The startup check that should have caught this

[`client-url.ts`](apps/backend/src/lib/client-url.ts) compares only the **port**. With `CLIENT_URL=http://localhost:8080` and the server on 8080 it concluded all was well and stayed silent — the mismatch was in the hostname. It now defers to `TRUST_HOST`.

### Rejected origins are now explained

Better Auth returns a bare 403; the operator could not see which origin was sent or which were trusted. New middleware logs both, plus the `Host` and `TRUST_HOST` state.

### One-time hint for unconfigured TLS proxies (second commit)

The Coolify / Dokploy default — the platform's Traefik terminates HTTPS, forwards plain HTTP — is the one misconfiguration no startup warning can catch: sign-up works thanks to `TRUST_HOST`, nothing fails, so nothing tells the operator that cookies are not `Secure` and rate limiting keys on the proxy's address. At boot there is no request to inspect.

New middleware: when a request carries `X-Forwarded-Proto: https` while `TRUST_PROXY` is unset, log a **one-time** hint naming `BETTER_AUTH_URL` and `TRUST_PROXY` (cookie half dropped if `BETTER_AUTH_URL` is already set). The header is used only to decide whether to print the hint — never for a security decision, which stays gated on `TRUST_PROXY` — so a client sending it directly triggers one log line and nothing else.

### Docs

`DOCKER.md` gains a **Deployment scenarios** table (including a Coolify/Dokploy row), a **Serving over HTTPS** section, and a **Coolify, Dokploy and similar platforms** section (zero-config sign-in, the two production settings, and the `/app/storage` persistent volume without which redeploys lose all data). Both `.env.example` files (root and `apps/backend/`, the latter rewritten by #78) and both compose files document `TRUST_HOST` and the HTTPS requirement.

## How to Test

```bash
docker build -t wordyme:test . && docker run -d --name wm -p 8099:8080 \
  -e BETTER_AUTH_SECRET="$(openssl rand -base64 32)" wordyme:test
```

Note that **no `CLIENT_URL` is set** — this is a default self-host.

1. Sign up through a non-localhost address:
   ```bash
   curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8099/api/auth/sign-up/email \
     -H 'Host: 192.168.1.50:8099' -H 'Origin: http://192.168.1.50:8099' \
     -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
     -d '{"email":"a@b.co","password":"TestPassw0rd!","name":"a"}'
   ```
2. Confirm a cross-site origin is still refused:
   ```bash
   curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8099/api/auth/sign-in/email \
     -H 'Host: 192.168.1.50:8099' -H 'Origin: https://evil.com' \
     -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"email":"a@b.co","password":"TestPassw0rd!"}'
   ```
3. Confirm the flag is what changed it — rerun step 1 against a container started with `-e TRUST_HOST=false`.
4. Check `docker logs wm` for the startup lines and, in step 3, the rejection diagnostic.

**Expected result:** 1 → `200`; 2 → `403`; 3 → `403` plus a logged explanation naming the Origin, the Host and `CLIENT_URL`.

Verified with an 11-case matrix against a running server — origin accepted for LAN IP / domain / Tailscale, refused for `evil.com` and for a lookalike subdomain, previous behaviour intact under `TRUST_HOST=false`, `CLIENT_URL` additive, `X-Forwarded-Host` refused without `TRUST_PROXY` and honoured with it, cookies `Secure` only when an HTTPS address is declared. The full matrix was re-run after rebasing onto `main` (post-#78), and the image was rebuilt and re-verified end to end: sign-up/sign-in 200 from a LAN-style host, CSRF and forged-header cases 403, web app and health 200, plain-HTTP cookies `HttpOnly`/`SameSite=Lax` without `Secure`, HTTPS-declared cookies carrying the `__Secure-` prefix, and the `TRUST_PROXY`-without-HTTPS warning firing exactly when it should. (One sign-in during the run answered 429 — that is the login rate limiter reacting to five rapid attempts from one address, and the same request returned 200 after the window.)

The proxy hint has its own 4-case matrix: fires once across repeated requests, silent when `TRUST_PROXY` is set, silent without the header, and drops the cookie line when an HTTPS address is declared.

Backend lints and typechecks clean. The pre-existing `web` typecheck error at `src/queries/revisions.ts:152` and the `@repo/shared` / `@repo/lib` lint warnings are unrelated and present on `main`.

## Reviewer notes

1. **`TRUST_HOST` defaulting to on** is the decision worth a second opinion — it changes behaviour for existing deployments on upgrade. The argument for it is that the current default produces a broken first run for nearly every self-hoster. Anyone wanting the old behaviour sets `TRUST_HOST=false`.
2. **Accepting both schemes for a matched host.** Behind a TLS proxy the container is spoken to over plain HTTP while the browser reports `https://`, so requiring the schemes to agree would break every proxy deployment that had not also set `TRUST_PROXY`. Reaching the same host over th

author: czearing
body:
## Problem

Launching the app could take many seconds, and sometimes appeared to sign the user out.

Two causes, both on the authentication path:

**1. A MongoDB query on every authenticated request.** `callbacks.session` looked the user up by email to populate `session.user.id`. Every API route calls `getServerSession`, which runs that callback, so each request paid an extra round trip before doing any real work.

**2. Connection settings that turn a blip into a hang.** `serverSelectionTimeoutMS` was only set in development, so production used the driver's 30s default. When that expired, the SRV connection fell back to a direct connection against `cluster:27017` — which an Atlas SRV cluster does not serve — burning a second timeout. The rejected promise was then cached for the life of the instance, so that instance never recovered.

## Fix

Resolve the user id once in `callbacks.jwt` and cache it on the token. NextAuth re-encodes and re-sets the session cookie after running the callback ([`core/routes/session.js`](https://github.com/nextauthjs/next-auth/blob/v4/packages/next-auth/src/core/routes/session.ts)), so later requests read the id from the JWT with no database access.

`events.signIn` creates the user document *after* `callbacks.jwt` first runs, so a missing document is retried rather than cached as a miss. A failed lookup no longer throws — that returned an empty session and signed the user out.

On the connection: `serverSelectionTimeoutMS` now applies in production, the direct-connection fallback is development-only (where it exists for mobile-hotspot DNS issues), a rejected promise is evicted so the next request retries, and `maxPoolSize` drops 50 → 10 since serverless multiplies the pool by instance count.

## Measured

Against an unreachable database, identical requests:

| case | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| session with a cached id | 41144ms, empty body | **60ms**, valid session |
| session without one | 41144ms, empty body | **24ms**, valid session |

The empty body matters as much as the time: the old path signed the user out whenever the database was slow.

## Tests

Five new cases in `src/__tests__/api/auth/nextauth.test.ts` covering the cache, the no-query steady state, the new-user retry, and the failure path. **Three of them fail against the unmodified baseline.**

Full suite 367 passing, lint clean, production build clean with all static routes preserved and shared JS unchanged at 195 kB.

author: seanbrasse
body:
Foundation for **Chameleons**, the multi-tenant portfolio builder. Nothing here touches the existing portfolio — the new app is entirely self-contained under `chameleons/`, with its own `package.json`, config and dependencies.

## Why it lives in a subdirectory

The plan calls for a fresh repo, and this should become one. My GitHub access is scoped to `seanbrasse/portfolio-builder`, so I couldn't create `seanbrasse/chameleons`. Extracting it later preserves history:

```bash
git subtree split -P chameleons -b chameleons-main
```

`next.config.ts` pins `turbopack.root` for the same reason — root inference otherwise walks up to the outer lockfile and picks up the portfolio's `postcss.config.mjs`. That line is harmless to keep after extraction.

## What's here

**Tenant resolution.** One pure function (`src/server/domain/tenant.ts`) turns a `Host` header or a path into a tenant, in either of two modes:

| Environment | Mode | A published portfolio |
|---|---|---|
| Production | `host` | `sean.chameleons.dev` |
| Vercel preview | `path` | `<preview>.vercel.app/s/sean` |
| Local dev | `host` | `sean.localhost:3000` |

Path mode exists because Vercel preview deployments cannot have wildcard subdomains — without it, tenant routing can't be exercised on a preview at all. Both modes rewrite into the same route group, so only `proxy.ts` branches on the mode. `TENANT_MODE` is server-only and read at runtime, so **one build serves production and previews**; as a `NEXT_PUBLIC_` var it would have been inlined at build time and couldn't.

**Schema** (`supabase/migrations/0001_foundation.sql`). `profiles`, `sites`, `site_versions`, `site_version_media`, `reserved_subdomains`, `platform_admins`. Publishing is a single pointer move — `sites.current_version_id` names the live snapshot — so it's atomic and rollback is a pointer write. That FK is `deferrable initially deferred` because `sites` and `site_versions` reference each other and a cascade delete would otherwise trip on the site's own pointer.

RLS is enabled **and forced** on every table with **no policies** for `anon`/`authenticated`: a leaked browser key returns zero rows. Authorization lives in the application tier, which is why `src/lib/supabase/service.ts` imports `server-only`.

Reserved subdomains are enforced by trigger, since a `CHECK` constraint cannot contain a subquery.

**Layering.** `app/` is transport, `server/domain/` is pure, `server/repos/` is the only place that imports a database client. Conventions are written down in `AGENTS.md` (which the old repo referenced but never had).

## Testing

Tests run at the layer that suits them: **Vitest** over the pure domain (23 tests), **Playwright** over routing in both modes (9 tests).

Both caught real bugs before commit:

- `normalizePath` stripped the trailing slash, so `/s/` became `/s`, missed the site prefix, and fell through to **marketing** instead of 404.
- The render route was at `src/app/_sites/[subdomain]/` — App Router treats underscore-prefixed directories as **private folders**, so the route silently never registered. It's now `(render)/s/[subdomain]`, and because that path is a public URL in path mode, host mode explicitly refuses direct `/s/*` requests so a tenant can't be read off the apex.

`playwright.config.ts` points at a preinstalled Chromium when one exists rather than downloading a second copy.

## Verification

```
typecheck   clean
lint        clean
unit        23 passed
build       4 routes: / · /_not-found · /app · /s/[subdomain]
e2e         9 passed (host + path, same build)
```

## Not done here

Two steps I can't do from a repository, both needed before this deploys:

1. Delegate `chameleons.dev`'s nameservers to Vercel — a wildcard cert needs DNS-01 challenge control, and a CNAME-only setup won't get `*.chameleons.dev`.
2. Add `chameleons.dev`, `app.chameleons.dev` and `*.chameleons.dev` to the Vercel project, then set `TENANT_MODE`/`ROOT_DOMAIN` per environment.

Also still ahead: no template exists yet, so the render route serves a seed record; the builder is a placeholder; and the CI workflow sits at `chameleons/.github/workflows/` where it won't run until extraction.

author: jsonbored
body:
## Summary

`/api/v1/subnets/{netuid}/ownership-history` answered an empty list for 127 of the 128 subnets the poller has ever watched. That was **not** a missing reader — the lakehouse cold tier landed in #9198 and serves (`meta.source: "lakehouse-cold-tier"` in production right now). The reader is complete with respect to the stream it reads, and that stream is nearly empty. Measured 2026-08-03 against the whole 895M-row event table:

```sql
SELECT method, count(*) FROM chain.chain_events
 WHERE pallet = 'SubtensorModule' AND method = 'SubnetOwnerChanged' GROUP BY method
-- [{"method":"SubnetOwnerChanged","n":1}]
```

**One** `SubnetOwnerChanged` event chain-wide (netuid 18, block 8,724,813). The permissionless conviction contest is only one of the ways a subnet's owner can change; the others leave no event of that method behind.

This PR gives the route the source that actually has rows, labels the two apart, and moves the payload's assembly out of the three surfaces that were each doing it themselves.

## What Changed

**The second source.** `chain.subnet_ownership_history` is the poller's own record of who it observed owning each subnet, appended only when the observed owner changes (`deploy/postgres/schema.sql` documents the writer). 135 rows across 128 netuids; three subnets changed owning account between consecutive captures — **18, 86 and 102** — and only 18 has a chain event. So 86 and 102 are transfers that provably happened and that the route published as "never changed hands", in the same words a subnet that really never had would get. `src/subnet-ownership-cold-tier.ts` reads the ledger per netuid and both sources feed the **same** `buildSubnetOwnershipHistory` formatter.

**Deduped, event first.** For netuid 18 the decoded event's old/new coldkeys equal the ledger's consecutive owners (verified by running the shared decoder over the real args), so publishing both would read as two flips. Dedup is on the `(old, new)` account pair.

**A first-ever observation is not a transfer.** It records when tracking began. 128 subnets have exactly that one row — treating them as transfers would invent 128 flips that never occurred. They contribute `observed_through` and nothing else.

**Labelled, because the two mean different things.** Each record carries `source`:

| `source` | `observed_at` means | `block_number` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `chain-event` | when the chain announced the transfer | the block that emitted it |
| `owner-observation` | when the poller **noticed** (an upper bound) | `null` |

A caller that cannot tell them apart would read a capture lag as a transfer time.

**The capture stamp.** `observed_through` is the newest owner observation for the subnet, so "watched, never changed hands" stops being indistinguishable from "not watched since". The ledger is frozen at 2026-08-01; **building a refresh lane is deliberately out of scope** (the poller lives in a private repo), but publishing a stale answer as current is this route's problem and is fixed here — the discipline #9273 and #9296 established.

**One composer, not three reshapes.** All three surfaces already reached the same reader and then each rebuilt the answer by hand: MCP's `narrowOwnershipHistory` kept four fields, GraphQL's resolver kept the same four separately, REST forwarded the payload whole. They agreed only by coincidence, and `source`/`observed_through` would have reached REST alone — #9285 and #9296's shape a third time. The cascade and the field mapping now live in `src/subnet-ownership-answer.ts`; the surfaces stop deciding. `tests/subnet-ownership-surface-parity.test.ts` pins both halves: **structurally**, no surface imports a tier reader or projects the payload (read from source, not from behaviour); **behaviourally**, one set of store responses yields the same records, labels and coverage on REST, MCP and GraphQL.

**R2 SQL constraints.** The ledger read narrows by `netuid` in SQL (unlike the event stream, whose `args` is an opaque JSON string with no netuid predicate expressible at all); the netuid goes through `safeBlockNumber` because there are no bound parameters; there is no `count(DISTINCT)` anywhere. Either leg failing declines the whole read — half a two-source history is a wrong answer wearing the shape of a complete one.

### Live verification (not "tests pass")

`answerSubnetOwnershipHistory` run against the real warehouse, for the exact netuids the issue reported as empty plus the three that changed hands:

```
netuid   0: count=0 observed_through=null                      sources=[]
netuid   1: count=0 observed_through=2026-07-20T08:46:40.378Z  sources=[]
netuid   4: count=0 observed_through=2026-07-20T08:46:40.378Z  sources=[]
netuid   8: count=0 observed_through=2026-07-20T08:46:40.378Z  sources=[]
netuid  18: count=1 observed_through=2026-07-29T03:05:51.987Z  sources=["chain-event"]
netuid  64: count=0 observed_through=2026-07-20T08:46:40.378Z  sources=[]
netuid  86: count=1 observed_through=2026-07-24T17:55:20.256Z  sources=["owner-observation"]
netuid 102: count=1 observed_through=2026-07-21T23:20:19.105Z  sources=["owner-observation"]
netuid  27: count=0 observed_through=2026-07-22T13:15:19.143Z  sources=[]
```

Every line is the intended behaviour, including the zeros:

- **18** publishes ONE record from the chain event, not two — the ledger's matching pair was deduped away, and the surviving record keeps its block.
- **86 and 102** were `ownership_changes: []` before this PR and are real transfers.
- **1, 4, 8, 64, 27** are still `count: 0`, but now carry `observed_through` — the poller watched them and saw no transfer, which is a different statement from the empty they used to return.
- **0** (root) has `observed_through: null`: it has no owning account and no ledger row, so nothing is claimed about it.

### Scope notes

- **Account history is already fixed on `main`.** #9317 landed while this was in flight and computes the per-day series live from `chain.account_events`. That half of #9312 is done, and better than reading the frozen `account_events_daily` rollup would have been; nothing here touches it.
- **`/subnets/{netuid}/conviction` is deliberately untouched, and is also already fixed on `main`.** There is no `chain.subnet_conviction` table at all (the catalog returns "absent"), so it never needed a lakehouse reader — #9320 landed while this was in flight and serves it live from chain storage. Nothing here touches it; the rebase onto that commit keeps its `coldTierChainEventsPayload` conviction branch and only moves the ownership-history branch onto the composer.

## Registry Safety

- [x] Links a tracked, currently-open issue (`Closes #<n>`) — required.

body:
Reworks the terminal UI: navigation, layout and the delete dialog.

**Navigation**

`q` and `esc` closed the whole app from any view. Only the connection list quits now; every sub-view goes back. `ctrl+c` still exits from anywhere.

**Layout**

Views drew their own headers and dividers at column zero, so nothing lined up. Every view now sits in a titled panel:

- Tunnel rows use fixed columns, so status and provider line up instead of drifting with the length of each name. The provider column is measured once for the whole list rather than per row.
- The new-tunnel form centred itself on a width it never used, leaving it offset with empty space beside it. It is now a centred panel, as are settings and the empty state.
- The logs view printed every line it had and overflowed the terminal. It is now clipped to the terminal and shows the newest lines.

**Delete dialog**

Built on the lipgloss canvas and layers, so it floats over the list instead of replacing the screen.

**Colours**

Buttons painted a background without setting a foreground, leaving the label at the terminal default — dark text on bronze, invisible on a light theme. They now carry their own colour pair, covered by a contrast test in both modes.

The README documented `s` for start/stop, which is settings; the shortcut table now matches the keymap.

Verified with `go test -race`, `golangci-lint`, cross-compiles for windows/linux/darwin, and by driving the built binary in a pty.

body:
## What & why

Follow-up to Phase 3.4.1 (cloud playlists). Stabilizes cloud-playlist runtime defects, adds an **in-app invitation notification** system, **playlist privacy management**, and a **flag-gated Party entry scaffold**. **Additive DB migration only** (extends the pre-existing `notifications` table — no `paax-api`/Railway change). UI preserved, playback untouched, still Provider + ChangeNotifier.

## Changes

**Playlist runtime (§A–D, H)**
- **Reorder overlap** — Edit-Order first row no longer renders under the fixed top bar; the list top inset is composed from the real bar height via a pure, unit-tested helper (`editOrderListPadding`).
- **Delete/leave/unfollow by role** — root cause of *"deleted in app but still in Supabase"* was optimistic local removal with no RPC and no rollback + role confusion. Delete is now **RPC-first with rollback** (owner-only `playlist_delete`, throws before any local change → no local-only deletion). Overflow shows one correct action per role: owner=Delete, collaborator=Leave, follower=Remove-from-library, invitee=Decline. UI visibility is convenience; **RPC/RLS is authoritative**.
- **"Last modified…" always tappable** for every cloud playlist (on-demand fetch + synthesized "created" event; actor username, never a UUID).
- **Edit privacy (owner)** — Private/Public via version-checked `playlist_update_metadata`, grouped `visibility_changed` activity, conflict rollback. Visibility ⊥ collaboration.

**Invitation notifications (§E, F)**
- `notifications` extended (`actor_user_id, entity_type, entity_id, acted_at, dedupe_key, deleted_at`) + partial-unique dedupe index + realtime.
- Trusted `private.emit_playlist_notification` (EXECUTE revoked from all client roles) fires **inside** the collaboration RPCs (invite/accept/decline/leave/remove/transfer) to the correct recipient, deduped.
- Flutter inbox layer (`AppNotification`, `NotificationInbox`, `NotificationRealtimeService`, `NotificationController`) + **Home bell** (live red badge, hidden@0, caps "99+", never blocks tap) + **Notifications screen** (Today/Earlier, unread-distinct, relative time, pull-to-refresh, realtime, inline Accept/Decline, mark-one-on-open, "Mark all as read", loading/empty/error states). Account-switch safe (realtime filtered `user_id=eq`, rebound + rows discarded).

**Create action sheet + Party (§G)**
- "+" opens Create-playlist / **Start-a-Party**. Create playlist unchanged. Party is an **entry scaffold behind `AppConfig.partyEnabled` (default OFF)**: informational prep sheet, **creates nothing**, no Party backend.

## Security (adversarial review)

Notification rows are **server-authored only** — RLS has no client INSERT policy; SELECT/UPDATE/DELETE own-rows-only; emitter payload is display-safe (playlist title/cover + actor username, no private track data). Verified in **production with disposable users in rolled-back transactions**:
- Direct client INSERT of a forged notification → **blocked**.
- Direct call to the emitter as `authenticated` → **blocked** (revoked EXECUTE).
- Non-owner invite → `FORBIDDEN`.
- Full lifecycle (invite/accept/decline/leave/remove/transfer) emits to the correct recipient exactly once; re-invite **dedupes**; removed collaborator's pending invite is revoked. Zero test data left behind.

## Tests

+32 automated (notification model, inbox realtime lifecycle, controller state/realtime/mark-read/invite-response/account-isolation, Home bell badge, reorder-header geometry, create/Party sheet). Full suite green; `flutter analyze` clean. One **pre-existing** empty smoke test fails on `path_provider` headless (unrelated).

## Build

Debug + release APKs built (`app-debug.apk`, `app-release.apk` 61.9 MB).

## Not in scope (deliberately unchanged)

Playback; cloud likes / hidden tracks / playback-session persistence / listening history / full Party. Supabase authoritative; Hive = cache/journal/device-local pins.

## QA notes

Multi-device realtime delivery + audible playback are **on-device QA** (not verifiable headless). Two-account manual QA recommended before merge.

body:
### Motivation

- Provide a safe, repeatable rehearsal for migrating a hosted Supabase/Postgres database and private GPX Storage to a self-hosted Compose project. 
- Ensure data integrity and compatibility by validating SQL dumps, counts, relationships, and object storage metadata before any cutover. 
- Prevent accidental production changes by enforcing strict project naming, filesystem permissions, and non-destructive orchestration rules. 

### Description

- Add `infrastructure/migration/README.md` documenting the rehearsal process, required input layout, and safety contract. 
- Add orchestration and validation scripts: `run-rehearsal.sh` to perform an isolated migration rehearsal, `validate-inputs.sh` to vet evidence files, and `run-tests.sh` as a test harness. 
- Add utility scripts and SQL: `install-storage-objects.sh` to install GPX files with xattrs into the storage volume, `render-compatible-sql.sh` to strip PostgreSQL-17-only commands from pg_restore output, `clear-targets.sql` and `counts.sql` for reset/count checks, and `validate-restored-data.sql` to assert referential and storage consistency. 
- Update `infrastructure/README.md` to reference the new `migration/` runbook and tools. 

### Testing

- No automated tests were executed as part of this change in the rollout. 
- A bundled test harness `infrastructure/migration/run-tests.sh` was added which exercises `install-storage-objects.sh`, `render-compatible-sql.sh`, and `validate-inputs.sh` with deterministic fixtures and will exit non-zero on failure; run it locally or in CI with `./infrastructure/migration/run-tests.sh` to validate the tooling.

body:
## Summary

- **Bug fix**: `CwmmediafilesController::checkDeleteFiles()` and `CwmmessagesController::checkDeleteFiles()` both called `$this->getModel()->getDatabase()` — but `BaseDatabaseModel::getDatabase()` is `protected`, so calling it from a controller is a scope violation. This is not new to this PR: it predates the refactor (confirmed via `git show` on the pre-refactor commit) and means both AJAX endpoints have been returning HTTP 500 on every real invocation. Confirmed live: `cwmmediafiles.checkDeleteFiles?cid[]=<id>` and `cwmmessages.checkDeleteFiles?cid[]=<id>` both 500'd with `Call to protected method ...getDatabase() from scope ...Controller` before this fix, and return 200 with the expected JSON shape after.
- **Dedup** (#1448): the two controllers' `checkDeleteFiles()` bodies were a ~70-line near-verbatim duplicate (same join query + `Registry` parsing loop), differing only in matching `mf.id` vs `mf.study_id`. Extracted into `CwmmediafilesHelper::findFilesForDelete(DatabaseInterface $db, array $ids, string $idColumn)`.

**User-facing impact of the bug fix**: this endpoint backs the "physical files will be affected" warning modal in `media/js/delete-confirm.js` on the Media Files and Messages list views. When the endpoint fails, the JS `.catch()` deliberately falls through to the normal delete (`origSubmitbutton(task)`, "never block deletion on AJAX failure") — so delete itself was never broken, but the warning modal that tells an admin their action will also delete files off disk has not been firing.

**Not fixed here — filing separately**: while confirming this fix, I found the JS's own CSRF-token lookup (`form.querySelector('input[type="hidden"][value="1"]')`) matches the `delete_physical_files` hidden field before the actual token field in both list templates (same order in both `admin/tmpl/cwmmediafiles/default.php` and `admin/tmpl/cwmmessages/default.php` — `delete_physical_files` renders immediately before `HTMLHelper::_('form.token')`). That sends the wrong param to the endpoint, `Session::checkToken('get')` fails, and the modal is skipped for that reason too — independent of the bug fixed here. That's a JS-only fix with different blast radius, so it's out of scope for this PR; will file as a follow-up issue.

## Test plan

- [x] New/updated tests: `CwmmediafilesHelperTest` (4, including 2 real DB round-trips against `Factory::getContainer()->get(DatabaseInterface::class)`), `CwmmediafilesControllerTest` / `CwmmessagesControllerTest` (3 each, including a dedicated regression test pinning the `getDatabase()` fix)
- [x] Verified fail-before/pass-after via `git stash` (7 failures + 3 errors of 10 pre-fix; all 10 pass post-fix)
- [x] Full unit suite green, lint clean
- [x] Live-tested both endpoints in-browser with a valid CSRF token: `cwmmediafiles.checkDeleteFiles?cid[]=2470` → `{"success":true,"hasFiles":false,"files":[]}`; `cwmmessages.checkDeleteFiles?cid[]=829` → same shape
- [ ] Not exercised: the `hasFiles: true` branch / full delete-confirm modal flow — no server on this dev site has `delete_files=1` set, and triggering a real delete to test the modal path risked destructive side effects on dev data. That branch has no live or automated coverage beyond the helper's query-validity tests.

author: mrmogulmaker-bot
body:
## Summary

Automates the §32 **pre-merge** migration proof (§24 — stop hand-running the chunked `BEGIN..ROLLBACK` mechanic). On a migration PR it restores a **read-only dump of prod's current schema** into a throwaway `supabase/postgres` container, applies **only the PR's new migrations** on top, and reports pass/fail. It never touches prod except the read-only dump. This is the PRE-merge twin of `deploy-migrations.yml` (the post-merge actuator).

## ⚠️ ADVISORY / NON-REQUIRED (owner-ruled 2026-08-03)
This check reports status but **MUST NOT be added to branch-protection required checks yet** — it does **not** gate merge. Rationale (§13/§32): the baseline-restore step (Finding B) can't be proven viable headless, so making it blocking risks false-RED-ing legitimate migrations. **Promote to required only after BOTH:** (1) green across **3+ successive real migration PRs**, and (2) **Finding B empirically resolved** (restore succeeds against the real prod schema — `auth.users` FKs, `pg_cron`, `vector`). Until then, migration PRs keep the manual chunked proof (Slice A pattern); merge under that manual proof is authorized.

## Adversarial-hardened (crew RESIDUAL_HOLE folded)
The design crew's adversarial pass found the naïve Option-A shape would false-RED real migrations; all folded:
- **Finding A** — apply **per-statement** (no `psql -1`) to match prod's `db push` autocommit. Avoids false-RED on self-wrapping `BEGIN;…COMMIT;` files (`20260802120000`), top-level `ALTER TYPE … ADD VALUE` (`20260628013738`), and `CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY`.
- **Finding C** — **skip** migrations already recorded on prod (`schema_migrations` Remote list) — a hand-applied migration is already in the dump; re-applying a non-idempotent file would false-RED.
- **Finding D** — `search_path` parity (`extensions` on path) so unqualified extension calls resolve. (Role parity imperfect — psql superuser; a superuser-permitted DDL a prod role would reject is an advisory-phase false-GREEN risk, accepted until promotion.)
- **Finding B** — the baseline restore may choke (`auth.users` FKs / `pg_cron` / `vector`); treated as **INCONCLUSIVE** (non-failing), disclosed in the PR comment, never a merge gate.
- **#275** — restore a **dump end-state** + apply only new migrations — never replays the broken full chain (duplicate `profiles`, `realtime.messages` RLS).
- **Same-repo guard** — fork PRs (no credentials) **error visibly**, never a silent no-op. `SUPABASE_DB_PASSWORD` is scoped to the dump step only (never in the PR-controlled apply/harness step's env).

## §13 output posture
The workflow posts an advisory comment on every migration PR:
- **PASS:** "§32 pre-merge proof: advisory PASS — migration applied cleanly against prod schema baseline. Reviewer verification still recommended until this check is promoted to required."
- **FAIL:** "§32 pre-merge proof: advisory FAIL — [error]. This is a NON-BLOCKING advisory check; owner has authorized merge under manual proof if verified via chunked `BEGIN..ROLLBACK`. Do not treat this as a merge gate yet."
- **INCONCLUSIVE:** restore couldn't complete (Finding B) — didn't evaluate the migration; not a gate.

## Testing / §13 honesty
This workflow is path-filtered to `supabase/migrations/**`, so it does **not** run on its own PR (which adds only a `.github/workflows` file) — it first runs on the **next migration PR** (e.g. Slice B). That is the intended advisory-first shape: it can't false-block anything, and its first real run is the empirical test of Finding B. The `supabase/postgres` image tag (`15.8.1.020`) is **illustrative** — confirm it against prod's Postgres major before promotion. YAML validated (`yaml.safe_load` clean).

## Scope + Known Gaps
**In scope:** the advisory workflow + all four fidelity fixes. **Promotion-gated (not now):** required-check status; the least-privilege scoped read-only dump role (advisory phase reuses `SUPABASE_DB_PASSWORD`); empirical Finding B resolution. **Follow-up if restore proves unviable:** a lighter-weight verification or pre-configuring extensions in the container.

author: jkup
body:
Records the owner's answers to task 0570's seven open questions, unblocking the T1–T8 implementation chain.

**0043 — the power curve is long and shallow.** Levels matter early, then the player caps out and grinds gear for hours with gear that keeps getting better. The measured **×2.59375** EHP multiplier from one max-rolled chest rare is explicitly **not** ratified as the target: a curve where one slot doubles a character ends the grind in an evening. Calibrate to an endgame fully-geared-vs-ungeared ratio — the ×2.6 was measured against a deliberately weak level-5 avatar wearing nothing else, always the most dramatic case. Expect some shipped affixes to need re-costing (content files, no schema change).

**0044 — Model A: per-stat item-level ceiling curves.** Static, readable from authored files, enforceable in `checkReferences` with no new infrastructure — this is what makes `ARCHITECTURE.md`'s "no item exceeds the power budget for its level" invariant executable at last. Model B rejected for now (its weights are outcome claims; 0570 measured one affix swinging 12× across builds, so it would need a harness to mean anything). Plus: `more` denied on affixes; attribute affixes priced through `ATTRIBUTE_DERIVATIONS`; the 3/3 per-slot floor stays until a phase-4 content task raises it; any future harness runs beside `verify`, not inside.

Both entries carry forward the two constraints 0570 proved, so no implementing task re-litigates them: converted crit is computed at the call boundary and **never stored on a component** (widening `Combatant` moves five of six golden replays — demonstrated by hash), and DoT riders stay rng-silent because decision 0036 already forecloses DoT crit.

author: gonzaloagustins
body:
Seguimiento de #88, que ya está mergeado. Ahí el dropdown de Producto quedó con seis filas; dos no se ganaban el lugar.

## Qué se saca

**"Vista general del producto"** era andamiaje de navegación. El hub ya es alcanzable desde el footer y desde el breadcrumb de cada página de capacidad — una tercera vía solo empujaba las capacidades hacia abajo sin agregar nada.

**"Cómo funciona"** duplicaba lo que esas páginas ya cubren. De las tres pestañas de `/como-funciona`, dos repiten los pasos casi textualmente:

| Pestaña de /como-funciona | Estado |
|---|---|
| **Para asistentes**: Accede → Explora la carta → Realiza tu compra → Retira o recibe | Versión genérica de las tres páginas de venta. Compará con Compra y retiro: *Accede a Ronda Privé → Explora y compra → … → Retira tu pedido* |
| **Para barra y cocina**: Recibe el pedido → Inicia preparación → Escanea y entrega → Actualiza estado | Duplica `/producto/operacion-de-cocina` |
| **Para organizadores**: Configura → Monitorea → Controla → Analiza | Lo único genuinamente nuevo — y es otra audiencia, no encaja bajo Producto |

Es exactamente la canibalización que las páginas separadas venían a evitar.

El menú queda en las cuatro capacidades: compra anticipada, entrega en asiento, compra y retiro, y operación de barra y cocina.

## Un detalle no obvio

`/como-funciona` **sigue siendo poseída** por la entrada Producto aunque ya no esté listada. Así, caer ahí desde el home enciende Producto en vez de dejar el menú apagado — que era justo el bug que arreglaba #88. Poseer una página y listarla son cosas distintas; está comentado en el código y hay un test que verifica las dos mitades: que enciende Producto y que no aparece en el dropdown.

## Verificación

- 25 tests verdes. El test del dropdown ahora afirma la lista exacta de cuatro hrefs, así que agregar una fila de vuelta sin pensarlo rompe el build.
- `tsc` y eslint limpios.
- Verificado en el navegador: cuatro items, sin divisor, panel más compacto.
- `product.overview` sigue en uso (footer y pie del teaser del home). `navbar.howItWorks` queda como clave i18n sin uso, igual que varias que ya existen en el repo (`footer.howItWorks`, `navbar.insights`, `navbar.dashboard`).

## Seguimiento sugerido

Dos cosas que quedan planteadas y no toca este PR:

1. **`/como-funciona`** ahora tiene dos de tres pestañas redundantes. La salida honesta es plegar asistentes y cocina en las páginas de producto y reubicar organizadores donde vive el relato de negocio.
2. **Los labels**: "Compra y Retiro" con R mayúscula contra el resto en minúscula, y en en/pt/fr esa capacidad se llama "Pick Up Express" mientras el español es descriptivo.
